Дорогой товарищ, – Позволь мне сказать несколько слов о статье Кропоткина об антимилитаризме, опубликованной в вашем последнем номере. По моему мнению, антимилитаризм – это доктрина, утверждающая, что военная служба есть отвратительное и убийственное ремесло, и что человек никогда не должен соглашаться брать оружие по приказу господ и никогда не должен воевать иначе как за Социальную Революцию.

Разве это - неправильное понимание антимилитаризма?

Кропоткин, похоже, забыл об антагонизме классов, о необходимости экономического освобождения и обо всём анархистском учении; и говорит, что антимилитарист всегда должен быть готов, в случае если разразится война, взяться за оружие в поддержку «страны, которая подвергнется нападению»; что, учитывая невозможность – по крайней мере, для рядового рабочего – своевременно установить, кто истинный агрессор, на практике означает, что «антимилитарист» Кропоткина всегда должен подчиняться приказам своего правительства. Что остаётся после этого от антимилитаризма и, в самом деле, даже от самого анархизма?

Фактически Кропоткин отказывается от антимилитаризма, потому что думает, что национальные вопросы должны быть решены прежде социального вопроса. Для нас национальные соперничества и ненависть относятся к числу лучших средств, которыми располагают господа для увековечения рабства рабочих, и мы должны противостоять им всеми нашими силами. Что же касается права малых национальностей сохранять, если они того пожелают, свой язык и свои обычаи, – это просто вопрос свободы, и он найдёт реальное и окончательное решение только тогда, когда, после разрушения государств, каждая человеческая группа, более того, каждый индивид получит право объединяться с любой другой группой и отделяться от неё.

Мне очень больно выступать против такого старого и любимого друга, как Кропоткин, который сделал так много для дела анархизма. Но именно по той причине, что Кропоткин столь ценим и любим всеми нами, необходимо дать знать, что мы не следуем за ним в его высказываниях о войне.

Я знаю, что эта позиция Кропоткина не вполне нова и что более десяти лет он проповедовал против «немецкой угрозы»; и признаюсь, что мы были неправы, не придав значения его франко-русскому патриотизму и не предвидя, куда приведут его антинемецкие предрассудки. Это потому, что мы понимали: он намеревался призвать французских рабочих ответить на возможное немецкое вторжение, совершив Социальную Революцию, – то есть взяв в свои руки французскую землю и пытаясь побудить немецких рабочих брататься с ними в борьбе против французских и немецких угнетателей. Разумеется, мы никогда не могли бы вообразить, что Кропоткин призовёт рабочих к единению с правительствами и хозяевами.

Надеюсь, что он увидит свою ошибку и встанет снова на сторону рабочих против всех правительств и всех буржуа: немцев, англичан, французов, русских, бельгийцев и так далее.

title: Palestinian Arts Workers Call for Solidarity
content:
Palestinian cultural workers living through apartheid, occupation, and genocide are

calling for solidarity

 from their counterparts abroad.


Not every artist has as large a platform as rapper Macklemore, children’s TV star Miss Rachel, or country singer Zach Bryan—who wore a “Free Palestine” shirt last weekend while playing a packed show at the same stadium where billionaire Robert Kraft had barred Macklemore for saying those words—but there’s plenty that artists and art workers can do to end complicity in Israel’s ongoing atrocities.


We as Palestinians have long decried Israel’s war crimes and crimes against humanity. Now the

Palestinian Performing Arts Network

 (PPAN), representing hundreds of Palestinian dancers, actors, musicians, playwrights, and circus performers, has

outlined

 four ways that U.S. arts unions can lend solidarity:


1. Reject the blacklisting and censorship of members who speak out on behalf of Palestinian rights.


For example, British Actors’ Equity

passed a motion in the UK’s Trade Union Congress

, representing 5 million workers, affirming the right of artists to “critique institutions and bring attention to issues through overtly political art without fear of censorship or losing their public funding.”


In the U.S., over 700 entertainment industry union members signed a 2024

open letter calling on SAG-AFTRA

 to back a ceasefire, protect members from blacklisting, and condemn the targeting of journalists.


2. Refuse to work with institutions and corporations—such as venues, festivals, publishers, broadcasters, and foundations—that are verifiably complicit in Israel’s crimes against Palestinians, and divest union funds from such corporations.


In fall 2025, over 5,500 film industry workers

signed such a pledge

. Earlier that year, Norway’s actors union Norsk Skuespillerforbund (NSF)

recommended that its members

 “reject work and collaboration with Israeli cultural institutions that operate in violation of the Palestinian cultural boycott.”


3. Exclude Israel from international labor federations

 such as the International Federation of Actors (FIA) and International Federation of Musicians (FIM).


4. Pressure governments to compel Israel to end its genocide and apartheid through lawful sanctions.


“Historically, including in the struggle that ended apartheid in South Africa, organized labor has been the working person’s leverage,” the PPAN said. “[Unions are] a powerful force for peace and justice when governments fail.”


UNION MOVES


Drawing inspiration from the global movement to end South African apartheid, Palestinian unions and workers have consistently

called on unions worldwide

 to use sanctions, boycotts, and divestment (BDS) campaigns as pressure points to end Israel’s genocide and occupation.


The United Auto Workers has

endorsed divestment

 from Israel bonds and acted on it. Since 2023, a smattering of Palestine solidarity groups across unions have pushed for pension fund divestment, joined other unions abroad to

block arms to Israel

 at international docks, and

protested complicit corporations>

.


The United Auto Workers, the United Electrical Workers (UE), National Nurses United, and the Painters have also thrown their support behind an

end to military funding

 to Israel and

divestment

. UE also became the first national union to endorse the BDS movement.


Some rank and filers have been forming loose solidarity networks like

Entertainment Labor for Palestine

,

Purple Up for Palestine

 (SEIU),

CWA4Palestine

, and

IATSE Members for Palestine

.


Union members can find resources like

Ethical Investment

 and

Ethical Procurement Policies

 to keep union pension funds and vendor contracts out of companies complicit in human rights abuses anywhere, including Palestine.


In the UK, on September 8, British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband called illegal settlements in the West Bank “ethnic cleansing,” as part of the announcement of sanctions against Israel. Shortly thereafter, the UK’s Trade Union Congress, representing 5 million workers,

endorsed the Palestinian-led BDS movement

.


ATROCITIES ONGOING


The calls come as Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza reaches horrifying numbers. At least

80,000 Palestinians had been killed by Israel

 as of January 2025, which is likely an undercount as Israel’s destruction in Gaza is so extensive that it has obstructed our ability to even count our dead. Israeli settlers’ land theft in the West Bank …

author: labor4pal
title: Eyewitness report: Strikers and students rock France, Anti-fascism and Palestinian liberation mixed with anger at president Emmanuel Macron and the establishment (Socialist Worker-UK)
content:
Anti-fascism and Palestinian liberation mixed with anger at president Emmanuel Macron and the establishment

On the streets of Paris (Picture: Guy Smallman)

There were protests in 40 cities across France on Tuesday as workers and parents joined the movement of secondary school students demanding a future.

In Paris, organisers said 100,000 packed the streets. They were overwhelmingly young school and university students.

Young people chanted anti-fascist slogans. They included, “La jeunesse emmerde le Front National”—“The youth tell the Front National to fuck off” in a reference to the previous name of the fascist RN. And, “Siamo tutti antifascisti”—“We are all anti-fascist”.

They sang the Internationale and the French national anthem La Marseillaise. And there were Palestinian flags and chants of “free Palestine”. Other home made placards referenced the student and worker uprising of 1968.

When the presidential candidate for the left wing LFI party, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, arrived at the start of the march, he was mobbed by crowds of people. Both young and older protesters greeted him with chants of “president Mélenchon”.

Mélenchon called on his supporters, including many members of parliament, to join the protests. He wore a white armband on Tuesday to symbolise his support for the high school students.

As the march arrived in Place de la Nation, hundreds of riot police attacked with huge clouds of tear gas and charged at the crowd with batons. Protesters threw fireworks and set bins on fire.

Nora, Sarah and Sonia, three university students, spoke to Socialist Worker about their reasons for joining the protest.

“We protest for the rights of high school students,” they said. “All the media talks about is violence. But there are real reasons behind their protests.

“The RN is fascist. It’s homophobic and Islamophobic”.

Another student, Alice, said that young people are worried about their futures, “We are all worried about fascism, every student is worried about that. And about finding a job, everything is kind of scary.

“High school students are very stressed. We went through that so we want to be here with them.”

Trade unionists linked arms and faced up to cops with tear gas.

Pierre works in the tax office and is part of the Solidaires union federation. He told Socialist Worker, “I am on strike today, in solidarity with the students against repression and because we have the same problems with austerity.”

Clement, from the CFDT union federation, told Socialist Worker, “The demands of the school students are totally legitimate. The buildings are crumbling, there are rats in the classrooms, there are 30, 35 or even 40 people in a classroom.

“It’s a terrible period with the far right rising across Europe. We could see fascism in France for the second time in its history.”

Clement added that the current president Emmanuel Macron has “rolled out the red carpet for the RN’s Marine Le Pen”.

Another protester mentioned that there are already fascists joining the police force and that Le Pen would use them to smash the movement on the streets if she was in office.

Meet the pupils’ blockade: ‘We are young, determined and revolutionary’

Macron’s austerity measures and repression, combined with the normalisation of racism against migrants has created the conditions for the far right to rise.

Le Pen is currently leading in the polls, while Mélenchon is currently in second place.

The best hope of beating Le Pen will be if the movement stays on the streets and links the anger of the students with the power of the organised working class.

Key opportunities to deepen the movement are coming this month. Total Energy workers are set to strike Thursday—and there is a day of action on 17 October.

Anti-fascists are planning to demonstrate against the far right RN party’s conference on 24 October.

If the movement of school students and strikes deepens, it has the power to transform the political situation in France.

author: Michael_1973
title: Abahlali baseMjondolo archive - 2005 - 2026
content:
Abahlali was formed at a meeting of 34 people held in Durban on 4 October 2005. When the movement celebrated its 21st anniversary in Durban on 4 October 2026 it had more than 200 000 members across five of South Africa's nine provinces.


In 21 years of struggle it has won large tracts of urban land, extracted significant policy concessions and resolutely opposed the xenophobia that is systemically used to divided impoverished and working class people in South Africa. It has also built strong connections with radical movements around the world and has, in recent years, moved towards building communes.


The struggle has come at a high cost. As of 4 October 2026 26 lives have been lost in the course of the struggle.


This archive runs from the movement's formation in 2005 till 4 October 2026 and includes a complete list of all the statements it has issued, memoranda delivered at marches as well as the articles and speeches by its members which are archived on the movement's website.

author: Ezra
title: Bring Maja back: Antifaschist*in muss sofort aus Ungarn hierher überstellt werden!
content:
Bring Maja back: Antifaschist*in muss sofort aus Ungarn hierher überstellt werden!


Der Fall gehört zum sog. Budapest-Komplex: Maja und weiteren Antifaschist*innen wird vorgeworfen, sich im Februar 2023 an körperlichen Auseinandersetzungen mit Nazis am Rand des

NS

-verherrlichenden Großevents „Tag der Ehre“ in Budapest beteiligt zu haben. Seither läuft eine internationale Verfolgungsjagd gegen Antifaschist*innen, die vor allem von Ungarn und Deutschland vorangetrieben wird. Ende 2023 wurde Maja in Berlin von deutschen Ermittlungsorganen verhaftet und im Juni 2024 in einer rechtswidrigen Nacht-und-Nebel-Aktion an Ungarn ausgeliefert – nur Stunden, bevor das Bundesverfassungsgericht diesen Schritt explizit untersagte: Insbesondere für eine non-binäre antifaschistische Person ist die Situation im weiterhin rechtsautoritären und offen queerfeindlichen Ungarn lebensgefährlich. Das Gericht hatte dabei am 24. Januar 2025 nicht nur die Rechtswidrigkeit von Majas Auslieferung festgestellt, sondern auch die deutschen Behörden verpflichtet, sich für eine schnellstmögliche Rückführung einzusetzen.

Seit diesem Rechtsbruch der deutschen Behörden war Maja unter katastrophalen Haftbedingungen in Budapest eingekerkert: Schimmliges Essen, Ungeziefer in der Zelle, defizitäre Duschmöglichkeiten, ständige nächtliche Kontrollen und demütigende Nacktdurchsuchungen, Trennscheibe bei allen Besuchen – und vor allem anhaltende Isolationshaft, die nach internationalen Standards als Folter gilt. Mit einem mehrwöchigen Hungerstreik protestierte Maja im Sommer 2025 gegen diese unmenschliche Behandlung. Am 17. Juli 2026 kam es sogar zu brutaler körperlicher Gewalt durch vermummtes Wachpersonal, das Maja in der Zelle zusammenschlug, zwangsweise entkleidete, um Maja zum Tragen von nach ihrer Ansicht geschlechtsentsprechender Kleidung zu zwingen, und dann auch noch disziplinarisch verfolgte. Es war genau diese Situation, vor der im Auslieferungsverfahren immer wieder gewarnt worden war.

Für die Farce des offenkundig politischen Schauprozesses in Ungarn war keine angemessene Vorbereitung möglich: Anwaltsgespräche konnten nur beeinträchtigt stattfinden, die meisten Unterlagen lagen nur auf ungarisch vor, und Maja konnte die digitale Akte kaum sichten. Im Gerichtssaal wurde die non-binäre Person in Ketten und an einer Hundeleine vorgeführt, begleitet von medialer Stimmungsmache. Obwohl der Prozess keinerlei Hinweise erbrachte, dass Maja aktiv an den vorgeworfenen Handlungen beteiligt war, belief sich das erstinstanzliche Urteil am 4. Februar 2026 auf acht Jahre Haft unter schwersten Bedingungen. Die Berufung reduzierte dieses absurde Strafmaß am 30. September 2026 nur geringfügig auf sieben Jahre sowie eine Geldstrafe und machte damit erneut deutlich, dass in erster Linie die antifaschistische Haltung bestraft werden sollte.

Dass Maja spätestens nach dem Urteil umgehend zurück nach Deutschland überstellt wird, war ohnehin die bindende Grundvoraussetzung für die rechtswidrige Auslieferung gewesen.

„Der Fall von Maja ist ein politischer und juristischer Skandal, der von den deutschen Behörden durch die nächtliche Auslieferung offen rechtswidrig produziert und seit nunmehr weit über zwei Jahren durch Tatenlosigkeit fortgesetzt wird“, empörte sich Hartmut Brückner vom Bundesvorstand der Roten Hilfe e. V. „Wir fordern insbesondere das Bundesjustizministerium auf, endlich das Urteil des Bundesverfassungsgerichts umzusetzen und sofort die Rücküberstellung in die Wege zu leiten.“ Zudem appellierte Brückner: „Wir rufen die Öffentlichkeit dazu auf, gemeinsam politischen Druck auf die zuständigen Behörden auszuüben – durch Petitionen, öffentliche Proteste und Kampagnen. Schluss mit der Folter in Ungarn: Bring Maja back!“

Damit endete ein politischer Schauprozess, der auf rechtsstaatliche Mindeststandards verzichtete, doch die unmenschlichen Haftbedingungen im ungarischen Kerker dauern an und haben sich in der Strafhaft teilweise noch verschärft. Vorausgegangen war Majas rechtswidrige Auslieferung durch deutsche Behörden im Sommer 2024, woraufhin das Bundesverfassungsgericht die deutsche Regierung verpflichtete, sich umgehend für eine Rücküberstellung einzusetzen. title: Küçükçekmece'de eğlence mekanında silahlı saldırı: 1'i polis, 2 kişi hayatını kaybetti
content:
İstanbul - Küçükçekmece'de bir eğlence mekanında silahlı saldırı yaşandı. Çıkan çatışmada 1’i polis, 2 kişi hayatını kaybetti, 2 kişi de yaralandı.

DHA'da yer alan habere göre silahlı saldırı, Atatürk Mahallesi İkitelli Caddesi’nde saat 03.40 sularında meydana geldi. Müzikhole gelen bir kişi henüz bilinmeyen nedenle çevreye ateş açtı. Bu sırada içeride olan ve izinli olduğu öğrenilen polis, ateş açan kişiye karşılık verdi. Çıkan çatışmada polis ile ateş açan kişi ağır yaralandı. Çalışanların ihbarı üzerine olay yerine ekipler sevk edildi. Sağlık ekiplerinin yaptığı kontrolde polis ile saldırganın hayatını kaybettiği belirlendi. Çatışmada 2 kişinin de yaralandığı öğrenildi.

İş yerine ait güvenlik kamera görüntülerini inceleyen ekipler, çalışanların da bilgisine başvurdu. İncelemelerin ardından hayatını kaybeden polis ile saldırganın cansız bedeni Adli Tıp Kurumu morguna kaldırıldı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: anonerror
title: Crónica de Naada en Ceuta
content:
Van a cumplirse un par de semanas desde que volví de Ceuta, y el panorama está cada vez más calentito en nuestro país. Es difícil hablar de cualquier tema político o social sin que surja enemistad… Primero la crisis de Ceuta. Manifestaciones en defensa de España. Mari Carmen. La acampada en Sol y en otras ciudades. Más manifestaciones. El rechazo de los dos decretos. Las elecciones anticipadas…

Me demoré en escribir estas líneas porque me parecía que en este momento podría juzgarse de frivolidad. Que hablar de Ceuta en la actualidad, con otros muchos problemas, sería tachado de inoportuno. Pero me doy cuenta de que ha sido, sigue siendo y será imprescindible no silenciar su voz. Especialmente tras mi visita a la ciudad autónoma, donde pude despertar y ser consciente de que vivimos una gran desinformación desde fuera. Como si a las noticias; las publicaciones en redes sociales y los reportajes les costara cruzar el estrecho sin deformarse, tergiversarse o manipularse en el intento.

Un pueblo mal informado es un pueblo manipulable. Y un pueblo además dividido es un pueblo controlable. Ya lo decía Julio César.

Por eso no es de extrañar que haya una buena campaña de desinformación en marcha desde la entrada masiva de migrantes el 30 y 31 de julio en Ceuta. Existen unos creadores de contenido en redes sociales que buscan, precisamente, la polarización de la sociedad en pensamientos realmente radicales. Hay bulos por todas partes que siembran y alimentan los pensamientos retorcidos llenos de racismo, odio y, a fin de cuentas, miedo. Mientras organizaciones humanitarias, vecinos y vecinas ceutíes y grupos autogestionados se organizan en terreno para responder a contrarreloj y sin medios a todas las necesidades humanitarias de los migrantes que el Gobierno no cubre, otros seres a los que no quiero poner nombre, pero defensores de pensamientos fascistas, se dedican patrullar las calles para “cazarlos a todos”, como un diputado de Vox animaba a hacer. Organizados por redes sociales, se dividen los barrios marginales para dar ueltas en sus coches, amenazar, violentar y perturbar tanto a los dadores de ayuda como a sus receptores.

Es real el descontento de los ceutíes. Hay críticas sobre la situación de la ciudad; sobre la intervención- o su ausencia-, su alcance, su demora, y el modo de ejecutarla del Gobierno y las instituciones. Hay quejas y más quejas. Sin embargo se ven pocas manos tendidas a ayudar. Lo fácil es colgar la bandera del balcón, sacarla al escaparate de tu negocio, o ponérsela en la muñeca, solicitando que tu ciudad vuelva a ser la misma. Más difícil y valiente es jugársela a ser apartado e ir contracorriente de tus vecinos odiadores por acoger en tu casa a unas cuantas personas. Esos casos también los hay y me llenan de emoción, dándome todavía algo de esperanza en la humanidad. Hay estos vecinos y vecinas, que son los que están levantando Ceuta a pasitos pequeños pero constantes.

Sin embargo, lamentablemente, hay un discurso que nos venden como el predominante, porque es lo que interesa que España vea. El de odio y de racismo que están calando en estratos de la sociedad que no deberían hacer manitas con dichas ideologías. Básicamente por puros principios.

Pero creo que ya no sabemos ni qué quiere decir esa palabra. Porque antes que crisis política o social estratégicamente buscada por los hilos invisibles de los poderes fácticos americanos y sionistas, esto es una grandísima crisis humanitaria. Y lo que más está escaseando es la humanidad. Lo que estamos viviendo en Ceuta no es casual y, como vemos, tampoco será inocuo. Pero en este texto no me quiero extender en el análisis de sus orígenes y consecuencias geopolíticas. Eso se lo dejo a los expertos.

Yo tan solo soy una enfermera que ha estado en terreno y que necesita sacar de las entrañas toda la frustración acumulada en mi paso por Ceuta. Así que hablemos de lo que pude experimentar allí, de todo aquello que fui testigo y que contrasta fuertemente con lo que se difunde en redes. Hablemos de lo que realmente está sucediendo a los migrantes y a las vecinas ceutíes.

El día 20 de septiembre celebraron en Ceuta una manifestación en la frontera, a la que acudieron según los reportes 200 personas, con nuestra bandera de España ondeando al grito de “¡invasores fuera! Expulsión”. Bandera que siguen haciendo suya y con la que defienden lo indefendible; la segregación, el maltrato, la violencia. Hablan de defender España y a los Españoles, a los ceutíes …

title: Daxwaza ji bo wergêrê kurdî qebûl nekirin: Penaberê îraqî yê Kurd wekî hemwelatiyê Efxanistanê tomarkirin
content:
Salih Omer Celalê iraqî ji sala 2018an ve li Afyonkarahisarê dijî. Salih Omer Celal xwediyê serlêdana parastina navneteweyî ye ku di 20ê Gulana 2026an de ji bo serlêdana wî ya mafê rûniştinê bê qebûlkirin ket mulaqatê.


Celal diyar kir ku ew nikare di mulaqata parastina navneteweyî de bi asteke ku xwe bi zelalî îfade bike bi tirkî biaxive û ji Rêveberiya Îdareya Koçê ya Bajar daxwaza wergêrê kurdî kir. Lêbelê daxwaza Celal nehat qebûlkirin. Di belgeya serlêdanê ya Celal de jî ew weke “hemwelatiyê Efxanistanê” hate nivîsandin.


Celal weha behsa tiştên ku di hevdîtinê de jiyaye kir: “Ji min re gotin ku wergêrê kurdî tune ye. Piştre ji min re gotin ‘an tu yê bikevî mûlaqatê an jî em ê neçar bimînin ku te bişînin bajarekî din.’ Ji ber vê yekê min nekarî sedemên serlêdana parastina navneteweyî û bûyerên ku rûbirû bû me di mûlaqatê de bi tevahî bînim ziman. Ez wekî hemwelatiyê Efxanistanê tomar kirim. Ji ber vê statûya min ket xetereyê.”


Li gorî Xala 70emîn ya Qanûna Parastina Navneteweyî û Biyaniyan ya Bi Hejmar 6458an, heke serlêderê parastina navneteweyî, di hevdîtinên kesane yên qonaxên serlêdan, tomar û mûlaqatê de daxwaza wergêr bike, divê bê peydakirin. Rêxistina Penaberan a Neteweyên Yekbûyî (UNHCR) diyar dike ku di çarçoveya kiryarên parastina navneteweyî yên li Tirkiyeyê de piştevaniya wergêriyê dê bi rêya rayedarên Rêveberiya Îdareya Koçê ya Bajar bê dabînkirin. Di xeta şêwirmendiyê ya UNHCRê de hatiye diyarkirin ku li ser daxwazê piştevaniya şêwirmendiya kurdî jî dikare bê dayîn.


Ji bo piştevaniya hiqûqî çûye SGDD-ASAMê


Celal di 17ê Tîrmeha 2026an de ji bo ku li ser pirsgirêka wergêriyê ya di mûlaqatê de jiyaye piştevaniya hiqûqî wergire, çûye ofîsa Komeleya Piştgiriya bi Penaber û Koçberan re (SGDD-ASAM). Celal da zanîn ku wî ji xebatkaran re ragihandiye ku zimanê wî ê dayikê kurdî ye û pêdiviya wî bi piştevaniya hiqûqî ya derbarê dosyaya wî ya parastina navneteweyî de heye. Lêbelê hat îdîakirin ku ji wî re weha gotine: “Heke tu ji vir neçî em ê li polîsan bigerin.”


“Armanca min ne derxistina pirsgirêkan bû”


Celal destnîşan kir û weha got: 


“Armanca min tenê ew bû ku ez kêşeya xwe ya wergêriyê ya di dema mulaqata parastina navneteweyî de rûbirû bûme bînim ziman û piştevaniya hiqûqî wergirim,” û axaftina xwe wiha berdewam kir: “Bi taybetî serlêder divê bikaribin behsa xwe û kêşeyên xwe bikin. Pêdiviya me bi gihîştina xizmeta wergêriyê û wergirtina piştevaniya hiqûqî heye. Ji bo min wergêr peyda nekirin. Ji ber vê yekê Rêveberiya Îdareya Koçê ya Bajar tevî ku ez hemwelatiyê Iraqê me jî, ez wekî hemwelatiyê Efxanistanê tomar kirim. Divê ev tişt bê sererastkirin. Serlêdanên min ketin ber xetereyê. Ked û xebata min a heşt salan dê vala biçe.”


(FY/AY)

title: Ephéméride des luttes : 8 octobre
content:
Le 8 octobre, l'éphéméride des luttes est profondément antimilitariste, mais elle n'est en rien pacifique. Elle sait que glisser une fleur dans le canon d'un fusil ne l'empêche pas de tirer. Alors elle s'organise contre les structures de la guerre et du fascisme.


1901 :

 A Barcelone, l'anarchiste Francisco Ferrer ouvre "l'école moderne", dans le but d'offrir une éducation libre et sans dogmes.


1936 :

 En Espagne, mort d'Emile Cottin, membre du bataillon international de la Colonne Durruti lors de combats contre les fascistes de Franco.


1963 :

 Mort à Mexico de la peintre surréaliste anarchiste Remedios Varo. Une de ses peintures illustre l'éphéméride d'aujourd'hui.


1967 :

 En Bolivie, Ernesto Che Guevara est capturé puis assassiné par l'armée bolivienne (soutenue par la CIA) alors qu'il tente de lancer un mouvement de guérilla de libération dans le pays. Roberto Quintanilla, considéré comme étant l'un des principaux responsables de cette mort, sera abattu à Hambourg le 1er avril 1971 par la révolutionnaire Monika Ertl alors qu'il occupe la fonction de consul de Bolivie.


1968 :

 La faction Weatherman du SDS (qui passera dans la clandestinité et la lutte armée deux ans plus tard) organise les 'Jours de Rage' dans les rues de Chicago, contre la guerre du Vietnam et l'impérialisme américain, avec pour but de créer le plus de dégâts possibles dans les quartiers bourgeois. Le mot d'ordre : "

Bring the War Home

".


1975 :

 A Paris, les Brigades Internationales commando Juan Paredes Manot (du nom d'un militant d'ETA fusillé quelques jours plus tôt avec deux autres membres d'ETA et deux membres du FRAP) touchent de plusieurs balles Garcia Plata, attaché militaire de l'ambassade de Franco.


1977 :

 - A Paris, les NAPAP (Noyaux Armés Pour l'Autonomie Populaire) commettent un attentat contre le domicile du garde des Sceaux de l'époque Alain Peyrefitte rue du Ranelagh.


 En Irlande du Nord, l'IRA abat une officière de l'Ulster Defence Regiment.


1984 :

 A Evere (Bruxelles), les Cellules Communistes Combattantes (CCC) font sauter le QG de l'entreprise d'informatique et électronique Honeywell, qui participe au programme de construction des missiles. C'est notamment un ordinateur Honeywell qui coordonnait les attaques au Vietnam en 1972 (que la Fraction Armée Rouge fait sauter le

24 mai

 72). L'entreprise avait aussi déjà été attaquée attaquée le 8 avril 1980 à Toulouse par le CLODO (Comité pour la Liquidation ou la Destruction des Ordinateurs), le 20 novembre 1983 à Düsseldorf par les Cellules Révolutionnaires (RZ) et le 14 décembre 1983 par l'United Freedom Front (UFF) à New York. Lire le

communiqué de revendication

.


1985 :

 A Bruxelles, les Cellules Communistes Combattantes (CCC) font sauter une camionnette piégée devant le siège principal du trust de l'énergie INTERCOM, début de leur 'campagne Karl Marx'. Le communiqué de l'action peut être lu

à cette adresse

.


2016 :

 - A

Marseille

,

plus de 300 antifascistes manifestent

 contre la présence de l'Action Française, un groupuscule royaliste, dans le quartier. Le cortège est attaqué par la police (massivement présente pour défendre les fachos) et quelques personnes sont blessés rue des Bons Enfants par des coups de matraque et une grenade, mais celui-ci se poursuit jusqu'à revenir sur la Plaine.


 A Notre-Dame-Des-Landes, plus de 40000 personnes manifestent pour répondre à l'appel de défense de la ZAD contre les menaces d'expulsion par le gouvernement.

 A Montpellier, des conteneurs à poubelle

sont incendiés

 devant le local du Parti Socialiste avec l'inscription "Fini de trahir".


Voir

l'éphéméride anarchiste

 du 8 octobre.

title: Υποχρεωτική η καθαρογραφή αθωωτικών αποφάσεων από το Εφετείο Αθηνών
content:
Όπως αναφέρει στο Δελτίο Τύπου που ακολουθεί ο Κώστας Παπαδάκης, μέλος του Δ.Σ. του Δ.Σ.Α. και εισηγητής του σχετικού αιτήματος, στην υποστήριξή του ενώπιον της Ολομέλειας του Εφετείου Αθηνών: “

Το επόμενο βήμα είναι να μην περιοριστεί μόνο στο Εφετείο Αθηνών αλλά να επεκταθεί σε όλα τα δικαστήρια και εν τέλει να νομοθετηθεί με ανάλογη τροποποίηση του άρθρου 142 παρ. 4 Κ.Ποιν.Δ, ώστε να είναι υποχρεωτική παντού η καθαρογραφή όλων των αθωωτικών αποφάσεων χωρίς καμμία προϋπόθεση..”

ου Υπουργού Δικαιοσύνης (επισυνάπτεται) έγινε δεκτή η γνώμη που περιλαμβάνεται στην υπ αριθμ. 1/2026 απόφαση της Ολομέλειας του Εφετείου Αθηνών σχετικά με την καθαρογραφή των αθωωτικών αποφάσεων.


Με την υπ. αριθμ. 61301οικ/30.9.2026 Απόφαση του Υπουργού Δικαιοσύνης (επισυνάπτεται) έγινε δεκτή η γνώμη που περιλαμβάνεται στην υπ αριθμ. 1/2026 απόφαση της Ολομέλειας του Εφετείου Αθηνών σχετικά με την καθαρογραφή των αθωωτικών αποφάσεων.


Η απόφαση είχε ληφθεί από την Ολομέλεια του Εφετείου Αθηνών στις 19.2.2026, όπου είχε κληθεί και παρέστη η αντιπροσωπεία του Δ.Σ. του Δ.Σ.Α. αποτελούμενη από τον πρόεδρό του κ. Ανδρέα Κουτσόλαμπρο και μέλη του Δ.Σ,. του, μεταξύ των οποίων και ο υπογράφων ως εισηγητής που ανέπτυξε τα σχετικά αιτήματα. Ενώ είχε προηγηθεί η διοργάνωση εκδήλωσης στις 11.2.2026 στα γραφεία του Δ.Σ.Α. στις για την προβολή του αιτήματος.


Το αίτημα είχε στηριχθεί πάνδημα από όλους τους δικηγορικούς φορείς και από τις Ενώσεις Ποινικολόγων και πολλά νομικά περιοδικά. Όχι ωστόσο από τις δικαστικές και εισαγγελικές ενώσεις.


Σύμφωνα με την παραπάνω Υ.Α. η καθαρογραφή των αθωωτικών αποφάσεων του Εφετείου Αθηνών καθίσταται η υποχρεωτική εφόσον το ζητήσει ο κατηγορούμενος εντός 6 μηνών από την έκδοση τους χωρίς να απαιτείται η επίκληση εννόμου συμφέροντος.


Ανεξάρτητα από την καθυστέρηση έκδοσής της Υ.Α. πρόκειται για μία μεγάλη νίκη που πιστώνεται σε όσους συνέβαλαν με κάθε τρόπο διότι άρχισε να αποκαθίσταται μια μεγάλη αδικία, της οποίας οι πτυχές έχουν αναλυθεί λεπτομερώς, αλλά και ένα έλλειμα δικαίου που είχε οδηγήσει στην εξαφάνιση της επιτυχούς υπερασπιστικής νομολογίας.


Το επόμενο βήμα είναι να μην περιοριστεί μόνο στο Εφετείο Αθηνών αλλά να επεκταθεί σε όλα τα δικαστήρια και εν τέλει να νομοθετηθεί με ανάλογη τροποποίηση του άρθρου 142 παρ. 4 Κ.Ποιν.Δ, ώστε να είναι υποχρεωτική παντού η καθαρογραφή όλων των αθωωτικών αποφάσεων χωρίς καμμία προϋπόθεση.


Με θερμές ευχαριστίες προς όσους/ες συνέβαλαν.


Αθήνα, 7.10.2026


Κώστας Παπαδάκης


Δικηγόρος, Μέλος του Δ.Σ. του Δ.Σ.Α.

author: Redazione_web
title: Un mese all’inferno. Autistici/Inventati
content:
Abbiamo già raccontato quanto è accaduto a partire dal 26 agosto scorso al Collettivo Autistici/Inventati (vedi UN

n.24

 e

n.25

) e in questo articolo aggiorniamo agli ultimi sviluppi quella storia.


In seguito allo spegnimento dei server gestiti da A/I si è verificata una cosa facilmente prevedibile: migliaia di compagn* in Italia e in tutto il mondo hanno dovuto cercarsi un nuovo indirizzo di posta elettronica che avesse almeno qualcuna delle caratteristiche offerte da quelli che avevano usato fino al 18 settembre. I pochi server gestiti da gruppi di attivist* sono stati presi d’assalto dalle richieste e molt* hanno dovuto ripiegare su e-mail gestite da servizi commerciali che promettono una comunicazione elettronica più sicura.


Il vuoto più grande e meno colmabile è stata la chiusura della piattaforma noblogs.org che da venti anni permetteva la creazione e la gestione di siti a singole persone, collettivi, gruppi di attivisti e attiviste impegnati nella lotta per il cambiamento sociale. Un danno enorme, difficilmente calcolabile e che probabilmente non verrà riparato presto.


In uno dei suoi comunicati, il Collettivo A/I aveva scritto: “Ora mollate il pc, uscite, lottate, abbracciatevi e non perdete il sorriso. Perché noi ci fermiamo. Ma la resistenza e le idee no. Restiamo umani.”.


E il 25 settembre a Firenze e a Roma alcune centinaia di persone hanno auto-organizzato due iniziative in solidarietà e sostegno ad A/I. A Firenze quella che doveva essere una manifestazione statica si è trasformata in un corteo che dall’Ambasciata statunitense è arrivato davanti alla Prefettura.


Anche se si è trattato di iniziative non certo oceaniche il segnale è stato chiaro: l’attivismo digitale non basta ed è necessario uscire dalle “bolle” nelle quali sono confinate anche le posizioni più radicali. In questo momento si stanno organizzando altri momenti pubblici allo scopo di continuare a mantenere alta l’attenzione su questa vicenda.


Dopo lo scioglimento del Collettivo A/I, anche la collegata “Associazione AI ODV” ha iniziato la procedura per la sua chiusura, un percorso reso più complicato dalla decisione di “Banca Etica” di bloccarne il conto corrente. Il primo appuntamento è fissato per il 22 ottobre prossimo, quando a Pisa inizierà la discussione sul ricorso urgente presentato per chiedere la riattivazione del conto dell’Associazione. Come già scritto, ma è necessario sottolinearlo, il comportamento dell’Istituto bancario ha costretto chi gestiva AI ODV in una situazione paradossale. Per sciogliersi, l’Associazione deve devolvere il suo patrimonio a un altro ente senza scopo di lucro, cosa che non è possibile fare stante il blocco del conto.


Paradossi burocratici a parte, sempre restando nel campo istituzionale, le numerose interpellanze e interrogazioni presentate sia al Parlamento italiano che a quello europeo sono, per il momento, ancora in attesa e, se non sono prevedibili i tempi, è più facile prevedere che le risposte non saranno che aria fritta, visto che i problemi che il caso di A/I ha sollevato sono molto, ma molto più grandi di un piccolo collettivo. Si tratta infatti di mettere in discussione il potere di alcuni stati di gestire in modo privato la rete Internet e di avere il quasi completo monopolio di alcuni dei principali canali di funzionamento delle transazioni finanziarie mondiali. Due argomenti che saranno ritenuti in questo momento storico di secondaria importanza, tenuto conto dello scenario attuale, tra guerre in corso e immaginate, problemi di approvvigionamento energetico e crisi economiche.


Sempre in questo campo va segnalata la supplica presentata il primo ottobre da Banca Etica e firmata da altre 14 associazioni alla Commissione Europea e al Governo italiano, anche a sostegno di alcune delle interrogazioni presentate da alcuni parlamentari.


Va anche segnalato l’intervento di un solito noto (a volte ritornano) che ha proposto di “costruire un’alleanza tra “democratici e ribelli”, dove tutti stanno alla pari. Chi fa una banca e chi è accusato di essere, come capita a noi di Mediterranea, una “minaccia alla sicurezza nazionale”. author: Unknown
title: Scuole occupate: facciamo come in Francia!
content:
A Torino si prende esempio dalla Francia: l’aria di rivolta proveniente dal paese oltralpe ha superato i confini geografici, ridando un senso di possibilità di rivalsa studentesca anche alle nostre latitudini.


All’istituto Lagrange, come al Regina, Giulio e Gobetti le mobilitazioni studentesche francesi hanno squarciato il velo che impediva alle contraddizioni di tradursi in lotta aperta.

Da rivendicazioni di edilizia alla presa di coscienza dell’attacco complessivo alla formazione tecnica con la riforma del 4+2, il mezzo dell’occupazione si sta consolidando come mezzo adottato dalle scuole per porre una critica complessiva alla gestione capitalistica della scuola.

Attraverso i social i contenuti tutti politici legati alla rivolta francese costruiscono un immaginario di rivalsa collettiva che ipotizziamo diano le possibilità di un rilancio generalizzato di riappropriazione giovanile del proprio protagonismo.

La crisi generalizzata causata dalla crisi a sfondo bellico si propaga, seppur con delle specificità nazionali, in egual misura in tutti i paesi del continente europeo.

Le contraddizioni legate al modello sociale del neoliberismo occidentale vedono la possibilità di venire a galla e poter essere tradotte in un programma politico concreto.

Siamo i figli della crisi, e in questo contesto, le uniche possibilità di riappropriazione di decisionalità sulle proprie vite non possono che passare dalla lotta.

Da Parigi si alza un urlo di lotta: sta a noi tradurlo alle nostre latitudini in un movimento capace di mettere le nostre necessità al centro di un assalto al presente.

Nelle scuole torinesi il messaggio è chiaro: espandere la lotta e prendersi lo spazio politico per poter contare.

ci vediamo sulle barricate!

author: Ibrahima Diallo
title: Drongo Company: Can Washington’s new PSYOP unit win back African trust?
content:
In mid-July, the US Army activated

Delta Company

 of the 7th Psychological Operations (PSYOP) Battalion under 3rd Special Forces Group. The unit has taken on the informal name ‘Drongo’, a nod to an African bird known for its ability to vocally mimic other species to drive off competitors. Its declared purpose is to support US Africa Command’s (AFRICOM) influence and information operations across the continent, though it is not technically an AFRICOM unit as it belongs to Army special operations and executes missions in AFRICOM’s area of responsibility.


Drongo’s existence says less about African security dynamics than about Washington’s shrinking appetite and capacity for direct military engagement on the continent. AFRICOM

 told Congress

 earlier this year that the command’s regional posture has declined by roughly three-quarters over the past decade,

 degrading intelligence collection and security cooperation

 even as terrorism, near-peer competition, and economic rivalry intensify. That decline reflects both access lost to successive coups and a deliberate shift toward a lighter footprint through partner-nation capacity-building, selective drawdowns, and standoff tools such as airpower, visible in the Command’s

 intensified strikes in Somalia

. Read in that context, standing up a unit to project influence through phones, broadcasts, and local intermediaries is a rational, inexpensive way to maintain relevance where Washington can no longer sustain a physical presence. The question is not whether it should exist, but whether it can do the job it was built for.


The Department of Defense

defines

 psychological operations or PSYOPs as influencing the emotions, motives, reasoning and, ultimately, the behavior of foreign audiences. In practice it spans two very different objectives. The first is narrow and behavioural, e.g., persuading fighters to defect, villagers to report roadside bombs, or communities to disregard specific rumours. These objectives do not require audiences to like or trust Washington. The second is what might be called strategic persuasion, i.e., getting audiences to accept an account of US intentions that competes with rival narratives. That depends almost entirely on the credibility of the sender. Drongo’s stated purpose, operating

across contested environments

 where strategic rivals are shaping foreign opinion, places it in the second category. Countering adversarial narratives about the US is, by definition, a contest over what Africans believe about American intentions. The credibility deficit is therefore not a hedge on the unit’s prospects, but the terrain it operates in.


That deficit and animosity toward the West is due largely by France. Paris’s post-colonial legacy and persistent failure to deliver mutually beneficial economic and security arrangements eroded its credibility on the continent long before

Opération Barkhane

 wound down. Additionally,

Françafrique’s

 one-sided extractive models persisting from the colonial era ran their course, and a military presence once justified as counterterrorism assistance came to be seen as another means through which Paris preserved its regional influence. The result was a surge in

anti-French sentiment

, mass protests and, between 2022 and 2025, the

departure of French forces

 from the region: forced in the Sahel, negotiated on the coast. By failing to distinguish its own approach, Washington has been pooled into the same category of actors some Africans view as exploitative. And while adversarial messaging often casts

the West as one bloc

, the US has built a record of its own.


In September 2021, then-Colonel Mamadi Doumbouya’s special forces overthrew then-Guinean President Alpha Condé, who had grown increasingly dubious of Western, and particularly French, motives. Doumbouya is a former French Foreign Legionnaire who had

trained

 in Israel, Senegal, Gabon, and at l’École de Guerre in Paris. He has also participated in US-led exercises, and his coup took place while US Green Berets were in-country training his units. Washington

condemned the takeover

, suspended training, and denied foreknowledge, and no evidence of American involvement has surfaced. However, the optics fueled uncorroborated suspicions and reinforced the belief that Western powers manipulate African politics to suit their strategic interests. In January 2026, Doumbouya was sworn in as president with a

US delegation in attendance

, and …

author: Mada Masr
title: Prosecution says journalists’ testimony indicates Matsda2sh was ‘Brotherhood media cell,’ EIPR says statement unproven position
content:
The Public Prosecution issued a

statement

 on Wednesday regarding the investigations into the six Matsda2sh fact-checking platform’s journalists, stating that one of them admitted that all the defendants — as well as others — had joined a media committee affiliated with the Muslim Brotherhood.

 


It said they had been tasked with carrying out “media plans” based on spreading and broadcasting rumors and false news about state institutions, exclusively highlighting the shortcomings of those institutions, disparaging the roles and performance of their officials and overblowing issues related to select groups, as well as fabricating and exaggerating events related to them. 


From its side, the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, whose lawyers are leading the defense counsel representing the journalists, repeated its demands for their release, for the charges against them to be dropped and for the case to be closed.


In

response

 to the prosecution’s statement, EIPR said that its media statements published on social media hold no evidentiary value in law and amount only to a summary of the prosecution’s case, none of which has been presented before a court, while none of its claims has been proven.

 


The organization pointed out the prosecution’s failure to address the fact that the six journalists did not appear before the prosecution until five days after their arrest, during which time they were denied contact with their families and lawyers, in violation of the law, despite relatives and lawyers filing 18 complaints with the prosecution during that period.


The prosecution’s statement also failed to mention that the order to hold the journalists in custody is issued by investigating authorities under the exceptional provisions of the counterterrorism law, which only permit the measure “when there is a threat of terrorist crimes and when such measure is required to confront that threat,” according to EIPR.

 


Yet the prosecution’s claims, based on the security investigations, accuse the journalists only of publishing rumors or “false” reports, without identifying “the imminent terrorist threat that required depriving the six journalists of their right to appear before a judicial authority within 24 hours of their arrest, during which documented violations were committed against them.”  


The six journalists appeared before the prosecutions five days after their forced disappearance following their arrest, during which they were held at National Security Agency premises. 


None were brought before prosecutors until the first of the six was presented to the Supreme State Security Prosecution on Saturday, with the other five interrogated on the following day. The prosecution ordered that one of the six be brought for forensic medical examination, after some of the defendants complained of being subjected to torture and maltreatment at the NSA premises, with lawyers calling for officers responsible for those premises to be investigated.


The prosecution stated that the first journalist who was investigated admitted that the defendants received “monthly funding of sums in foreign currencies,” via bank transfers from a company owned by a “fugitive member of the Muslim Brotherhood” in a foreign country.


The prosecution also said it found communication groups on a secure messaging app on his phone, connecting him and the other detainees with the “fugitive member,” as well as emails from the latter to them. All but one admitted to regularly receiving sums of money in US dollars, transferred from a foreign country.


After the statement’s publication, EIPR director, Hossam Bahgat, told Mada Masr that the prosecution is pointing to the procedural steps Matsda2sh took to regularize as though it were incriminating evidence.

Bahgat noted that following the “

Zambia plane crisis

,” the company that owns the platform registered employment contracts for its staff, which were presented to Egyptian banks in order for accounts to be opened through which the journalists would receive their salaries.

 


Authorities previously

arrested

 a former member of the Matsda2sh team in 2023, after the platform published a series of investigations about a private jet carrying cash, counterfeit gold and weapons, that was taken into custody in Zambia with a number of Egyptian nationals on board, some of whom had alleged military and police backgrounds.

author: Sanya Osha
title: Art by Rock Hard African Women
content:
Oftentimes, mass acts of violent rebellion primarily driven by youths are viewed as counterproductive and nihilistic. But it is important to note that this isn’t always the case, as three major examples in African contemporary history demonstrate notably: the anti-colonial theory of violence proffered by Frantz Fanon that galvanised Algeria into civil disobedience and warfare during the colonial era; the Arab Spring that gripped North Africa and parts of the Middle East in 2011; and the #RhodesMustFall movement that rattled South Africa in 2015.  Each of these instances of mass rebellion were largely youth-driven and shook the political status quo in their respective countries, leading to sociopolitical reform and fervent collective contemplation.


In this sense, rebellion in and of itself becomes a thoroughly creative act, a measure to shake up jaded and monolithic political edifices in urgent need of transformation as atrophy and retrogression set in within the body politic. Youths often excluded or marginalised in key decision-making bodies and processes are left with no option but to revolt. And in the act of rebellion, they are not only offering their voice but also their signature as an essential component of the body politic. When dominant political structures become unresponsive to the needs and aspirations of the majority, when they become complacent and incapable of growth and innovation, then the rebellion of youth and other segments of the populace becomes not only unavoidable but also desirable. Indeed, the desirability of revolt as a creative act is the line of thinking behind this discussion. Revolt as a massive glitch in the polity can also be viewed as a rite of purification, a collective cleansing of the communal being before renewed energies are unleashed for social reconstruction.


Having established that the physical act of actual revolt could sometimes have therapeutic and reconstructive properties, it is important to note that Africa has produced many contemporary female artists whose works stand as testaments to powerful creative agency within the continent and defiant feminist sensibilities.


“Strike a woman, strike a rock” (

imbokodo

) is a Zulu proverb that became popular after the 1956 women’s march to Union Buildings in Pretoria to protest the apartheid pass laws. It is possible to explore other equally productive meanings of rock art by rock hard people and, in this instance, the San communities of Southern Africa come to mind. The San, also known as “the First People”, can be found principally in Angola, Namibia, Botswana and, of course, South Africa. Centuries ago, they mastered the art of making paintings and engravings on rock surfaces. These works of art were not merely decorative. They tell stories, communicate healing and enact rituals for communal wellness and cohesion. In spite of colonisation and various forms of oppression, these works of art have endured and this attests to the strength and resilience of the people who created them. Indeed, San communities are littered across the Southern African region despite mounting challenges, and their survival represents a broader African narrative of durability and adaptability. Their story forms the essential backdrop to this article on women who struggle against all kinds of dispossession: political, cultural, economic, and sexist, among other types of oppression.


The work of two black South African photographers, Zanele Muholi

and Ingrid Masondo, can be construed as efforts to debunk the misrepresentations of the black African woman by centuries-long colonial imagery, on the one hand, and — in spite of the constitutional recognition of gay rights — within the matrix of a largely homophobic, patriarchal, post-apartheid South Africa, on the other. Within colonial consciousness, the black female body was preposterously exoticised, anaestheticised, and hypersexualised. By being thrust into a vortex of unruly instincts, the black African female was grossly violated in more ways than one.


Sarah Bartmann was an unfortunate indigene of what eventually became South Africa who was enslaved to be paraded in the freak shows of London and Paris during the nineteenth century on account of her well-endowed posterior ( a contemporary equivalent would be the Brazilian Butt Lift – BBL). Bartmann was constantly dehumanised, abused, and subsequently left for dead for no reason other than her natural physical attributes. Judging by her …

author: Abahlali_3
title: Record Fuel Price Increase: A Crisis for the Poor
content:
6 October 2026 Abahlali baseMjondolo Press Statement

Record Fuel Price Increase: A Crisis for the Poor

The record increase in the fuel price, which will take inland 95 petrol to R30.25 a litre from 7 October, will push poor people even deeper into suffering.

We are already living through a devastating social crisis. Around 13.1 million people are unemployed or have given up looking for work. There are around 5 million unemployed young people between the ages of 15 and 34, and the unemployment rate for this group is 47.4%. Among young people between 15 and 24, unemployment has reached 62.8%. Around 3.8 million young people aged 15 to 24 are not in employment, education or training. Around five million people continue to live in shack settlements, and there are around 3,400 shack settlements across the country.

Millions of people do not have sufficient access to healthy food. The Pietermaritzburg Economic Justice and Dignity group calculated that in September the average household food basket cost R5,488.06, while a basic nutritionally adequate food basket cost R6,655.29. The average cost of feeding one child was R970.27 a month, while the Child Support Grant is only R580 a month.

A worker earning the national minimum wage can work for the whole month and still not earn enough to buy a nutritionally adequate food basket for a household, even before paying rent, electricity, transport, school costs and other necessities.

Official statistics show that 14% of households have inadequate access to food and 8.2% have severely inadequate access to food. Almost one in four South African children under five are stunted.

The social devastation has plunged millions of people into deep suffering, and robbed millions, especially young people, of any hope for a viable future.

We cannot continue like this. Yet in this crisis a corrupt and morally depraved political elite, now organised across a number of political parties, continues to loot public funds. At the same time a deeply cynical business elite continues to make enormous profits from the labour and consumption of poor and working-class people. Supermarkets make massive profits while people go hungry. Executives earn millions while workers struggle to feed their families. Food has become a commodity from which large companies make profit while millions of people cannot afford enough to eat. This is simply immoral and it must be stopped.

The first thing that needs to be done is to stop cutting public spending to please business. Austerity must be immediately stopped and public money must be used for the public good. Social grants must be increased to protect people from hunger. Wages must be increased to give people enough to live on. Public transport must be safe and affordable. The social value of land must be put before its commercial value and land must be made available for housing, food production and recreation.

There can be no food security in a country where wealth and land are so unequally distributed. Hunger is not caused by a lack of food. It is caused by impoverishment, unemployment and inequality, and by a food system in which land, production and distribution are controlled for profit.

We need a massive project to build food sovereignty. Poor people cannot remain dependent on a food system controlled by a small number of large supermarket chains and food corporations. Urban land reform must make land available for people to grow food close to where they live. Municipalities must support community gardens, small farmers, street traders and local food producers, and establish public and community markets where healthy food can be sold directly and affordably.

It is critical that we break the control of the large supermarkets over the food system and build a food system organised around public need rather than private profit.

Food cannot continue to be treated as a commodity in a country where millions go hungry. Access to healthy food must be treated as a right.

In a social crisis of this extent the corrupt political elite, the state and capital have lost all moral and political credibility and we cannot continue to accept their authority while millions go hungry and millions of young people have no future.

Land must be occupied and put to democratically managed social purposes while we build the democratic power of the poor and the working class to put land, wealth and power in the hands of the people.

author: Folashade Roberts
title: Old Nollywood 2.0
content:
Scroll to the comments under the movie

Love in Every Word

 on YouTube, and you will find viewers from Lagos to London, Accra, Houston, and beyond, tagging sisters to “come and watch this.” Even though the movie had no cinema release and no streaming deal, it reached 15 million views within a week of its March 2025 release on the Omoni Oboli TV YouTube channel. It reached roughly 30 million by year’s end. Actress and filmmaker Omoni Oboli and her business partner, Tomi Adeoye, launched Omoni Oboli TV in December 2023. Since then, the channel has gained more than two million subscribers. The success of

Love in Every Word

 and its sequel pushed their YouTube television channel past 182 million total views across 550 videos, and it was named YouTube Nigeria’s Top Creator Channel of 2025.

The story and style of

Love in Every Word

 are typical of Nollywood cinema, but there is something about the success of its format that raises questions. Is it an example of a new paradigm for how we understand the present-day movie industry in Nigeria? Or is it marking a return to the spirit of the original Nollywood? Does this format’s mix of “New Nollywood” and “Old Nollywood” betoken a new concept? Perhaps we could call it “Old Nollywood 2.0.”

Sometimes journalists and scholars like to divide film history into neat periods of succession. But looking at the history of Nollywood cinema, the reality is that there have been overlapping industrial formations. For the past three decades, the Nollywood phenomenon and its global impact have been described, analyzed, and debated, and the storyline goes something like this. Once upon a time, in the late 1980s, in the street markets of Onitsha and Lagos, movie theaters were declining because the cost of production and distribution of celluloid films was prohibitive. Independent producers were shooting television drama on video, working with Nigerian television networks, while the Yoruba traveling theater troupes were experimenting with video. Alongside this development, traders and marketers, who were already distributing imported and pirated Hollywood and Bollywood films, began to make and market their own cheaply produced melodrama on VHS.

Before Nollywood, there was a politically Pan-Africanist movie industry across Africa into which the recently liberated postcolonial nation-states enthusiastically invested. In the 1970s, the Nigerian government expanded its involvement in film and cultural production when it hosted FESTAC ’77 and repositioned the existing Nigerian Film Unit (formerly Colonial Film Unit) into the Nigerian Film Corporation, with a mandate to broaden its responsibilities and foster development of the national film industry. Filmmakers such as Ola Balogun and Adamu Halilu made artistically stunning films, sometimes collaborating with Black artists from across the world.

With the onset of structural adjustment policies imposed by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), alongside the devastation of civil wars and repressive regimes, the state’s investment in a liberated media crumbled. What some consider the “golden age” of artistically brilliant, politically progressive Nigerian cinema was diminished. Into the void stepped entrepreneurial, commercially minded filmmakers who took advantage of the straight-to-video format and what economists call the “informal market” of the street. The new “video-films” (first made on VHS and then on VCD and DVD) were quite popular for a multitude of genres, from crime (

Issakaba

, 2001), domestic melodrama (

Violated

, 1996), and family drama (

Rattlesnake

, 1995), to religion (

Agony of a Mother

, 2002), romance (

Keeping Faith: Is That Love

?, 2002), slapstick comedy (

Osuofia in London

, 2003), social mobility (

Glamour Girls

, 1994), urban aspiration (

Domitilla

, 1996), and occult and supernatural narratives (

Living in Bondage

, 1992, and

Nneka the Pretty Serpent

, 1994). The rapid success of these movies far exceeded expectations.

Nollywood’s enormous local and global popularity attracted new investors and renewed interest in theatrical exhibition. The opening of new multiplexes from 2004 created another route to audiences and encouraged a strand of filmmaking characterized by larger budgets, improved production values, and theatrical premieres. The transformation did not stop at the cinema. The South African company MultiChoice/Africa Magic expanded its investment in Nigerian content, while digital …

author: AfricanFeminism
title: Who Can Afford to Imagine Liberation?
content:
I recently had a conversation with an acquaintance who had applied for activist welfare support after the floods in Accra, Ghana this June destroyed much of what they owned. Their appliances, gadgets and other belongings were gone or damaged, rent was still due, and they had the very reasonable fear that the rains could return and the next flood could be worse. They work full-time with a grassroots organization, which can mean having a job without necessarily having the financial security to suddenly move house, replace their belongings and start again. They never received feedback on that application. Through the kind of backdoor follow-up that has become an unofficial administrative system of its own in social justice movements, they eventually learned that the welfare fund was specifically for activists who needed relocation, medical assistance, provisions and other forms of support as a result of their activism.


I understand why such a fund exists. People face threats, violence and displacement because of the politics of the work, and there should be resources when that happens. But I kept returning to the question of what counts as care in activism and what has to happen before suffering becomes recognizable as an activist emergency. A flooded home is an emergency. Losing almost everything you own is an emergency. Having rent due while trying to find somewhere safe to live is an emergency. You can spend your working life asking why the state has failed people, and still discover that the existing welfare responses want to know whether the state failed you because of your activism.


A friend recently underwent surgery and is carrying a substantial medical bill while continuing her work as the executive director of a Lesbian, Bisexual Queer organization. She cannot easily access her organization’s welfare fund because of her position, which would be a conflict of interest, and the external fund does not cover medical needs unrelated to activism.


Professionalization that overlooks precarity


Over time, we have professionalized the work of liberation, and a relatively small group of people now spends their working lives organising, documenting, researching, advocating, and building movements around questions that affect far more people than those on the payroll. Health, safety, dignity, discrimination, economic security and democratic participation remain enormous public questions, while the labour of pursuing them has become professional work. 


If we have decided that social change requires people to do this work as their jobs, what have we built around the people whose working lives now carry it?                                   


Philanthropy has made much of this professionalization possible. The work may be funded while the people doing it remain precarious. This is especially visible among grassroots activists, organisers, mobilisers and younger groups working around social justice, many of whom move from one short contract, stipend or grant period to the next. They are still living ordinary lives around the work: paying rent, taking public transport, dealing with medical expenses, supporting family and trying to meet the everyday costs of being alive. Stipends are often treated as wages for full-time work while covering very little of what a life actually costs. 


This work is also happening amid growing political hostility toward the very questions activists are organising around. Across the continent, gender and sexuality have become an increasingly contested political terrain, with governments and political actors advancing laws and policies that restrict the lives of women, girls and LGBTQIA people, while broader civic spaces are being narrowed through arrests, restrictions of protest, expression and association. In many places, the consequences of being associated with this work can include surveillance, intimidation, detention or violence. Activists are working amid growing militarism and political repression, while being expected to organise, support communities and keep these questions in the public eye. To do this work, therefore, is to work within the consequences of the politics one is trying to change. 


Professional security would mean earning a salary that sustains a life, having insurance and healthcare when things go wrong, and having some form of welfare that can absorb the ordinary shocks of being alive. Without those things, working in a nonprofit can feel almost synonymous …

author: Mzi Velapi
title: Memorial service held for victims of the Strand mass shooting
content:
In the early hours of Sunday morning, 27 September, gunmen opened fire on patrons at a shisanyama in Lwandle, near Cape Town, killing ten people. “Five individuals died on the scene while five others succumbed to injuries sustained after being transported to medical facilities. Eleven others are receiving medical treatment for injuries sustained. Lwandle police have opened murder and attempted murder cases,” said the police. The community believes the mass shooting is related to the extortion racket that is ravaging Cape Town townships.


One of the victims, Khululekani Ndlovu, will be laid to rest this weekend. The nine other people killed will be buried next weekend in the Eastern Cape. The Nomzamo Community Hall in Strand, south east of Cape Town, was packed with mourners and members of political parties for the memorial service.


Speaking to

Elitsha

, the chairperson of the police board in South Africa, Francina Lukas, said that extortion and business rivalry and lack of opportunities for young people are some of the factors contributing to high crime rates in the townships of Cape Town. She said that the lack of trust the community has in the police contributes to high crime rate.


“The police need to do much more than what they are doing in terms of compliance to make sure that businesses in the township comply with their licenses and bylaws. But the issue of trust is still a burning issue in our communities. So we need to overcome that issue to see that trust in the police is restored,” she said.


Families of the Strand 10


Speaking on behalf of the Sikweza family who lost their daughter, Avuyile, her uncle, Luyanda Macokeni, said she had plans to return to school next year. The 20-year-old passed her matric in 2024. She applied to continue her education next year and had just received responses from two universities offering her a place to study. She was expected to make a choice between the two. “Avuyile is supposed to the one burying us as elders but we are the ones burying her. It’s not God’s will that we are here today, it is because of someone’s will,” he said.


Siyathemba Jilaji was one of the victims who died on his way to the hospital, according to his friend. “He said he was going to change in the car so when the shooting began, I thought he was still in the car. A bullet grazed me under my arm. After the shooting, I went to the car to check for him. But, I didn’t know that he was amongst the bodies that were lying next to the entrance that I ran past,” she said.


Sivenathi Manxiwa’s father, Lubabalo Ndamane, said that he is not going to forgive the person who murdered his son. “I also don’t want to know who they are. Even if they can be arrested, I would not go to court. I leave everything to God and God will deal with him. I want to know what drove him to shoot at the young people who were out enjoying themselves,” he said.


The 10 people who died during the mass shooting in Strand last weekend

.

Photo from Facebook

.


The police said that the investigation into the mass murder is still ongoing.

author: ROAPE
title: What is the Real Marxist Tradition in Africa?
content:
John Molyneux’s classic statement of Marxist theory and practice

What is the Real Marxist Tradition

? was first published in 1984. The short book provided an incredibly sophisticated description of Marx’s method, and his relentless and insistent focus on the core agency of the working class.


Only the working class – however it is interpreted, described or labelled in social theory – can deliver a revolutionary anti-capitalist project. There cannot be, Molyneux argued, any substitute – no enlightened project of state development, or ‘socialist’ military leadership who deliver socialism on behalf of working people. Molyneux – in restating Marx’s central tenet – emphasised the role of the working class in their self-emancipation. Marx was the original prophet of the self-emancipation by working people. Without this class, and this project, there is simply no Marxism, no socialism, and no possibility of international revolution.


For an African audience the book speaks to multiple failed projects of socialism delivered by military coups, ‘enlightened’ governments and guerrilla movements. Each of these movements at different times dressed themselves in the language of Marxism, class and anti-imperialism but systematically broke genuine efforts at working class power.


What is the Real Marxist Tradition

? speaks directly to those on the continent trying to find a way to a genuine and emancipatory theory and practice of liberation.


Molyneux’ brilliant short book has now been reissued by the UK based publisher Bookmarks, and the Ugandan publisher Editor House Facility (EHF) who focus on readers across the African continent.


The new issue of the book comes with a major new introduction by the Ghanian socialist Gyekye Tanoh. Tanoh writes about the development and transformation of the working class on the continent since Molyneux wrote the book, and the continued capacity of this class to bring about socialist and revolutionary transformation across Africa.  


Join us for the launch of the African edition of

What is the Real Marxist Tradition?

 on 22 October at 18.30 (BST) with Gyekye Tanoh, Tafadzwa Choto

, 

Martin Empson and Mark Thomas. Reserve your place 

here

.


For readers based in Africa, John Molyneux’s 

What is the Real Marxist Tradition?

 can be purchased through Editor House Facility


here

. 


Endorsements of the book:


‘John Molyneux cuts through a century of distortion to recover Marxism’s authentic, revolutionary essence. This classic work distinguishes between living theory and dead orthodoxy, showing that Marxism is not a relic of the past but a vital method for understanding and transforming the world. It is essential reading for anyone seeking to understand capitalism and how to change it. For young activists and students alike, it is a must-read as it offers a powerful weapon for today’s struggles.’ 


Tafadzwa Choto

, International Socialist Organisation, Zimbabwe


‘In this book, John Molyneux undertakes a principled exercise by applying Marxism as a “method of analysis” to Marxism itself. He thereby provides not just a description of what Marxism is, but a method for detecting what isn’t. His application of this exercise—in the form of an autopsy of the interests and classes represented by three self-proclaimed Marxist tendencies—provides a valuable model for defining Marxist politics and organizations in our own contexts while enabling us to avoid the “hybrid ideologies of the petty bourgeoisie.” This is crucial, for us in the Global South, where reality differs greatly from that of Europe, thereby demanding a Marxism of contextualized design, not rigid imitation. The method offered is therefore a vital tool in enabling Marxist projects capable of fulfilling its role in “guiding revolutions to victory.” Such is true whether in the Global South or in global contexts marked by increasing economic complications and the co-option of Marxism by bourgeois ideologies fighting for survival amid the clear failure of neoliberal models … One need not agree with all of Molyneux’s conclusions to find his method a timely and indispensable resource.’


Muzan Alneel

,Marxist researcher and writer from Sudan

What is the Real Marxist Tradition in Africa?
