author: Pip Hinman
title: High Court’s landmark climate ruling counts true cost of coal
content:
The High Court of Australia ruled on October 7 that the New South Wales Independent Planning Commission (IPC) must consider how the burning of fossil fuels, exported from this country, contributed to climate damage.

It upheld an earlier unanimous NSW Court of Appeal ruling that the expansion approval of MACH Energy’s open-cut thermal coal at Mount Pleasant was invalid.

The Denman Aberdeen Muswellbrook Scone Healthy Environment Group (DAMS HEG), from the Upper Hunter Valley, had battled for four years over the coal mine’s expansion.

Climate activists believe this is a landmark judgement. Judging from the negative responses from One Nation and NSW Labor, that would seem to be the case. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese also weighed in on the side of MACH Energy in May, telling 2HD Newcastle Radio that he supported the expansion.

The campaign group, motivated by broader notions around climate justice, is also concerned about the transition for those working in the coal industry. Tony Lonergan, from DAMS HEG told a media conference on October 7 that NSW Labor had failed to put in place, and properly fund, a fair transition plan for affected communities.

Wendy Wales, president of DAMS HEG, said: “Today the High Court has said what we have always known: We cannot dig up coal, ship it overseas, watch it drive climate change and then pretend the consequences have nothing to do with us and won’t be felt by us.

“The droughts, the bushfires, the floods — are directly connected to greenhouse gases, and massive fossil fuel projects like Mt Pleasant Optimisation simply add fuel to the fire.”

Wales and Lonergan, both retired science teachers, live on a farm in the Upper Hunter Valley adjacent to the Mount Pleasant mine.

The Hunter Valley community group has been fighting MACH Energy’s expansion plan — to double Mount Pleasant’s output to 21 million tonnes a year and extend operations until 2048.

The community group initially lost its challenge last year in the NSW Land and Environment Court, after the IPC approved the 22-year expansion. It then successfully appealed that decision, prompting Mach Energy to take the case to the High Court.

The High Court dismissed MACH Energy’s appeal, saying the IPC had not considered how pollution from its coal would affect the region, through increased bushfire risk, drought, flooding and extreme heat. MACH Energy argued that Scope 3 emissions (emissions produced from burning the exported coal) from its mine should be considered through Australia’s pre-existing obligations under the Paris Agreement.

Three of the five judges found that the NSW IPC needed to “consider imposing conditions to minimise to the greatest extent practicable all greenhouse gas emissions, including Scope 3 emissions”.

The judgement means that the Mount Pleasant coal mine expansion approval to 2048 is invalid. But MACH Energy was given approval, in August, to operate until 2032. It had sought to double the output to 21 million tonnes a year.

Wales said the court decision “has finally made a change in direction in our laws. The [planning rules] will now have to reflect the need to consider climate impacts of our scope three emissions from the coal that we export.”

Lonergan said: “This ruling is in line with the International Court of Justice ruling [in July 2025] that said countries that use fossil fuels are responsible for the mitigation of emissions.

“We cannot just say, ‘Well, 98% of emissions comes from the burning of the coal overseas — that’s somebody else’s problem. Nothing to do with us!’ That’s just not going to work any more.”

Nic Clyde, coordinator of Lock the Gate Alliance NSW, said the ruling would affect 17 coal projects currently in the state’s planning pipeline. “Today’s decision sends a strong message to the planning system: the price households and communities are paying for coal pollution must be weighed properly in the planning system,” he said. “It’s no longer okay to ignore the climate cost of coal revenues.”

“The upper hunter economy needed to be diversified away from coal mining,” Lonergan said. “The area is completely dependent on coal mining, and everyone is pretending that we are just going to carry on.

“There’s the Future Jobs and Investment Fund which has stalled in the Upper House because the Labor Party won’t pass legislation to assist in the transition of the economy, diversify the economy.

“This landmark case shows that governments have to start getting serious about emissions …

author: Vashti Fox
title: Three years of Palestine solidarity
content:
In mid-October 2023, after the first major march against Israel’s attacks on Gaza, the director of the Palestine Solidarity Campaign UK, Ben Jamal, said to his staff: “We are probably going to need to be responding to this through marches until potentially Christmas”. He was wrong. The protests did not abate. As Israel’s offensive in Gaza continued, the number of actions across the world multiplied rapidly, eventually blossoming into one of the largest and most sustained antiwar movements in generations. From the world’s largest cities to the smallest hamlets, millions of voices rose in the same chant, with the same cadence: “Free, free Palestine!” 

The numbers tell part of the story. The Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project (ACLED), an international monitor, estimated that, in the three weeks after 7 October, some 3,700 demonstrations calling for a ceasefire and showing solidarity with Palestine took place in almost 100 countries and territories. In the first months of the genocide, most were in the Middle East and North Africa and were especially frequent in Yemen, Iran, Turkey and Morocco. In several of these countries, major government or religious institutions backed the demonstrations. 

In the West, however, governments were overwhelmingly hostile. In France, for instance, pro-Israel demonstrations were legal and encouraged. But the Macron government banned all Palestine solidarity demonstrations on 12 October, Interior Minister Gérald Darmanin determining that they were “likely to generate public disorder”. Nevertheless, on 22 October, 15,000 people took to the streets chanting “Gaza, Paris is with you!”

Two years after 7 October, ACLED provided data to SBS Australia showing 50,122 Gaza-related protests, the overwhelming majority in support of Palestinians—more than 40,000 Palestine solidarity events took place between 7 October 2023 and 5 September 2025. In contrast, just 3,120 pro-Israel demonstrations took place, more than two-thirds of them (2,159) held in Israel. 

What was striking about these actions was not simply their geographic breadth but their regularity. While the movement against the Iraq war in 2003 organised the largest single set of coordinated antiwar demonstrations in history, attracting an estimated 12 to 14 million people on 14 and 15 February, it did not sustain such mass mobilisations. The Palestine solidarity movement, by contrast, mobilised consistently over three years. London, for example, hosted the largest demonstrations in the UK, with 100,000 on 21 October, 70,000 on 28 October, 30,000 on 4 November, and 300,000 on 11 November 2003. Then, in 2024, 400,000 attended a demonstration on 9 March, followed by 200,000 again in March, April and October. 

Israel is a major participant in US-dominated imperial capitalist networks, and governments across the world (of all political colours) have been reluctant to break economically, politically or even symbolically from the Israeli-US coalition. Mass mobilisations, regardless of how mass and how determined they are, are unlikely on their own to force a government to break these relationships, especially in this new era of intensifying imperial competition. The stakes are simply too high. 

Nevertheless, the Palestine demonstrations were important for several reasons. They aimed not just to express moral outrage at Israel’s brutality but also to push their own governments for a change of policy. The demonstrations first demanded (with many local specificities) a ceasefire, and then, the longer the genocide continued, that their own governments break militarily, economically and diplomatically from Israel itself. 

Furthermore, the size and consistency of the demonstrations forced the issue of Gaza into the public debate. Governments responded differently to these protest movements, but most Western countries (with the notable exception of the USA) eventually backed the call for a ceasefire. (Of course, it was too late to stop the murder of tens of thousands of Gazans.). Some European governments, such as Spain and Ireland, moved more significantly in the direction of breaking ties with Israel, while others enacted more symbolic changes such as the recognition of Palestine and increased measures against Israeli settlements in the West Bank. None of these stances was anywhere near enough, but they likely would not have happened without the protest movement.

While protest movements’ impact on governments matters, the …

author: Editors
title: The world since 7 October
content:
Gaza is a generational touchstone and the key dividing line of politics in the West. It has laid bare the lies of the society we live in. It has exposed the genocidal bloodlust of the political right. And it has tested official “progressive” liberal politics, which has so often shown itself to be utterly hollow or cowardly. 

Anyone can now use Google Maps’ satellite view to see for themselves the apocalypse wrought by Israel and its allies over the past three years. Gaza City, once home to around 700,000 people, is a mostly bombed-out hellscape of ruins. The same is true of Beit Hanoun, Jabalia and other major centres. 

Rafah was a city thousands of years old, first recorded in an inscription from 1303 BCE. It has now been wiped off the face of the earth. Google still displays location markers for what once existed: “Kamal Adwan School”, “Playground”, “Musab bin Amir Western Mosque”, now a pile of rubble—“temporarily closed”, according to Google.

About 80 percent of structures in the Gaza Strip have been damaged; two-thirds of those are destroyed, according to the United Nations agency for Palestinian refugees. Israel has used the so-called ceasefire since last December to systematically demolish remaining structures in the 60 percent of the Strip occupied by its forces, while killing another 1,200 Palestinians and herding around 2 million into unliveable tent cities in an ever-shrinking concentration camp.

When millions around the world poured into the streets to take a stand against this barbarism, they were viciously attacked and slandered by the institutions of our “democracy”, which have cried about “social cohesion” while turning a blind eye to the genocide and the growth of fascism they are helping to stoke.

The ruling class and the political establishment want to go after not just the Palestine movement, but the left more generally, which has naturally been at the centre of that movement. Hence the persistent effort to define antisemitism as a problem of the left rather than the far right, to ban the word “genocide”, and to criminalise opposition to the state carrying it out. 

This is not because loyalty to Israel itself is so important to the establishment, but because this loyalty test is a proxy for loyalty to Australian capitalism; a test of subservience to Australian billionaires, bosses and bureaucrats. 

Will you keep your mouth shut? Will you force that student to remove their keffiyeh? Will you cancel that author? Will you censor that article? Your answer will determine your place in Australian society. With troublemakers pilloried and purged, the apparatus can be hardened, ready to oversee the next war, the next genocide, the next round of cutbacks and layoffs, the next racist campaign against immigrants and refugees, as capitalism lurches towards its next crisis.

Despite the establishment’s intimidation and slander, and partly because of it, a seismic shift in attitudes has occurred. A July Pew Research poll found that 79 percent of Australians have a negative view of Israel, and just 4 percent have a strongly positive view. Hundreds of thousands have taken to the streets. The movement globally has been big, defiant, and defining for so many people who have thrown themselves into it. 

Yet it has not produced a widespread radicalisation or a sizable new left committed to confronting and overthrowing the capitalist system more broadly. There are many reasons for this, from the relative weakness of far-left organisations going into this period, to the weakness of the workers’ movement and spinelessness of trade union leaders.

The depth of feeling and moral commitment to the cause of Palestinian liberation is palpable, but the general political level remains low. Instead of generalising from the atrocity in Gaza to develop a critique of capitalism and imperialism, there is an obsession with the pro-Israel lobby, and there are illusions in reactionary opponents of the US and Israel such as the Iranian regime. Instead of open debate about the best strategies and tactics of resistance, recriminations focus on who is qualified to lead campaigns against the Australian government—not based on ideas or organisational skills, but on individuals’ identities. 

While our side sustained the largest anti-war movement in Australian history, the far right, rather than the left, has emerged as the most organised political force and is making all the running to push society in its desired direction: more …

title: More than 1000 people protest genocide, AUKUS at Land Forces expo
content:
More than 1000 people joined the protest in against the Land Forces International Land Defence Exposition 2026, on October 6.

The weapons fair, which had more than 950 exhibitors, described itself as “Australia’s premier platform for advancing land-based defence capability”.

Companies whose weapons facilitate human rights abuses and war crimes are among the exhibitors, including Israeli firms Elbit Systems and Rafael Advanced Defense Systems.

The protest was initiated by the WA Anti-War collective, with the support of Stop AUKUS WA, Friends of Palestine WA and a range of other organisations.

The cost to the taxpayer for security alone at Land Forces is more than $10 million. People joined the protest because they are angry that money is being used on weapons and defence at the expense of mitigating climate change and properly funding housing, health and education.

The WA Labor government wants to make “defence” the state’s second-largest industry, including a proposed “missile manufacturing hub”, possibly in Collie, with no consultation.

Protesters also voiced their opposition to AUKUS and Australia’s war alliance with the United States.

[Sam Wainwright is an activist with Stop AUKUS WA.]

author: Nick Everett
title: How the media sold the Gaza genocide
content:
When 700,000 Rohingya were forced to flee Myanmar for Bangladesh amid widespread killings, sexual violence and village burnings in late 2017, an

Age

editorial pleaded for Australian government action: 

“There is a genocide happening today in Myanmar. Our government should urgently, repeatedly and loudly call for international intervention, and lead in imposing sanctions. We should send bountiful aid to the victims, and halt economic and diplomatic relations with Myanmar unless and until the savagery is stopped. All of us, as Australians, should shun travel to Myanmar for tourism or business. And our government should, as it did with the Syrian refugee crisis a few years ago, rapidly engineer an intake of Rohingya refugees.”

The

Age

 didn’t wait for an International Court of Justice ruling before issuing its dire warning. It repeatedly used the term “genocide” to describe the Myanmar state’s atrocities despite no case of genocide having been brought before the ICJ at the time (it wasn’t until late 2019 that Gambia brought such a case and the ICJ still hasn’t ruled on it).

After three years of Israeli genocide in Gaza, no similar editorial can be found in the

Age

, nor in any of the mainstream media in Australia. That is despite Israel having killed more than 74,000 Palestinians, including over 21,280 children who,

according to

 a UN Commission of inquiry, have been targeted as “part of a deliberate strategy to destroy the future of the Palestinians in Gaza”. 

Indeed, “genocide” is a term that journalists—at the behest of their editors—routinely shun, despite the ICJ’s preliminary ruling back in January 2024 that there is a plausible case Israel is committing genocide. And when the term is used, we are reminded that Israel denies such claims, despite the UN Human Rights Council, the International Association of Genocide Scholars and numerous international human rights organisations having all concluded that Israel is indeed committing genocide in Gaza.

It is not just that the media fail to acknowledge this simple fact. For the past three years, they have been accessories to Israel’s crimes: dehumanising Palestinians, sanitising Israel’s atrocities, and silencing its critics. 

In his groundbreaking book

How to Sell a Genocide

, author Adam Johnson sets out to “prove beyond a reasonable doubt that the genocide in Gaza was enabled, facilitated, and cheered by establishment US media providing cover for months of a nihilistic campaign of starvation, bombing, arbitrary detention, shooting and sexual violence”.  

Johnson’s approach is methodical and meticulous. His research draws on more than 12,000 articles and 5,000 TV clips from nine major outlets during the first year of the genocide, including the

New York Times,

 the

Washington Post,

CNN


and


MSNBC


(now MSNOW

)

. He focuses on the liberal media because “there was a Democratic president in office when the genocide began in earnest, and support from Democrats in Congress and in the think-tank and media world was dispositive [decisive] in continuing said genocide during the given time of my study”.

Johnson argues that the “centre-left” (i.e., liberal) media engaged in “an elaborate framework of excuse-making, deflection, faux-savvy realpolitik, orientalist tropes, and glaring double standards … to justify the White House’s lockstep support for producing carnage everyone could easily witness across their social media timeline on a daily basis”.

“The primary role of [US liberal] media”, he argues, “was to rationalise, negotiate, obscure and ultimately, deny the most inconvenient of truths: a genocide carried out, defended and authorised by elite liberals and liberal institutions”.

Johnson demonstrates how the media were willing accomplices to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s efforts to portray 7 October as Israel’s “9/11 moment”, and to equate Hamas violence with that of ISIS, despite the two Islamist groups being implacable enemies. They did so by repeating and perpetuating a series of lies that emanated from Israeli media spokespeople: that Hamas beheaded 40 babies on 7 October 2023, that they targeted children and that they systematically used rape as a weapon of war.

New York Post

title: CHP’de butlan yönetiminin işçi kıyımı sürüyor: 3 çalışanın daha işine son verildi
content:
CHP’de mahkemenin mutlak butlan kararıyla göreve gelen yönetimin 85’i aşkın genel merkez çalışanını işten çıkarmasının ardından 3 kişinin daha işine son verildi. İşten çıkarılanların eşlerinin daha önce CHP’de çalıştığı, ardından Yeni Parti’de işe başladığı öğrenildi.

CHP’de Kemal Kılıçdaroğlu’nun mahkemenin mutlak butlan kararıyla yeniden genel başkanlık görevine gelmesinin ardından başlayan işten çıkarmalar devam ediyor. Genel merkezde çalışan 85’i aşkın kişinin işine son veren yönetimin, son olarak eşleri Yeni Parti’de çalışmaya başlayan 3 çalışanı daha işten çıkardığı belirtildi.

Cumhuriyet’in haberine göre, işine son verilen Hasan Demirhan’ın eşi Yeni Parti’de büro personeli, Ozan Çiftçi’nin eşi kat görevlisi, Simge Cansu’nun nişanlısı ise büro personeli olarak çalışıyor. Söz konusu kişilerin daha önce CHP’de görev yaptığı, işten çıkarılmalarının ardından Yeni Parti’de işe başladıkları öğrenildi.

CHP’nin 7. Genel Başkanı Kemal Kılıçdaroğlu, 21 Mayıs’ta mahkemenin mutlak butlan kararıyla yeniden genel başkanlık görevine gelmişti. Kararın ardından genel merkez çalışanlarına yönelik işten çıkarmalar 26 Mayıs’ta, Kurban Bayramı arifesinde başlamıştı. İşine son verilen 85’i aşkın çalışan arasında sekreterler, fotoğrafçılar, kameramanlar, temizlik görevlileri ve çay ocağı emekçileri de bulunuyordu.

İşten çıkarmaların bir bölümünde, SGK’ye yapılan bildirimlerde Kod-48'in kullanıldığı belirtilmişti. İşçinin devamsızlığı, işverene veya ailesine yönelik hakaret gibi gerekçelerle iş sözleşmesinin feshedilmesinde kullanılan bu kod nedeniyle çalışanlar kıdem ve ihbar tazminatları ile işsizlik ödeneğinden yararlanamadı. İşten çıkarılan bazı çalışanlar, haklarını aramak için CHP yönetimine karşı dava açmıştı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Amy Goodman
title: Humanitarian Workers Keep at “Noble Mission” Despite Risks, Gaza Journalist Says
content:
“Every single aspect of the life of the people of Gaza has changed once and forever,” says Akram al-Satarri.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

In Gaza, October 7, 2023, is viewed as the beginning of the genocide. Over the past three years, Israel killed over 74,000 people, according to the Gaza Health Ministry, but many believe that number is a vast undercount. The killing continues despite a so-called ceasefire that took effect about a year ago.

“Every single aspect of the life of the people of Gaza has changed once and forever,” since October 7, says Akram al-Satarri, a Gaza-based journalist. He points out that a large majority of structures in the Gaza Strip have been reduced to rubble and that Israel controls around 70% of Gaza. “The Israeli Air Force is still hovering all around different parts of the Gaza Strip, and the IDF is still hunting Gazans, disturbing the already disturbed life, spreading death and displacement once and once again.”

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org. I’m Amy Goodman.

We end today’s show in Gaza, where today’s date, October 7th, is seen as the beginning of Israel’s genocide. In the three years since the Hamas attack on Israel that killed nearly 1,200 people, Israeli forces have killed over 74,000 Palestinians. Many believe the death toll is a vast undercount. This is a displaced Palestinian from Beit Hanoun speaking today in Gaza City.

AKRAM ABU JARAD: [translated] The worst three years that have passed in our lives. There is no life, no living, no food, no basic necessities of life. We wait for water from 5:00 to 10:00. And we are living in the streets, homeless, tired, worn out. I mean, a life worse than this? We are not living, my friend. We are dead in Gaza.

AMY GOODMAN: We go now to Gaza City, where we’re joined by journalist Akram al-Satarri.

I want to thank you so much for being with us. We spoke to you a few years ago as a journalist. You then went on to work with a humanitarian aid organization for several years. Now we’re back, being able to speak to you in Gaza City. Can you describe what’s happening on the ground? We just reported that as Israelis mourn the dead at the music site in southern Israel, they could hear the booms of Israeli airstrikes on the Gaza Strip right nearby. Tell us what’s happening where you are, Akram.

AKRAM AL-SATARRI: Well, October 7th was a day when Gaza changed once and forever. The way Palestinians have been living has changed. The way Palestinians have been managing their life has changed, as well. The way Palestinians were defining their life has changed. The Palestinians now are living in a de facto that has redefined everything — their understanding of life, their way of running and managing that life, their way to access things, their way to live, their way to stay in homes, their way to live in tents. Every single aspect of the life of the people of Gaza has changed once and forever.

Around 85% of the built environment in Gaza is already destroyed. Around 74% of the land of the Gaza Strip is also controlled by Israel and the IDF. Gazans have been struggling to access water and to access food. They have been facing significant public health hazards because of the fact that they were consuming water that was not properly treated. Organizations have been struggling for the sake of helping the people of Gaza. Statements were made by international and U.N. figures, diplomats all over the world, condemning the situation that has been going on, calling for Gazans to live and lead a normal life.

Unfortunately, for the third year now, and on October 7th, Gazans are reminded by the fact that they have been living in death and fear, destruction and displacement. author: Soraya Kishtwari
title: Labour Council’s Palantir Investments Increased 1,200% During Gaza Genocide
content:
Labour-run Camden Council’s investment holdings in Israel-linked tech firm Palantir have increased by more than 1,200% since October 2023, new figures show.


The figures were obtained by the

Palestine Solidarity Campaign (PSC) and first reported on by Declassified UK

. 


Camden Council’s leader, Sagal Abdi-Wali, is running for Labour against Green leader Zack Polanski in the Holborn and St Pancras byelection on Thursday, hoping to win Keir Starmer’s old seat. Abdi-Wali has led the council since May this year. 


Palantir shares in the council’s local government pension fund were worth £3.65m as of December 2025, up from £276,444 in October 2023. The company has provided Israel’s defence ministry with technology amid the genocide in Gaza. 


The council has holdings in 60 companies accused of complicity in Israeli human rights abuses in Palestine, the new figures also show, and the value of these has risen from £104m to £133.5m since June 2024.


As of 31 December 2025, Camden’s pension fund had more than £2.4bn of registered investments, including more than £10m in defence companies also tied to the Israeli military, including Boeing (£1.69m), Lockheed Martin (£1.12m) and Israeli weapons manufacturer Elbit Systems (£46,837). Campaigners have repeatedly called on the council to divest.


In January 2025, more than

4,000 people signed a petition

 demanding an audit of the pension fund and possible divestment from arms companies, triggering a council debate. The matter was subsequently referred to its pension committee. 


A

council-commissioned audit later identified £15.9m of investments

 across 46 companies as having significant human rights concerns related to conflict zones.


But the council’s wider holdings in companies identified by PSC as complicit in Israel’s occupation and violations of Palestinian rights have continued to rise in value.


Abdi-Wali has not commented on Gaza or divestment, according to a review of her public statements cited by Declassified, and did not respond to requests for comment.


Camden Council’s pension fund investment policy

 says it is committed to responsible investment.


A spokesperson for the council told Declassified that it has strengthened its approach to environmental, social and human rights concerns.


“We have a duty to act with the best long-term financial interests of members but, alongside this, we also expect environmental issues, social values, and human rights to play a central role in decision-making,” he said.

title: İş cinayetlerinde 2013’ten beri ilk kez beş ay üst üste 200’ün üzerinde ölüm
content:
İşçi Sağlığı ve İş Güvenliği (İSİG) Meclisi, Eylül 2026’ya ilişkin iş cinayetleri raporunu açıkladı.


Rapora göre Eylül ayında en az 226 işçi çalışırken hayatını kaybetti. Böylece 2026’nın ilk dokuz ayında iş cinayetlerinde yaşamını yitirenlerin sayısı en az 1736 oldu.


Ocak’ta 155, Şubat’ta 129, Mart’ta 151, Nisan’da 190, Mayıs’ta 214, Haziran’da 228, Temmuz’da 216 ve Ağustos’ta 227 işçi öldü.


2013’ten bu yana veri tutan İSİG Meclisi’nin raporlarda ilk kez beş ay üst üste aylık işçi ölümleri 200’ün üzerinde kaydedildi.


Ölümlerin 79’u sanayide, 54’ü inşaatta, 48’i hizmet sektöründe ve 45’i tarımda yaşandı. İşçilerin 21’i kadın, 14’ü göçmendi. Suriye, Azerbaycan, Türkmenistan, Bulgaristan, Irak, Rusya ve Ukrayna’dan gelmişlerdi.


Ayrıca Eylül ayında hayatını kaybeden işçilerin en az 7’si sendika üyesiydi. 219 işçi ise sendikasızdı. Ölen işçilerin yüzde 97’sini sendikasız çalışanlar oluşturdu.


Dokuz ayda en az 66 çocuk işçi öldü


Rapora göre bu ayda çalışırken ölen 226 kişinin 8’i çocuktu. Çocuklardan beşi 14 yaşında veya daha küçüktü; üçü ise 15-17 yaş grubundaydı.


Ölümlerin üçü tarım, diğerleri gıda, tekstil, metal, inşaat ve konaklama işkollarında meydana geldi.


2026’nın ilk dokuz ayında en az 66 çocuk işçi çalışırken hayatını kaybetti.


İSİG Meclisi, Mesleki Eğitim Merkezleri’nin (MESEM) son iki yılda çocuk işçiliğinin en görünür alanlarından biri haline geldiğini belirtti. Çocukların işyerlerinde çalışmasının MESEM modeliyle yaygınlaştırıldığı savunularak, sorunun yalnızca denetim ve iş güvenliği eksiklikleriyle sınırlı olmadığını ifade etti.


“Çocuk emeğinin düşük maliyetli hatta bedava, güvencesiz ve denetimsiz biçimde üretime dahil edilmesinin kurumsal ve yasal aracı yaratıldı. Bu noktada, MESEM’lerle ilgili tartışılması gereken şey yalnızca MESEM’lerde denetimin veya iş güvenliği önlemlerinin yetersizliği değil, çocuk emeğini işgücü piyasasının olağan ve kabul edilebilir bir unsuru haline getiren bu modelin kendisidir.” dedi.


İSİG Meclisi, MESEM dışındaki çocuk işçiliğinin özellikle tarım, küçük işletmeler, sanayi siteleri ve mevsimlik işlerde kayıt dışı biçimde sürdüğüne de dikkat çekti.


Ayrıca bu ayda ölenlerin 11'i de 65 yaş ve üstündeydi.


En fazla ölüm inşaatta


Eylül ayında en fazla iş cinayeti inşaat ve yol işkolunda meydana geldi. Bu işkolunda 50 işçi hayatını kaybetti.


Tarım ve orman işkolunda 45, taşımacılıkta 28, belediye ve genel işlerde 16, gemi, tersane, deniz ve liman işkolunda 15 işçi öldü.


Bunları 10 ölümle ticaret, büro, eğitim ve sinema; 9 ölümle konaklama ve eğlence, 7 ölümle de madencilik izledi.


İlk sırada trafik ve servis kazaları var


İş cinayetlerinin nedenlerine göre dağılımında trafik ve servis kazaları ilk sırada yer aldı. Eylül ayında 49 işçi trafik veya servis kazalarında yaşamını yitirdi.


Yüksekten düşme sonucu 41, ezilme ve göçük nedeniyle 40, kalp krizi veya beyin kanaması sonucu 30 işçi öldü.


Elektrik çarpması 15, zehirlenme ve boğulma 14, şiddet 13 işçinin ölümüne neden oldu


En fazla ölüm İstanbul’da


Eylül ayında Türkiye’nin 62 kentinde ve yurtdışında altı ülkede iş cinayeti kaydedildi.


En fazla ölüm 39 işçiyle İstanbul’da meydana geldi. İstanbul’u 9 ölümle Antep, 8’er ölümle Ankara ve Urfa, 7’şer ölümle Düzce ve Manisa, 6’şar ölümle Samsun ve Trabzon izledi.


(HA)

author: anred
title: No todo lo que brilla es un subsidio: ¿cuáles son las Zonas Frías de la política energética de Milei?
content:
Foto: Martín Álvarez Mullally


La misma semana en que el INDEC informó que la pobreza fue del 32% en el primer semestre de 2026, el Senado aprobó la modificación del régimen de Zona Fría. La decisión le quita ese subsidio en la tarifa de gas a 1,6 millones de hogares en 11 provincias y les condona 1.800 millones de dólares de deuda con el Estado a Edenor, Edesur y otras distribuidoras eléctricas. ¿Para quiénes son los salvatajes y para quiénes las deudas en la política energética de Milei?

Por Analía Zárate y Rosaura Barletta / OPSur. 


En el debate público sobre los subsidios a la energía en Argentina, gobiernos y buena parte de los medios se dedican a auditar el poder adquisitivo de las familias y la cantidad que -según ellos- le corresponde consumir a un hogar. 

“No podemos subsidiar piletas climatizadas”

, 

“el subsidio tiene que llegar a los que verdaderamente lo necesitan”

, 

“nos hicieron creer que la luz y el gas eran gratis”

, son argumentos que se amparan en la necesidad de eficiencia económica en la gestión de la energía y reducen la discusión a cómo y cuánto tiene que incidir el Estado en las tarifas que pagan los usuarios. Un abordaje que omite por qué y para qué existen los subsidios.


“Yo no uso televisión, ni microondas, ni lavarropas, ni computadora, ni pava eléctrica. Uso el cargador del celular, la heladera y las luces. También las de afuera, porque el barrio tiene muy poca iluminación y cuando llegamos de noche por la calle prendemos la linterna del celular”, dice Ana Pereyra, docente jubilada, lejos de utilizar la electricidad para climatizar una pileta como sugirió el jefe de Gabinete Diego Santilli. Vive en un barrio periférico de la ciudad de Mar del Plata, una de las ciudades que perdió la clasificación de Zona Fría, en una casa que alquila desde hace tres años y no sabe por qué no le otorgan el régimen de Subsidios Energéticos Focalizados (

ReSEF

) para la electricidad. Paga la tarifa plena, unos 200 mil pesos por mes.


El tarifazo del invierno afectó a todos los usuarios, incluso a ella, aunque dice que su consumo eléctrico no aumentó porque se calefacciona a gas. Aun cuando después de ponerse al día le quedan 50 mil pesos para vivir el resto del mes, asegura: “estoy pagando la boleta de luz completa porque aceleran los cortes por mora”. En las movilizaciones contra el tarifazo que convocaron diferentes organizaciones políticas y sociales de Mar del Plata, los usuarios presentaron boletas por montos aún mayores: 

7 millones de pesos para cuatro familias

, por ejemplo. Los damnificados por servicios impagables también se manifestaron en 

Santa Teresita

 y 

San Clemente del Tuyú

, entre otras localidades costeras de la provincia de Buenos Aires. “El invierno para mí es una situación muy delicada. Estos ajustes nos están aniquilando. Yo antes tomaba café, ahora té. Ya no uso la tarjeta de crédito para comprarme un par de zapatillas o hacer regalos, sino para ir al súper, y con cuidado”, cuenta Ana.


Foto: latecla.info


El 

Índice de Precios al Consumidor

 que elabora mensualmente el Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos (INDEC) es un indicador de lo que valen ciertos productos y servicios y se utiliza para seguir la evolución de la inflación. Para estimar qué rubros de la canasta pesan más sobre otros, la actualización de esos precios se combina con un ponderador elaborado en base a la Encuesta Nacional de Gastos de los Hogares (ENGHo) realizada en 2004. A comienzos de 2026 se anunció que se reemplazaría esa encuesta de 2004 por una medición de 2018. Con ese cambio, el ítem “Vivienda, agua, electricidad, gas y otros combustibles” iba a pasar de pesar el 9,4% al 14,5%. Finalmente, el gobierno nacional impidió la actualización y Marco Lavagna, el entonces titular del organismo, renunció.


Marcela Almeyda, Coordinadora de IPC Nacional y delegada de ATE INDEC, dice sobre el episodio: “Nuestro lema siempre es que las estadísticas tienen que ser independientes de los gobiernos de turno, tienen que servir para medir lo mejor posible la realidad y hay que usar el mejor instrumento disponible”. Y aclara: “Probablemente, las tarifas 

(de los servicios)

 hayan subido aún más su ponderación respecto de 2018 

(año de la medición que pretendía aplicar Lavagna)

, si bien para entonces el macrismo ya había hecho una readecuación y sacado subsidios”. De todas maneras, asegura Almeyda, el parámetro “queda viejo teniendo en cuenta que en 2024 hubo un aumento grande. Es evidente …

author: asn
title: Debate on the Australian United Workers Union  Election & Industrial Strategy
content:
Article from Rebel Worker Paper of Anarcho-Syndicalist Network www.rebelworker.org Vol. 44 No.2 (243) Sept. - Oct. 2026

Debate on Australian United Workers Union Election & Industrial Strategy

The United Workers Union leadership election (and why it didn't really matter)

11/9/26 Back in June, the United Workers Union (UWU) wrapped up a hotly contested election for its National Convention. The UWU is one of the biggest unions in the country, with 150,000 members in dozens of industries, including warehousing, hospitality, aged care, and early childhood education.

Two tickets pitched themselves to members. 'United for You', led by union president Jo Schofield, ended up winning with a slim majority. But they faced a serious challenge from a group calling itself 'Members First'.

Members First had a slick campaign and some of what they had to say sounded pretty good: Less focus on the Labor Party, no back room deals without delegates present, and more money for strike funds and organisers.

But despite its name, and what some on the Left claimed during the campaign, Members First was no rank-and-file movement. The ticket was the project of UWU's national secretary, Tim Kennedy, and was run with very little member involvement.

The election, then, was a factional battle between sections of the officialdom, and the parts of the Labor Party they align themselves with.

Two sides, same coin The UWU was founded as a merger between the National Union of Workers (NUW) and United Voice (UV) in 2019. The forces behind the two election tickets can be traced back to the separate unions.

United for You represented the UV wing. The ticket's campaign carried on their faction's tradition of prioritising political lobbying over industrial organising. Under their model, unionism is a kind of 'service' that members sign up for: legal advice and other perks are provided by the staff of the union in exchange for dues.

The NUW, on the other hand, placed more emphasis on traditional industrial organising, in industries like warehousing, logistics and food manufacturing. The leadership of the Members First campaign came from the NUW faction, and their election promises - more organisers, support for delegates, the occasional serious strike - reflect their own priorities.

The NUW approach, and the promises of Members First, might look pretty good at first glance. But the two strategies aren't as far apart as they seem.

The empowerment of members promised by Members First was incredibly limited, and largely focussed on 'transparency'. Even the promised strike funds were a fraction of the union's actual resources. Members weren't engaged in democratic structures as part of the campaign, and very few attended election events.

Members First wasn't an example of organisation from below-it was an advertising campaign, controlled from above.

Power to the rank-and-file? Despite the hundreds of thousands spent on campaigning by both sides, only 31% of members actually voted. Neither ticket mobilised members in a genuinely democratic or militant way, because, ultimately, both want to maintain the power of the officials and their links with the Labor Party.

Throwing money at an election isn't how you build the confidence, militancy, or participation of members. On paper, Members First may have been a marginally more militant ticket. But had they somehow managed to win, they would still be in the exact same position as their United For You opponents.

Without a real, well-organised rank-and-file movement, with power based in workplaces, the officials are left balancing between members, the bosses, and their mates in the ALP. With all the power on the bosses side, and pressure from the government to keep members in line, they have every reason to settle for bad deals.

The only people that can really put members first are the members themselves. To win democratic control over our union, we have to get organised at the level of the rank-and-file.

The UWU election was a fight for control of the National Convention, a body of 500 which then elects the day-to-day managers of the union. Rather than elect Convention delegates by industry or workplace, members are grouped together by the electorate they live in.

This system was designed to entrench the power of the Executive and prevent an alternative base of power forming among specific groups of workers on the shop floor.

Still, there are industry specific structures for parts of UWU's coverage …

author: Helmut Weiss
title: Wohngeld: Keine Lösung gegen Mietenwahnsinn – sondern Bestandteil des Problems
content:
Dossier


„

Das Wohngeld soll zum 1. Januar 2020 erhöht werden, zu diesem Zweck werden die Mittel für Wohngeld durch Bund und Länder aufgestockt. Im Jahr 2020 werden insgesamt 1,2 Milliarden Euro zur Verfügung stehen. Die Bundesregierung argumentiert mit den deutlich gestiegenen Wohnkosten und den Verbraucherpreisen. Die Leistungsfähigkeit des Wohngelds nehme dadurch mit der Zeit immer mehr ab. Zusätzlich würden bereits Erhöhungen der Einkommen, die ja nur die Entwicklung der Verbraucherpreise ausgleichen würden, zu einer Reduktion oder zum Verlust des Wohngeldanspruchs führen, mit der Folge, dass die Zahl der Wohngeldempfänger und die Reichweite des Wohngelds sinke. Mit dieser Argumentation setzt man weiter auf die Subjektförderung, bei der das Wohngeld durch die Mieter an die Vermieter weitergeleitet wird und damit die erhöhten Mietpreise legitimiert bzw. subventioniert werden. Man setzt nicht auf die Objektförderung, was konkret heißt, auf den Bau von Sozialwohnungen

…“ – so beginnt der

Beitrag „Wohngeld trägt nicht zur Lösung des Problems von Wohnungsnot bei – es ist Teil des Problems“ am 01. August 2019 beim Gewerkschaftsforum Dortmund


 zur Problemlösung, die gegenteilig wirkt. Siehe dazu:


Bund und Länder wollen beim Wohngeld Milliarden Euro einsparen – und die sozialen Kosten auf Kommunen und die ärmsten Menschen statt auf Vermieter umwälzen


Bund und Länder wollen beim Wohngeld Milliarden Euro einsparen – der Kahlschlag trifft eine Rekordzahl an Wohngeldhaushalten


Kahlschlag beim Wohngeld trifft vor allem Rentner*innen, Geringverdienende und Kinder


„

Zu den geplanten Kürzungen beim Wohngeld ein Statement von Anja Piel, DGB-Vorstandsmitglied: “Der Kahlschlag beim Wohngeld sucht seinesgleichen in der Geschichte unseres Sozialsystems. Die Kürzungen treffen mit voller Härte vor allem Rentner*innen, Geringverdienende und Kinder. Insgesamt trifft die Kürzung 1,3 Millionen Haushalte, alles solche, die jetzt schon kaum über die Runden kommen. 400.000 Haushalten raubt die Bundesregierung die finanzielle Hilfe für die Miete komplett, sie gehen zukünftig beim Wohngeld leer aus.

Umso unbegreiflicher, weil sich die Union gleichzeitig weigert, selbst sehr große Vermögen und sehr hohe Einkommen heranzuziehen, um Haushaltslöcher zu stopfen. title: Far Right Gleeful Over Firing Squad Death Sentence for Muslim Fort Hood Shooter
content:
Trump has approved the killing of Muslim US soldier Nidal Malik Hasan — the first Army execution in over 60 years.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Conservative figures have reacted with glee to the Trump administration’s approval of a firing squad death sentence for Muslim Army member Nidal Malik Hasan, in what would be the first execution carried out by the U.S. military in over six decades.

Hasan was convicted of committing a mass shooting at Texas’s Fort Hood in 2009, killing 13 people, with jurors recommending a maximum sentence of death. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth said in September 2025 that he was seeking President Donald Trump’s final approval for the military to execute Hasan, and the Pentagon has since laid out a plan to carry out three more executions for those who remain on the military’s death row.

Sean Parnell, the Pentagon’s spokesperson, announced on Monday that Trump has given his approval for the execution, characterizing Hasan as a “jihadist” and highlighting that he shouted “Allahu Akbar,” meaning “God is great,” during the attack.

“The Secretary of the Army will set the time and place of the execution. Judgement day for Hasan has finally come,” Parnell said in a post on X.

Hasan is a U.S.-born Muslim of Palestinian descent. At the time, he admitted to committing the killings, saying that he was against his upcoming deployment to Afghanistan and opposed to the U.S. military’s biases against Muslims. His family said that he was discriminated against for being Muslim while in the military.

If Hasan’s execution is carried out, this would be the first execution done by the military since 1961, when Army private John Bennett was executed by hanging. Bennett, who was Black, was accused of raping and attempting to kill an Austrian girl, who was white, and retrospective reports said that his case was not tried properly; in the six years leading up to his execution, eight other Black soldiers on the military’s death row were executed, while six others who were white lived.

Execution by firing squad is also relatively rare in the U.S. According to the Death Penalty Information Center, only 34 out of over 8,700 executions in the U.S. between 1890 and 2010 were carried out through firing squads. This method is only legal in a handful of states, but Trump has moved to bring it back in order to ramp up the use of the death penalty.

Typically, in an execution by firing squad, the prisoner is hooded and bound to a chair. A doctor pinpoints the prisoner’s heart and puts a target on it. Between three and five shooters are in an enclosure nearby and aim at the target through a slot; in some protocols, one shooter’s gun is randomly loaded with blanks. The shooters all fire at once, and the prisoner dies via gunshot to the heart, or bleeds out.

Conservatives online were exuberant following Parnell’s announcement, which Hegseth described as “[j]ustice.”

“More of this please. This is what I voted for. More dead jihadists!” said conservative influencer and Trump confidante Laura Loomer.

Some right-wing accounts on X called for the administration to televise the execution for Americans to watch.

“I volunteer to pull the trigger,” said Carl Higbie, a former Navy SEAL and current daily host on far right outlet Newsmax.

“This is the way,” said NewsNation host Katie Pavlich.

The Trump administration’s announcement came just days after the botched execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee. Pike, who was convicted of murdering a classmate in 1995, was hospitalized after Tennessee prison officials administered two doses of pentobarbital that were supposed to kill her, against medical recommendations. Pike’s attorney said on Sunday that she is on a ventilator and in critical condition.

title: The Marxist Roots of Spanish Fascism
content:
The political regime of General Francisco Franco, which came about following the conclusion of the Spanish Civil War, is often described as being conservative, clerical, and authoritarian. The distinctive features of the fascist rule under General Francisco Franco are revealed in a curious episode from history – on his death, the very first flowers laid at his coffin came from China, signed by Communist leader Zhou Enlai. It just happened to be about the same period of time when communist Cuba led by Fidel Castro observed three days of national mourning. It’s beyond irony for communist regimes to express such friendliness to a fascist dictator. However, rather than indicating some form of ideological sympathy, this unusual episode reveals another side of Cold War diplomacy, a possible precursor of nowadays campism.

However, looking closer, the earlier movement of the Franco regime before it suffered an internal coup had the rhetoric, symbols, and even some aspects of the organizational structure characteristic of National Syndicalism as the pre-cursor to their Spanish fascism. The earlier Spanish National Syndicalism did not emerge from the typical right-wing Spanish conservatism. Rather, the radical ideology was formed in the early 1930s and the main authors of this movement were Ramiro Ledesma Ramos and Onésimo Redondo Ortega. Being inspired by the revolutionary ideologies that dominated the European left of that period, such as Sorelian Marxism (revolutionary syndicalism), anarchism, and Marxist socialism, National Syndicalism rejected any attempts to preserve the existing capitalist or agrarian order in favor of a total revolution of the working class. Between 1936 and 1937, however, due to the physical elimination of the leadership of the movement and the purely tactical actions of Franco, who managed to seize military and political power, National Syndicalist movement in Spain was thoroughly co-opted by Franco. Having deprived the ideology of its social-revolutionary nature and keeping the symbols and slogans of the movement, Franco transformed the movement of total state transformation into a means of labor control.

In order to see how Franco managed to pervert National Syndicalism, it is necessary to take a look at the ideological origin of the movement. The main ideologist of National Syndicalism, Ramiro Ledesma Ramos, created his political newspaper "La Conquista del Estado" (The Conquest of the State) in March 1931, stating from the very beginning that his purpose was to channel the revolutionary spirit of the Spanish proletariat for the sake of the national project. His paper (The Conquest of the State) even became a subject of debate in a CNT assembly, yet, it did not have the intended impact. Ledesma was well-versed in continental philosophy and embodied what is called the greatest assimilation of Georges Sorel's revolutionary syndicalism in Spain. The syndicalism of Sorel proclaimed direct actions of workers' syndicates to crush bourgeois liberal regime. The key reference point of Ledesma on the left side of Spain was the Confederación Nacional del Trabajo (CNT), a strong anarcho-syndicalist labor union. It was obvious that Ledesma admired the fighting spirit, anti-bourgeois combativeness, and revolutionary passion of the masses of the CNT. In his opinion, anarcho-syndicalists were the best combat forces in Spain, and it was his main aim to "nationalize" the CNT, that means to redirect revolutionary power of CNT from internationalist anti-statism to the national state. It is important to note that this influence was not only theoretical. The early National Syndicalist cells included many former members of anarchist and communist organizations. One of the leaders of CNT, Alvaro de Sotomayor, became the head of National Syndicalist union of taxi drivers in Madrid. Similarly, Dr. Santiago Montero Díaz from Communist Party of Spain also joined them. Both National Syndicalists and anarchists shared the following superficial values: their common hatred of bourgeois democratic system, opposition to gradual reforms, and support of direct action through workers' unions. Similarly, the relations between National Syndicalism and Marxism were also very similar. The movement was defined by structural mimicry and fierce ideological rivalry. First of all, Ledesma admitted Karl Marx as a great philosopher and agreed with the basic ideas of his criticism of bourgeois liberal capitalist system. Even though the …

Antifascism, as a meaningful path for resisting fascism, has been dead in the water for some time now. Perhaps, it was dead on arrival. It is not entirely or even mostly the fault of many enthusiastic anti-fascists, I do not want to dismiss the brave souls that took to the streets, that took up the gun to fight back by any means necessary, but rather those who constructed the scaffolding for what antifascism out to be and failed to illustrate what exactly fascism was and how it was to be defeated. Anti-fascism may have emerged from the most radical sects of society, the anarchists and communists, but it was immediately tainted, defanged, and co-opted by capitalists so thoroughly as to mean nothing. My analysis is not simply a critique, but it’s an introduction into how I think we must move forward if we want to survive what is to come.

There are multiple problems here.

First are the people unwilling to engage in history and theory, it is a form of anti-intellectualism where they seek to solve for a problem they aren’t capable of diagnosing. They call themselves antifascists, they fail to meaningfully study anything, then other antifascists who are bit more well-read tend to coddle these people, a thousand excuses to avoid theory are given, and then theorists are made to simply be bookworms, which is absolutely true if you’re a liberal, but radicals have shown that our theorists are often engaging in action as much as they are theory. Their view and understanding of anti-fascism permeate the scene, so you get god awful takes like American soldiers being anti-fascist or you get groups like the American Iron Front, and these people don’t eagerly create resistance, they eagerly recreate the conditions for failure.

Second, the people who are willing to engage in history and theory, but they only do so from the lens of recent antifascist authors who themselves completely neglect radical history and theory.

Their work is so egregious that we almost must start a theory of anti-fascism from scratch entirely, if it were not entirely too late, and if there was not another means to address the current political moment.

Robert Paxton, author of the Anatomy of Fascism, will be the focus of this episode to illustrate how bad our framework is. I don’t even know if he identifies as an anti-fascist. He is seen as the leading expert on fascism, having been well-sourced by many modern antifascists, and I’ll break down why he is so bad at being said-expert, to include that he didn’t even identify Trump as a fascist until after his first term as president.

Next is Mark Bray, supposedly an anarchist who could not be bothered to even reference one of the first Italian antifascists and one of the best anarchist theorists, Errico Malatesta, in his Antifascist Handbook. He also couldn’t be bothered to source Daniel Guerin, another anarchist, who like Malatesta, had thorough firsthand experience with fascism, and wrote extensively on the subject in his book, Fascism and Big Business.

title: Manifestaciones del 3 de octubre, vivienda y antifascismo en Sevilla
content:
El corresponsal de alasbarricadas para Andalucía, Murcia, Canarias, Norte de África y Badajoz, me manda su crónica y la pongo tal cual.


--------------------------------------------------------


Manifestaciones del 3 de octubre


Primero que nada, hay que tener en cuenta que mi visión se limita a lo que vi en la acampada. Por tanto, hablar a partir de una visión tan cerrada de un solo día es muy parcial. Puede que haya mucha más gente de alguna organización o colectivo que esté más implicada y que no nombre, porque ese día concreto yo no la viera. Teniendo esto en cuenta, y tratando de hacerlo lo más objetivo posible, comento un poco lo que vi.


La acampada representaba, más o menos, el microcosmos de los colectivos de izquierdas en Sevilla: desde CGT hasta Izquierda Revolucionaria, por ejemplo. Esto último lo digo por las banderas que había y porque se veía a alguna gente de ellos. También estaban aficionados al fútbol que se autodenominan de izquierda radical y que, en cuanto al tema de la violencia o la autodefensa, tienen una concepción bastante exagerada, desde mi punto de vista.


Pero, sobre todo, el gran peso lo llevaban los colectivos de barrio y los relacionados con la vivienda. A muchos de ellos, por la gente que conozco directa o personalmente, se les podría denominar gente del área de la autonomía. Algunos vienen de CNT, CGT o de otros ámbitos sindicales, y otros han desarrollado todo su recorrido dentro del área de la autonomía. Aparte, claro está, del Sindicato de Inquilinas e Inquilinos.


No sé si me salto algún colectivo. Adelante Andalucía, por supuesto, tenía una pequeña representación. También había gente de Podemos, de Izquierda Unida y otros espacios. Pero lo más curioso es otra cosa: el 99 % de la gente era menor de 35 años. Los «abuelos», ayer éramos más bien poquitos, tanto en la acampada como después en la manifestación antifascista.


Y hay un grupo nuevo que se llama algo así como Movimiento Juvenil Socialista. Son de tendencia leninista. Hacen teatros con banderas. Muy ceremoniosos. Desde mi punto de vista, son vanguardistas, intentando chupar medios por un tubo y aparecer estratégicamente en todos lados. Hablé con alguno. Lo típico: “Todos son malos menos nosotros; nosotros llevamos las instrucciones de Lenin en el bolsillo y hay que hacernos caso. Todos los demás son socialdemócratas, electoralistas, no se aclaran, no se organizan...  Nosotros sí tenemos la verdad en las manos”. Básicamente, eso es lo que vi allí.


Puede ser que me falte algo. Ya digo que quizá yo no lo viera en ese momento o que no estuviera. Eché en falta algo de CNT: solo había dos afiliados, que yo supiera, y no militantes. Aunque, claro, por ejemplo, cuando veo a los de CGT, identifico fácilmente a la gente porque llevan la camiseta de CGT. Me supongo que había más gente de CGT, gente muy joven, pero tampoco conocía a la gente de CGT que estuvo por allí.


 


Diferencias con el 15-M


En cuanto a las diferencias con la acampada del 15-M, yo veo dos fundamentales.


La primera es que aquí hay un único tema que une a todos: la vivienda. Por supuesto, cada grupo mantiene sus propios intereses, pero les une un solo asunto. Por tanto, siempre será más fácil ponerse de acuerdo sobre un único tema que sobre un millón de cosas.


La segunda diferencia es el tema de la violencia. Bien es cierto que es una acampada pacífica y que la gente es pacífica. Pero tienen claro, por lo menos en su mayoría, el asunto de la autodefensa. Al contrario que en el 15-M, donde había una posición sistemáticamente no violenta, esta gente, ante el asunto de los nazis y demás, tiene bastante claro que, si hay que defenderse, hay que defenderse. Y también hay bastante preocupación por la seguridad.


Qué puede pasar con la acampada


Por lo que estoy viendo, por la parte que escuché en la asamblea, por los correos y por la gente con la que hablé, parece que al Sindicato de Inquilinas e Inquilinos de Sevilla le viene grande todo esto.


Es normal. No se esperaba la repercusión que iba a tener. Entonces, asumir el liderazgo de esta lucha les viene muy, muy grande.


Y ahí creo que la socialdemocracia, que es muy buena en estas cosas, puede darle una alternativa para negociar. Porque hay en ciernes una huelga general. Esto ha salido un poco a bote pronto y me imagino que ha sido apoyado por todo el mundo, porque a todo el mundo le parece una herramienta de máxima utilidad cuando desde el electoralismo se han agotado las vías, especialmente …

title: Bertolt Brecht : Écrire contre le fascisme
content:
Combattre le fascisme y compris et jusque dans les mots. Cela ne demande pas seulement de la détermination et du courage, mais aussi une analyse et une méthode de critique et de combat qui refuse l'absence de perspective. Le poète et homme de théâtre, Bertolt Brecht, demeure en ce sens une source d'inspiration.


« Les opinions tombaient d'accord pour dire que se levait une nouvelle ère de barbarie. Les atrocités étaient les conséquences d'un horrible esprit guerrier qui avait eu le dessus de bien mystérieuse façon. On comparait ça à une catastrophe naturelle, à un tremblement de terre ».


Ces quelques phrases, non dénuées d'ironie, ne dénoncent-elles pas un certain état d'esprit qui sévit de nos jours face à la multiplication et intensification des guerres – et du génocide en Palestine – et à la montée des extrêmes droites ? Elles furent pourtant écrites il y a près d'un siècle, en 1933, par le dramaturge et poète Bertolt Brecht. Ce dernier venait de fuir l'Allemagne. Les nazis avaient pris le pouvoir, fait brûler ses livres sur la place publique et lui enlèverait bientôt sa nationalité. Les éditions Divergences ont eu l'excellente idée de publier des textes – articles, poèmes, etc., dont plusieurs inédits –, écrits par Brecht au cours des années 1933-1939 ; « la période la plus ouverte et bagarreuse de l'exil », selon Irène Bonneaud qui a préfacé ce recueil et contextualisé chacun des textes.


Brecht se distingue d'emblée en ce qu'il se confronte directement aux effets de sidération provoqués par le fascisme, en refusant de simplement opposer la culture à la barbarie – « Quand on lui fait remarquer qu'il est brutal, le fascisme répond par un éloge fanatique de la brutalité » – et en cherchant une façon d'écrire antifasciste. Celle-ci passe par l'ironie, le détournement, le refus de se payer de mots. Ainsi, il raille « les bavardages sur la barbarie », les déclarations générales et floues, les revendications universelles sans conséquence pour l'action. Et le caractère partiel, inoffensif et limité de la critique :


« Beaucoup de condamnations du fascisme ne sont que de simples dénonciations d'un

excès

, comme si on lui reprochait seulement d'

aller trop loin.


(...)


Exploitez, mais pas trop fort ! Faites la guerre, mais pas contre la population civile ! Avec des canons, mais pas avec des gaz ! »


En réalité, dès décembre 1933, il écrit que « le temps des appels et des protestations est fini jusqu'à nouvel ordre, il faut se consacrer à la pédagogie et à l'étude ».


Une vérité pratique


Le fascisme était pour Brecht le signe que le capitalisme ne pouvait plus mener ses affaires sans brutalité, qu'il lui fallait désormais se débarrasser de ses derniers scrupules et jeter « par-dessus bord ses propres concepts, les uns après les autres, tels que liberté, justice, personnalité, et même, concurrence ». L'auteur comptait sur le prolétariat et entendait recourir au matérialisme dialectique de manière étroite. Ce sont là les éléments les plus datés de sa critique. Autrement plus pertinente – plus pertinente et plus actuelle –, sa réflexion autour d'un marxisme hérétique, souvent en écho aux conversations qu'il avait alors avec Walter Benjamin, cherchant à dégager une manière de penser, de dire la vérité.


Mais cette vérité devait avoir quelque chose de concret, de « guerrier », en ce qu'« elle ne combat pas seulement la non-vérité, mais ceux qui la répandent » et, en fin de compte, « une portée pratique ». C'est que Brecht rejetait les explications qui « suffisaient peut-être à susciter des sentiments mélancoliques, mais guère à apprendre à se rendre maître d'une situation expliquée ainsi ». Il fallait clairement expliquer « pourquoi nous en sommes arrivés là ? » en refusant de s'abandonner paresseusement à la fatalité ou à la «

nature

 humaine ».


La vérité ne pouvait se muer en un vague sermon que l'on se contenterait de dire ou d'écrire et qui demeurerait sans effet, sans écho, n'offrant aucune perspective. Elle devait s'adresser « à quelqu'un qui saura en faire quelque chose ». Et qui d'autre sinon « la masse de celles et ceux qui produisent, cette masse de gens qui a été si longtemps objet de la politique et doit devenir son sujet » ? L'intelligence devait d'autant plus devenir une arme «

que les bons n'ont pas été vaincus parce qu'ils étaient bons, mais parce qu'ils étaient faibles

 ».


Le spectacle n'aura pas de happy end


Le fameux « effet de distanciation » théorisé et mis en avant par Brecht …

title: Angriffe auf die Freiheit der Wissenschaft: Nicht nur AfD hetzt gegen Hochschulen
content:
Dossier


„

Die AfD Sachsen-Anhalt fragt gezielt nach Listen postkolonialer Seminare und Lehrstühle. Wie die Universitäten beginnen, sich gegen die Angriffe zu wappnen. Lehrstellen seien umzuschichten und zu streichen. (…) Die Anfrage liest sich, als arbeite man bei der AfD schon an einer Feindesliste (…) „Ich war schockiert über Kollegen, die Listen mit Namen und Projekten durchgegeben hatten – anstatt sich souverän hinzustellen und diesen Angriff auf die Wissenschaftsfreiheit abperlen zu lassen.“ (…) Nach der Anfrage habe das Rektorat eine Kommission gegründet, um die Universität resilienter gegenüber wissenschaftsfeindlichen Angriffen zu machen

…“ Umfangreicher

Artikel von Gareth Joswig vom 14.10.2025 in der taz online

Angriff auf die Freiheit der Wissenschaft

AfD gegen Studierende: Wie die Rechtsradikalen Mitbestimmung bundesweit abschaffen wollen

Hochschule und Wissenschaft sind für die extreme Rechte Kulturkampfeld Nummer 1. Sie gehen von wenig Widerstand und großer Zustimmung aus. In Bayern gibt es seit 52 Jahren keine verfasste Studierendenschaft. Minister Hans Meier (CSU) sagt dazu 1973 offen, er wolle “den linken Sumpf trockenlegen”. Die Argumente sind dieselben: zu wenig Legitimierung, zu “politisch”, zu links. Die AfD beruft sich darauf. Was jetzt passieren muss:


– Bekenntnis zur verfassten Studierendenschaft und zur demokratischen Hochschule durch die hessische Landesregierung und alle Fraktionen!


– Neupositionierung bei JU, JuLis, RCDS und LHG, klar gegen rechtsaußen!


– Klare Positionierung zu immer weiterer Demokratisierung aller Gesellschaftsbereiche durch alle Verantwortlichen in Bund und Ländern!


– Prüfung eines Verbots der AfD als verfassungsfeindliche Partei in der Tradition des deutschen Faschismus!“

title: Çetintepe: Constitutional Court ruling may leave women more helpless
content:
The Constitutional Court annulled on 4 June 2026 the provision in Article 175 of the Turkish Civil Code that allowed a spouse who would fall into poverty as a result of divorce to claim alimony from the other spouse “indefinitely,” finding it unconstitutional. The reasoning for the annulment was published in the Official Gazette on 30 September. The ruling will take effect nine months later, on 30 June 2027.


Gamze Çetintepe of the Women’s Defence Network spoke to ANF about the Constitutional Court’s ruling and drew attention to how the reasoning portrays men who pay alimony as “victims.” Çetintepe said women’s acquired rights were being taken away and women’s labour was being rendered invisible.


Çetintepe said the ruling was based on a narrative suggesting that women were trying to “take away” something that rightfully belonged to men and that this created a grievance for men.


Çetintepe described the ruling as part of propaganda aimed at trapping women in families marked by exploitation and violence, in line with the “Decade of the Family” policies of making divorce more difficult, encouraging marriage and increasing birth rates. She said the reasoning behind the ruling states:“The reasoning states: ‘Due to the contested provision, the obligation to pay poverty alimony may continue until the end of a person’s life, which could prevent that person from remarrying, acquiring property and providing for future children, and therefore the provision imposes a disproportionate restriction on the person’s right to respect for private and family life and their right to property…’


The so-called disproportionate restriction is alimony averaging 2,000 lira a month. If there is to be a debate about alimony, it should be about why it is so inadequate and why it fails to prevent women from falling into poverty after divorce.”


‘Women are forced to give up even their existing rights’


Çetintepe said the reality of how alimony works in practice is very different from the picture presented by the ruling. She said, “Apart from the inadequacy of alimony payments, it is also very common for even these amounts not to be paid, or for men to tell women, ‘If you don’t ask for alimony, I won’t cause trouble and I’ll agree to the divorce,’ forcing women to give up even their existing rights so that they can escape households of exploitation and violence as quickly as possible.”


Çetintepe said that many men also fail to pay child support, the financial contribution paid by the parent who does not have custody to cover expenses such as the child’s care, education, healthcare and housing in proportion to their financial means.


Çetintepe said, “Many men do not even pay the child support they are required to provide for the care of their children, continuing to place the burden of shared responsibilities on women even after the marriage ends. The same concern shown for men’s private lives and their ability to acquire property is not shown when it comes to monitoring whether the alimony women are entitled to receive is actually paid and ensuring that those payments are made.”


‘Men’s “victimhood” is that they can no longer exploit women’


Çetintepe said the law approaches marriage and divorce in a way that disregards women’s unpaid labour and is implemented in a misogynistic manner. She explained the actual purpose of the ruling and its possible impact on divorce rates as follows: “If women are nevertheless divorcing at increasingly higher rates, it may not be accurate to say that this ruling will change that. But that is certainly the intention. What they call men’s victimhood is precisely this: that they can no longer exploit women.


Still, if we consider this ruling together with all the pro-family policies of which it is a part, as well as the country’s deepening poverty and persistent sexism, it could make women feel more helpless about how they would survive on their own if they divorced.”


‘Women are expected to find work while caring for their children alone’


Asked about claims that ending alimony after a certain period would encourage women to enter the workforce, Çetintepe described this discourse as another part of the propaganda portraying men as victims of women. She explained why women fall into poverty after divorce: “It is not because women can live on monthly alimony payments of 2,000 lira that they do not take paid jobs. The reason women fall into poverty after marriage is the exploitation of their paid and …

title: Projection / discussion : Jeux vidéo et politique
content:
Projection du documentaire Le jeu vidéo, une affaire d'hommes 

 

? dimanche 18/10 16h à la librairie Publico à l'invitation du Groupe libertaire d'Ivry.


Le jeu vidéo, une affaire d'hommes 

 

? Documentaire de Nostalgeek (2023, 35 min)


Je ne peux pas m'identifier au protagoniste de ce jeu car c'est une femme et je suis un homme. 

 

» Est‐ce que ce genre de déclaration ne cache pas quelque part des soucis un brin plus profonds

 

?


Le jeu vidéo — comme le cinéma, la

BD

, la littérature… — peut servir de support à des idées politiques de tous bords. Ce court métrage s'attaque plus spécifiquement au sexisme 

 

; mais, de façon plus générale, existe‐t‐il des jeux luttant contre toutes les formes de discrimination, contre le capitalisme, l'État, la religion 

 

? Des jeux vidéo anarchistes 

 

?


Le sexisme dans le milieu du jeu vidéo


Les femmes travaillant dans l'industrie vidéoludique constatent une différence de salaire (25,3 % d'écart au bénéfice des hommes). Certains rejettent les designs de personnages féminins non hyper‐sexualisés. Dans les studios de développement français, les femmes représentent 24 % des effectifs alors qu'elles n'en constituaient que 10,6 % il y a 10 ans. Depuis 2018, nous constatons toujours la même disparité selon les catégories de métier, avec une sous‐représentation des femmes dans les métiers techniques (programmation, data). La question du harcèlement au bureau est également régulièrement soulevée. D'autres formes de sexisme évoquées sont le manque de volonté d'inclure des personnages féminins bien représentés dans les jeux vidéo.


Les jeux qui cherchent à mettre en avant des personnes non hommes peuvent entraîner un harcèlement de leurs scénaristes et développeurs : c'est le cas de Amber Scott, scénariste du jeu Baldur's Gate : Siege of Dragonspear, harcelée en 2016. Elle a en effet inclus un personnage principal féminin et un personnage secondaire transgenre dans le jeu, en plus de se moquer du Gamergate

 [

1

]

 dans une réplique. En réponse à ces actions, elle est la cible d'une campagne de harcèlement et le jeu reçoit des retours négatifs en masse.


En juillet 2021, suite à son harcèlement par un manager, une employée du studio américain de jeux vidéo Activision Blizzard se suicide. Deux mille de ses collègues signent alors une pétition protestant contre des méthodes de management, et organisent un mouvement de grève. De manière plus générale, c'est la «

 

 culture Bro 

 

», culture sexiste répandue dans les milieux de la tech, qui est mise en accusation.


Sur les 152 major games publiés en 2022, 61 % des personnages sont des hommes, 39 % des femmes, et 31,7 % des jeux vidéo mettent en scène des personnages exclusivement masculins. Dans les 50 RPGs les plus joués ces 30 dernières années, les hommes parlent en moyenne 2 fois plus que les femmes.


67 % des françaises jouent aux jeux vidéo, elles ont 39 ans en moyenne et représentent 48 % des personnes qui jouent au moins une fois par semaine. Mais 40 % d'entre elles affirment avoir déjà dû se résoudre à cacher leur genre dans des parties en ligne, 46 % des gameuses jugent les contenus qu'elles voient en ligne trop sexistes ou misogynes, et elles sont aussi 40 % à avoir déjà vécu des situations de harcèlement en ligne.


Il n'y a sans doute pas plus de sexistes dans le jeu vidéo que dans le reste de la société : ce triste constat n'est que le reflet de l'état des lieux en général. Mais, comme dans la littérature ou le cinéma, changer le contenu ne devrait‐il pas participer à changer les mentalités 

 

?

Entrée libre (accueil dès 15 heures)


Librairie du Monde Libertaire, 145 rue Amelot, Paris 11

]

Le Gamergate est une série de polémiques née durant le mois d'août 2014 ayant évolué en une campagne de harcèlement sexiste contre des femmes journalistes et développeuses.

title: Eylül ayında 28 kadın cinayeti: Kadınlar en çok evlerinde öldürüldü!
content:
Kadın Cinayetlerini Durduracağız Platformu raporuna göre, 2026 Eylül ayında erkekler tarafından 28 kadın öldürüldü, 19 kadın şüpheli şekilde ölü bulundu. Kadın cinayetleri oranı bir önceki aya göre yüzde 21 arttı.

Öldürülen 28 kadından 2’si ekonomik bahanelerle, 2’si hayatına dair karar alma bahanesiyle öldürüldü. 23’ünün hangi bahaneyle öldürüldüğü tespit edilemedi.

Platformda yer alan bilgilere binaen, “23 kadının hangi bahaneyle öldürüldüğünün tespit edilememesi, kadına yönelik şiddetin ve kadın cinayetlerinin görünmez kılınmasının bir sonucudur. Kadınların kim tarafından, neden öldürüldüğü tespit edilmedikçe; adil yargılama yapılmayıp şüpheli, sanık ve katiller caydırıcı cezalar almadıkça, önleyici tedbirler uygulanmadıkça şiddet boyut değiştirerek sürmeye devam ediyor.” ifadelerine yer verildi.

Eylül ayında öldürülen 28 kadından 5’i evli olduğu erkek, 3’ü birlikte olduğu erkek, 2’si tanıdığı biri, 2’si babası, 1’i oğlu, 1’i kardeşi, 1’i eskiden evli olduğu erkek, 1’i eskiden birlikte olduğu erkek, 1’i akrabası, 1’i eski damadı tarafından öldürüldü. 4 kadının öldüren kişi ile yakınlığı tespit edilemedi. Eylül ayında öldürülen kadınların yüzde 23’ü evli olduğu erkek tarafından öldürüldü.

Kadınların 4’ü evde, 6’sı sokakta, 2’si iş yerinde, 1’i arabada, 1’i arazide, 1’i diğer bir kamusal alanda öldürüldü. 3 kadının öldürüldüğü yer tespit edilemedi. Bu ay öldürülen kadınların yüzde 50’si evde öldürüldü, öldürülen kadınların yüzde 54’ü ateşli silah ile öldürüldü.

Öldürülen kadınların yüzde 4’ü, 6284 kapsamındaki koruma kararına rağmen öldürüldü, öldürülen kadınların yüzde 68’i evliydi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Leyte farmer files harassment complaint vs military
content:
By Veronika Barbosa TACLOBAN CITY – A farmer filed a complaint on September 22 with the Commission on Human Rights Regional Office 8 against the Philippine Army’s 93rd Infantry Battalion (IB) due to intimidation against her and her family.

Accompanied by the National Union of People’s Lawyers Eastern Visayas and Katungod Sinirangan Bisayas, Brenda Lagado said that the first incident happened on July 28 in their house in Jaro, Leyte. “We were visited by elements of the Armed Forces of the Philippines. At first, they were just checking in on us but they eventually pressured us to confess that we have connections with the New People’s Army even if we have none.”

In the same month, Lagado said that her 16-year-old cousin was also interrogated by soldiers and alleged military assets.

“He [my cousin] was tending to farm animal when he was approached by seven soldiers and seven other individuals. At first, he was told to wait for a certain Basas who was supposed to talk to him but the latter did not arrive. He was instead confronted by a certain Simon who later grabbed him by the collar, hit him with a piece of chopped wood, and threatened that he will be hanged or electrocuted if he does not cooperate with them.”

Lagado said that his cousin was coerced by at least 14 men to divulge information about certain individuals that the victim does not know about.

She said that in August, a certain Sgt. Andres visited their house and compelled her to go to the barangay hall to purportedly “clear her name” which she refused to do. “We already went to the barangay before but the harassment still continued.”

In the same month, Lagado said that a child development worker of the Daycare Center where her child 3-year-old child was enrolled in, also experienced interrogation. “The teacher told us that a certain Cris Edison Rivera, who we later found out was from the 93rd IB, asked for the name and even live birth of my child. He also interrogated the teacher and asked information about our family.”

On September 11, Lagado received a letter from an unknown sender via express delivery. The letter included an unknown number and contained statements maligning Brenda and her family. “The letter pressured me to cooperate and call the number written on the letter within 24 hours or else they would let my entire family and my husband know that I have a relationship with an NPA rebel.”

“I am scared for my family and worried about my children’s safety. I am scared because the military have pictures of my family and even my children,” Lagado said. In a statement, Katungod SB condemned the 93rd IB’s series of harassment targeted against the Lagado family and their intimidation tactics involving innocent children.

“Children are not the tools of war…they should never be used, threatened, or assaulted to serve the military’s agenda. The 93rd IB, the entire AFP, and the NTF-ELCAC should all be held accountable for using a child and physically assaulting a minor to force the family to surrender or report to the 93rd IB.” Katungod SB called on the Commission on Human Rights to swiftly investigate and to protect the Lagado family against further intimidation and harassment. (DAA)
