title: Antiimperialistische Aktionswoche 7. - 11. Oktober
content:
Aufruf zur Antiimperialistischen Aktionswoche


💥Vor fast einem Jahr sind in Bern tausende Menschen zusammengekommen, um ein Ende des Genozids in Gaza und ein freies Palästina zu fordern. Und die Schweizer Kompliz*innenschaft dabei zu konfrontieren. Der Widerstand auf den Strassen Berns war kräftig und gebündelt. Verständlich, nachdem wir in Lausanne, Genf, Basel, Zürich, Lugano, Bern und so vielen anderen Orten verschiedene Unis besetzt und bereits unzählige Demos und andere Aktionen organisiert hatten, die ungehört blieben. Während der Genozid weiterhin geläugnet wurde. Unsere Wut über den Genozid in Gaza, die Kolonisierung Palästinas und den Imperialismus liess entsprechend die Strassen beben und verschlug dem Staat die Sprache. Er hatte keine andere Wahl, als sein wahres Gesicht zu zeigen und zu versuchen unseren Widerstand gewaltsam im Keim zu ersticken. Er hatte keine andere Wahl, als am Rattenschwanz zu ziehen, der der Öffentlichkeit als Verschärfungen der Repressionsmassnahmen und der Roadmap für nationale Sicherheit präsentiert wird.


👉Ob in Lugano, Genf, Lausanne, Bern, Zürich oder Basel: Überall spüren wir die Gewalt des Schweizer Staats. Er beschützt mit Schlagstock und Gummischrott auf Ausbeutung beruhendes System. Er beschützt - indem er unseren Aufstand unterdrückt - die Interessen der Grosskonzerne, welche Rekordprofite am Krieg, am Genozid und der Vernichtung unseres Planeten und dem Leben von hundertausenden von Menschen erzielen.


❤️‍🔥Doch wir lassen uns davon nicht einschüttern und bilden weiterhin überregional Banden! Wir lassen uns nicht beeindrucken von ihrer Propagandamaschinerie, wir lassen uns nicht beeindrucken von Bullen, Geheimdienst und sonstigen Taugenichtsen. Wir lassen uns im Gegenteil vom unbeugsamen Widerstand gegen die koloniale Kontinuität und den Imperialismus beeindrucken. Und darum rufen wir auf zur Antiimperialistischen Aktionswoche:

Vom 7.10. - 11.10.2026, vom Mittwoch bis zur grossen Demo am Sonntag.


✊Wir richten uns mit diesem Aufruf an alle Gruppen, Kollektive, Netzwerke, Einzelpersonen und Organisationen überall in und ausserhalb der Schweiz! Wir richten uns an all jene, die so unglaublich wütend sind, wie wir. Die wütend sind auf den Zustand dieser Welt. Lasst uns kreativ werden, organisieren wir Workshops, Filmevents, Theater oder Vorträge zu Austerität, Repression, Militarismus, Genozid, Zionismus, Klimakrise oder Imperialismus und vieles mehr, um der westlichen Propagandamaschinerie die Stirn zu bieten. Denn entgegen der Aussagen von Alec von Graffenried, sind wir weder ein Sauhaufen noch herrscht in Gaza Frieden! Lassen wir die Fassade der heilen und ach so gutmütigen Schweiz weiter bröckeln.


🇵🇸Lasst uns kreativ, bunt, laut und kämpferisch sein.

title: Elecciones Brasil 2026, una batalla contra el imperialismo
content:
Las amplias elecciones que el próximo 4 de octubre tendrán lugar en Brasil, en las que se elegirán presidente, gobernadores y legisladores, son de importancia estratégica para nuestra Abya Yala y para todo el globo terráqueo. Brasil es el 5to país más extenso, está entre las 10 economías más grandes y demográficamente ocupa el séptimo lugar en el mundo.


Por otra parte, el Brasil de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, del Partido de los Trabajadores (PT), forma parte de los BRICS, quienes vienen abogando por un orden mundial más justo y equilibrado; su principal socio comercial es China, con una tendencia al crecimiento en su intercambio comercial; ha hecho fuertes críticas al ente sionista que, con la ayuda de los EE. UU., está ejecutando un genocidio contra el pueblo palestino. Todo lo anterior lo convierte en el principal objetivo del presidente Trump en el hemisferio. Ya le ha impuesto a las importaciones de EE. UU. desde Brasil, entre el 12.5 % y el 50 % de aranceles, lo que ha hecho descender las exportaciones brasileñas hacia los EE. UU. a sus niveles más bajos desde 1997, lo que ha afectado negativamente su economía, expresado esto, en el bajo crecimiento de su PIB durante 2026.


Trump y su secretario de Estado, Marco Rubio, se han estado pronunciando a favor de la candidatura de Flavio Bolsonaro y criticado ferozmente el juicio que se le siguió a Jair Bolsonaro, por el intento del golpe de Estado, llegando al extremo de tomar medidas coercitivas unilaterales contra el juez que llevó la causa.


La intromisión de los EE. UU. en los asuntos internos de otros países es bien conocida. En Nuestra América han derrocado decenas de gobiernos e instalado dictaduras militares, han desestabilizado gobiernos legítimos, han bloqueado e impuesto medidas ilegales e inhumanas contra pueblos enteros y han llegado a violar la soberanía de varios países con agresiones militares directas: México, Cuba, Haití, Nicaragua, República Dominicana, Panamá, Granada y Venezuela son ejemplo de ello. Han manipulado elecciones abiertamente, teniendo los últimos 18 meses los ejemplos de Honduras, Ecuador, Colombia y Perú, donde, de manera grotesca y descarada, han impulsado candidatos, amenazado a la población con bloquear el envío de remesas, amedrentado a los gobiernos y empresarios con elevar aranceles y han utilizado sus mecanismos de manipulación y desinformación contra amplios sectores de la población, utilizando técnicas como la Big Data, los algoritmos de las redes sociales y buscadores y la última tendencia que es el uso de la inteligencia artificial como una más de estas nefastas herramientas.


La injerencia de EE. UU. en los asuntos internos de decenas de países, ha quedado registrado en diversos libros, como los de William Blum (2005) y (2006), Guenther Roppel (2005) y Luis Suárez Salazar (2006) entre otros. En el caso brasileño ya en 1960 los militares, por presión de la embajada yanqui, exigieron y lograron la salida del presidente Quadros, quien pocos meses antes de ser destituido había otorgado la máxima condecoración, para autoridades extranjeras, al Che Guevara. En 1964 le darían un golpe de Estado al presidente Joao Goulart, poco después de anunciar la expropiación y redistribución de tierras privadas y la nacionalización de refinerías de petróleo y lograrían la destitución de la presidente Dilma Rousseffa del PT, a través de un impeachment, en 2016.


Por otra parte, el candidato con mayores posibilidades de disputar la presidencia a Lula, es el actual senador del Partido Liberal (PL), Flávio Bolsonaro. Como digno hijo de su padre, el ex presidente Jair Bolsonaro, viajó a Washington a reunirse con el secretario de Estado, para planear la campaña en contra de Lula, lo que resultó en la aplicación de aranceles del 50 % a importantes productos provenientes de Brasil, pretendiendo afectar a todo el pueblo de Brasil, con la intención de robarle apoyo al gobierno de Lula. Pocos días después de esta visita, llegó Rubio a declarar que, “Brasil no es amigo de Estados Unidos”, lo cual fue dirigido a genera malestar y angustia en las clases medias y altas del país.


Flavio Bolsonaro también visitó Tel Aviv, buscando el apoyo de Netanyahu y ofreció cambiar la embajada de Brasil a Jerusalem, en caso de ganar las elecciones. El apoyo sionista es muy importante, ya que tienen relaciones muy importantes con los grandes grupos económico-financieros que manejan la economía brasileña y mundial. title: Nationale Demo - Smash Imperialism - 11. Oktober
content:
Bewegung 11. Oktober


Der Imperialismus hat seine Transformation in eine neue Phase begonnen. Die Hegemonie des von den USA angeführten imperialistischen Blocks läutet ihr eigenes Ende ein. Dies zeigt sich – um nur einige Beispiele zu nennen – in eskalierenden Angriffskriegen (Iran), Genoziden (Palästina, Sudan) und Ressourcenkriegen (Kongo). Ebenso werden im Stellvertreterkrieg zwischen der NATO und Russland in der Ukraine abertausende Leben von oftmals zwangsrekrutierten Arbeiter:innen für europäische und US-Interessen geopfert. Andernorts bestrebt das US-Imperium – wie sich in Kuba und Venezuela in äusserster Brutalität zeigt – verstärkt den absoluten Machtanspruch auf Lateinamerika, in US-Perspektive als eigene Einflusszone angesehen, auch "backyard" genannt.


Aus Angst unterzugehen, schlägt die Bestie wild um sich. Die materielle Übermacht schwindet immer mehr und der Hauptkonkurrent China – und damit auch viele Verbündete der Volksrepublik – gewinnt an globalem Einfluss. Die Kapitalist:innen schüren Krise um Krise: Sei es der unmittelbar bevorstehende Klimakollaps, die Faschisierung der westlichen Staaten, die zunehmende Überwachung durch KI und die aggressive Umverteilung von unten nach oben.


Die Lügen der herrschenden Klasse werden immer offensichtlicher. Sie versuchen uns für dumm zu verkaufen, indem sie uns erzählen, in Gaza gäbe es einen Waffenstillstand. Indem sie legitimen und notwendigen Widerstand als "Terrorismus" deklarieren. Indem sie Palästina als "Israel" bezeichnen. Damit versuchen sie den Status Quo aufrechtzuerhalten: Eine weisse Vorherrschaft, die es ihnen erlaubt, ungebremst Kapital anzuhäufen und ihr Territorium gewaltsam zu erweitern.


Im Kongo fördern multinationale Konzerne im Dienste westlicher Mächte seit über 30 Jahren Genozid, um das Land im Chaos versinken zu lassen. Durch aktive Destabilisierung lassen sich die Ressourcen leichter abbauen und das Land ausbeuten. Dasselbe geschieht im Sudan, wo ein sogenannter "Bürgerkrieg" befeuert wird, um die zahlreichen Bodenschätze auszubeuten.


Dies sind nur einige wenige Beispiele von zu vielen, die aufzeigen, dass Millionen von Menschenleben (vor allem Schwarzes und Braunes Leben) den Herrschenden scheissegal sind. Was zählt, sind kurzfristige Gewinne. Alles auf Kosten von Mensch und Natur.


Das US-Imperium agiert dabei mit einer militärischen Gewalt und einer Grösse, die alle bisherigen Ausmasse übersteigt. Weiter ist das US-Militär der mit Abstand grösste Einzelverbraucher fossiler Brennstoffe und damit der grösste Umweltverschmutzer der Welt.


Unsere individuellen Initiativen, die Umwelt zu schützen und zu respektieren, verenden im Angesicht der wütenden Bestie in völliger Bedeutungslosigkeit. Doch der Fokus auf individuelles Konsumverhalten offenbart einen tieferliegenden Mechanismus: Nachhaltiges Verhalten wird zum Massstab erhoben und wer davon abweicht, wird verurteilt. Die Logik dahinter: "Divide and rule"


So wird unser Fokus und unsere Energie auf die gegenseitige Kontrolle gelegt, anstatt die Tausenden von Bomben zu stoppen, die Mensch und Natur komplett zerstören. Symptombekämpfung wird als Lösung hochstilisiert; wertvolle Zeit, die wir im Kampf für Klimagerechtigkeit brauchen könnten, geht verloren.


Wir müssen endlich verstehen: Der Kampf gegen die globale Kriegsmaschinerie und der Kampf für Klimagerechtigkeit ist ein und derselbe Kampf!


Die bürgerliche Demokratie möchte uns klarmachen, dass wir mittels Abstimmungen etwas verändern können und verkauft uns, dass wir mit unserem individuellen Konsumverhalten die Natur "retten können". Demokratie gibt uns zu verstehen: "Alle Menschen sind gleich". Doch wenn wir genauer hinschauen, verstehen wir die bürgerliche Demokratie als Teil des Problems. Denn auch sie ist nur ein Mittel, das Volk zu unterdrücken und eines freien Lebens zu berauben und somit die Kapitalinteressen der herschenden Klasse zu befriedigen. Unter dem Vorwand der "Demokratsierung" (eigentlich "Zivilisierung") werden seit jeher Länder angegriffen, Überausbeutung legitimiert und Proteste gewaltsam niedergeschlagen. Die Aussengrenzen werden aufgerüstet, Menschen illegalisiert. Militarisierung und Aufrüstung wird auf Kosten der Gesundheit und Bildung vorangetrieben. Faschistoides Gedankengut schiesst wie Pilze aus dem Boden und zeigt sich in Form von Parteien, in Gesetzesvorlagen, in medialer Hetze, oder dem Antifa-Verbot. Der Diskurs wird mithilfe von liberalen Parteien schrittweise gegen rechts verschoben …

title: Çeşme Belediye Başkan Yardımcısı 16 aydır tutukluydu: Tahliye edildiği gün yine gözaltına alındı
content:
İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediyesine (İBB) yönelik yürütülen soruşturma kapsamında yaklaşık 16 aydır Silivri Cezaevi’nde iddianamesiz tutuklu bulunan Çeşme Belediye Başkan Yardımcısı Onur Gülin, hakim karşısına çıktığı ilk duruşmada tahliye edildi. Ancak Gülin, aynı gün Çeşme Belediyesine düzenlenen eş zamanlı operasyonda hakkında verilen yeni gözaltı kararı nedeniyle özgürlüğüne kavuşamadan İzmir İl Jandarma Komutanlığı’na sevk edilecek.

Onur Gülin, 20 Mayıs 2025 tarihinde eşi Yelda Gülin’in ameliyatı için bulunduğu hastaneden gözaltına alınarak tutuklanmıştı. Kasım 2025’te hazırlanan yaklaşık 4 bin sayfalık ana İBB iddianamesinde yer almayan Gülin, süreç içerisinde kısa süreli bir tahliye kararı alsa da savcılığın itirazı üzerine Silivri Cezaevi’nde kalmaya devam etti. İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı’nın ana dosyadan ayırarak 21 Temmuz 2026’da hazırladığı ek iddianamede, Gülin ve beraberindeki sanıklara İBB Basın Yayın ve Halkla İlişkiler Daire Başkanlığı ihalelerine ilişkin "ihaleye fesat karıştırma", "rüşvet" ve "kamu zararından dolandırıcılık" suçlamaları yöneltildi.

İstanbul 7. Ağır Ceza Mahkesi’nde dün görülen davanın ilk duruşmasında mahkeme heyeti, aralarında Onur Gülin’in de bulunduğu 5 sanığın tahliyesine karar verirken bir sanığın tutukluluğunun devamına hükmetti.

İzmir Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanı Cemil Tugay'ın AKP'ye geçtiği günün sabahında dün Çeşme Belediyesine yönelik 12 kişi hakkında "suç örgütü kurma", "rüşvet", "irtikap" ve "resmi belgede sahtecilik" suçlamalarıyla başlatılan soruşturmanın ihbarla başladığı öğrenildi.

Onur Gülin'in yarım kalan tahliye sevinci ise ilk değil. 4 Aralık’taki aylık tutukluluk incelemesinde aralarında Ekrem İmamoğlu’nun şoförlerinin de bulunduğu 21 kişilik gruptan Gülin dahil 19 kişi hakkında tahliye kararı verildi.

İzmir’den gelen ailesi ve iki küçük kızıyla cezaevi kapısında buluşmayı bekleyen Gülin, savcılığın jet hızıyla yaptığı itiraz üzerine cezaevinden çıkamadan, gece yarısı jandarma karakoluna götürülerek 9 saat içinde yeniden tutuklandı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Steven Methven
title: How Labour Put Big Property Above Camden’s Local Residents
content:
A little more than a week before Thursday’s crucial byelection in the London constituency of Holborn and St Pancras, prime minister Andy Burnham laid out

a radical social and economic programme

 at Labour’s party conference in Liverpool. If the ideas were big, the shift in Labour’s direction was even bigger. Words not heard in years peppered the speech:

the working class

,

public control

, and apologies for political failures. Beginning with a curt acknowledgement that former prime minister Keir Starmer won a general election he could hardly lose, Burnham spent the rest of his speech slamming the door on Starmerism. 


Not in Holborn and St Pancras, though, Starmer’s old parliamentary seat.


Labour’s candidate in the byelection, Sagal Abdi-Wali, has been

a fixture of Camden council

 (the London borough in which the constituency falls) since the 2022 local elections. She quickly rose to prominence, appointed cabinet member for the council’s Better Homes programme in 2024, before being voted council leader in May this year.


But sources close to Camden council have described it as a stronghold of the Labour right. Characterised by purges of dissenters, cosiness to corporate interests and a lack of vision, the Labour group running the council, Novara Media was told, is ground-zero for Starmerism. 


That empty philosophy is epitomised in the council’s approach to housing, a topic – especially in the form of social housing –

at the heart of Burnham’s national plans

. While the new prime minister has promised a generational transformation in building council home capacity, Camden council has repeatedly sided with wealthy corporate developers when they’ve requested massive cuts to promised affordable and social housing allotments in new developments. Described as a “weak touch” by one source, another was more blunt: “They are fucking aroused by private developers.”


One example is the redevelopment of the O2 centre on north-west London’s Finchley Road. The three-phase plans, drawn up by Landsec, Britain’s largest commercial property developer, were originally approved by the council in 2023. Involving the demolition of an existing shopping centre, cinema and leisure centre, Landsec promised that 570 of the 1,796 new flats would be a mix of social and affordable housing. At a meeting last month, Camden council

approved an enormous reduction

: now, just 330 flats will meet those criteria, a drop from 32% to 18%. In the first phase of the construction, the slash has been even deeper, with

barely 15%

 of the total being classed as affordable. (A council spokesperson told Novara Media that the permission granted includes 20% affordable housing across the whole site, and that the development also supports the delivery of other community benefits, including funding for step-free access at West Hampstead Station.)


If the prime minister is to be believed, neoliberalism is on its way out of Burnham’s Britain. But in Camden, it appears in rosy health.


In the O2 centre case, Landsec took advantage of a Starmerite innovation. In October last year, then-housing secretary and

self-proclaimed Starmer-loyalist

 Steve Reed (since returned to the backbenches) announced a two-year window in which developers who promised a 20%, rather than the previous 35%, affordable housing quota

would have their plans fast-tracked

. This didn’t require Camden to accept Landsec’s changes. But the council rolled over anyway. 


The council’s approach to private development has also raised questions over future social housing. Approved in January, the Camley Street development near King’s Cross currently promises 401 new homes of which

almost half will be for social rents

. History suggests this too may be revised downwards before the first completions – and several longstanding businesses have already been

forced out, they say without council support

 (the council

denied this

). In the constituency’s northern-most area, the Labour stronghold of Kentish Town,

residents were perturbed

 by the permission granted for the construction of a £1bn Film Quarter. Promising 11 purpose-built sound stages, production suites and workspaces, developer Yoo Capital has also committed to

243 affordable homes

 – 50% of the sites’ planned 485 flats. Asked in a recent profile whether the developer could be trusted not to slash those figures, Abdi-Wali refused to consider that highly-plausible possibility. “I don’t want to talk like that,”

title: Das Projet-Evasions braucht Cash Money
content:
Das Projet-Evasions ist ein mehrsprachiges Netzwerk anarchistischer Freundschaften, das seit 2019 besteht. Nach sieben fröhlichen Jahren, in denen wir unsere kleinen Aktivitäten* durchgeführt haben, ist es nun an der Zeit, euch um Unterstützung zu bitten.


Mit „kleinen Aktivitäten“ meinen wir: Dinge zu tun, in denen wir Sinn, emanzipatorisches und revolutionäres Potenzial sowie anarchistische Perspektiven sehen. Mit „Dingen“ meinen wir die Erstellung zahlreicher Inhalte (Bücher, Broschüren, Artikel, Podcasts, Audio-Clips, Aufkleber, Zeitschriften, Postkarten, Spiele, Ausstellungen, Plakate), die Durchführung von

Workshops und Präsentationen,

 das erschaffen von tools gegen die Repression, sowie umfangreiche Verbreitungsarbeit. All das in vielen verschiedenen Sprachen, denn – haben wir es schon gesagt ? – sind wir ein mehrsprachiges Projekt, das sich über mehrere Sprachräume erstreckt.


Wir erstellen Inhalte, weil wir diese teilen wollen, sowie Werkzeuge, die andere Menschen nutzen können. Meistens erstellen wir unsere Inhalte selbst, manchmal arbeiten wir aber auch mit externen Personen zusammen. Wir geben alle gedruckten Versionen zum frei wählbaren Preis heraus; jede Person kann frei entscheiden, je nach ihren eigenen Möglichkeiten, was sie dafür geben kann und will. Parallel dazu sind alle

digitalen Versionen

 unserer Produktionen kostenlos auf unserer Website verfügbar.


Das Geld, das wir haben, wird größtenteils für die Druckkosten verwendet. Auch wenn wir hauptsächlich mit einer befreundeten Druckerei zusammenarbeiten, die uns unglaublich unterstützt, bleiben die Druckkosten unser größter Ausgabenposten. An zweiter Stelle stehen die Versandkosten, die jedes Jahr steigen. Bei Sendungen ins Ausland sind die Porto- und Zollgebühren oft höher als die Druckkosten der Publikation, die wir verschicken. Daneben kaufen wir auch regelmäßig Bücher und andere selbstveröffentlichte Publikationen, die wir zum freien Preis weitergeben, und in den besten Zeiten unserer Finanzlage konnten wir mehrmals inhaftierte Anarchist*innen und Projekte, die auf der Suche nach Geld waren, unterstützen sowie in seltenen Fällen einen Teil unserer Reisekosten und unserer Arbeitzeit finanzieren. An letzter Stelle unserer Ausgaben stehen die Kosten für unsere Website und ein paar logistische Kleinigkeiten.


Zum Zeitpunkt der Abfassung dieses Textes beläuft sich unser Kontostand auf genau 741 Schweizer Franken und 123 Euro, und wenn wir ihn wieder auffüllen möchten, dann deshalb, weil wir mehrere Projekte haben, die bald bereit sein werden, in den Druck zu gehen. Um eine Idee zu geben : Der Druck der 1'000 Exemplare von „

Illégale élégance

“ kostete uns 3'000.–, also 3.– pro Exemplar, und der Druck der 4'000

Bücher über die Verhöre

 kostete uns 16'000.–, also 4.– pro Buch.


Deshalb haben wir beschlossen, im Oktober eine kleine Spendenaktion zu starten. Und die beginnt mit diesem Newsletter. Ihr könnt uns eure kleinen oder großen Spenden mit dem Vermerk „EVASIONS“ hier zukommen lassen

author: ACG
title: When history accelerates: Maricarmen’s eviction
content:
We publish below the statement from the Spanish group Liza on the Maricarmen mobilisation and the need for revolutionary organisation.


Context: On Saturday, September 26, thousands of people marched through the streets of Madrid to protest the eviction of 87-year-old disabled  Maricarmen Abascal from her home. Her door was broken down by local riot police, and she was evicted on a stretcher despite the resistance of a cordon of protesters. Maricarmen, who had lived in her apartment for 70 years, instantly became a symbol of the housing crisis plaguing Spain, particularly in major cities. Whose fault is it? Rampant gentrification, in which real estate developers systematically buy up buildings in city centres, taking the opportunity to “revise” rents. Maricarmen’s rent, which was around 500 euros per month, was increased by 275% to 2,750 euros! Anger swept across Spain, withtens of thousands mobilised and fifty demonstrations,, particularly in Madrid, where the demonstrations, claimed as involving as high as 500,000, culminated in an impromptu encampment at Puerta del Sol, reminiscent of the 2011 protests that sparked the Indignados movement. This time, a few nights of occupation were enough for the real estate company that had evicted Maricarmen to reverse its decision, release her from the hospital, and reinstate her in her apartment, cancelling the rent increase it had planned to impose. While applauding this outcome, the Puerta del Sol “campers” are maintaining the pressure, as numerous other evictions are taking place daily across Spain. They are demanding that the “socialist” government enact a new, more protective law to curb rising purchase and rental prices.

Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez promised once more to introduce a new bill to regulate rent levels.  However, this was blocked by the conservative People’s Party (PP) and far-right Vox and the centre-right, pro-independence Together for Catalonia (JxCat). Sánchez has now called a snap election.


On the political climate and the need for revolutionary organisation


“Revolutions have their own rhythm, punctuated by accelerations and decelerations. They also have their own geometry, in which the straight line breaks at the bifurcations and sharp turns of history.” Daniel Bensaid,

Politics as a Strategic Art


There is a fundamental difference between chronological time and political time. The former unfolds in a seemingly uniform manner: days follow days, and development is linear. The latter, however, under the dialectical logic of a contradictory reality, is very different: There are historical periods in which months or even years seem to contain very few substantial transformations, while there are moments in which, in a matter of days, political reality can be radically transformed.


This means that political time cannot be understood simply as the succession of events on the calendar. It is, above all, the pace at which the relationships between social forces, institutions, organisations, and the possibilities for political action change. There are specific events that, based on the accumulation of internal contradictions, appear as turning points, making possible, in qualitative terms, what until recently was unthinkable.


A society can remain seemingly stable for years and yet be accumulating contradictions. These contradictions don’t necessarily manifest themselves immediately. They can remain separate, partially invisible, or even appear unconnected. An economic crisis, a labour dispute, a housing crisis, a particular police action, a popular mobilisation, or an institutional crisis may seem, individually, like isolated phenomena. However, they can establish connections between them: each event modifies the conditions under which the next ones occur, and each new conflict can amplify, accelerate, or transform the previous ones. It is at this point that the acceleration of political time appears, the concrete expression of latent contradictions.


It is not that an isolated event creates a revolutionary situation out of thin air. Rather, it happens that a prior accumulation of contradictions finds certain events capable of condensing them and making them politically visible. The event then acts as a catalyst for processes that were already developing in society.


“Men make their own history, but they do not make it as they please; they do not make it under self-chosen circumstances, but under circumstances directly encountered, given and …

author: Judy Mundey
title: Judy Mundey: ‘Public housing needed as housing crisis deepens’
content:
This is a slightly abridged version of a speech by Judy Mundey, housing campaigner and women's rights activist, to a meeting focused on NSW Labor’s development plan in the Bays West precinct, organised by Better Futures Coalition on September 29.

The Sydney Morning Herald, in May, referred to twin babies born to a mother who lived and gave birth to them in a tent on the banks of the Murrumbidgee River at Wagga Wagga in NSW. One died; the other had to be hospitalised.

A local councillor said the tragedy was a predictable result of systemic failures to address homelessness. He put the problem down to a lack of public housing.

The SMH editorial referred to the surge in people living in cars, tents and caravan parks, describing it as having echoes of the Depression era.

In Sydney, people are sleeping in the St James railway station tunnel, parks and other forms of less than salubrious accommodation.

Then there is the scourge of domestic violence and the desperate need for safe housing for the victim-survivors. For many women it is a choice between living with domestic violence or homelessness. The refuge system is unable to cope and thousands are on the waiting list for public housing.

Renting in the private property market also presents problems.

A recent estimate said that, nationwide, more than 1.25 million low-income households are in financial stress. Even where people can find rental accommodation, it is often less than stable.

A new report from Adelaide University said children who grow up in rental housing move every 2.3 years, on average, and that by the age of 14 a child in private rental had moved an average of six times, with some as often as 10 times.

Such frequent moves can incur or inflict other disadvantages, such as changing schools and the loss of friendship, sporting and social relationships.

We are not only in the midst of a housing crisis, we are experiencing a systemic failure to address it.

There is no shortage of promises meant to rectify the problem. Recently, NSW Labor announced some 9,400 homes would be built in the Woolahra/Edgecliff area, with towers of 32 and 34 stories. Almost all such proposals involve the private sector and that has not always gone well.

People will recall the examples of developer-built projects with serious defects, such as Opal Towers in 2018 and Mascot Towers in 2019, with some homes remaining uninhabitable.

Peoples’ lives have been ruined. They save and borrow, only to find they cannot not live in their new home but there is no financial recovery. At that time, developers were able to employ private certifiers.

The explosion of defect-riddled apartment project failures with their multi-million dollar repair bills prompted the NSW government to appoint NSW’s first Building Commissioner in 2019.

But then came the collapse of Dyldam disaster in 2020, one of NSW’s biggest apartment builders, with debts of half a billion dollars. The NSW building regulator identified serious defects in a 230 apartment development in Baulkham Hills, including defects so serious as to be labelled a threat to human life. That development is still undergoing repair work.

There are almost daily reports about the impact of these dodgy developers.

The latest dodgy developer in the spotlight is Bathla. It has collapsed, owing debts of $3.3 billion. Many buyers have been left in the lurch, losing large sums paid as deposits.

Bathla’s work was not only riddled with defects, it also engaged in unsafe work practices. It was fined $135,000 in 2018 over a serious injury on a project at Doonside and was slapped with more than 300 notices by Safe Work NSW relating to safety issues.

Thousands of partially-built properties have been left unfinished.

These collapses has inevitably had a devastating effect on those further down the supply chain — suppliers, sub contractors and employees are owed, as are those who paid deposits.

Bathla’s collapse is also a disaster for the national housing supply, as there are 14,000 apartments stalled.

The NSW target for new housing is already running well behind target.

The Chris Minns Labor government pledged to build 378,000 homes by mid 2029. This requires 22,000 homes to be delivered each year until mid 2029. There appears to be a massive disparity between the government’s promises and its actual delivery.

Notwithstanding these dodgy developer disasters, Labor seems wedded to private development.

But there is an alternative — public housing …

title: City Of Blood [Part l]
content:
Mein Gespräch, meine Lieder


Mein Hass und mein Glück


Mein Tag, meine Nacht, mein Vor, mein Zurück


Meine Sonne und Schatten, Zweifel, die ich hab


An dir und in mir bis zum letzten Tag


Deine Straßen, wo ich fliehe, stolper und fall


Deine Wärme, die ich brauch, die ich spüre überall


Klaus Hoffmann – Berlin


„Das Gedächtnis der Menschheit für erduldete Leiden ist erstaunlich kurz. Ihre Vorstellungskraft für kommende Leiden ist fast noch geringer.“


Bertolt Brecht


2004 verkaufte der Berliner Senat in einer SPD-PDS Regierung 65.000 Wohnungen der städtischen Wohnungsgesellschaft GSW zum Schnäppchenpreis von 400 Mio Euro an private Spekulanten, der Wohnungsbestand ging 2011 schließlich an die Deutsche Wohnen über, die mittlerweile in einer Fusion mit Vonovia zum größten börsenorientierte Wohnungsunternehmen in Deutschland wurde. 2019 werden 6000 Wohnungen, also rund 10 Prozent der 2004 verkauften Wohnungen, für 920 Mio Euro vom ‘rot-rot-grünen’ Senat unter Federführung der PdL Stadtentwicklungssenatorin zurückgekauft. 2021 werden dann für knapp 2,5 Milliarden Euro an die 15.000 weitere Wohnungen mit Schwerpunkt Kreuzberg von Deutsche Wohnen/Vonovia zurückgekauft. Seitdem dürfen sich die Mieter in den Hochhäusern rund um das Kottbusser Tor über steigende Mieten und explodierende Nebenkosten freuen, die alles weit in den Schatten stellen, was die Profitmaximierungsexperten der Deutsche Wohnen zu verantworten hatten.


Sämtliche im Zuge der Kahlschlagsanierung Ende der 70er entstandenen ‘Neubausiedlungen’ rund um das Kottbusser Tor weisen einen extremen Sanierungsstau auf, ständig fallen wichtige Infrastruktur wie Fahrstühle aus, behinderte Mieter, die auf Rollstühle angewiesen sind, sitzen teilweise monatelang in ihren Wohnungen fest. Wie sich die städtische Wohnungsbaugesellschaft HOWOGE, die jetzt auch in Kreuzberg besitzt, eine “Mieterfreudliche Sanierung” vorstellt, exekutierte sie jüngst in Reinickendorf, wo 170 Mieter mit einer Vorlauffrist von nur 6 Monaten darüber informiert wurden, dass ihre Wohnanlage komplett saniert werde und sie Umsetzwohnungen verteilt über das gesamte Stadtgebiet erhalten sollen, was gegen jede Rechtsprechung auf eine ‘Wohnortnahe Umsetzung’ verstößt.


Während börsenorientierte Unternehmen wie die ‘Deutsche Wohnen’ aufgrund von medialen Meltdowns gezwungen waren, besonders skandalöse Zustände in ihren Wohnungsanlagen abzustellen, glänzt die HOWOGE seit Jahren mit der weitgehenden Verweigerung der direkten Kommunikation mit ihren Mietern und dem Aussitzen von Problemen. Bezeichnenderweise wechselte der operative Leiter des Vorstandes der HOWOGE im Frühjahr dieses Jahres zu genau dem technischen Dienstleister, der in den letzten Jahren zahlreiche Aufträge der diversen ausgegliederten HOWOGE-Tochtergesellschaften erhalten hatte. Eigentlich können die betroffenen Berliner Mieter im Nachhinein wahrscheinlich froh darüber sein, dass sich der “Sieg” des ‚Volksentscheids Deutsche Wohnen und Co enteignen’ bisher im typischen Berliner Wohnungssumpf verloren hat. Denn nun kommt ja der “Vergesellschaftungshammer” der PdL.


Verkauf dich nicht


Berlin


Jung bist du nicht


Du alterst so schnell


Buckelst zu sehr


Trägst an den Geldern der Freier so schwer


Die werden gehn


Dich sterben sehn


Berlin


Geliebte Berlin


Klaus Hoffmann


“Ein Drittel Heizöl, zwei Drittel Benzin” sangen Slime einst, in Berlin bauen die Punks jetzt Molotows mit Urin und rufen dann dazu auf, nicht zu einer laufenden Räumung zu kommen, weil das den Standort der ‘angemeldeten Mahnwache’ gefährden würde. Der ‘Wohnungskampf’ in der geschichtsträchtigen Hausbesetzer-Hochburg Berlin ist auf den Hund gekommen, während der TikTok Wahlerfolg PdL auf dem harten Boden der staatstragenden Realität aufgeschlagen ist. Erste Bauern werden geopfert, die Nahost Frage wird erneut in Neukölln entschieden und zur der Demo von DGB und anderen Verbänden gegen den Generalangriff von BlackRock Merz auf die Überreste der “sozialen Marktwirtschaft” kommen gerade mal ein paar tausend Leute, darunter die wichtigsten Repräsentanten der aus dem geschichtlichen Mausoleum auferstandenen K-Gruppen. Während draußen alles in Kleinstaaten zerfällt, die Mauern hochgezogen werden und der Klimawandel und Pandemien ihr Werk verrichten, macht Berlin weiter auf weltoffen. title: On Saturday, as tens of thousands of people took to the streets of Madrid to protest against the…
content:
On Saturday, as tens of thousands of people took to the streets of Madrid to protest against the country’s deepening housing crisis, the retired schoolteacher was among a small group who had sought to take the protest one step further. “At first we were 10 tents,” she said, gesturing to the sprawling encampment set up in the central Puerta del Sol plaza behind her. “Now, we’re more than 300 tents, and it keeps growing.” Days earlier, many across Spain had watched in shock as news channels showed Maricarmen Abascal, an 87-year-old woman with a disability, being evicted from the home where she had lived for seven decades. The shock soon gave way to anger as the octogenarian was shown being brought out of her home on a stretcher, flanked by protesters on one side and police officers on the other.

Maricarmen, 87, waits at home for police to arrive before being evicted from the home where she lived in Madrid, Spain, Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026. (Fernando Sánchez/Europa Press via AP)

Housing campaigners seized on the moment. “The whole country has seen that housing speculation has no mercy on anyone,” said Alicia del Río of the Madrid Tenants’ Union. “We’re not sad, we’re angry. And we’re not going to stop until we change things.” Abascal’s lawyers reportedly reached a deal for her to return home on Monday evening. “If this agreement we have reached is signed, it will obviously be a better and happier outcome for everyone,” her lawyer, Beatriz Duro, told reporters, saying it could “help to change the paradigm when it comes to housing in general”. At the encampment earlier on Monday, many described the days of nationwide protests and the encampment as a turning point in a movement that had long simmered as rents rose by 80% within a decade, while the cost of homes climbed by 63%. “We need stability,” said David Iglesias, 25, as he described how the ever-soaring prices had forced people to put their lives on hold to try to keep a roof over their heads. “People who want to have children should be able to do so, even if they are renting. People who dream of becoming musicians or barbers should have the chance to do so and not have to worry that they need to work, work, work to pay for housing,” he said. “It’s an endless loop that is undermining the mental health of young people.” As he spoke, a large banner flapped nearby, reading: “You can speculate on watches, jewels, cryptobros and Ferraris. But not on our fucking homes.” […] It was a nod to the informal camp slogan, launched by housing campaigners and oft-repeated by protesters in recent days: “Either the rentier economy falls, or the government does.”

[Video]: “Hundreds of protesters across Spain took part in pot banging demonstrations to demand political action over soaring rents, evictions and the shortage of affordable housing. The protests come ahead of a parliamentary vote on Friday on measures to strengthen tenant protections.”

author: Cormac Mills Ritchard
title: Demolishing the idea of public housing
content:
The United Nations’ special rapporteur on adequate housing, Koldo Casla, usually deals with slum demolitions in third-world countries. Last month, he took aim at the Victorian Labor government, claiming its demolition of Melbourne’s 44 public housing towers and the “forced evictions and mass displacement of approximately 10,000 residents” could be a violation of their

human rights

. This follows a Victorian parliamentary inquiry in December, which called for an

immediate pause

 to the demolitions, and a class action against the demolitions filed by Inner Melbourne Community Legal (IMCL), which has been granted special leave to

appeal

 to the High Court on 7 October.

Despite growing challenges, Premier Ben Carroll is ploughing ahead with the demolition of Melbourne’s public housing towers. Of course, Labor doesn’t characterise what it’s doing as “eviction” and “demolition”, but “renewal” and “redevelopment”, which it claims will increase the number of residents on the estates from 10,000 to 30,000, and replace towers that have “reached the end of their useful life”. There is no truth to this.

If Labor’s multi-billion-dollar project is aimed at addressing the waiting list for social housing, it’s missing a couple of zeros. Only 11,000 of the new residents will be in social housing, an increase of just 1,000. As of June this year, there were 58,021 people on the Victorian Housing Register’s

growing waiting list

, of which 33,253 have been assessed as “priority”—mostly those who are currently homeless or experiencing family violence. The redevelopments will mean that just 1,000 more people will have places in social housing ... by 2051.

The redevelopment won’t help others affected by the housing crisis, either. The other 19,000 residents of the new mixed-tenure developments will live in a combination of build-to-rent, a model that the

 Age

 has found to be between 20 and 70 percent

more expensive

 than the market rate, and “affordable housing”, which is not that affordable and does not provide long-term security, as exposed by a recent

Four Corners


investigation

. 

The North Richmond public housing precinct is a telling example. In September, the state government briefed the City of Yarra on its plans for the tower at 139 Highett Street. The

Age

 reported last month that the tower, which currently has 220 public housing units, will be replaced with a development that has

only 150 social housing units

 and 650 build-to-rent units.

Simon is a former resident who grew up in the North Richmond precinct after his parents emigrated from Vietnam. After the latest announcement about the precinct, he attended a community meeting of public housing tenants who demand the towers be refurbished rather than demolished. He told

Red Flag

 that his parents, a labourer and kindergarten worker, were both poorly paid. Living in the public housing tower allowed them to escape the anarchy of the private rental market. “We knew what the rent was next week and didn’t have to worry about eviction or not being able to afford food. I could attend school and university without many issues. That security meant you could plan your life”, he said.

“Social housing” is an umbrella term that covers both public housing, run by the government, and community housing, run by not-for-profits. When Labor talks about social housing, it usually means community housing—so its claim to be replacing 10,000 public housing places with 11,000 social ones actually represents a huge cut in public housing.

Public housing rent is capped at 25 percent of a household’s income or the market rate, whichever is lower, while community housing providers can charge up to 30 percent. However, community housing organisations (CHOs) are entitled to 100 percent of any tenant’s Commonwealth Rent Assistance and can charge extra fees on top. In its

submission to the inquiry

, IMCL notes that some of its clients pay up to 50 percent of their income to a CHO through “rent, utilities, lift fees, concierge and management fees”. Community housing residents also have fewer rights than public housing residents; West Heidelberg Community Legal found that “long-term community housing tenants were 3 to 5 times more likely to face eviction than public housing tenants”.

Worse still, unlike the government, CHOs don’t have to allocate places based on need, which means that the more the social housing waiting list is serviced by community rather than public housing …

author: Shireen Akram-Boshar
title: Thousands of Cornell Students Protest for Accountability in Rape Case
content:
In a 2025 survey, 35 percent of undergraduate women reported experiencing sexual assault during their time at Cornell.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

On Monday evening, thousands of Cornell University students protested on the university campus, demanding accountability for Cornell’s alleged mishandling of the 2024 rape case that has come under a national spotlight.

Students held signs that said “We are Jane Doe,” “Stop Protecting Rapists,” and “We Want Sentences, Not Essays.”

The demonstration was organized by Students for a Democratic Cornell alongside over 20 other student organizations at Cornell, including Gender Justice Advocacy Coalition, Planned Parenthood Generation, Cornell Grad Students United, Black Students United, and other cultural organizations on campus.

Outrage has followed the case of a sexual assault that occurred in October 2024 at Cornell’s Chi Phi fraternity house, where a victim, known as Jane Doe, says that she was drugged and raped by seven fraternity members. This anger has boiled over after Jane Doe filed a civil lawsuit in mid-September, pushing the local district attorney to reopen the case.

On campus, students have highlighted the university’s failure to hold the alleged perpetrators accountable, citing the university’s decision to allow some to write essays as punishment and the university police providing the district attorney with a “summary” of Jane Doe’s complaint that omitted mentions of rape, drugging, and sexual assault, leading to the DA closing the initial case.

Students for a Democratic Cornell (SDC), which called the protest, put forward demands that include an independent judicial system to replace Cornell’s current internal judicial system; an external investigation of Cornell’s administration; mandatory sexual assault prevention trainings for students; and Cornell’s compliance with New York State’s Enough is Enough law.

They have also called for the university to expel the men accused in the Jane Doe case and to revoke the degrees of those who have already graduated. (Only two of the seven men named by Jane Doe were expelled for the assault in 2025 after the university’s Title IX investigation.)

“SDC is really focused on attacking the institutional systems that enable sexual violence to be so prevalent on campus,” Jack Huber, an activist in Students for a Democratic Cornell, told Truthout.

“Between 2018 and 2024, there were over 1,200 reported instances of sexual violence on campus. Only seven of those cases resulted in expulsion,” he said. “So when we have a statistic like that, it is clear that the administration is not interested in seeking justice for survivors, and so we must return to an independent judicial system, one where decisions about discipline are not made behind closed doors based on what looks best for the university.”

Other on-campus organizations, like Cornell Graduate Students United (CGSU), have issued additional demands.

“In coalition with Students Not Bombs, we’ve publicly demanded the resignation of [Cornell University President] Michael Kotlikoff and other administrators implicated in the mishandling of Jane Doe’s case,” Cornell graduate student Kaori Quan told Truthout, speaking for CGSU.

CGSU has also called for “the abolition of Greek Life at Cornell, and the dissolution of the Office of Student Conduct and Community Standards.”

Calls to ban fraternities, and for the university president to resign, were echoed in the chants at Monday evening’s protest, with students chanting “All the frats have got to go” and “Kotlikoff has got to go.”

“The prevalence of sexual assault on campus is due in no small part to Greek life and the way Cornell promotes it,” Quan told Truthout.

“Many of the fraternities on campus have been around for decades — wealthy donors are members of these organizations, and that stream of cash incentivizes the university to preserve their reputation over the health and safety of students,” she added. “The protection that fraternities enjoy from administration makes it easier to get away with sexual assault.”

According to a 2025 survey, 35 percent of undergraduate women at Cornell — more than one in three — reported experiencing sexual assault during their time at the university.

Campus organizations are mobilizing to continue the fight for their demands beyond Monday’s demonstration …

author: Anonym
title: In Solidarität mit Daniel Viehmann, Strom-Saboteur
content:
DANKE DANIEL


Ein paar Wochen sind vergangen, seit Öko-Saboteur Daniel bundesweit Angriffe auf das Deutsche Stromnetz durchgeführt hat. Dafür hat er selbst gebaute Raketen über Hochspannungsleitungen geschossen, eine Methode, die er selbst erfunden hat. Bei einem der Angriffe in NRW gingen infolge 5 Kraftwerksblöcke (Braunkohle) für mehrerere Tage vom Netz. Es folgte viel Medienaufmerksamkeit und nach einer bundesweiten Fahndung, wurde Daniel festgenommen. Aktuell sitzt Daniel in U-Haft und es drohen ihm bis zu 10 Jahre Knast.


SEINE WORTE


Bis jetzt, haben wir wenig – oder gar keine – öffentliche Solidarität mit Daniel gesehen. Wir fragen uns was hinter dem Schweigen steckt. Für uns gibt es keinen Grund zur Stille oder gar zur Distanzierung. Mit diesem Text wollen wir dieses Schweigen brechen und zeigen das es viele Gründe gibt anzunehmen, dass Daniels Kampf gleichermaßen auch unser Kampf ist.


Die stärkste Begründung für unsere Solidarität steckt in Daniels eigenen Worten. Aus seinen Bekennerschreiben gelangen zuerst nur wenige Sätze an die Öffentlichkeit. Die veröffentlichte erste Seite gibt mehr Aufschluss über Daniels Motivationen. Hier veröffentlichen wir diese Seite (siehe Foto) und rufen dazu auf, wer Zugang zu den fehlenden Seiten seiner Bekennerschreiben hat: Gebt Daniels Worte an die Öffentlichkeit, so dass Daniel für sich selbst sprechen kann.


Was die Presse nicht berichtete, er aber selbst als Gründe für sein Handeln beschreibt: seine Aktionen wendeten sich nicht nur gegen eine fossile Stromerzeugung sondern auch gegen die deutsche Rüstungsindustrie und vor allem deren Teilhabe am Völkermord in Palästina.


EINE ADÄQUATE ANTWORT AUF DIE FOSSILE REALITÄT


„Stromerzeugung aus fossilen Brennstoffen ist ein Verbrechen, das unsägliches Leid nach sich zieht.“


Das ist kein komplizierter Zusammenhang, nichts was nicht lange wissenschaftlich verstanden ist. Die fossile Energieerzeugung ist einer der Hauptverursacher des globalen Klimawandels – all das ist einfach zu verstehen. Genauso einfach ist es, dass um aus dem Kreislauf des Leids aus zusteigen, der Ursprung dessen zerstört werden muss. Genauso logisch ist aus unserer Sicht Daniels Reaktion.


Er hatte also gute Gründe zu tun, was getan werden muss(te). So muss auch die Klimabewegung die Tatsache anerkennen, dass CO2 Emissionen weiterhin Jahr für Jahr signifikant steigen. Nach vielen Jahren weitreichendem bürgerlichen Protest und des zivilen Ungehorsam wird klar, es ist keine realistische Lösung für das Problem. Es ist also eine logische Konsequenz für die Klimabewegung Akte der Sabotage im Kampf einzusetzen.


DIE BEWEGUNG SCHWEIGT


Viele Menschen (auch Gefährt*innen) behaupten Daniel wäre entweder verrückt oder sicherlich einer von Putins Agenten. Auch sei es unlogisch, dass er seinen Namen und Adresse veröffentlicht hat. Jede dieser Argumentation befreit uns von der Pflicht (oder Chance) seine Aktionen ernst zu nehmen. Ist es nicht das was Daniel versuchte umzusetzen genau eine heimliche Sehnsucht die in vielen von uns steckt?


UND DER STAAT WILL KRITISCHE INFRASTRUKTUR BESSER SCHÜTZEN


In Folge Daniels Aktionen stellt Staat und Presse die sogenannte kritische Infrastruktur als stark-gefährdet dar. Es werden Zählungen Sabotage-Verdachtsfällen veröffentlicht, neben Daniel ein Datenleak in Berlin, und russische Drohnenangriffe am Leipziger Flughafen. Auch soll im Zuge des im März in Kraft getretenen KRITIS Dachgesetz vermehrt KI-Überwachung der sogenannten kritischen Infrastrukur (kritsch für wen und für was?) umgesetzt werden.


Unabhängig davon wie gefährdet die sogenannte kritische Infrastruktur wirklich ist, drückt die dargestellte mediale Brisanz rund um Daniels Aktionen auch die Wirksamkeit derer aus. Gesteigerte Überwachung und Repression zeigt Un-Sicherheit & Schwachstellen des Staates. Und so denken wir, wenn die eine Aktion nicht dem Trugschluss verfällt über Forderungen an die Regierenden Zustände verändern zu wollen muss vermehrte Repression erwartet werden. Alles andere hätte keinen ausschlaggebenden Effekt auf den Status Quo. So erschreckend die Unsicherheit für manche auch klingen mag, so sehr glauben wir dass sie nötig ist um tatsächlich die Zerstörung dieser industriellen Zivilisation zu stoppen.


WAS WÄRE ALSO WENN DANIELS AKTION ZÄHLT?


Wichtiger als die ‚Macht‘ die man tatsächlich hat, ist die Macht die unsere Gegner glauben das wir sie haben. Wenn also der deutsche Staat von Unsicherheit seiner kritischen Infrastruktur …

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: French High School Students Lead Mass Protests over School Funding, Inequality; Thousands Arrested
content:
Nearly 2,000 French high schools are blockaded or closed today amid massive student-led protests over school funding and inequality. The demonstrations began in September at a single school in the economically deprived suburbs of Paris, where students protested teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms and dilapidated school buildings beset by rats, falling debris and more. But the scope of the protests has widened amid a violent crackdown by French police. French authorities have arrested more than 5,000 people, largely underage students, since the movement began. Violent police tactics have led to serious injuries. One protester lost an eye after being hit by a rubber bullet, while another lost a hand when he picked up a police stun grenade.


We hear from an anonymous protester who describes the violence meted out on students, who “aren’t even adults yet,” and from Claire Vigneau, general secretary of Fédération Syndicale Étudiante, the French student union, who reports from a protest in Rennes, Brittany, “where we are trying to escape from the policemen that are chasing us with tear gas and with water cannon[s].”


“The amount of spending that France has done on education has stagnated, if not declined,” explains French American journalist Cole Stangler. “The critiques that high school students are making are actually very similar to what teachers’ unions have been saying for quite some time.”


“Everyone is deeply, deeply angry. We are completely fed up [with] the living conditions, the school conditions, the work conditions that we have,” says Alys Rowlands, a university student in Lille and also a member of Fédération Syndicale Étudiante. “The true violence is the violence of the state that we are being faced with all day, every day, all year. That’s the true violence: having no money, having difficulty finishing the month, having less and less help from the state, having to choose between eating and putting your heating on during the winter.”

title: Iran executes two more people over anti-government protests
content:
Iran’s judiciary announced that two people accused of involvement in the killing of four police officers during anti-government protests earlier this year had been executed.


According to Mizan, the judiciary’s official news outlet, Alireza Sepahi and Alireza Reisi were executed by hanging on Monday morning after the Supreme Court upheld their death sentences. Authorities did not disclose when the two men were arrested or when their trials took place.


Iran’s judiciary accused the two men of involvement in the killing of four police officers in the central city of Isfahan. The court also sentenced them to death on charges of membership of an armed group and threatening national security.


The protests began in Tehran in December over economic grievances and quickly spread to many parts of the country, developing into demonstrations directly opposing the government. The protests intensified particularly on 8 and 9 January, with serious clashes and loss of life reported across the country.


Iranian authorities claimed that more than 3,000 people were killed in the unrest, including hundreds of security personnel. The Tehran government has described the violence as “acts of terrorism” directed by the United States and Israel.


Human rights organisations outside Iran, however, have reported much higher death tolls and said security forces deliberately opened fire on protesters.


Executions on the rise


The number of executions in Iran has reportedly risen, particularly in recent years. According to Amnesty International, Iran carries out more executions than any country in the world except China.


Figures released by Norway-based Iran Human Rights and Paris-based Ensemble contre la peine de mort (ECPM) showed that Iranian authorities executed at least 1,639 people in 2025. The figure was reported to be the highest annual number of executions recorded in the country since 1989.


Iran’s judiciary also announced on Saturday that another person had been executed after being sentenced to death for using a weapon against police officers during the same protests.

author: Kodao Productions
title: Exhibit on Palestinian heritage, struggle opens in UP
content:
An art exhibit opened at the University of the Philippines (UP) this week celebrating Palestinian Heritage Day on Wednesday, also Al-Aqsa Flood’s third anniversary. A selection of photographs, crafts, and devotional objects are on display at UP’s-College of Fine Arts (CFA) Art Gallery representing Palestinian way of life and struggle against Zionist occupation and genocide.


Palestinian Ambassador to the Philippines Mounir Anastas and UP President Angelo Jimenez opened the month-long exhibit entitled “Palestine: Living Heritage, Enduring Steadfastness,” offering visitors a direct connection to the nation’s enduring cultural traditions.


Photographs of historic sites across the West Bank are juxtaposed alongside images of Gaza’s heritage sites before and after their destruction by Israeli occupation forces.


Ambassador Anastas acted as the exhibit’s first guide, explaining traditional Palestinian arts, ranging from embroidery, painting, and devotional items. He expressed appreciation to the university and its Office of International Linkages as well as the CFA for their commitment to cultural preservation, education, and international solidarity.


Palestinian Ambassador to the Philippines Mounir Anastas and UP President Angelo Jimenez opened the month-long exhibit. (Palestinian Embassy photo)


CFA meanwhile said the exhibit presents as testimonies a culture’s enduring beauty and vitality amid the systematic annihilation of Palestinian identity, collective memory, history, and land.


The country’s foremost fine arts school said the exhibition is a presentation of “Palestinian visual culture to testify to the catastrophic loss of a people’s physical and cultural memory alongside the genocide happening across the Gaza Strip today.”


By putting the spotlight on both tangible and intangible cultural heritage in this time of crisis, the exhibit extends the message of solidarity and aspiration for social justice, the University said.


​

Protest rally for Palestine in Manila


Meanwhile, various organizations announced a protest march to the United States Embassy in Manila to commemorate the third anniversary of the Al-Aqsa Flood on Wednesday.


The Philippine chapter of the International League of Peoples’ Struggles, Bagong Alyansang Makabayan, and the Philippine-Palestine Friendship Association said US imperialism and its agents are “genocide-complicit states.”


“The Palestinian resistance is a beacon to our resistance. It inspires all peoples struggling for national and social liberation, and therefore, we must support their resistance as if it were our own,” the groups said.


Up to 80,000 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli forces, including children and journalists, since October 2023.


United Nations Secretary General Antonio Guterres urged a permanent ceasefire in Palestine, demanding the that humanitarian assistance and full respect for international law are scaled up in the occupied Palestinian territories. #

 (Raymund B. Villanueva)

title: La mobilisation lycéenne à travers les yeux d'une professeur du 93
content:
J'voudrais écrire avec mes tripes, mon corps, ses joies et ses dégoûts, loin de toute moraline (Nietzsche) parce que les tribunes de circonstance, les communiqués, syndicaux ou autres, les déclarations d'intention, les mots creux, les rodomontades resteront lettre morte et ne sont que vétilles en considération de ce qui se joue en ce moment dans les lycées de toute la France, et au-delà (universités, monde du travail, perspective du 17 octobre…).


DÉGOÛTS !


L'intersyndicale nationale, au soir du 2 octobre, après plus de 5000 interpellations en 5 jours (pire qu'au plus fort du mouvement des Gilets Jaunes) et des centaines de cas de violences policières avérées, n'est pas même foutue d'appeler à la grève et à manifester le mardi 6 octobre (date posée par le mouvement lycéen pour une grande journée d'actions). Elle préfère en effet le « dialogue social », soit la complicité avec les pouvoirs en place, à la solidarité et aux véritables changements… L'intersyndicale qui précise encore dans ses communiqués qu'il faut que le gouvernement

entende

 les revendications lycéennes, déclaration totalement hors sol, comme si, de là où nous en sommes, le lion affamé allait entendre la plainte de l'antilope… Bref, l'intersyndicale, avec ses éternels atermoiements, c'est le maintien du système tel qu'il est, or certain.es ne le comprennent toujours pas, ce qui est bien désespérant, alors même qu'elle s'est évertuée à faire perdre tous les mouvements sociaux conséquents des dix dernières années (au moins), à commencer par la mobilisation contre la contre-réforme des retraites.


La liste des exactions de la police est tellement longue qu'un recensement exhaustif ne peut en être dressé : tentative de noyade à Belfort par un flic en civil, tentative d'écraser des élèves, par un flic à moto au Blanc-Mesnil, tentative d'homicide à Troyes : une voiture de police fonce à vive allure sur une foule de jeunes, calmes, réunis dans une rue, tout en les gazant depuis les vitres ouvertes du véhicule, étranglement d'une lycéenne de 14 ans à Alençon, éborgnement d'un lycéen de 16 ans, à Argenteuil du fait d'un tir à bout portant de LBD. À Tours, Maël, 16 ans a aussi été éborgné, Mâchoire brisée du fait d'un tir tendu de grenade en plein visage d'Eden, 15 ans, dans le Val d'Oise

 [

1

]

.


Etc.


Une copine me raconte : présence de flics avec des chiens à Carnot (collège-lycée à Paris 17è), mouvement de foule à l'intérieur du collège, son fils de 11 ans blessé au genou dans la panique. Bah au moins, il détestera la police, et pour longtemps !


Dans mon lycée du 93, au terme de deux jours de blocus, on dénombre 5 élèves placés en garde-à-vue dont l'un, mineur, sera peut-être déféré au tribunal ; des blessures : une jeune fille, à l'œil, ayant reçu un projectile suite à l'envoi de gaz lacrymogène par les forces de l'ordre, d'autres présentant des contusions dues à des coups de matraques ; des mises en joue d'élèves par des flics armés de LBD et moult tirs de gaz lacrymo ; des insultes, évidemment ; des intimidations : un flic en mode prêcheur qui déclare à un élève : « tu sais, ce que tu fais là, à la mosquée, même si tu le confesses, on t'le pardonnera pas »… Et aussi une voiture bélier fonçant à vive allure dans le tas, pas de blessés mais une catastrophe aurait pu avoir lieu.


À noter que les élèves embarqués l'ont été alors qu'ils n'étaient plus devant le lycée mais sur le chemin les reconduisant chez eux, par des keufs en embuscade aux environs du lycée, bel exemple de crapulerie et veulerie.


On les pensait bien soumis, pour toujours


Dociles à souhait


Esclaves, sans fin


Dominé.es sans répit


Qui ça ?


Les sauvageon.nes des banlieues, les relégué.es des quartiers populaires… mais ils n'en peuvent plus et relèvent la tête !


Dans mon lycée du 93, depuis des années, on « joue » aux chaises musicales, il n'y a bien souvent pas assez de chaises pour les classes à 35, il faut donc aller en chercher dans d'autres salles qui, de fait, connaîtront à leur tour le même sort, le problème n'est donc pas réglé et se poursuit sempiternellement. Les chaises, en outre, de piètre qualité, sont pour beaucoup endommagées, s'entassent dans les salles et ne sont pas jetées


Depuis l'an passé, Pécresse a fait installer des systèmes bloquant les fenêtres qui s'ouvrent donc à peine maintenant, empêchant toute réelle ventilation ; système anti-suicide paraît-il, mais les élèves peuvent allégrement se jeter dans le vide depuis les passerelles menant …

title: ‘The Struggle Continues’ for Today’s Generation of French Students
content:
The French student movement has a long history of political activism based on organized protests and occupations not only for the improvement of their learning experience and school conditions but also against capitalism, consumerism, imperialism, and police repression.


 


By

C.J. Polychroniou


Common Dreams


 


France

 is presently in the throes of nationwide student

protests

 that have turned increasingly violent as the police crack down on students, using tear gas and heavy-handed tactics as students blockade entrances to their schools and even set fire to several schools across France.


 


The students, aged between 15 and 18, are protesting over poor school conditions (overcrowded classrooms, crumbling

infrastructure

, heavy workloads, teacher shortages) and demand increased funding for schools. Thousands have been

detained

, mostly minors, and dozens injured, including some 50 law enforcement officers.


 


The high school protests begun in Aubervilliers, a low-income Paris suburb, but quickly spread nationwide, as usually happens with students protests in France. University students have now joined high school schools across France, thus creating an even more volatile situation for the French government. Incidentally, the student protests are unfolding alongside massive public-sector protests over pay and working conditions.


 


French students have also shown that they are always on the side of the workers’ fight for better working conditions and in their struggle for an alternative socioeconomic and political order.


 


France is indeed in crisis mode, economically, politically, and socially. Weak growth and deteriorating public finances have been the norm for several years now, while

austerity

 is being advanced by the political establishment as the only available solution to the country’s economic problems and financial misery. French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu presented an austerity-driven government

budget

 on October 1 that proposes 43 billion euros in new fiscal measures to reduce the deficit.


 


However, the

budget

 bill is surely expected to face a rough ride as France has a deeply divided parliament that has repeatedly rejected austerity-driven budget proposals, forcing in fact several prime ministers since 2022 to step down. Lecornu’s government may very well be the next one to collapse as it is highly unlikely that either Marine Le Pen’s far-right National Rally (RN) party or Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s left-wing France Unbowed (LFI) party (which France’s

Interior Ministry

 has actually classified as far left) will make compromises, especially in light of the fact that France’s next presidential election is scheduled for April 18 and May 2, 2027, and looks like the

run-off election

 will be between Le Pen and Mélenchon.


 


In addition, France’s

bond market

 is under growing pressure as its 10-year yield has reached the highest level since 2002. With the cost of borrowing money hitting a peak, France, which has faced sluggish growth for years, is likely to see even slower growth in 2027 than in 2026. This situation seems to be serving the far-right RN party particularly well, which has already scored a “

historic victory

” by securing enough seats in the recently held Senate election to establish its own caucus for the first time.


 


In the meantime, the student protests are being used both by Le Pen and government officials to

target

 Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s party for allegedly deploying agitators and using rhetoric to stoke students’ anger.


 


There is little doubt that the concerns of French students are legitimate. Their grievances with the poor state of schools have been building since this summer’s

heatwaves

, which exposed “the poor state of schools, with poor insulation and no air conditioning,” according to

Vincent Latour

,

 a professor of British Studies at the University of Toulouse-II-Le Mirail. Moreover, the president of Union Syndicale Lycéenne (USL), 19-year old

Ryad Rani

, said that student grievances had elicited no response from the government and that the movement will continue with the protests until its demands are satisfied.


 


The French student movement has a long history of political

activism

capitalism

content:
Israel has killed over 1,700 Palestinian health care workers in three years of genocide in Gaza.

A group of House Democrats has called for Israel to release hundreds of health care workers, including physicians like Hussam Abu Safiya, from detention as Israel’s genocide in Gaza reaches into its fourth year.

Six Democrats, led by Rep. Jesús “Chuy” García (Illinois), released a joint statement on Tuesday condemning Israel for its “systematic persecution” of Palestinian health care workers and demanding their release from arbitrary detention.

“Over the last three years, the Israeli government has systematically destroyed the health system in Palestine, murdering at least 1,700 Palestinian doctors, nurses, paramedics, and other healthcare workers and destroying dozens of hospitals. It has arrested and arbitrarily detained hundreds of Palestinian healthcare workers, including at least 16 physicians who continue to be held in inhumane conditions,” the lawmakers wrote.

The Democrats specifically call for the release of Abu Safiya, who Israel has held in its torture camps for nearly two years, where they have starved and tortured him, his lawyer says. Abu Safiya is a pediatrician who served as the director of Kamal Adwan Hospital in northern Gaza when Israel besieged the area.

The world watched in December 2024 as Israel’s ground raid closed in on Kamal Adwan, with Israeli forces eventually ordering the entire facility to be evacuated, setting it ablaze and arresting Abu Safiya. The hospital was left in ruins after Israeli soldiers were done with it.

“Among [those detained] is Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya, whom the Israeli government has arbitrarily detained since 2024 and tortured to the point of near-death after previously murdering his son and brutally attacking his hospital,” the lawmakers went on.

The statement was signed by Representatives Pramila Jayapal (Washington), Summer Lee (Pennsylvania), Ilhan Omar (Minnesota), Delia C. Ramirez (Illinois), and Rashida Tlaib (D-Michigan).

Israel's systematic destruction of the Palestinian healthcare system and targeting of healthcare workers is at the heart of its genocide. We must stand up for those targeted for saving lives. Free Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya. Free Dr. Mazen Rantisi. Free Dr. Dima Amin.…

The Democrats also called for an end to arms transfers to Israel and urged Congress to block the Trump administration’s planned $2.8 billion package of 2,000-pound bombs to Israel — which is slated to be paid for by U.S. taxpayers. Other Democrats have also vowed to work against that transfer.

In three years of genocide in Gaza, Israel has killed more than 1,700 health care workers and has left zero hospitals fully functioning in the enclave. Israeli forces have also detained more than 400 health care workers from Gaza without charges or a trial in their torture camps.

Israel has killed nearly 600 aid workers since October 7, 2023, according to UN counts.

“Over the past three years, people’s ability to access health care in Gaza has deteriorated dramatically, with medical facilities lying in ruins, hospitals increasingly running out of basic supplies, and patients unable to access essential medicines and treatments. Restrictions on essential supplies such as engine oil and spare parts are also crippling the infrastructure needed to keep hospitals, ambulances, and water systems running, with generators breaking down and water-trucking operations reduced,” said Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) in a statement on Monday.

“It will take generations to recover from the harm that has already been done over the past three years, and in the preceding decades, while the excruciating consequences of Israel’s ongoing genocide are still being felt every day,” said Amande Bazerolle, the head of MSF’s emergency response in Gaza.
