author: webadmin
title: The Rural Connections Behind Illegal Hunting
content:
Thanks to Wiltshire Hunt Sabs for this guest post, who, alongside Cirencester Illegal Hunt Watch, Bristol Hunt Sabs and Bath Hunt Sabs, have been keeping the pressure on the Beaufort Hunt.


The Duke of Beaufort’s Hunt is one of Britain’s most prominent fox hunts and has been terrorising wildlife across the countryside surrounding the Badminton Estate in Gloucestershire for hundreds of years. But the Beaufort Hunt does not exist in isolation. Behind it lies a wider rural network of landowners, estate managers and property professionals.


One of the most striking examples is Rupert Sturgis, Partner and Head of Knight Frank’s Cirencester office.


Rupert Sturgis, Partner and Head of Knight Frank, Cirencester. Image: Wiltshire Hunt Sabs


Knight Frank’s website describes Sturgis as specialising in the sale of town and country property across Gloucestershire and North Wiltshire.


Screenshot:

Knight Frank


He is also a Field Master of the Beaufort Hunt.


On Saturday we filmed Rupert directing the field riders to surround a covert. This is so foxes become trapped inside, whilst hounds are sent in to kill them. It’s a classic cubbing technique that teaches the new hounds to kill.


Rupert Sturgis directing the field to surround the covert in a classic cubbing formation. Image: Wiltshire Hunt Sabs


Watch the video below


Rupert’s role with the hunt is not recent. In 2015, Horse & Hound described him as an estate agent who was then in his 12th season as a Beaufort Field Master.


Image: Wiltshire Hunt Sabs


The Field describes him as a Beaufort Field Master, quoting him discussing the hunting country where they were openly hunting foxes just last Saturday, and where our drone was shot down in December 2025:

“Field Master Rupert Sturgis recommends the Widleys hedges as part of a run west from Common Wood Farm”

.


Beanie Sturgis laying a trail of cigarette ash. Image: Wiltshire Hunt Sabs


His wife, Beanie Sturgis, is also a Beaufort Field Master. Badminton Horse Trials states that she married Rupert in 2007 and describes her as a Beaufort Field Master, as well as an event organiser, show judge and course designer. Beanie accepted a community resolution in respect of a hate crime committed against a hunt sab in October 2024.


Knight Frank and the Badminton Estate


The connection between Knight Frank and the Badminton Estate goes well beyond Rupert Sturgis. In fact, Knight Frank has been involved with the estate for decades, with senior figures from the firm becoming closely involved in the management structure surrounding Badminton.


In its 2015 Rural Report, Knight Frank stated that it had been involved with the Badminton Estate for 15 years. The report featured Simon Dring, then Badminton’s senior resident agent, who said he had worked at the estate for more than 30 years, including 15 years as senior resident agent. He described working closely with the Duke and his family, as well as coordinating the various specialists and advisers involved with the estate.


Dring retired from the Knight Frank LLP partnership on 31 December 2016, but his relationship with Badminton continued for almost another decade. He remained the estate’s senior resident agent until his retirement from Badminton in late 2025.


Dring once hilariously told us, via deluded hunt supporters, that we couldn’t fly our drone in the ‘Duke’s air space’.


Companies House records show that he was secretary of Swangrove Estates Ltd from 31 March 2000 until 9 March 2026. The company is registered at the Estate Office, Badminton, and its stated business is mixed farming. He was also secretary of Swangrove Holdings Ltd from 31 March 2000 until 9 March 2026, another company registered at the Badminton Estate Office.


Both companies show current officers including members of the Somerset family alongside other directors. The records show the overlap between the people managing the estate and the companies through which its interests are held.


And Dring is not the only former Knight Frank figure with a connection to the Badminton Estate.


Christopher Smith, who was a Knight Frank partner heading its rural consultancy, renewables and energy consultancy, is now listed as a person with significant control of Badminton Hospitality Ltd, with ownership and voting rights of 75% or more. His correspondence address is the Badminton Estate Office.


Alexander (Sandy) Douglas provides another link. He has been a director of Swangrove Estates Ltd since 2000 …

author: L214
title: Marche pour la fermeture des abattoirs
content:
Chaque année, des milliards d’animaux sont tués pour l’alimentation : environ 69 milliards d’animaux terrestres et plus de 1 000 milliards de poissons dans le monde. Derrière ces chiffres se trouvent des individus sensibles, capables de ressentir la douleur, la peur et la détresse.

La Marche pour la fermeture des abattoirs est un appel à mettre fin à cette hécatombe. L’élevage, la pêche et l’abattage condamnent des êtres sensibles à une vie d’exploitation, puis à une mort violente et prématurée, alors même que nous n’avons pas besoin de produits d’origine animale pour vivre en bonne santé.

C’est dans ce contexte qu’aura lieu la nouvelle édition de la Marche pour la fermeture des abattoirs à Paris le 3 octobre 2026. Une Vegan Place (village associatif et commerçant) sera organisée le même jour pour apporter une touche gourmande et festive à l’événement.

author: Lucas
title: Veganes Wichteln
content:
Veganes Wichteln mit ARIWA geht in die nächste Runde

Danke an über 500 Wichtel beim veganen Wichteln 2025!

Bei der Aktion „Veganes Wichteln 2026 von ARIWA“ senden sich unbekannte Personen Überraschungspakete. Was verschenkt wird, ist dabei komplett offen, unterliegt aber zwei Bedingungen: Der Inhalt muss komplett vegan sein und das Geschenk soll von Herzen kommen.


Es kann gebastelt, gehäkelt, genäht, gebacken werden, du kannst zum Laden um die Ecke gehen und eine Kleinigkeit kaufen – Hauptsache ist, dass du dich ebenfalls über den Inhalt freuen würdest! Deiner Kreativität ist daher keine Grenze gesetzt!


So funktioniert das Vegane Wichteln von ARIWA

1.

Anmelden

: Trage dich im Formular unten mit deiner E-Mail-Adresse ein. Teilnehmen können alle Menschen mit einer Postanschrift in Deutschland.


2.

Bestätigen

: Nach dem Absenden bekommst du sofort einen 6-stelligen Code per E-Mail. Gib ihn direkt im Formular ein – fertig! Kommt keine Mail an, schau im Spam-Ordner nach oder fordere im Formular einen neuen Code an. Solltest du dich vertippt haben, kannst du deine Adresse dort korrigieren.


3.

Adresse erhalten

: Nach dem Anmeldeschluss wird jedem Wichtel per E-Mail die Adresse einer anderen Person zugeteilt – auf magische Weise (und ein bisschen IT-Zauber).


4.

Paket verschicken

: Pack dein Überraschungspaket und schicke es bis spätestens 10. Dezember 2026 los.


5.

Freuen

: Jetzt heißt es abwarten – bald erreicht dein Überraschungspaket die Postadresse deines Wichtels und du bekommst im Gegenzug ein Paket voller Überraschungen.


6.

Danke sagen

: Ist dein Paket angekommen? Über den Link in deiner E-Mail gibst du deinem Wichtel Bescheid und kannst ihm eine kleine Nachricht schicken.


7.

Teilen & verbreiten

: Hilf uns, das vegane Wichteln noch bekannter zu machen! Verteile unseren

Aushang

 oder erzähle deinen Freund*innen auf Social Media davon. Vielen Dank für deine Unterstützung!


Rückblick

Nach über 300 Wichtel-Paketen im Jahr 2023 haben

2024 und 2025 sogar jeweils mehr als 500 Menschen

 beim veganen Wichteln von ARIWA mitgemacht!

Damit hätten wir nicht gerechnet – umso schöner zu sehen, wie viel Freude es euch bereitet, Überraschungspakete zu packen und zu verschicken.


Wir – das Wichtelteam von ARIWA – sagen von Herzen

Danke

 an alle Teilnehmenden. Eure lieben Mails, Dankesworte und guten Wünsche haben uns sehr berührt.


Darum ist klar: Auch 2026 wird es wieder ein veganes Wichteln geben!


Anmeldeschluss: 23. November 2026


Hinweise zum Paket

Was ist vegan?


Veganes enthält keine tierischen Bestandteile wie Milch, Fleisch, Eier, Honig oder auch Bienenwachs, Leder, Wolle. Es ist so hergestellt worden, dass dafür kein Tier leiden musste.


Solltest du dir nicht ganz sicher sein, dann schreib uns unter

wichteln@ariwa.org

.


Wie hoch sollte der Wert des Geschenkes sein?


Der Paketinhalt sollte bei ca. 10 € exklusive Verpackungs- und Versandkosten liegen. Selbstgemachtes ist immer schön, jedoch kein Muss. Wenn du eher nicht zu den Do-it-yourself-Menschen gehörst, freuen sich die Händler*innen bei dir vor Ort.


Können Lebensmittel verschickt werden?

Dies ist möglich, jedoch mit Einschränkungen:


Bitte beachte die jeweils individuell angegebenen Allergien, diese erhältst du direkt mit der Versandadresse.


Bitte verschicke keine Kühlware!


Verpacke die Lebensmittel ordnungsgemäß und am besten luftdicht.


Verzichte bitte gänzlich auf Alkohol! Das Vegane Wichteln steht allen Personen offen und es können auch Kinder unter den Beschenkten sein.


Bitte beschrifte deine Geschenke eindeutig, sodass die beschenkte Person weiß, was sie da gerade genießt. Lege auch gerne das Rezept bei! Wenn du zum Beispiel selbst gebackene Plätzchen verschickst, empfehlen wir, die Zutatenliste beizulegen – für den Fall, dass Allergien bestehen.


Wann solltest du das Paket verschicken?


Spätestens zum 10. Dezember solltest du das Paket versendet haben. Wir erinnern dich daran via E-Mail. Es wäre sehr schade und traurig, wenn eine Person sich auf dein Paket freut und nichts ankommt!


Kann ich mich mit meinem Wichtel austauschen?


Ja! Wenn du bei der Anmeldung zustimmst und dein Wichtelpartner ebenfalls, bekommst du mit der Adresse auch die Mailadresse – so kannst du z.B. nachfragen, ob alles angekommen ist.


Außerdem findest du in deiner Mail einen Link „Paket ist angekommen“. Darüber sagst du der Person, die dich beschenkt hat, Bescheid und kannst ihr eine kleine Dankesnachricht schicken …

author: admin
title: Dixon Mink Farm in Bluffdale, Utah will be Forced to Close
content:
Dixon Mink Farm at 15028 Pony Express Road in the town of Bluffdale, Utah will be forced to close.

The city council of Bluffdale has eliminated fur farming as a permitted use. Fur farms will be unable to operate in Bluffdale.

The councilperson who pushed for the change said:

“I saw the serious issue the mink farm had on the lives of our residents. As I knocked on doors of our independence area there were so many flies people couldn’t open their door to talk to me. Because of this ordinance change the city can not approve the business license for this or any other mink farm.”

author: winter oak
title: Never Accidentally Offer Luxury Recycled Cream Cakes to Portuguese Vegan Punks!
content:
This is the fifth and final chapter from the book 

King of the Squatters

 by jaybo which we are delighted to be able to share on Winter Oak. The whole text can be found as a pdf

here

.


I had enjoyed going for food at the social centre twice weekly. But it became tiresome for me to recognise blatant hierarchies and leaders when their on-line blurb claimed that they were anarchists against leaders, organised along horizontal lines, not vertical, top-down power structures. But my relationship with the social centre was completely destroyed one afternoon, after I had just recycled some expensive, fancy cream cakes.


In front of our house, a fiesta had been happening all weekend, so lots of drunken revellers engulfed our usually quiet home. Our squat had been under siege for the three days, being attacked by young adults who threw stones and came into our building looking for trouble. I had not been sleeping well and was very tired one day as I ate some luxury recycled cream cakes in the city centre. Then the social centre’s leader passed me and stopped to speak. We had only ever seen each other previously at the centre, never in public. I offered yer man a fancy cake, without thinking that they were patently not vegan.


He refused and asked me exactly where our squat was. I innocently told him directions to our home. Then he left to go on a demonstration against workers’ exploitation. That night as I walked home, I was stopped dead in my tracks by fresh graffiti on the bridge just before our squat. In big white letters it simply stated, “vegan limit!!!” I had no doubt that the vegan punk anarchist leader had just sprayed the graffiti as some kind of attempted bullshit intimidation directed at me. Because I had offered to share my hard-earned cakes with him.


I never went back to the social centre after that. I was so angry that I knew if I had returned then I would have certainly made trouble and probably have given the leader an excuse to ban me anyway. I hate egos and authoritarians. However, as always, I tried to turn a negative into a positive. That incident inspired one of my most popular signs for The Whimsical Atrocity Theatre (TWAT): “I only eat vegans”.


The next day, TWAT proudly unveiled its new message to the world. It worked immediately. The show was good. I was a little bit worried that one or more of the social centre vegan punks would pass by, see the sign and beat me up. I was probably safe in my theatre, as I usually had a police escort at one side, looking out for the tourists’ safety. But they knew where I lived.


Some brave souls came and spoke to me during or after my cardboard shenanigans. But things reached dizzying heights for TWAT when an American woman came up to me and asked me how much my signs were. I was absolutely flabbergasted. Someone wanted to buy my recycled carton signs. I replied to her spontaneously that, if she wanted to buy a sign, then she had to tell me how much it was. She put four euros into my hat for “I only eat vegans”. Black permanent marker pen on quality recycled cardboard.


Women were flirting with me almost every day when I performed, but I was caught completely off guard when an extremely attractive, well-dressed young French woman came up to me with her friends, picked up the condoms and said, “OK, let’s go!” She was absolutely serious and in a pathetic response, I replied, “You’re wearing a wedding ring.” She countered with, “It’s only an engagement ring. This is my last chance. Are you coming?” Her friends’ looks assured me that she was absolutely serious. I did not go. One of her friends looked at me as though I must have been insane. One of several potentially delicious sexual opportunities that I missed in life.


As the summer really heated up, it felt as though all of Portugal’s crazy folk were coming out of the woodwork and heading for fun in Lisbon. As I worked one day, a sun-drenched, handsome, young man swaggered up the steps towards me. He wore rags as clothes, had matted, unkempt hair flopping all over his face and had a long stick over his shoulder, with a cloth bundle tied up at the other end. He asked if he could write something on one of my signs. I told him he could, so he picked up “this sign was my bed” and wrote on it, “but I washed it in my jacuzzi first”, which killed me and the audience. Then he shouted for all to hear, “We are homeless because we choose to be.”


Before his departure, he asked me if he could take a condom because …

author: PETA-Team
title: Geheimsache Tierversuche: Neue ZDF-Doku zeigt Tierleid hinter verschlossenen Labortüren
content:
Symbolbild


Die neue „37°“-Dokumentation „Geheimsache Tierversuche – Unter Ausschluss der Öffentlichkeit“ geht der Frage nach, was eigentlich mit Tieren in Versuchslaboren geschieht – und warum die Öffentlichkeit so wenig davon sehen darf.


Am 

29. September 2026 um 22:15 Uhr im ZDF

 sehen die Zuschauer:innen hinter die Kulissen einer Branche, in der Mäuse, Ratten, Hunde, Affen, Kaninchen, Schweine und viele weitere Tiere für Experimente missbraucht werden.


Millionen Tiere leiden für „wissenschaftliche Zwecke“


Nach den offiziellen Zahlen wurden in Deutschland

im Jahr 2024 über drei Millionen Tiere

 für „wissenschaftliche Zwecke“ missbraucht. Einen großen Teil nimmt die Grundlagenforschung ein, in der Tieren zum Beispiel der Schädel aufgebohrt wird, um Elektroden in ihr Gehirn zu setzen. In regulatorischen, gesetzlich vorgeschriebenen Tests werden die Tiere teils vergiftet und getötet.


Solche Experimente finden nicht irgendwo weit entfernt statt, sondern an verschiedenen Forschungseinrichtungen in Deutschland.

Experimente an Affen

, die in der Dokumentation ebenfalls thematisiert werden, sind in der Hälfte der Bundesländer vertreten.


Was passiert in den Versuchslaboren?


Für die Dokumentation hat der Journalist Manfred Karremann mehr als ein Jahr lang versucht, Einblicke in deutsche Tierversuchslabore zu bekommen. Trotz angebotener Anonymität erklärte sich nur eine Einrichtung bereit, ein wenig Einblick zu geben.


Die Dokumentation macht damit ein Problem sichtbar, das Tierschützer:innen seit Jahren kritisieren: Tierversuche finden weitgehend im Verborgenen statt. Sie werden verharmlost und die wenigsten Menschen erfahren, was den Tieren tatsächlich angetan wird. Dabei geht es um Lebewesen, die Angst und Schmerzen empfinden wie wir – und die schlichtweg nicht dazu da sind, dass wir an ihnen experimentieren.


Die Dokumentation zeigt unter anderem Aufnahmen aus einem britischen Labor. Zu sehen sind Hunde,

Affen

, Kaninchen und Ratten, die für sogenannte

Giftigkeitstests

 missbraucht werden. Die Versuche gelten als standardisierte Verfahren und werden nach internationalen Richtlinien durchgeführt – auch in der EU. Tiere müssen dabei beispielsweise Chemikalien einatmen oder bekommen Testsubstanzen über einen Schlauch direkt in den Magen verabreicht.


Jetzt lesen


Forschung und Medizin


Tierversuche in Deutschland: Was wirklich in den Versuchslaboren passiert


In deutschen Tierversuchslaboren werden Affen, Hunde, Katzen, Nagetiere, Fische & Insekten gequält. Erfahren Sie hier mehr über die Versuche!


Jetzt lesen


Tierversuche sind keine gute Wissenschaft


Tierversuche werden oft als „wissenschaftlich notwendig“ gerechtfertigt – doch die Dokumentation zeigt, dass die Wissenschaft längst mit Methoden arbeitet, die ohne Tiermissbrauch auskommen. Expert:innen aus Industrie und Wissenschaft kommen zu Wort und erklären, warum modernste Methoden wie menschliche Zellkulturen oder Organs-on-a-Chip Tierversuchen nicht nur ethisch, sondern auch wissenschaftlich überlegen sind.


Diese Ansätze arbeiten direkt mit menschlichen Zellen und menschlichem Gewebe. Dadurch können sie bei bestimmten Fragestellungen auch Erkenntnisse liefern, die sich besser auf Menschen übertragen lassen.


Jetzt einschalten und hinschauen!

title: Guilty Verdict For King’s Sheep Rescuers In Theft Trial
content:
After a four-day trial at Norwich Crown Court, Rose Patterson, Sarah Foy, and Rosa Sharkey have all been found guilty of theft after the rescue of three lambs from King Charles III’s Sandringham Estate in May 2023. Sentencing to follow today.

Despite the verdict, Animal Rising claims that the rescue and subsequent trial have helped to put a spotlight on the reality behind animal farming in the UK, with over 10 million sheep being slaughtered yearly [1].

The controversial rescue made front-page news across the UK and headlines around the world [2]. It captured the attention of the British public, questioning how we relate to animals in the food system and if it’s a rescue or a theft to take them from farms.

Animal Rising director Rose Patterson, alongside Rosa Sharkey and Sarah Foy, rescued the lambs - Sammy, Sunny and Sooty - before informing police the following day. The women held signs outside Windsor Castle reading “I rescued the King’s sheep” before reporting what they had done to police. They each face up to 7 years' imprisonment.

Earlier this year, Patterson was found not guilty by a jury over another Animal Rising open rescue, after helping to rescue beagle puppies from MBR Acres, a facility breeding animals for testing [3].

Animal Rising director Rose Patterson, one of the three defendants found guilty today, said:

Sammy, Sunny and Sooty remain safe and are now fully grown.

The trial followed a series of open-rescue trials relating to Animal Rising’s rescue of beagles from MBR Acres. In January this year, Animal Rising made history by securing the UK’s first-ever not-guilty verdict in an open-rescue case [4]. The lambs were rescued from Appleton Farm, which forms part of the Sandringham estate.

Defendants Patterson and Foy are available for comment or broadcast interview upon request.

For further information, comment, or to arrange an interview, please email press@animalrising.org or call +44 1225 29 6691

High-Quality Pictures and Videos: https://show.pics.io/animal-rising-breaking-news

All images and videos in this file, on our social media, and website can be used with credit to Animal Rising under ‘fair use’ for the purposes of reporting.

https://www.dailymail.com/news/article-12126009/Will-stop-eco-clowns-Just-Stop-Oil-throw-orange-powder-Animal-Rising-kidnap-lambs.html

Rose Patterson, 37, is the Director of Animal Rising. An advocate for animals since 2012, she holds an MSc in Animal Welfare Science, Ethics, and Law and previously worked with World Animal Protection before joining Animal Rising in 2020.

Sarah Foy, 26, has been involved in a range of campaigns advocating for a just and sustainable food system that works for animals, farmers, and the planet. She brings a practical, hands-on approach to her advocacy, with real-world experience caring for rescued farm animals at sanctuaries and protesting alongside farmers.

Rosa Sharkey, 26, is a food charity worker. She is passionately committed to reducing the impact of our food system on the climate crisis, community action, and animal rights.

Animal Rising is a nonviolent campaign group working to fundamentally transform our relationship with animals and nature, and build a more sustainable future for animals, people and the planet. Animal Rising is calling on the Government to end factory farming by 2040 and support a transition to a sustainable plant-based food system.

author: Sophie Lemcke
title: So ist es, als Huhn in der Fleischindustrie leben zu müssen
content:
Die Hühnermast ist ein grausames System, das auf maximale Schnelligkeit, Wachstum und Profit ausgelegt ist und mit einem gewaltvollen Tod für die Tiere endet.


Wie fühlt es sich an, als „Masthuhn“ geboren zu werden

, ohne die Möglichkeit, der leidvollen Industrie zu entkommen

?


Der einzige Grund, weshalb die Industrie dich „produziert“ hat: Du sollst so schnell wie möglich so schwer wie möglich werden – und wirst dann getötet.


Du kommst in einem Hühnerschlupfbetrieb mit tausenden anderen Küken zur Welt. Um dich herum piepsen sie verzweifelt. Und auch du suchst nach Nähe und Wärme. Aber da ist keine Mutter, in deren Gefieder du dich kuscheln kannst – und du wirst sie auch niemals kennenlernen.

Noch am ersten Tag deines Lebens wirst du über Förderbänder geschleudert und in eine Kiste gepackt. Dann beginnt die oftmals stundenlange Fahrt zum Mastbetrieb – eingepfercht mit Dutzenden anderen Küken, ohne Wasser, ohne Nahrung.


Foto: Andrew Skowron


Du kommst in einer riesigen Halle an. Hier wirst du die nächsten rund 5 Wochen verbringen – die einzigen Wochen deines Lebens.


Um dich herum Tausende andere Küken. Du teilst dir einen Quadratmeter mit bis zu 23 anderen Tieren. Jetzt seid ihr noch klein, doch das wird sich schnell ändern.


Du wächst. Unnatürlich schnell. Das Futter steht dir Tag und Nacht zur Verfügung – hochkalorisch, proteinreich, entwickelt für maximales Wachstum in kürzester Zeit.


Du hast keinen Platz, um dich natürlich zu bewegen, es gibt nichts zum Erkunden. Keinerlei Möglichkeiten, deine natürlichen Verhaltensweisen auszuleben. Es ist trist und laut. Da ist nur diese Enge.


Die Luft ist stickig. Der Ammoniakgeruch von den Ausscheidungen Tausender Tiere brennt in deinen Augen, in deinen Lungen. Du bekommst Atemwegserkrankungen. Jeder Atemzug tut weh.


Dein Körper wurde durch jahrzehntelange Züchtung so manipuliert, dass du in wenigen Wochen das Gewicht erreichst, für das ein Huhn unter natürlichen Bedingungen Monate bräuchte.


Foto: Andrew Skowron


Deine Brustmuskeln wachsen so schnell und werden so schwer, dass deine Knochen dein Gewicht nicht mehr tragen können. Deine Beine verformen sich. Dein Herz ist zu klein für deinen massiven Körper, es hat Probleme, deine Organe mit ausreichend Blut zu versorgen. Du hast Schmerzen beim Gehen und deine Gelenke sind entzündet.


Um dich herum sind Hühner, die gar nicht mehr aufstehen können. Sie liegen in ihrem eigenen Kot und leiden unter extremen Schmerzen. Sie verdursten und verhungern.


Andere Hühner werden aufgrund der Enge von ihren Artgenossen versehentlich totgetrampelt und erdrückt – ihre Körper verwesen zwischen dir und den tausenden anderen Tieren. Auch du hast keine Chance, den anderen Hühnern auszuweichen.


Dann ist es soweit. Menschen kommen und packen dich. An deinen Beinen, kopfüber, werden du und deine Artgenossen gegriffen und in enge Transportkisten geworfen. Deine ohnehin schon schmerzenden Beine brechen unter der groben Behandlung. Du hast Schmerzen und Todesangst.


Zusammengepfercht, ohne Wasser, ohne Futter, geht es zum Schlachthof. Die Fahrt kann Stunden dauern. Manche Hühner sterben bereits im Transporter – vor Stress, vor Erschöpfung, erdrückt von anderen Tieren.


Foto: Andrew Skowron


Im Schlachthof riechst du Blut. Du hörst die Schreie anderer Hühner. Dann bist du selbst an der Reihe. Unter grausamen Bedingungen wirst du betäubt und getötet. Du bist gerade einmal 35 bis 42 Tage alt geworden.


Es ist unvorstellbar, was Hühner in der Fleischindustrie erleiden müssen.


Die Wahrheit hinter „Hähnchenfleisch“


Wie grausam das kurze Leben von sogenannten Masthühnern ist, haben wir schon mehrfach bei Undercover-Recherchen aufgedeckt, beispielsweise in einem (jetzt ehemaligen) Zuliefererbetrieb der großen Marke Wiesenhof. Hier erfährst du mehr über unsere Aufdeckungen und kannst unsere Petition für strengere Tierschutzvorgaben, -kontrollen und -strafen unterzeichnen:


Jetzt für Hühner unterschreiben 


In Deutschland wird mehr Fleisch von Hühnern konsumiert als produziert – und die Nachfrage ist in den vergangenen Jahren stetig gestiegen. Unterstütze dieses grausame System nicht: Entscheide dich konsequent für pflanzliche Lebensmittel.


In den meisten Supermärkten findest du mittlerweile eine Vielfalt tierfreundlicher Alternativen, die hervorragende Proteinquellen sind – probiere sie aus. Oder koche unsere zahlreichen pflanzlichen Rezepte von Love Veg nach, wie unsere

knusprigen Tofu-Nuggets

.

author: webadmin
title: Lessons in Hare Hunting: Inside Britain’s School Beagle Packs
content:
The private schools schooling children in a masterclass of wildlife criminality.


Recently we revealed the

full footage of the Stowe School Beagles

 during what school headteacher, Dr Anthony Wallersteiner, describes as a

“huge variety of activities”

 available to pupils, including

“field games…beagling”

.


Kennedy giving direction to the pupils


The school’s Games Coach, Phillip Kennedy, was in the fields surrounding Crockwell Farm, alongside school pupils, ‘coaching’ them as the Stowe School Beagles hunted a hare.


The school lesson ended with a dead hare and a criminal conviction for its Games Coach.


The now-deleted reference to Kennedy’s role at the Stowe School.


Kennedy pleaded guilty to hunting a wild mammal with dogs after drone footage captured his pack chasing the hare, first through the farmyard and then across open fields before catching and killing her against a fence.

Police said

 that Kennedy knew allowing his dogs to chase and kill the hare was cruel and illegal.


Just as importantly, the footage shone a spotlight on something that has gone on behind the closed doors of some of Britain’s most prestigious private schools: children being introduced to illegal hunting, more than twenty years after hunting wild mammals with dogs was banned.


There are serious safeguarding questions which Stowe School, in particular, appear determined to ignore. What risk assessments are made before children are taken out with packs of hunting dogs? What are staff instructed to do when those hounds begin pursuing a live animal? What safeguarding procedures kick in when pupils witness that animal being caught and killed?


Nothing in the footage suggests this was some unexpected aberration. They all know the routine, the kids congratulate each other, congratulate the dogs. Nobody looks shocked. The huntsman joins in with the handshaking. They’ve clearly done this before haven’t they!


Games Coach Philip Kennedy congratulating pupils as the hounds rip the remains of the hare apart close by.


Stowe is not alone.


There are other school beagle packs still taking children out into the countryside, maintaining the hounds and traditions of hare hunting.


Eton College has one of the oldest and most famous school beagle packs in the country.


Its history stretches back to the nineteenth century

. Long before the Hunting Act, generations of Eton boys learned their “hound lore” by pursuing hares with the school pack. Boys became Masters and Whips, and learned to handle hounds.


The Hunting Act came into force in 2005, but school lessons in hare-hunting continue.


In 2013, eight years after the ban, the Hunt Saboteurs Association

revealed plans

 for a Young Hare-Hunters’ Day at Eton. This was no historical re-enactment of hunting, children were actually being offered coaching in the skills and traditions of hare hunting.


Pupils were to receive training in hare hunting from experienced huntsmen, including Steven Duckmanton, the huntsman of the Dummer Beagles.


Steven Duckmanton, hare-hunting huntsman of the Dummer Beagles. Image: West Midlands Hunt Saboteurs.


In 2024,

West Midlands Hunt Saboteurs

 put a drone above those same Dummer Beagles. The footage they captured showed a hare breaking from the field and the pack pursuing her line across field after field, whilst hunt staff watched.


In October 2015,

footage was filmed

 at an Eton College Beagles meet in North Yorkshire, which showed a live hare fleeing across a field with the pack in pursuit. The footage was handed to North Yorkshire Police in January 2016 and Eton announced an urgent investigation.


Eleven years after hunting with dogs had supposedly been consigned to history, one of Britain’s most prestigious schools was having to investigate its own beagle pack over footage of a hare being hunted.


This year, Sir Jacob Rees-Mogg revealed his eldest son had brought 41 Eton beagles home with him during the school holidays.


His son, Peter Theodore Aphege Rees-Mogg, left Eton this summer. He wasn’t a mere follower of the hunt – he had been a Master of the Eton College Hunt during his final year.


Peter Theodore Aphege Rees-Mogg at home out with the Mendip Farmers Hunt. Image: Mendip Hunt Sabs.


Peter’s mother Helena, herself a regular fox hunter and meet host for the

recently-charged

 Mendip Farmers Hunt, went even further in an article published in September 2026.


Writing about why she believes Eton should remain an all-boys school …

title: Nourrir ou trahir. Comment l’élevage intensif saigne la France.
content:
On doit changer de modèle, découvrez comment :

Peu importe qui vous êtes et ce en quoi vous croyez : l’élevage intensif trahit vos valeurs.

Nous mangeons 85 kilos de viande par personne et par an, le double de la moyenne mondiale. Ni accident ni dérive, cette consommation de masse est le produit d’un système dont l’élevage intensif est la pierre angulaire.

Souveraineté alimentaire, santé publique, déforestation, biodiversité, ressource en eau, revenu des agriculteurs, sort des animaux : sur chacun de ces fronts, l’élevage intensif nous trahit. Il nous rend dépendants d’engrais et de soja importés, endette les éleveurs, favorise pandémies et antibiorésistance, nuit à l’environnement et entraîne l’abattage de plus de 3 millions d’animaux chaque jour pour la seule consommation française.

Nous n’avons pas choisi ce modèle. D’autres l’ont choisi pour nous. Ce livre, rédigé par Brigitte Gothière et Sébastien Arsac, cofondateurs de L214, défend une proposition pour reprendre la main ensemble : donnons-nous l’objectif de réduire de moitié le nombre d’animaux tués d’ici 2030. Parce que c’est possible. Parce que c’est vital.

d’animaux abattus chaque jour pour la seule consommation française.

Vous entrez dans un supermarché. Vous prenez un caddie. Vous suivez un itinéraire balisé. Vous voyez ce qui doit être vu, à la hauteur qu'il faut, au prix qu'il faut. Vous croisez la viande partout, les légumineuses presque nulle part. À la sortie, vous avez le sentiment d'avoir choisi.

« On nous a fait croire qu’il fallait choisir son camp : pour les agriculteurs ou pour les animaux, pour le climat ou pour la souveraineté alimentaire. Mais l’élevage intensif ne défend aucun de ces camps, il les renie tous en même temps. C’est ce que ce livre documente, chiffres à l’appui. »

« C’est un livre sur une impasse dont nous devons sortir collectivement. Réduire de moitié le nombre d’animaux tués d’ici 2030 est une nécessité, soutenue par une majorité de Français. Ceux qui croient que l’élevage intensif peut durer se bercent d’illusions. »

Nourrir ou trahir, comment l’élevage intensif saigne la France paru le 30 septembre 2026 aux éditions Payot, disponible au prix de 19 € sur notre boutique en ligne et en librairie.

title: Contre Janco et son monde !
content:
Cette brochure s'appuie sur la BD Le monde sans fin de Jancovici (les numéros des pages desquelles sont tirées les citations sont entre parenthèses) pour illustrer l'incompatibilité profonde entre l'analyse des écologistes et les fantasmes des technologistes. Cette critique n'a pas la prétention d'être exhaustive. De plus, les nombreuses références qui ponctuent le texte, comme autant d'invitations à aller plus loin, témoignent du temps qu'il m'a manqué pour développer plus en profondeur la pensée naturienne, anti-industrielle, qui me nourrit. J'ai préféré me concentrer sur un ensemble de pistes à explorer ainsi qu'à démontrer en quoi cette critique me semble constructive et stratégiquement bénéfique à la lutte pour la nature et la liberté.


Introduction


Certes, il y a plein de choses intéressantes dans cette BD et dans le discours de Jancovici de façon générale. Il comprend très bien certaines limites physiques du système actuel et sait parfaitement vulgariser des notions parfois complexes avancées par les chercheurs du GIEC notamment. D'un point de vue scientifique son discours parait clair, limpide, d'une grande rigueur et en de nombreux points implacable. Il paraît seulement., En effet, ses omissions et sa grille de lecture techno-centrée évacuent de nombreuses réalités pourtant largement avérées. D'un point de vue politique, nous sommes bien loin du discours des écologistes qui défendent la nature et la liberté comme conditions essentielles d'une vie bonne, juste, égalitaire et soutenable.


Je crois qu'il est important, dans le contexte des luttes actuelles, de critiquer et dénoncer ces discours qui, définitivement, ne vont pas « dans le bon sens ». Malgré toutes les bonnes intentions qu'on peut lui prêter et malgré la rigueur apparente de ses analyses, l'horizon politique qu'il dessine n'est pas enviable et doit être combattu.


« Notre tâche consiste à proposer une critique impitoyable, et de nos prétendus amis bien plus que de nos ennemis manifestes. Nous renonçons avec plaisir, en adoptant cette attitude, à une popularité démagogique. »


 Karl Marx & Friedrich Engels, « Gottfried Kinkel »


 « Pour progresser sur une route qui sera brumeuse et ardue, le mouvement écologique devra s'exercer à la critique de soi et de ses pseudo-alliés ; et pour ce travail de dépollution intellectuelle et morale, les matériaux ne manqueront pas. »


 Bernard Charbonneau


Technologistes vs Écologistes


Aujourd'hui, quand on parle d'écologie, plusieurs courants coexistent et s'affrontent. On peut, notamment, différencier schématiquement les écologistes des technologistes :


https://www.partage-le.com/2022/01/29/leur-ecologie-et-la-notre-technologistes-contre-naturiens-par-nicolas-casaux/

.


Évidemment, seuls les technologistes ont la faveur des grands médias. C'est pour cela que, dans cette opposition asymétrique, les écologistes ont peu de chance d'exister auprès du grand public. Jancovici est un technologiste comme beaucoup de figures écolos mainstreams. A l'inverse, les écologistes portent les idées des courants anti-industriels, luddites, anarchistes naturiens, anarcho-primitivistes…


Une grande différence entre ces deux visions de l'écologie réside dans l'analyse du monde actuel et passé et dans les objectifs politiques qui en découlent.


Les écologistes, philosophiquement écocentristes, qui placent la vie au centre, ont pour objectif de préserver et régénérer la diversité biotique sur Terre. (L'écocentrisme reconnaît que des formes de vie existent par et pour elles-mêmes dans la nature, et qu'elles sont dignes de considération morale indépendamment des services qu'elles pourraient rendre à l'espèce humaine). Pour eux le problème est la civilisation, en tant qu'organisation sociale intrinsèquement expansionniste, hiérarchisée, extractiviste, patriarcale, inégalitaire, militarisée (la civilisation industrielle, ou contemporaine, étant sûrement la pire), qui détruit la nature et aliène les individus. Ils souhaitent donc que l'effondrement de la civilisation advienne le plus rapidement possible, avant l'effondrement des communautés biotiques, avant l'effondrement de la vie sur Terre. Il ne peut pas, par définition, exister de civilisation soutenable.


(pour en savoir plus sur le concept de civilisation, ses implications sociales et les destructions écologiques inhérentes à son maintien, il existe Endgame, un très bon livre de Derrick Jensen en 2 tomes et traduit en français aux Éditions LIBRE. J'invite aussi à la …

title: Geothermal development threatens villages in the Zilan Valley
content:
In the Zilan Valley near Erciş district in the province of Van, the conflict over geothermal development in the region is intensifying. The villages of Şorik (İkizçalı), Karakilise (İşbaşı) and Çaxirbeg (Çakırbey) see their living environment threatened by the expansion of the projects. Residents report that the possible evacuation of the villages is now also being discussed and that signatures are being collected.


According to the information available so far, no official evacuation order has been issued. However, work sites and drilling areas have already been established in Karakilise and Çaxirbeg. The projects are therefore directly encroaching on residential areas, agricultural land and the livelihoods of the local population.


The conflict is not new. State-backed geothermal development in the Zilan Valley has been underway since at least 2020. Since then, drilling operations, further planning and large-scale tenders for the exploitation of geothermal resources have followed.


Project launched in 2020


At the end of November 2020, the Eastern Anatolia Development Agency (DAKA) and the Van Governor’s Office signed an agreement for a project to develop geothermal resources for agricultural use in Erciş. The project was part of the Turkish Ministry of Industry and Technology’s support program for so-called attraction centers.


With a budget of 2.6 million Turkish lira at the time, the project envisaged the exploration and development of thermal water resources as well as the planning of the necessary pipeline infrastructure. The aim was to establish a specialized greenhouse zone where geothermal energy would enable year-round vegetable production.


The use of geothermal energy for greenhouse cultivation did not remain merely a plan on paper. In June 2023, drilling operations in Çaxirbeg reached thermal water with a temperature of 65 degrees Celsius at a depth of 750 meters. Ozan Balcı, then governor of Van and state-appointed trustee of the Metropolitan Municipality, announced plans to increase the number of geothermal wells. The water was to be used to heat greenhouses.


The agricultural use of geothermal energy is therefore an implemented component of the project. At the same time, the development of the valley’s geothermal resources expanded significantly in geographical scope over the following years.


Criticism over discharge of thermal water


As drilling operations expanded, their ecological impact also came under greater scrutiny. As early as the summer of 2026, environmental groups in Van drew attention to the discharge of thermal water from the drilling areas. They warned that liquids containing heavy metals could enter irrigation systems and the Koçköprü Reservoir.


Residents also report that contaminated thermal waters from the current operations are being discharged into the valley. There are concerns about the potential impact on soil, water resources, agriculture and, consequently, the livelihoods of the villages.


However, the information available so far does not indicate which heavy metals have been detected in connection with the current operations or at what concentrations. Water contamination therefore remains one of the key issues that must be clarified as development of the area continues.


Zilan Valley is a geologically sensitive area


Interest in the region is linked to its considerable geothermal potential. At the same time, it is a complex geological system. A study published in 2022 in the Journal of the Institute of Natural Sciences of Van Yüzüncü Yıl University identifies around eleven thermal water sites along the Erciş-Zilan-Ilıca Valley. The springs are largely aligned parallel to the Zilan Fault.


The study describes the Zilan Fault as an active, northeast-to-southwest-trending left-lateral strike-slip fault. Thermal waters reach the surface along the fault structures. Active tectonics and volcanism are also the basis of the region’s geothermal potential.


In addition to the hot springs, this natural environment includes groundwater, travertine formations, river terraces and the Zilan River. The scientific study thus documents the close interconnection between the valley’s geological and hydrological structures. However, it does not examine the specific environmental impacts of the current drilling and development activities.


Nearly 9,000 hectares put out to tender for geothermal development


Tenders issued in 2024 illustrate the scale the development has now …

title: What will Nunavut look like by the end of the century?
content:
By the end of this century, there’s an even chance that winter temperatures will exceed 10 C across much of


Heavy rains wash out a bridge in Pond Inlet on Sept. 5. (Photo courtesy of Andrew Tagak)


Nunavut, and that glaciers in western Canada could lose more than 75 per cent of their ice, say scientists behind a new climate change forecast,

Canada’s Changing Climate.


That report, released in September by climate scientists with Environment and Climate Change Canada and other academics, predicts what Canada’s Arctic might look like if average global temperatures exceed pre-industrial levels by 1.5 C.


That’s the threshold most nations committed, under the 2015 Paris Agreement, to avoid crossing in order to prevent the most severe and irreversible impacts of climate change.


It also considers what could happen if average temperatures rise to 4 C above pre-industrial levels.


The planet is expected to exceed the 1.5 C threshold in the next few years, according to a United Nations Environment Programme

report

 on climate change also released in September. The Arctic has already warmed three times faster than the global average since 1970, according to the federal Environment Department.


Many climate scientists agree some impacts, like sea-level changes, glacier melt, and permafrost thaw, will be irreversible. The oceans are projected to lose sea ice as well, but this loss may be temporary if temperatures stabilize. These changes will alter ecosystems and habitats in significant ways.


Sea ice reflects far more heat than the ocean does, for instance.


A road once used by ATVs in Pond Inlet on Sept. 5, 2026, is damaged following coastal erosion. (Photo courtesy of Andrew Tagak)


“You see ice- and snow-covered surfaces replaced by dark water that’s now absorbing more heat,” said Gregory W. Thiemann, associate dean of the Faculty of Environmental and Urban Change at York University.


Permafrost also operates as a carbon sink. When it thaws, it releases greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide and methane into the atmosphere, contributing to an increase in global greenhouse gas emissions. The northern permafrost region, which covers Canada, Alaska, Siberia, and Greenland, contains up to three times the amount of carbon currently in the atmosphere, which is why even small releases drastically influence global emissions, a 2025

study

 in the journal Science highlights.


Permafrost thaw also causes the ground itself to sink. This causes landslides and coastal erosion, threatening homes, roads and other critical infrastructure.


The damage could be “catastrophic,” said Daniel Fortier, a University of Montreal geography professor who studies permafrost, climate change and adaptation in the North.


“The High Arctic is reacting very strongly,” he said, adding permafrost thaw will persist at a rapid pace for some time before the ground begins to stabilize once again.


“Images we see of landslides and gullies forming and things like that, it’s true, it’s happening, but it’s not going to stay like that for 30 years,” he added. “It’s a short-term response.”


Cameron DeLong, director of the Government of Nunavut’s Climate Change Secretariat, described permafrost thaw as the most pressing issue communities are facing.


“We’re seeing the impact of that on a variety of fronts,” he said, adding his office works with builders to ensure they can access the right information about how to plan projects with climate resilience in mind.


Thermosyphon systems, which measure underground temperatures, have been integrated into many buildings in Nunavut, including the new airport terminal in Rankin Inlet, according to Nunavut’s Transportation and Infrastructure Department. These systems, like the one at the Iqaluit Airport, can also be used to remove heat from below to stop thawing.


DeLong said the GN’s adaptation and mitigation priorities include expanding maps of permafrost and climate hazards, which is currently happening in Iqaluit; staying up to date on coastal erosion; emergency planning to assess how well communities are prepared for major weather events like flooding; and updating infrastructure like culverts to reduce the chances of heavy rain causing flooding.


Heavy rain in Pond Inlet last month caused damage to roads and culverts throughout the hamlet.


Resident Andrew Tagak said the flooding was unlike anything he had seen before.


“This year was definitely different,” said Tagak, who is 37 and has lived in …

author: Josiah David Quising
title: Family, advocates remember 1987 killing of peasant leader, son
content:
Almost four decades later, they still remember. Friends and family held a memorial and candle lighting activity on October 3 to remember Valeriano Caro and his son who were killed 39 years ago by members of the Composite Reaction Force, a unit of the Regional Special Action Force, under the Cory Aquino administration.

Caro was a peasant leader from Kilusang Magbubukid ng Pilipinas (KMP) and chairperson of the Kahublagan sang Mangunguma sa Isla sang Panay (KAMIPA).

He and his son Rolito were killed in Barangay Galang, Oton, Iloilo on October 3, 1987. The memorial and candle-lighting were held on the roadside near the site where they were killed.

According to his wife in a report published by Amnesty International in 1988, Valeriano and her son were taken by the military at around 9:25 a.m. and were shot by a military officer just 70 meters from their own home.

On his 39th death anniversary, Valeriano’s family recalled his dedication to the plight of farmers in Panay.

“His legacy lives on in the continuing struggle to free farmers from landlessness, from bondage to the land, and from abuses at the hands of the regime,” Panay Alliance Karapatan said in a statement. (DAA)

author: Unknown
title: Balık tutmak için denize açılmıştı: Maden işçisi İlker Mızrap kayboldu
content:
Bartın — Bartın'ın Amasra ilçesinde balık tutmak için 4,5 metre uzunluğundaki teknesiyle denize açılan maden işçisi İlker Mızrap'tan (35) haber alınamıyor. Sahil Güvenlik Komutanlığı ekipleri, Mızrap için denizde arama çalışması başlattı.

Büyük Liman'dan dün saat 16.00 sıralarında teknesiyle denize açılan İlker Mızrap, geri dönmedi. Dün saat 19.00 sıralarında eşine ‘Balık tuttum, geliyorum’ mesajı atan Mızrap'a ulaşılamadı.

Ailesinin 112 Acil Çağrı Merkezi'ne yaptığı ihbar üzerine Batı Karadeniz Sahil Güvenlik Grup Komutanlığı ekipleri ve balıkçılar tarafından denizde arama çalışması başlatıldı.

Arama çalışmaları denizde 3-4 mil açıkta devam ederken, Mızrap’ın ailesinin endişeli bekleyişi sürüyor.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: winter oak
title: Modernity, metal and infernal inversion
content:
by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article

here


One of the great wonders of life, for me, is the way in which certain books find their way into my hands without me having actually

looked

 for them – indeed, it feels as if it were

they

 who were looking for

me!


Such was the case earlier this year when, after going for a walk beside the

Vidourle

 river, [1] I found myself wandering, for the first time, into a small warehouse filled with second-hand books for sale.


I emerged clutching two tomes – the book on the Druids by Jean Markale that was to inspire me to pen a

series of essays

 on the subject [2] and a work devoted to organic radical inspiration

René Guénon

 (1886-1951). [3]


The latter is in fact a special edition, from 1970, of a journal called

Planète

, which boasted an address in the very up-market Champs-Elysées in Paris.


There was plenty in its 140 pages to confirm and complement my understanding of Guénon’s life and thinking.


I was delighted to learn, in an extract from a book of Guénon’s that I have not yet read, that he had a positive view of the subject matter of the other book I bought that day.


Writing about the legend of the Holy Grail, he says that we do not know in whose hands this vessel was supposedly held before being filled with the blood of Jesus Christ, “but its recognised Celtic origin undoubtedly implies that the Druids would have played a role and must be numbered among the legitimate curators of primordial tradition”. [4]


I was also interested to learn how, as a maths student in Paris, young Guénon got involved with various strange “spiritual” and Freemasonic groups, before finding his own path.


If you are not lucky enough to unerringly identify the

right

 tradition for you, from an early age, exploring the

wrong

 ones has the advantage of teaching you what you are

not

, and thus clearing the way for you to become what you

are

.


I can identify with the way in which Guénon’s position, on any subject, always seemed to sit between or astride entrenched outlooks.


He argued, for instance, that although the Freemasonry of his time was a degraded version of the original, it could still serve to transmit authentic tradition – and he urged the Catholic Church to work with it to that effect.


But, at the same time, he was writing under a pseudonym for a review called

La France Antimaçonnique

 (‘Anti-Masonic France’), which led to some Freemasons condemning him as a “Jesuit agent”. [5]


With regard to the Church,

Planète Plus

 explains: “For René Guénon (

pictured

), Christianity was just one link in the chain of Tradition”. [6] He did not recognise the unique and totally unprecedented nature of the religion on which its adherents insist [7] and found it lacking in the esoteric aspect, being almost entirely exoteric. [8]


However, he also stressed the “perfect orthodoxy of Christianity” with regard to the primordial tradition which he sought to nurture and restore. [9]


Guénon was initially attracted to Hinduism, but since this was not a religion that accepted converts, in 1912 he became a Muslim, receiving the new name Abdel Wahed Yahia (‘Servant of the Unique’), which linked him to the Sufi tradition in Egypt, where, from 1930, he was to live out his days. [10]


Guénon was not involved or interested in the political sphere, but, as

Planète Plus

 notes, he was introduced into the Sufi world by Swedish anarchist artist

Ivan Aguéli

 (1869-1917), another organic radical inspiration. [11]


With his traditionalist outlook, it is perhaps not surprising that he should have had friends and contacts within the royalist

Action Française

, [12] but his interest in Eastern metaphysics did not go down well with everyone in that movement, not least its leader Charles Maurras, who openly mocked him in print on that account. [13]


What first attracted me to Guénon was his deep critique of industrial society in

La Crise du monde moderne

 (‘The Crisis of the Modern World’), another “chance” discovery in a second-hand bookshop, in fact.


Looking back over the centuries, he did not see the “progress” that we are conditioned to identify today, but rather a civilizational decline ever further into the

Kali Yuga

 and the darkest stages of that darkest age.


Writes Jean-Claude Frère: “There are so many contrasts between the traditional world that Guénon illustrates and the desacralised world in which we still now subsist – no knowledge is ever sought without …

author: The Canadian Press
title: Don’t mistake attendance at a press conference as support for a pipeline, chief says
content:
The grand chief of Treaty 8 First Nations stood behind Prime Minister Mark Carney and Alberta Premier Danielle Smith last week as they announced the

Pacific Link pipeline

 was the first project deemed to be in the “national interest” under the Building Canada Act.


But Trevor Mercredi said his presence shouldn’t be taken as a vote of confidence.


“I want to be clear that our presence should not be interpreted as support for the project,” Mercredi told The Canadian Press.


“Leadership was there to ensure our nations are not left behind. There are significant concerns that must be addressed, and it does not mean the pipeline is a done deal.”


The national interest designation under the Building Canada Act, puts the pipeline proposal in line for streamlined oversight and approvals.


The government said it will work over the coming year to complete consultations on the project itself, and to secure environmental safeguards, financing and Indigenous partnerships. It wants construction to begin in September 2027.


Some 130 Indigenous communities were given just two months for consultations on whether the pipeline should be granted a national interest designation, and that was still more than the government had planned.


A summary of those consultations posted online by the federal government says potentially impacted Indigenous groups decried a lack of information about the project, which they said prevented them from fully assessing its impact.


First Nations leaders have warned the federal government risks violating their rights with “national interest” designations through the Major Projects Office and the controversial Building Canada Act.


Carney promised his major projects agenda would not interfere with Canada’s obligations under the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples, nor their rights under the Constitution.


The UN declaration, which Canada adopted, states Indigenous groups must provide their free, prior and informed consent before decisions are made that could adversely affect their rights or lands.


Mercredi, who sits on the Indigenous advisory council in the Major Projects Office, said the Carney government appears to be flying the plane “as they’re building it” in a bid to strengthen the Canadian economy in the face of trade pressures with the United States.


“Sometimes when that happens you’re going to hit the ground, and that ground is our First Nations. Because regardless of any legislative changes, regardless of their processes, we still have our rights — they’re still intact,” Mercredi said.


“What they’re doing is weakening their own processes to develop the resources, which does not work in their favour if a (legal) challenge comes from a nation. They can still hold the key. That’s what people have to remember.”


First Nations along the ‘Pacific Link’ pipeline route are not happy with the Prime Minister’s announcement. Photo: Government of Alberta submission to Major Projects Office


It’s the same message he’s brought to the Major Projects Office. He isn’t sure if they’re listening — or if they even want to talk.


The government has been criticized by some Indigenous leaders for limited consultations, without providing much detail, about whether to designate the project under the act.


Mercredi said the Indigenous advisory council wasn’t tapped to offer feedback on if the consultation time frame was long enough or if a 10 per cent ownership stake for Indigenous groups was enough.


He said that, had he been asked, he would have said no to both.


“This is a concern that we have with the MPO. What is our purpose as an advisory council?” Mercredi said.


“We hear that we’re part of the process, but in instances like this it’s obvious that we are not.”


Assembly of First Nations National Chief Cindy Woodhouse Nepinak has said staff in the Major Projects Office do not understand how to work with First Nations communities and that “junior staffers” aren’t helping to build relationships.


She also said CEO Dawn Farrell has been unavailable to meet with leadership, including at Assembly of First Nations gatherings.


The Canadian Press has reached out to the Major Projects Office for comment but has not yet received a response.


Lawyer Jesse McCormick, co-chair of the Liberal party’s Indigenous Peoples’ Commission and a lawyer with Pape Salter Teillet LLP, questions how the national interest designation and eventual pipeline construction could have looked if …

author: ACG
title: French High School Students Rise Up
content:
From September 17

th

, high school students and staff staged blockades throughout France. This was to protest deteriorating educational conditions. The tempo of these blockades and demonstrations increased on September 29

th

 and 30

th

.


Lack of teachers, teaching assistants, special needs assistants, and nurses; poorly insulated and unrenovated facilities; and untenable class schedules… All high school students in France are suffering the consequences of insufficient funding for the national education system. This has sparked a nationwide mobilisation that is shaking the media and the government.

The national education budget has increased by 30% since 2017, so why is the situation in high schools deteriorating? For the start of the 2026 school year, approximately 4,000 teaching positions were eliminated in both public and private schools across France. Then there is Parcoursup (1) and its unfair selection system, which relies on “digital filters”. Then, in higher education, the freeze on housing benefits will prevent the most vulnerable from finding accommodation. Not to mention the “Welcome to France” decree imposed by the government before the summer, a blatantly anti-immigration project that aims to increase tuition fees for non-European international students. In short, for all high school students, stress is mounting regarding their future studies, all while enduring gruelling schedules and conditions that make optimal learning impossible.


A mass movement emerged. But on October 1

st

, the government sent in its riot cop attack dogs, and there was brutal repression, particularly in working class neighbourhoods. There were mass arrests of students, more than 5,000 in one week. Beatings, injuries, flashball shots, tear gas, mutilations—the number of injured is high.  This has not, so far, deterred the movement, with huge demonstrations across France on October 6

th

.


From the Union Communiste Libertaire website:


“Parcoursup is blocking lives.” With these words, a high school student summed up on Tuesday the reasons for the blockade of his school, a blockade that was part of the widespread student movement that has been mobilizing for a week to demand resources for education. Understaffed personnel, dilapidated buildings, overcrowded classrooms

“We lack everything”

 cry the students exposed daily to the stress of constant selection.


In working class neighbourhoods, students are sent to programs they didn’t choose, programs whose curricula are sometimes very opaque. Year after year, educational policies are reduced to managing a workforce in training and increasingly restrictive regulations. Student mobilisations in these neighbourhoods can take on more violent forms and are less like traditional demonstrations. How can we be surprised when we know the social and racial violence they endure daily? And let’s not be mistaken: when students take revenge on their schools, they are symbolically rebelling against this entire system of oppression and selection. We therefore warn staff against the knee-jerk moral condemnation that would dismiss this movement out of hand.


All these young people, who refuse to let their gaze towards the future be fixed only on catastrophe, make us proud.


This generation is aware of the systematic dismantling of its schools, the budget cuts being made at its expense, and the hostility directed towards it. In recent years, it has mobilsed against police brutality, for climate justice, and so on. This high school student movement is therefore not an isolated phenomenon. Its expansion across France since the initial blockades in the Paris region, and its alignment with the public sector strike on September 29th, is not a coincidence but rather the result of conditions shared throughout the country.


There’s plenty of money: let’s take it all! 450 billion: that’s the public money from the French rearmament plan, a windfall for the arms industry to maintain French imperialism. 655 million: that’s the funding allocated to developing AI in the public sector, without any consultation with employees on the usefulness of this tool, but simply to create opportunities for speculation. 1,400 positions: that’s the planned creation for the police and gendarmerie to continue the repression of our legitimate protests. No one can call this a technical problem; it’s a political choice.

It’s a class struggle

 .


The Macron regime is increasingly concerned about this uprising …

title: Desinformación climática y extractivismo: organizaciones presentan una investigación en el Congreso
content:
Imagen: Asambleas del Curru Leufu (Río Negro).


El conflicto por el futuro del Golfo San Matías se libra en el territorio, las calles y los tribunales, pero también en el campo de la comunicación. Este martes 6 de octubre, a las 13, la Multisectorial Golfo San Matías, junto a Roots, la Asociación Argentina de Abogados/as Ambientalistas y la Red Ecosocialista, presentará en el Salón Auditorio del subsuelo del Anexo A de la Cámara de Diputados de la Nación (Avenida Rivadavia 1841, CABA), los resultados de una investigación sobre desinformación climática y extractivismo. En la charla, titulada «Desinformación climática, empresas transnacionales y medios de comunicación», presentarán los principales hallazgos de la investigación

 «Narrativas de desinformación en el Golfo San Matías», realizada en el marco de un programa de Roots junto a Climate Action Against Disinformation, que identifica un ecosistema de medios tradicionales y digitales, contenidos coordinados y publicidad paga que presenta el avance de proyectos petroleros y gasíferos en la Patagonia como desarrollo, empleo y progreso, mientras invisibiliza impactos socioambientales, información científica y voces críticas de las comunidades afectadas.

Por ANRed.


Este martes 6 de octubre, a las 13, la

Multisectorial Golfo San Matías

, junto a

Roots

, la

Asociación Argentina de Abogados/as Ambientalistas

 y la

Red Ecosocialista

, realizará en el Congreso de la Nación la charla titulada «

Desinformación climática, empresas transnacionales y medios de comunicación».

 Allí se presentarán los principales hallazgos de la investigación «

Narrativas de desinformación en el Golfo San Matías

«

, desarrollada por integrantes de la organización rionegrina en el marco de un programa internacional impulsado por

Roots

 y

Climate Action Against Disinformation

.


La actividad busca llevar al ámbito parlamentario una discusión que atraviesa de manera directa a las comunidades costeras:

cómo se construye consenso alrededor de proyectos extractivos y qué lugar ocupan los medios, las redes sociales y la publicidad digital en ese proceso

. Según la investigación,

en el caso del Golfo San Matías se detectaron medios digitales de reciente creación que simulan ser portales informativos locales, contenidos automatizados y repetidos y una fuerte inversión en publicidad

 para amplificar determinadas narrativas.


Imagen: Asambleas del Curru Leufu (Río Negro).


El territorio en disputa es una de las regiones de mayor biodiversidad del Atlántico Sur:

el Golfo San Matías y la Península Valdés albergan ballenas, delfines, lobos marinos, aves migratorias y numerosas especies marinas, además de contar con áreas naturales protegidas

. Sobre ese espacio avanzan proyectos hidrocarburíferos vinculados al oleoducto

Vaca Muerta Oil Sur

, un puerto petrolero en

Punta Colorada

 y la futura operatoria de

buques de GNL

.


La investigación reconstruye también el proceso político que permitió ese avance.

En 2022, la Legislatura de Río Negro modificó la Ley 3308, que desde 1999 protegía al Golfo de actividades hidrocarburíferas, para habilitar la construcción del oleoducto Vaca Muerta Oil Sur

. El estudio señala que aquella reforma se realizó

sin consulta previa a comunidades indígenas y en una sesión cuestionada por organizaciones socioambientales

. Desde entonces, distintas comunidades y asambleas sostienen acciones judiciales, movilizaciones, campañas y actividades para disputar el modelo de desarrollo impuesto sobre el territorio.


En ese contexto, la investigación identifica una construcción comunicacional que presenta los proyectos petroleros y gasíferos como sinónimo de progreso. El informe señala que empresas,

organismos estatales y medios convergen en una narrativa que enfatiza empleo, inversión, desarrollo y reactivación económica, mientras los impactos ambientales y las resistencias territoriales quedan relegados

. La investigación también detectó un crecimiento de nuevos portales digitales y publicaciones patrocinadas alrededor de momentos clave de la expansión del proyecto.


Uno de los aspectos más relevantes del trabajo es que amplía la definición de desinformación: «la

desinformación climática

 no funciona solamente a través de noticias falsas o datos incorrectos: opera en diferentes niveles a partir de

narrativas históricamente diseñadas, con financiamiento, construyendo artificialmente consenso, amplificando determinados discursos a través de …

author: Rizomatica
title: 2do Koneltun de diversidades travestis trans Mapuche en Fiske menuko – Río Negro Puelmapu
content:
El viernes 09 de Octubre comienza el 2do koneltun de diversidades travesti trans Mapuche en una inmersión lingüística del Mapuzungun, que incluye diferentes niveles de idioma. Este fütxa txawün, gran encuentro, es parte del fortalecimiento de la memoria y existencia de identidades sexuales y espíritus diversos pertenecientes y caminantes del mapuche ngen. El koneltun, que tuvo su primera versión en Txaytxayko/Nueva imperial, Gulumapu/Araucanía, se dará lugar en Füshke menoko/Gral. Roca, Puelmapu, provincia de Rio Negro. Durante la jornada, habrá además, talleres de cartografía travesti de tiempo y espacio guiado por Pewmayen Figueroa, un nütxamkawün/conversatorio sobre la identidad afro kurüche por Tiwa Curiqueo finalizando con un taller de Pintura y cosmovisión guiado por las artistas visuales Poleo Painemal y Shakin Huaiquil.


La fecha elegida corresponde a la conmemoración y práctica de memoria al cumplirse 534 años desde la invasión colonizadora que hasta hoy intenta arrasar los territorios y vidas preexistentes.


No es casual que el 2do koneltun se decida realizar en Fiske menuko. En este lugar Geo Colicheo de ATTS, histórica travesti mapuche, ngen ruka, junto con su comunidad trans diversa del Alto Valle de Neuquén, han luchado años para nombrar a Roca como un agente que lideró el genocidio en la Patagonia del lado argentino.


“En medio de los continuos desalojos y del plan de exterminio que están llevando los gobiernos de chile y argentina contra el pueblo nación Mapuche, sumado a los continuos recortes en derechos del colectivo travesti trans, urge reencontrarnos y articularnos sin fronteras en una fuerza potenciadora y diversa para decir basta de militarización, de extranjerización de tierras ancestrales y del transodio que sostienen líderes de ultraderecha y sionistas”.

Añade Pewmayen Figueroa, Araucanía andina, una de las organizadoras desde el Gülumapu.


“Entendemos profundamente que en el marco del genocidio liderado por Roca también existió un etnotravesticidio y un generocidio. Un atentado y eliminación de nuestras formas de vivir como comunidades diversas».

 Comparte Ayla Rúa travesti Mapuche Tewelche de waqül Güyew – ingeniero Jacobacci.


El encuentro incluirá el día domingo 11 de octubre una jornada de varieté plurisexual abierta a todo público desde las 17:00 en el predio de ATE, barrio Mosconi Fiske menoko/ Gral Roca. Esta actividad contará con la presencia de distintos artistas, música en vivo, venta de comida (plato único), además de micrófono abierto para quienes deseen compartir pensamientos y sentires.


Relevamos la imagen gráfica de Flor de Jarilla en nuestro encuentro como forma de hacer memoria de nuestra ancestra travesti mapuche arrestada injustamente en Viedma a principios del siglo XX. Aquella gran bordadora de tejidos, fue muy querida por las comunidades aledañas de lo que hoy se conoce como General Conesa. Honramos su memoria y valentía, tras ser detenida por ser una persona trans indígena habitando la Patagonia en plena campaña del desierto.


Esta información se publicó en

Radio Kurruf

.

author: Unknown
title: Kurdish women’s movement delegation visits COPINH in Honduras
content:
A delegation representing the Kurdistan women’s liberation movement visited COPINH in Honduras, in Mesoamerica. COPINH (Civic Council of Popular and Indigenous Organizations of Honduras) is an organization dedicated to struggle and resistance, composed primarily of self-administered indigenous communities.


The Lenca people are one of the indigenous peoples of Central America, primarily distributed in southwestern Honduras, though their territories extend as far as San Salvador. To this day, many communities continue to resist in the mountains of that area, basing their survival on agriculture and livestock farming, carried out without industrial methods and in harmony with nature. On the slopes and among the trees, they grow corn and coffee, with corn being the staple food for these peoples. Following the Spanish occupation, they resisted fighting the colonization with a war led by the legendary Lempira. Despite this, they were subjected to forced conversion to Christianity; however, this failed to erase ancient traditions that still persist today, such as the “compostura” (a ritual of thanksgiving to Mother Earth for her bounty) or the spiritual connection to rivers, the earth, and fire. The spiritual dimension permeates every aspect of life, including political work: every assembly and every important gathering begins with the construction of an altar, on which—in addition to photos of the martyrs—earth, corn, incense, and candles of different colors are placed, carrying the purifying power of fire.


The Lenca communities, drawing their strength from their leader Berta Cáceres, have decided to carry on Lempira’s resistance and fight against those who seek to destroy their lands, their identity, and their very existence. COPINH is an organization founded on March 27, 1993, in response to the call of the Lenca communities, who decided to rise up to defend life, territory, and dignity. Since then, it has served as the organizational space where these same communities come together to fight in defense of their rivers, mountains, culture, and rights as indigenous peoples. They define themselves as follows: “COPINH is a space where we learn, analyze, dream, and act collectively against the injustices afflicting our peoples. We have based our struggle on three pillars: anti-capitalism, anti-patriarchy, and anti-racism. Through them, we confront the powers that seek to dispossess us, divide us, or silence our voices.”


Berta Cáceres was one of the founders of COPINH


The principal founder of COPINH was Berta Cáceres, born in 1971, who possessed the ability, education, and discipline—along with the love and determination necessary—to channel the Lenca people’s anger over the expropriation and destruction of their lands for the sake of capitalist interests, leading them to significant victories against extractivism. Her strength and charisma inspired many communities to organize, fight, and hold their ground in the struggle, even as the companies seeking to destroy their territory carried out a brutal crackdown, killing and forcing countless indigenous community activists into hiding. Berta was a woman and a feminist, recognized as a leader by the Lenca people for her actions and her closeness to them. We can recall here some of her most famous quotes, such as “Wake up, wake up, humanity: there is no time left!” and “Mother Earth—militarized, fenced off, poisoned, where basic rights are systematically violated—demands that we act.”


In fact, COPINH’s struggles have focused on defending the land, opposing deforestation, and opposing dams that were destroying rivers. In particular, it is worth recalling the struggle against the hydroelectric dam on the Gualkarque River, planned by the Honduran elite in collaboration with the Chinese multinational Sinohydro, which would have blocked one of the most vital waterways in Lenca territory. This river is not only a source of water and life, but also the home of sacred spirits that must be free to flow and not be stopped by dams built for extractive purposes. Led by Berta, the communities rose up and ultimately succeeded in preventing the dam’s construction, asserting that they were not defending nature but were part of nature itself, which was defending itself. This struggle led to severe repression; local witnesses report finding the bodies of their comrades thrown into the river and carried downstream by its current. author: Justice Not Jails
title: Stop the closure of Aboriginal community-controlled YiSSA housing
content:
Residents and the wider community are organising to stop the Northern Territory Country Liberal Party (CLP) government’s decision to close the Yilli Short Stay Accommodation (YiSSA) in Garramilla/Darwin.

YiSSA is an Aboriginal community-controlled facility that provides low-cost short-stay accommodation. It is used by people undergoing renal dialysis, families escaping domestic violence, homeless residents and people and families visiting Garramilla to access essential services.

When the CLP government’s announced YiSSA’s closure in July, 230 residents were reportedly living there, including 85 children. A further 300 people were on the waiting list.

YiSSA is owned by a private company, Ausco, while the land is owned by the NT government. The CLP government offered $3 million to buy YiSSA, but Ausco rejected the offer as too low. The federal government then announced it would contribute $3.5 million to assist the NT government in keeping YiSSA open.

The CLP government refused to purchase YiSSA. Instead, it has decided to evict residents and relocate them to Batchelor, more than 100 kilometres from Garramilla.

YiSSA’s proposed relocation to Batchelor will disconnect residents from public transport, services, employment opportunities and support networks, as well as schools for children who have been living at YiSSA. It will restrict people’s ability to access essential healthcare, as they will be outside the Danila Dilba catchment area, and there is no public transport between Batchelor and Garramilla.

The NT already has the highest rate of homelessness, sitting at nearly 12 times the national average.

The CLP government’s decision to evict YiSSA residents will make this worse. It will also put hundreds of vulnerable people needing to access renal treatment and schooling in a highly precarious position.

YiSSA residents are urging the CLP government to stop the eviction. The government’s decision has also sparked deep concerns from Aboriginal service providers and NT legal organisations.

Amid the controversy over the CLP government’s eviction of YiSSA residents, and in the final days leading up to the eviction, the NT government is hosting the Australian Homelessness Conference in Garramilla.

Justice Not Jails has organised a demonstration on October 7, outside the conference, calling on attendees to pass a motion urging the CLP and the federal governments to reverse the decision.

[Sign the petition to stop the closure of YiSSA housing here. Attend the community demonstration at 8am, October 7, outside the Darwin Convention Centre.]
