title: DEM Party: Events of October 6–8 must be fully investigated
content:
The Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) commemorated those who lost their lives during the protests of October 6–8, 2014, on the twelfth anniversary of the events and called for a full investigation into what happened. The party also demanded the immediate release of the politicians convicted in the Kobanê case.


The protests erupted in October 2014 during the attack on Kobanê by the terrorist organization Islamic State (ISIS). People took to the streets in numerous cities across the country in solidarity with the resistance of Kobanê’s population against ISIS and to protest against the Turkish government’s support for the jihadist group. The demonstrations and the violent events that followed resulted in numerous deaths.


According to various human rights organizations, 54 people were killed during the protests and violent clashes involving demonstrators, police, the military and organizations affiliated with ISIS, including 47 HDP members. “We respectfully commemorate our citizens who lost their lives during the protests of October 6–8,” the DEM Party stated. Even twelve years later, demands for a comprehensive investigation into the events remain unanswered, it added.


Instead of investigating the circumstances surrounding the events, the truth was obscured and proceedings that the DEM Party describes as the “Kobanê conspiracy trial” were brought against leading politicians of the then-HDP. The defendants included former HDP co-chairs Selahattin Demirtaş and Figen Yüksekdağ, as well as members of the party executive at the time. Some were sentenced to decades in prison, while an appeal remains pending.


The DEM Party explicitly linked its demand for their release to the ongoing peace and democratic society process aimed at resolving the Kurdish question. Social peace, the party said, also requires an end to unjust and unlawful judicial proceedings. “The rulings of the European Court of Human Rights must be implemented, and our friends who were prosecuted in the Kobanê conspiracy case must regain their freedom without delay,” the party stated.


Clarifying the events of October 6–8 and ensuring justice are crucial for social peace and a democratic future, the party said. “We will continue our struggle for truth, justice and freedom,” the statement concluded.

title: YRK announces the death of guerrilla fighter Çekdar Paytext
content:
The Eastern Kurdistan Defense Units (YRK) announced the death of their fighter Çekdar Paytext, who lost his life in an accident in the Pêncewîn region of Southern Kurdistan (Northern Iraq) on September 2, 2026. In a statement released by its Press and Communications Center, the YRK extended their condolences to the Akan family and the people of Kurdistan and commended his life and path within the movement.


Çekdar Paytext’s birth name was Barış Akan. He was born into a patriotic family in the province of Amed (Diyarbakır) in Northern Kurdistan and grew up in an environment closely connected to the Kurdish freedom movement. His older brother, Nizam Akan, who used the nom de guerre Çekdar, had lost his life in 1994. When Çekdar Paytext joined the guerrilla ranks in 2023, he adopted his brother’s name in his memory.


The YRK paid tribute to him as a committed fighter whose life, it said, was marked by a deep bond with his comrades, his homeland and the philosophy of Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan. Quoting his own writings, the YRK cited a passage reflecting his understanding of guerrilla life: “What matters is the organization. All comrades are prepared to give their lives for one another.”


“Çekdar Paytext will remain in our memory as a symbol of comradeship,” the YRK stated. “Realizing our fallen comrades’ dreams of a free life is our most fundamental task. Our commitment is to the promise of carrying the flag entrusted to us by the martyrs to victory,” the statement said.


The identity details of the fallen YRK fighter is as follows:


First-Last Name: Barış Akan


Nom de Guerre: Çekdar Paytext


Birthplace: Amed


Date and Place of Martyrdom: 2 September 2026, Pêncewîn

title: Iraqi Prime Minister: Agreement reached on the withdrawal of Turkish troops
content:
Iraqi media have reported details of a meeting between Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Zeydi and tribal leaders.


According to the reports, the Iraqi Prime Minister said that funds recovered through corruption investigations would be transferred to the “Development Fund.” He emphasized that the rule of law and Iraq’s independence in decision-making would be safeguarded.


Zeydi reportedly praised the tribes for supporting the government and drawing attention to the country’s most sensitive issues. He announced that five armed groups were prepared to hand over their weapons, describing the move as a practical step.


Addressing the presence of the Turkish military on Iraqi territory, the Iraqi Prime Minister reportedly said that talks had been held with Turkish officials on a number of issues and that an agreement had been reached on the withdrawal of Turkish forces from Iraqi territory.

title: Bakırhan calls for work to begin under Öcalan’s coordination
content:
DEM Party co-chair Tuncer Bakırhan has called for concrete steps in the peace and democratic society process as the new parliamentary year begins. The Council for Disarmament and Strategic Coordination must begin its work under the coordination of Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan. At the same time, he said, necessary conditions must be created for Öcalan to work freely, hold talks and communicate.


Bakırhan made the remarks at the DEM Party’s first parliamentary group meeting of the new legislative year. He devoted a substantial part of his speech to the peace process and the political and legal steps he believes must now be taken. “One concrete action is better than a thousand words,” Bakırhan said. Mutual trust, he added, can only be established if the developments so far are now followed by practical steps.


‘Disarmament requires a legal counterpart’


Bakırhan described the peace process as a scale with two sides. Disarmament, he said, must be matched by legal safeguards. “If the laying down of arms has been placed on one side of the scale, the law must be placed on the other. Because disarmament is a matter that requires a legal counterpart,” the Kurdish politician said. The same, he said, applies to the dissolution of the PKK (Kurdistan Workers’ Party). “Obstacles to the recognition of democratic rights and legal guarantees must be removed. If dissolution is on one side, legal guarantees and politics must be on the other. The political and legal dimensions of the process must therefore now become as concrete as the steps already taken by the Kurdish freedom movement.


‘Coordination Council must work under Öcalan’s leadership’


Bakırhan attributed a central role to the Council for Disarmament and Strategic Coordination, stating that the bodies and commissions established for the process must now begin carrying out their responsibilities in practice. “This council must begin its work under Mr. Öcalan’s coordination as soon as possible,” Bakırhan said. “To make this possible, the conditions necessary for Öcalan to work freely, hold talks and communicate must be ensured. At the same time, he must be able to maintain regular contact with the parties relevant to the process.”


The demand for appropriate working and communication conditions for Öcalan has long been one of the DEM Party’s central demands in the peace process. His role, the party argues, must not merely be recognized without also creating the conditions necessary for him to exercise it in practice.


‘Monitoring Commission must begin its work’


Bakırhan also called on parliament to assume responsibility and said that the Monitoring Commission provided for under the framework law must be established without delay. Its role will be to monitor the implementation of the process, address problems that arise, hold talks with the parties involved and initiate the necessary legislative measures. “We, as the DEM Party, are ready to assume responsibility,” Bakırhan said. He also called on all other parties to take responsibility in this historic process.


“No one has the right to exhaust the hope for peace”


Bakırhan also addressed the twelfth anniversary of the events of October 6–8, 2014. He described the period as a “very dark chapter” and called for those responsible for the deaths at the time to be identified. Twelve years later, he said, the events have still not been fully investigated. At the same time, he called for the politicians imprisoned in the Kobanê case to be released. “Our friends who were prosecuted in the Kobanê conspiracy case must finally regain their freedom.”


Bakırhan also criticized the government over allegations of corruption, access restrictions imposed on media outlets, the imprisonment of journalists, femicides and the continuing injustices resulting from emergency decrees (KHK). What matters now, he said, is advancing the peace process in a way that meets society’s expectations. Bakırhan warned against allowing the current phase to remain mired in uncertainty: “No one has the right to exhaust the hope for peace through uncertainty and keep postponing society’s expectations.”

title: 10-week ‘Women, Justice and Memory Vigil’ against femicides launched in Amed
content:
The Amed (tr: Diyarbakır) Network for Combating Violence announced launched a “Women, Justice and Memory Vigil” against femicides and suspicious deaths of women.


The vigil began outside the Diyarbakır Courthouse today and will continue at the same location every Tuesday for 10 weeks.


Participants carried a banner reading “Women Hold a Vigil for Justice and Memory,” along with photographs of women who had been killed. Representatives of numerous political parties and civil society organizations attended the vigil on its first week.


Reading out the press statement, lawyer Cansel Talay said they had come together because they refused to forget or remain silent in a country where women are killed by men and where their deaths are left unresolved by being labeled “suicide,” “accident” or “suspicious.”


‘Femicide is a war directed against the truth and existence of women’


Talay stated the following: “When a woman’s life is ended, the entire future she could have lived is taken from her as well. The years she would have lived, the words she would have spoken, the paths she would have walked and the dreams she would have realized are all left incomplete. For this reason, we emphasize that women are not merely numbers, case-file numbers, newspaper headlines or statistics. The systematic and continuous targeting of women’s lives is femicide. This femicide is a war directed against the truth and existence of women, who are the bearers of historical and social values. These murders are not isolated incidents, but the result of patriarchy, impunity and a male-dominated system that claims authority over women’s lives.


We would like to emphasize that memory is not merely about remembering. It is also a way of defending women’s right to life and challenging gender inequality and all structures that fuel male violence. The justice we demand is not limited to a verdict delivered after death. It is a broader and more complex issue. We want women to be protected while they are alive, reports of violence to be taken seriously by the relevant state institutions, suspicious deaths to be effectively investigated in all their aspects, and obligations to provide protection to be fulfilled.


A ‘suspicious death of a woman’ does not describe the manner of death; it describes the suspicion that investigative authorities are obliged to resolve. When a death is classified as suicide or an accident before all evidence has been collected, that suspicion has not been resolved; the truth has been left in the dark and those responsible have been allowed to go unpunished. We are here to ensure that the truth is not left in the dark and that no one is forgotten.


In the first week of the Justice and Memory Vigil, we are bringing into our collective memory the stories of women who lost their lives in different cities between September 25 and October 5 and whose cases we have been able to obtain information about. At the same time, we have not forgotten women who were killed in earlier periods, many despite having filed complaints and requested protective measures, and whose pursuit of justice continues or whose legal proceedings have recently seen new developments.


At this first vigil, we will tell the stories of Ayfer Çakmak from Diyarbakır, Fatma Çiğil from Kocaeli, Betül Arık from Sakarya and Nalan Temelkıran from Kütahya. We will also commemorate Buse Akgün Gök, who lost her life in Ankara; Dr. Özlem Gültekin Çelik, whose suspicious death in İzmir remains under investigation; Gökçe Alkan, who was killed in Bursa; and Zekiye Can, who died under suspicious circumstances in Mardin, as part of our Justice and Memory Vigil.


These names do not constitute a complete list of all women who lost their lives during the period we have identified. They represent the first record of our vigil, compiled from cases that have become public and about which we have been able to obtain information.


We know that our responsibility regarding women’s right to life is not limited to the week in which a death occurs. Days, months or even years may pass after a woman’s death. But the demand for the truth to be uncovered and justice to be served does not disappear with the passage of time.


For us, memory means remembering, leaving a trace and refusing to let others forget. Justice is the pursuit of conscience and truth; it means confronting what has happened and carrying our collective responsibility for women’s right to life into the present.

title: CDK-F launches France-wide campaign against drugs and criminal networks
content:
The Democratic Kurdish Council in France (CDK-F) has announced a nationwide community campaign aimed at protecting young people from drugs, violence and criminal networks. The campaign will include prevention and awareness-raising initiatives, support for families and young people, and greater efforts to connect young people with sports, cultural, social and educational activities. “Drugs and the recruitment of young people into criminal structures are not individual problems,” the CDK-F stated. “They affect the future of young people as well as their families and social coexistence in local communities.”


The CDK-F underlined that the sale of drugs to young people, their exploitation for criminal activities and the portrayal of violence as an expression of strength must not be tolerated. “Structures that profit from drug trafficking, threats, violence and the exploitation of young people must not be accepted within society. Gang crime is neither freedom nor success,” it stated.


The campaign will not be limited to condemning drug trafficking and criminal networks. Its main focus will be on prevention, awareness-raising and creating alternatives for young people. Information events for young people and families are planned in various French cities. Meetings with addiction specialists will also be organized, along with information sessions on the methods criminal networks use to recruit young people and involve them in their activities.


Another key focus will be social media. Young people will be made aware of how they can be drawn into criminal networks through digital platforms. At the same time, the CDK-F plans to work directly with families and strengthen efforts to connect young people with sports, cultural, educational and social activities. “Young people affected by addiction must not be marginalized. Instead, they must be given access to professional healthcare and psychosocial support.”


The CDK-F also emphasized that the campaign is not directed against any particular population group, identity or community.” Drugs, violence and organized crime are problems that affect French society as a whole. At the same time, such developments within its own community structures must not be ignored. Addressing a problem does not mean disparaging our society. On the contrary, it is an expression of our responsibility toward our young people, our families and our future,” the council stated.


The umbrella organization called on families, young people, associations, women’s and youth organizations, educators and other social actors to actively participate in the campaign. “We will not leave the future of our young people to criminal organizations,” the statement concluded.

title: Senior ISIS member arrested following attack in Hawija
content:

author: Soraya Kishtwari
title: Home Secretary Defends Palestine Action Ban by Invoking ‘Skinheads’
content:
Shabana Mahmood has defended the government’s ban on Palestine Action by saying its supporters should face the same law as “skinheads” who back a neo-Nazi organisation.


Speaking on

the Rest Is Politics podcast,

 the home secretary was asked about the thousands of people arrested for publicly supporting Palestine Action. 


Mahmood, who was previously a vocal supporter of the Palestinian cause, said that while she was “very uncomfortable” seeing people she knew “falling foul” of the law, it had to be applied consistently.


“When you get a group of skinheads standing outside a mosque, holding up a placard saying ‘I support National Action’, I’m going to want the Section 13 support offence to be applied,” she said.


“And I’m going to want the police to go and arrest those people… And I’m going to want them to degrade the capacity of a white supremacist terror organisation to recruit more members.”


National Action is a neo-Nazi organisation which was proscribed under the Terrorism Act in 2016.


Palestine Action was proscribed by former home secretary Yvette Cooper in July 2025, making it a criminal offence to belong to or express support for the group.


“You have to do these jobs in a consistent way that stands the test of time,” Mahmood said. “I’m not going to reopen every decision every previous home secretary has made. Was it lawful? Yes it was. Does it meet the legal test? Yes it does.”


She added that a decision to repeal the ban would involve having “to literally relitigate everything”.


Asked what triggered the government’s decision to outlaw the group, she said: “It’s proscribed because it’s met the test for proscription within the Terrorism Act,” and that “the facts of their behaviour and the escalatory effect of their behaviour” were contributing factors.


Critics of the ban, however, argue that the central question is not whether Section 13 should be applied consistently, but whether Palestine Action should have been placed under terrorism legislation in the first place – and whether expressing support for the group should constitute a terrorism offence.


A spokesperson for campaign group Defend Our Juries accused Mahmood of “missing the point entirely”, saying she had provided “no evidence that Palestine Action should have been proscribed in the first place”.


The

Morning Star quoted the spokesperson

 as saying: “The fact that elderly and disabled people are being arrested as terrorists for holding signs should be no less shocking.” 


Defend Our Juries has organised multiple protests against the ban on Palestine Action, resulting in mass arrests, most recently at the

Labour Party conference in Liverpool

.


Mahmood’s comments strike a different tone to that of foreign secretary Ed Miliband who told delegates in Liverpool that Britons were

“right” to be outraged by the plight of Palestinians

.


In June, the court of appeal upheld the government’s decision to proscribe Palestine Action, overturning an earlier high court ruling that found the ban unlawful. This was followed by a

supreme court ruling in July

 allowing Palestine Action founder Huda Ammori to appeal the ban. The hearing is expected this autumn.

author: Mada Masr
title: Syndicate submits prosecution complaint regarding Matsda2sh journalists’ torture, Interior Ministry denies claims
content:
Prosecutors are still investigating the six Matsda2sh journalists who are being held in remand detention for 15 days, effective from the day they were brought before the Supreme State Security Prosecution, according to Hossam Bahgat, the director of the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, whose lawyers are leading the defense counsel representing the journalists. 


Prosecutors largely repeated the same line of questioning the journalists faced in the first round of interrogations, focusing on the platform’s editorial policy and their professional backgrounds, according to lawyers informed of the investigations.


 Journalists from the independent fact-checking platform had previously been held at National Security Agency premises for almost an entire week, following the arrest campaign that targeted six of the outlet’s team members. 


After several of the journalists described being forced to record false “confessions” on camera and being subjected to torture at the hands of the National Security Agency officers, the Journalists Syndicate published a

statement

 on Monday night saying its members had decided “unanimously” to file a complaint with the public prosecutor regarding the charges.

 


Although prosecutors had decided that one of the journalists should be sent for a forensic medical examination to document signs of torture, he is yet to be brought in for medical examination, according to lawyers informed of the investigation who spoke to Mada Masr.


One lawyer told Mada Masr he had learned that a heightened security presence was observed on Tuesday morning around the Egyptian Forensic Medicine Authority at Zeinhom morgue, which he said could indicate that the journalists may be sent for the examination in the coming hours. Another lawyer said that the 24-hour delay in conducting the examination may have caused the visible signs of torture to fade beyond forensic recognition.


The Interior Ministry

denied

on Monday that the Matsda2sh journalists, whom it described as Muslim Brotherhood elements, were tortured or mistreated.

 It said that the torture claims were merely “echoed in the Journalists Syndicate statement and on some pages affiliated with the terrorist Muslim Brotherhood” and described the claims as an attempt by the defendants to “evade the charges attributed to them.”


In its Monday night statement, the syndicate board stressed its commitment to legally defending all practicing journalists, regardless of whether or not they have syndicate membership, citing the syndicate law, which requires that journalists already be practicing the profession as a prerequisite to membership.


The Interior Ministry had differentiated, in its announcement of the journalists’ arrest, between those who have syndicate membership and those who do not. 


The syndicate issued its statement following an emergency board meeting on Monday evening that ran for over four hours and was marked by a tense atmosphere, a syndicate source told Mada Masr. Tensions arose over disputes regarding the syndicate’s responsibility to provide legal defense for the five journalists who are not members and the need for action in response to their accounts of torture.


Several members of the syndicate’s general assembly gathered outside the meeting hall while the discussions were underway, chanting for the council to extend the syndicate’s defense to all detained journalists, whether or not they are members, saying “all six are our colleagues,” “you who are silent, speak up and don’t be afraid,” “freedom for Matsda2sh” and “no to torture.”


The syndicate said in its statement that it had submitted memoranda to prosecutors clarifying the legal basis of their intervention in defense of all the practicing journalists.


The syndicate board also indicated the Matsda2sh journalists’ commitment to regularizing their employment status under Egyptian law as evidence of their good intentions, noting they had taken legal steps to document their employment status in 2023 following an incident in which three of the platform’s team were briefly arrested and their names publicly circulated, while a fourth was taken into custody for two days before he was released following the syndicate’s intervention. None of the platform’s team were charged at the time.

Syndicate submits prosecution complaint regarding Matsda2sh journalists’ torture, Interior Ministry denies claims

 first appeared on

Mada Masr

.

title: Lottare nell’Antropocene: tossicità, grandi opere e conflitti territoriali
content:
Se la crisi ecologica è una crepa nel sistema, quali strumenti di pratica e d’analisi possiamo usare per forzare la breccia? Quali categorie ci permettono una lettura del presente che colga nella catastrofe reali possibilità di conflitto?


Da Radio Blackout


In questo

primo episodio di Cicorie

, cominciamo ad affrontare il problema della periodizzazione e dei termini che usiamo per designare il nostro tempo inaugurando una delle rubriche che ci accompagnerà nelle varie puntate: “

Indovina chi viene a Cene?

”.  Capitalocene, Plantagiocene,Tecnocene, Cthulucene, Proletariocene: tantissimi sono stati i neologismi che hanno caratterizzato il dibattito accademico dell’ecologia politica. Nonostante questa iper-produzione di termini specifici non ci convinca, vogliamo comunque partire da alcune riflessioni che questi stimolano per approfondire il punto di vista sulla realtà. Per iniziare ci inoltriamo nel dibattito più classico: quello tra Antropocene e Capitalocene. Un dibattito che caliamo nel contemporaneo e che facciamo interagire con ciò che è successo e succede al di fuori delle aule universitarie.


Ne parliamo nella prima parte dell’episodio insieme a

Emanuele Leonardi

, Professore di sociologia all’Università di Bologna e compagno storico dei collettivi di Ecologia politica.  


Segue un approfondimento sul volume “

Tossicità. Voci, saperi e conflitti in una zona di sacrificio

” (Orthotes, 2026), lavoro di ricerca di comunità incentrato su vita e lotta nei territori limitrofi al polo chimico di

Spinetta Marengo

 in Alessandria, segnati dall’avvelenamento da PFAS.


A chiaccherare con noi di conricerca e inquinanti eterni

Eleonora Bechis

, ricercatrice, compagna e curatrice del testo insieme a Vittorio Martone, Rosalba Altopiedi e Andrea Filippo Ravenda. 


Nell’ultima sezione del programma, ci rivolgiamo direttamente ai territori e alle forme di mobilitazione che continuano ad animarli, conquistando spazio e assumendo dimensioni sempre più conflittuali.

Ripercorriamo la marcia in Bassa Val di Susa “

Fermiamo insieme l’Avigliana-Orbassano

” del 3 ottobre attraverso i contributi e le voci di chi vi ha preso parte per poi spostarci a Reggio Emilia, dove la mobilitazione cittadina di

Bosco Ospizio

 si trova a un punto di svolta. A fare il punto della situazione in collegamento con noi da Reggio Alessio, dell’

Assemblea Permanente per la difesa del Bosco

.


Concludiamo con una breve panoramica sull’attualità – tra ritorno all’atomo in Italia, crisi energetica e caro carburanti – mettendo in

focus

 le recenti

mobilitazioni degli agricoltori

 del Centro e Sud Italia, che tra nuovi blocchi stradali e vecchie rivendicazioni tornano a prendere la parola e a scendere in strada.


Qui sotto l’audio integrale dell’episodio!

author: anonerror
title: Dualismo organizativo, la clase y la revolución: algunas aclaraciones para seguir debatiendo
content:
Dualismo organizativo, la clase y la revolución: algunas aclaraciones para seguir debatiendo


	En los últimos meses se ha desarrollado en distintos espacios libertarios una polémica alrededor del especifismo, la organización anarquista, la lucha de clases y la posibilidad de una transformación revolucionaria en el siglo XXI. El artículo de Capi Vidal,

“El especifismo, el proletariado y el anarquismo del siglo XXI: trazas de una polémica inacabable”

, resume buena parte de este debate en el que, además, toma posición frente a los diferentes autores que han participado en él.


Creo que merece la pena responder, no tanto para añadir otro capítulo a una polémica interminable, sino porque algunas críticas al especifismo parten de una comprensión bastante particular de lo que es esta corriente. Y, al mismo tiempo, porque algunas de las preguntas planteadas por Vidal, Tomás Ibáñez, Gustavo Rodríguez, Laura Vicente o Alfredo Apilánez son perfectamente legítimas y deberían ser asumidas por quienes nos consideramos anarquistas organizados, sociales y revolucionarios.


No se trata, por tanto, de demostrar que unos tienen toda la razón y otros ninguna. Se trata de aclarar conceptos y, sobre todo, de preguntarnos qué puede significar hoy ser revolucionario desde el anarquismo.


¿Qué es realmente el especifismo?


Empezaría por una cuestión bastante sencilla: el especifismo no es una doctrina cerrada ni un intento de reconstruir literalmente el anarquismo de hace cien años.


El término se utiliza para describir una corriente de organización anarquista que se desarrolló fundamentalmente en América Latina, especialmente a partir de la experiencia de la Federación Anarquista Uruguaya (FAU), y que posteriormente recibió influencias tanto del anarquismo social anterior como del plataformismo, pero que desarrolló sus propias concepciones estratégicas.


Su idea central tampoco es especialmente complicada: los anarquistas necesitamos organizarnos específicamente como anarquistas y, al mismo tiempo, participar en las organizaciones y luchas sociales donde se encuentran las clases populares.


Esto suele denominarse “dualismo organizativo” u “organización dual”:


Por un lado tenemos la organización política anarquista, formada por militantes que comparten unos principios, un análisis y una estrategia.


Por otro, las organizaciones sociales o de masas: sindicatos, organizaciones vecinales, de vivienda, estudiantiles, campesinas, feministas, etc., donde participan personas con diferentes posiciones políticas y que se organizan alrededor de necesidades e intereses concretos.


Ambas expresiones no son dos mundos separados; entre ambas se produce una sinergia y relación. Y precisamente la cuestión ahí es cómo se establece esa relación entre ambos.


Una organización anarquista específica no debería sustituir a un sindicato, a una organización de vivienda o a un movimiento popular. Tampoco debería convertirse en una dirección exterior que decida qué deben hacer los movimientos. Su función es intervenir dentro de ellos, organizarse, aportar propuestas, ampliar su número de adherentes y su implicación, aprender de las experiencias y tratar de desarrollar una orientación revolucionaria. Esta concepción anarquista nace ya con Bakunin, con su Alianza de la Democracia Socialista, y continúa estando presente en organizaciones contemporáneas influidas por el especifismo, el plataformismo o el dualismo organizativo. Como son Liza, Embat, Xesta, Hedra… o, en menor medida, FAI, Horizontal, Redes Libertarias… que suelen priorizar lo cultural o los proyectos sociales concretos libertarios.


Por eso resulta un poco extraño identificar automáticamente la organización política especifista con un partido en su concepción socialdemócrata o leninista. Un partido leninista pretende conquistar el poder político del Estado y dirigir el proceso desde su propia organización. El especifismo parte de la idea contraria: “la transformación revolucionaria debe ser obra de las propias clases populares organizadas.”


Naturalmente, esto no significa que una organización anarquista específica no pueda desarrollar dinámicas de vanguardia. Puede ocurrir. Es un riesgo real si no se entienden las dinámicas y funciones de las organizaciones, y merece ser discutido. Pero una cosa es señalar ese riesgo y otra afirmar que la existencia de una organización política anarquista implica necesariamente vanguardismo.


¿Y qué pasa con la Plataforma?

Your government, like most of our governments, is corrupt and secretive. author: Julia Conley
title: New Report Reveals Walmart’s Patents for Price-Gouging Tech
content:
Walmart’s US CEO said customers’ order value jumps 40 percent when they use the company’s AI shopping assistant.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

As Walmart attempted to debunk research into its pricing practices by watchdog group Groundwork Collaborative on Monday, the organization released a new report detailing more than a dozen patents the $833 billion corporation holds or has applied for — all aimed at monitoring customers’ behavior to determine what products to market to them, deceiving them about an item’s price, and upcharging them.

“Corporations don’t spend years building high-tech pricing tools, hiring experts, and filing patents just to let them collect dust. They do it because they see a path to higher profit — one that runs right through everyday consumers’ budgets,” said Lindsay Owens, president and CEO of Groundwork and the author of the book Gouged: The End of a Fair Price—And What That Means for Your Wallet.

On Monday, Owens and Elizabeth Pancotti, Groundwork’s vice president of policy, advocacy, and research, released “The Walmart Watchtower: Patents Speak Louder Than Pledges,” noting that Walmart CEO John Furner just recently attempted to do damage control on Owens’ reporting in Gouged regarding the company’s artificial intelligence-enabled pricing tactics.

While Walmart executives have “openly touted” the ability of “Sparky,” the AI shopping assistant the company launched last year, to push customers to spend an average of 40% more during a shopping trip, Furner insisted last month that Walmart will “price the product, not the person.”

But Groundwork said that beyond its deployment of Sparky, “Walmart’s own investments and patents suggest that the retail giant is building a vast arsenal of tools that can be used to track shoppers and even potentially determine what they pay.”

The report reveals that technology patented by Walmart can:

Estimate a child’s age through past purchases and steer families toward certain products and price points as they grow;

Run pricing experiments on shoppers to determine how much they are willing to pay, by pushing prices higher and higher over a period of time;

Withhold coupons from customers the store believes will be willing to pay full price;

Change prices of items based on what is already in a customer’s cart; and

Set the price a customer sees in search results on Walmart’s website based on their purchase history, where they live, and other identifying characteristics, with one customer being charged $90 while another sees a $110 price tag.

The company has also filed applications for technology that could:

Use facial recognition, in-store cameras, Wi-Fi signals, and heart-rate or glucose data to measure how shoppers react to any given product;

Monitor customers’ social media activity to determine whether they should be offered a coupon or be expected to pay full price; and

Monitor customers’ daily routines, including kids’ sports practices, exercise classes, work, and visits to friends and relatives.

“Walmart has amassed the most intimate information about its customers and is developing the technology that can be used to put that data to work at checkout,” said Owens. “Shoppers will have to decide whether to believe Walmart’s patent applications or its PR statements.”

As the report was released, Dan Bartlett, Walmart’s executive vice president of corporate affairs, released a public letter accusing Owens of “mischaracterizations” regarding the company’s pricing practices.

“Walmart does not and will not use an individual customer’s personal information, income, shopping history, urgency, or willingness to pay to set an individualized price,” said Barlett. “We do not engage in dynamic pricing, raising prices in response to a hot afternoon or an approaching snowstorm, for example.”

He also said Groundwork has wrongly taken Walmart’s patents “as evidence that we will pursue individualized or dynamic pricing,” and said the company has “committed not to.”

Although Bartlett denied that the company uses AI to upcharge customers, Walmart US CEO Dave Guggina told investors just last month that “when customers engage with Sparky, their average order value jumps 40%.”

Public claims deserve a public response. Especially when they’re inaccurate and misleading.@owenslindsay1 has repeatedly suggested Walmart uses or plans to use technology …

author: Chris Walker
title: Two-Thirds of Americans See Social Media as Harmful to Democracy
content:
Experts have pointed out that “falsehoods” on social media often “outperform true information” due to algorithm choices.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

New polling indicates that nearly two-thirds of Americans believe social media has had a negative effect on democracy.

In an international poll published by Pew Research last week, only 34 percent of Americans said they believe social media has had a positive impact on democracy, while 64 percent said the advent of social media has been a bad thing for democracy.

Sixty-eight percent of Americans polled said that access to the internet and social media has made people more informed. But 81 percent said the internet/social media has made people more divided in their political opinions, and 87 percent said it has made people more easily manipulated by false information and rumors.

Notably, the poll showed little change in perception among U.S. respondents from four years ago — around the same rate of Americans expressed skepticism over social media’s “benefits” to democracy in 2022. But the share of the global public who view social media as detrimental to democracy jumped substantially, coming close to or matching (or, in some cases, exceeding) American respondents’ attitudes. Indeed, in 16 of the 26 countries observed, there was measured growth in cynicism regarding social media’s effect on democracies.

Michael Best, a computer science professor at Georgia Tech who has examined the relationship between the internet and democratic systems, explained some of the threats posed by social media in 2023.

“Social media is one of the threats to democracy right now because it has become a cesspool in many instances of disinformation and of extremist content,” Best explained in an interview that year. “But there’s something a little more nefarious, which is that scholars have shown that falsehoods and extremist content on popular social media platforms outperforms true information and more bland content. That’s a design decision of these platforms.”

Best suggested that things didn’t have to be this way — social media users could “change the business models” by using “different platforms online that don’t have these features,” to create “a business incentive to not allow a total food fight in every online social media community,” he said.

New internet-based technologies, such as artificial intelligence, are threatening democracy in other ways, including causing significant harm to the fourth estate by making it more difficult for independent media to be reached on search engines. In a joint op-ed by Maya Schenwar, board president for Truthout and director of the Truthout Center for Grassroots Journalism; Negin Owliaei, Truthout’s editor-in-chief; and Ziggy West Jeffery, Truthout’s executive director, the three explained how Google’s decision to prioritize AI-generated summaries was harmful to independent publications.

“We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight,” they wrote, citing Truthout’s own experiences with the search engine’s changes. “This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.”

We know Truthout is not the only news organization taking a massive hit amid Google’s abrupt decision to prioritize showing internet users AI summaries instead of relevant news articles. Our peers in independent media and beyond — including among grassroots base-building organizations that depend on traffic — are struggling to stay above water.

“Every week brings a new encroachment of AI into our lives. This is terrifying, but it should also be motivating: We all have a stake in this struggle,” the trio concluded. “Don’t let AI take over our search results or our lives without a fight.”

We now have three full months of data since Google changed its search to feature AI results. The numbers are worse than we anticipated. Overall readership that comes to Truthout through Google is down 54 percent against last year. The number of new readers who discover Truthout via Google searches is down 49 percent, and returning users from Google are down 51 percent.

We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

title: Le Collectif antivalidiste de Marseille accueille des nouvelleaux !
content:
Le Collectif antivalidiste de Marseille organise un moment d'échange pour accueillir ses nouvelleaux membres le 1er novembre à 16h au Planning familial !


Depuis un an et demi, nous sommes un collectif autonome qui rassemble des personnes handies, malades chroniques et alliées en lutte contre l'oppression systémique de nos corps et de nos esprits non-valides. On organise des actions et des événements à Marseille pour radicalement sortir nos existences du silence et apprendre ensemble à détruire le validisme partout où il est !


On organise un goûter pour accueillir des nouvelles personnes qui voudraient nous rejoindre le

dimanche 1er novembre à 16h

 dans le jardin du Planning familial (106 boulevard National, 3e arrondissement).


INFOS D'ACCESSIBILITÉ.

 Le lieu et les sanitaires sont accessibles aux PMR. Dans une perspective d'autodéfense sanitaire, le port d'un masque FFP2 sera systématique si la météo nous pousse à l'intérieur (un stock gratuit avec différentes tailles de masques sera dispo). Pour n'importe quel besoin qui peut faciliter ton accès à ce moment, n'hésite surtout pas à nous contacter par mail à collectifantivalidistemarseille@mailo.com, on fera de notre mieux pour trouver une solution ensemble.


Pour en savoir plus sur le Collectif antivalidiste de Marseille


Nous sommes un collectif autonome de lutte et d'autodéfense antivalidiste qui rassemble des personnes handies, malades chroniques et alliées à Marseille dans une perspective intersectionnelle.


Le validisme est absolument partout autour de nous. À l'école, au travail, dans les familles, entre ami·es, dans l'espace public, dans la plupart des rues et des bâtiments, dans les discours institutionnels, dans les espaces militants, partout dans la société et dans les réflexes sociaux, tout est conçu par et pour les personnes valides, celles dont les corps et les psychés sont perçus conformes à la norme. Nous, toutes et tous les autres, les corps difformes et les psychés anormales, les handicapé·es et les malades chroniques, nos existences sont invisibilisées.


Le validisme est un système intégré et toléré par toute la société qui nous exclue, nous isole et nous prive de notre autonomie, quand il ne nous tue pas. Pendant que les gouvernements, les administrations et les associations caritatives se gargarisent sur notre dos au nom de la prétendue “inclusion”, notre parole est systématiquement instrumentalisée et dépolitisée.


Pour radicalement sortir nos existences du silence, notre collectif a pour but de mener des actions directes à Marseille pour dénoncer les lieux inaccessibles ou les comportements validistes, organiser des temps d'auto-éducation publics sur les luttes handies et pousser vers des dynamiques d'entraide entre pairs ou entre valides et non-valides.


Si nous avons fait le choix de la mixité au sein de notre collectif (c'est-à-dire qu'il ne se compose pas que de personnes concernées par le handicap ou la maladie, mais aussi de personnes valides), c'est que nous avons besoin d'allié·es qui se responsabilisent. L'idée est que la charge mentale et physique de la lutte antivalidiste soit partagée.


On tâtonne comme on peut : notre collectif apprend en faisant et nous sommes loin d'être irréprochables ! L'espace est ouvert aux personnes qui ne sont pas forcément à l'aise et qui ont envie d'apprendre.


Pour nous contacter par mail : collectifantivalidistemarseille@mailo.com

author: By Brendan Maslauskas Dunn, Contributor
title: Waging Peace in a Time of War in Thailand and Cambodia
content:
The fog of war has not fully dissipated from the mountains and dense forests of Cambodia and Thailand’s borderlands, well over a year after the two nations became ensnared in deadly clashes. It is still unclear who fired the first shot, although both governments blame the other side for starting the conflict. Both armies left a wake of destruction in many of the normally peaceful, serene villages and towns along the border. It may take years to repair the damage caused by the fighting. 


At the peak of the conflict,

rockets rained down on houses and hospitals in Thailand

. Civilians at a 7-Eleven in Thailand met their fate in an inferno of flames

caused by a Cambodian rocket that struck the building

. In Cambodia, children ran in a panic when their schools were evacuated. Thai F-16 fighter jets flew over Cambodia on

bombing missions

.


The ancient Khmer (Cambodian) temple and UNESCO World Heritage site

Preah Vihear was barraged by ordnance from the Thai army

,

shattering parts of it into pieces

.

. Hundreds of thousands of Thai and Khmer civilians were displaced from their villages, and moved into makeshift shelters. Many have not yet returned home.


In total,

at least 30 civilians in Cambodia, and 44 in Thailand were killed

, with many more wounded. The Royal Thai Army laid to rest 43 soldiers. The Cambodian government has not publicly disclosed the total number of soldiers killed but

estimates range from 73 to over 160

.


 A victim lies on the ground in front of the 7-Eleven and gas station that was struck by a 

Cambodian rocket in Sisaket Province, Thailand. Eight people were killed, and 13 injured. Scores of civilians have been killed in both Thailand and Cambodia during the conflict. (Source:

Royal Thai Army / AFP

)


Both countries agreed to a ceasefire in December, brokered by the U.S. and Malaysian governments, but this peace hangs delicately in the balance in a political environment overshadowed by the dominance of hyper nationalism and militarism, and the rapid spread of hatred and bigotry between Thai and Khmer people. Much of this has been fueled by social media, conspiracy theories, and AI. Since the conflict started, ruling elites and military hardliners in Thailand and Cambodia have consolidated more power and tightened the gears of repression.


Kosal Sorphea sits at the funeral ceremony for her mother, Mut Savern, 43, who was a 

Cambodian soldier. Mut was pregnant when she was killed by a bomb dropped from a Thai F-

16 jet during an airstrike in December 2025. (Photo: 

Cambodianess

)


In the midst of the politically volatile whirlwind where many citizens have lined up in support of their respective governments and militaries, a scattered network of Thai and Khmer activists forged solidarity with each other, spoke out against war and demanded peace at a time when it seemed impossible, even dangerous to do so.


‘We Firmly Oppose this War’


Paw Cratchang said she shut down her social media accounts when the fighting started between Cambodia and Thailand. The nationalist views expressed by many Thais, even from her friends, was “overwhelming,” she says. “People always think that war is black and white. They should have someone to lose and should have someone to win, and they hope the winning side is going to be their country,” she says. The reality, she explains, is much more complex.


“I was born in Surin province. It’s on the border with Cambodia,” she says. “Sometimes we speak a little bit of Thai and Cambodian language. It’s kind of like a mix.” Growing up so close to the border left an imprint on her understanding of national identity. “We are friends, we are relatives. People cross the border many times. They don’t think there’s a difference between each other,” she says of Khmer and Thai people.


And although she is a Thai citizen she says her family is “100% Lao” but were “colonized by Thailand” over the years. She also feels a deep affinity with and affection for Khmer people. 


Thai activists protesting against the Thailand-Cambodia border conflict on December 13, 2025 

in Chiang Mai, Thailand. The signs on far left and right both say ‘No war.’ The sign at middle says ‘Get to the negotiating table to find a peaceful solution.’ (Source: 

Prachatai

)


Cratchang is an anarchist. She holds a sharp critique of nationalism, nation-states, and borders. The Cambodian-Thai border, to her, is an arbitrary line that has ushered in a history of disaster and violence …

author: Steven Rodas
title: Water Bills Surged More Than Other Costs in US Homes Over a Decade
content:
A new analysis finds the price of water increased faster than inflation, grocery prices, and median household income.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Drinking water costs spiked faster than inflation, grocery prices and median household income, researchers at nonprofit Food & Water Watch outlined in a first-of-its-kind report released Tuesday.

The average community water system increased household drinking water prices by 62 percent between 2015 and 2025 — with costs in Louisiana, Maryland and New Hampshire having particularly steep rises, according to the 17-page report. California also stood out in the data when it comes to seeing expensive water bills.

Kristin Dobbin, an assistant professor of Cooperative Extension at the University of California, Berkeley, who was not involved in the report, called the analysis “extremely important.”

The finances behind drinking water are “not something we’ve had a big picture view on across the country before,” Dobbin told Inside Climate News on Monday, noting that broad trends are much easier to review for national electricity rates.

“We need to situate the water conversation within these broader concerns about affordability,” she said. “Certainly, it’s striking that they found just how quickly water costs have risen in the decade.”

Food & Water Watch gathered and analyzed 2025 water billing data for the nation’s 500 largest community water systems, which serve more than 155 million people, or 45 percent of the country. The nonprofit compared that data to household water bills from 2015.

The new report — “Surging Water Costs amid the US Affordability Crisis” — notes that last year, the average U.S. water system charged households $531 a year for 60,000 gallons of water, an estimate of annual average water use per household.

Eleven years ago, water systems typically charged about $336 a year per household, which is about $457 in 2025 dollars when adjusted for inflation.

While water bills vary greatly nationwide, a corporate water system in San Jose, California, had the highest price for water in the report, charging $1,416 annually in 2025.

Fifty-two percent of the 25 most expensive systems reviewed by Food & Water Watch were in California, despite the state’s systems representing just 18 percent of the 500 systems in the dataset.

In Louisiana, Maryland and West Virginia, water bills grew about twice as fast as state median household incomes, the report found.

In New Hampshire, bills grew nearly five times faster.

Mary Grant, the water policy director at Food & Water Watch, said West Virginia jumped out in the report.

Many water utilities claim that their bills are largely still affordable for median-income households, she said.

“But in some places like West Virginia, water bills are becoming unaffordable for a typical household at the median income, and that’s really a warning sign,” Grant said. “I think that we really need to have federal action to stop this crisis before more people suffer from unaffordable water bills.”

Affordability “is a legitimate challenge for many households,” said Jenn Kocher, a spokesperson for the National Association of Water Companies, which represents regulated, private water companies, which serve nearly 40 million U.S. customers.

Due to a publication embargo, Kocher could not review Food & Water Watch’s full report.

Still, after reviewing some of the findings Kocher said any assessment of water rates should also consider system performance, including reliability, water quality compliance and long-term infrastructure conditions.

Rising water bills “reflect sector-wide cost pressures, not ownership models,” Kocher, whose group has also fought for a permanent federal water-assistance program, said Monday. “In addition, rate comparisons should account for actual household usage and customer assistance programs, rather than posted rates in isolation.”

Why are water bills so high nationwide?

Dobbin, of UC Berkeley, said factors including inflation are having a big impact on the drinking water sector, which relies on specialized materials like treatment chemicals, a supply chain that was stressed during the COVID-19 pandemic and water infrastructure that is deteriorating nationally.

The Environmental Protection Agency recently found drinking water systems across the U.S. will need $625 billion in upgrades …

Dossier

Das Treffen des Europäischen Rats am 20./21.10. wird zum Abschottungsgipfel: Unter dem Label »Migrationspartnerschaft« werden Abkommen mit einer Reihe von Staaten in Afrika und Asien vorbereitet. Abahlali was formed at a meeting of 34 people held in Durban on 4 October 2005. When the movement celebrated its 21st anniversary in Durban on 4 October 2026 it had more than 200 000 members across five of South Africa's nine provinces.


In 21 years of struggle it has won large tracts of urban land, extracted significant policy concessions and resolutely opposed the xenophobia that is systemically used to divided impoverished and working class people in South Africa. It has also built strong connections with radical movements around the world and has, in recent years, moved towards building communes.


The struggle has come at a high cost. As of 4 October 2026 26 lives have been lost in the course of the struggle.


This archive runs from the movement's formation in 2005 till 4 October 2026 and includes a complete list of all the statements it has issued, memoranda delivered at marches as well as the articles and speeches by its members which are archived on the movement's website.

author: Julius Gavroche
title: French Youth Take the Streets against a Bleak Future
content:
from the

CrimethInc.

 collective, 06/10/2026


A Report


This past week, thousands of teenagers have taken the streets of France, clashing with police as they demonstrate against the deplorable conditions in their high schools and a rapidly collapsing future. This is a promising sign, shifting attention from the seemingly unstoppable rise of the extreme right to the question of what people can do on a grassroots basis to defend themselves. Our correspondents in Paris explore the situation in detail.


Another unprecedented summer of record

heatwaves

,

droughts

, and

wildfires

 throughout Europe underlines the desperate situation we are all facing today, while politicians of all stripes and their techno-industrial sponsors continue to turn a blind eye, forcing us down the path to catastrophe in the name of progress.


Hoping to turn the page on these environmental disasters, the French government has hurriedly shifted focus to other priorities. The coming months represent a crucial transition for Emmanuel Macron and his government, as they will bring Macron’s second term to a close, opening a new political era in France. Candidates are already battling to succeed Macron in power at the beginning of May 2027.


In the midst of this political spectacle, during an increasingly

menacing surge

 in the popularity of the National Rally (formerly, the National Front), the extreme-right party, it is especially meaningful that teenagers have started to organize at a grassroots level to defend themselves. This organizing gained momentum last week, when blockades of high schools, demonstrations, and riots erupted across France, taking everyone by surprise.


Students clash with police forces in Montpellier on October 2, 2026.


Licensed to Kill?


Since Macron was elected President for the first time in May 2017, the political discourse in France has been even more dominated by an emphasis on authoritarian and far-right ideologies in terms of security, immigration, and economic and social issues.


This political shift towards an even more aggressive form of governance has led to increasing state violence targeting the social movements and uprisings that have emerged since. From the eviction of the

ZAD

 at Notre-Dame-des-Landes in 2017 to the

riots

 following the murder of Nahel in 2023, not forgetting the

Yellow Vest

 sequence and the COVID-19 pandemic lockdown experimental

doctrines

, we have experienced a headlong plunge into a world of surveillance, repression, and loss of individual freedoms. This has become today’s new normal.


It was in this already suffocating context that last July, the French government decided to vote on a new bill giving police officers more latitude to use their firearms without consequences—a demand that the far right has promoted for years. If voted through, this legislation could set a

dangerous precedent

, as it would establish “a presumption of ‘legitimate use of arms’ by police and gendarmes ‘in the exercise of their duty’.”


Police arrest a student in Lyons on October 1, 2026.


In other words, not only will police officers be able to freely use their weapons if in any situation they claim to fear for their lives or the lives of others, but authorities will no longer have to prove that the officers acted within the framework of the law, as they are required to do today. It will be up to the victims and their families to provide evidence that the use of firearms was not justified. We can already see how this new law represents a legislative tool enabling law enforcement agents, and therefore, the state, to cover up future murders.


Unwilling to let such a law pass without resistance, political opponents and radicals, who had rightly rebranded this law the “license to kill,” decided to organize massive demonstrations and events throughout France on the weekend of September 18 to 20.

Thousands

 of people took part in these protests in different major cities alongside traditional leftist politicians, rights groups such as Amnesty International and the League of Human Rights, and various lawyers and magistrates’ unions.


In the meantime, another call for action reusing all the codes of the Yellow Vest movement spread online. The origins of this call remain obscure, as some national

newspapers

 have raised the possibility that AI-generated accounts had flooded social media platforms with this rumor on purpose. Nevertheless, media and politicians began commenting on this …

author: Andrés
title: Cuerpos que piensan, cuerpos que resisten: la danza tomó el Centro Cultural Universitario Paco Urondo
content:
Iara Pavanello, Dulcinea Segura Rattagan y Carolina Bergero, el equipo del IAE encargado de la curaduría del encuentro


Durante dos intensas jornadas, el Instituto de Artes del Espectáculo de la UBA reunió a decenas de investigadoras, bailarinas, creadores y docentes de distintos puntos del país y de Latinoamérica para pensar una pregunta urgente: ¿qué hacen los cuerpos cuando los poderes fácticos tienen tanto interés de desmaterializarlos? El VI Encuentro de Pensamiento sobre Danza y Prácticas Somáticas, titulado «Cuerpos en estado de resistencia» combinó ponencias académicas, talleres participativos, funciones y proyecciones de videodanza en un formato mixto que permitió seguir las actividades de manera presencial, y virtualmente. El Centro Cultural Universitario Paco Urondo fue el escenario para el despliegue artístico. Su arquitectura de estilo academicista funcionó como el cuerpo receptor del 6° enc

uentro de prácticas somáticas.

Por ANRed.


El 1 y 2 de octubre, el Área de danza y artes del movimiento del IAE-UBA,

que coordina la investigadora especialista en danza Dulcinea Segura Rattagan, junto al equipo que componen Iara Pavanello y Carolina Bergero

, organizó una nueva edición de su encuentro anual, que desde hace seis años viene consolidándose como uno de los espacios de reflexión sobre el cuerpo más importantes del ámbito académico porteño.


La convocatoria superó el formato de jornada universitaria tradicional:

43 ponencias distribuidas en dos días reunieron a más de cincuenta expositores/ as

, con una variedad de voces que incluyó a estudiantes de grado y posgrado, investigadores del CONICET, docentes de conservatorios, trabajadores de la salud y representantes de escuelas de formación artística.


Taller exploratorio de investigación corporal, por Soledad Manrique


Lo federal

fue una

 marca del encuentro

. A la participación de universidades porteñas y bonaerenses —la UBA, la UNA y la Universidad Nacional de Río Negro— se sumaron

expositoras de Chaco, Rosario, Córdoba y Neuquén

, además de la presencia internacional: Brasil, Chile, Colombia, Uruguay y España representados a través de ponencias que pusieron en diálogo tradiciones corporales y de la danza de muy variada procedencia. Del ballet barroco al zaar sudanés; desde la danza gawazi egipcia hasta las memorias somáticas de comunidades indígenas del Chaco argentino. La amplitud geográfica se tradujo en una conversación rica, donde

la pregunta por la resistencia se formuló desde contextos culturales y políticos diferentes

, sin perder nunca el hilo común.


«Estamos volviendo a casa» obra del grupo Bailarines toda la vida, del grupo de Danza Comunitaria dirigido por Aurelia Chimelli


La dinámica de trabajo favoreció esa multiplicidad. Las mesas temáticas, organizadas en bloques de entre cuatro y seis exposiciones breves, permitieron que cada jornada avanzara a ritmo ágil, con un diálogo rico de temas, que permitieron tender puentes entre un trabajo sobre eutonía y una reflexión sobre psicodrama, o con una investigación sobre danza y salud mental.

El tema: la resistencia

, sumada a la cuidadosa curaduría

fue un acierto.


La jornada del jueves tuvo una fuerte impronta práctica y artística.

title: Organizaciones sociales marchan a Capital Humano contra el ajuste y a la Corte Suprema por la recuperación de la Ley de Tierras
content:
Más de 70 organizaciones sociales, territoriales y piqueteras se movilizarán este martes 6 de octubre contra las políticas de ajuste del gobierno de Javier Milei y en rechazo al fallo de la Corte Suprema que dejó vigente la derogación de la Ley de Tierras Rurales. La jornada comenzará a las 13.30 con una conferencia de prensa frente al histórico edificio del Ministerio de Capital Humano (ex Desarrollo Social), a cargo de Sandra Pettovello, donde denunciarán el ajuste, la pérdida de ingresos y el desmantelamiento de políticas destinadas a los sectores populares. Luego, movilizarán al Palacio de Justicia, donde confluirán con una amplio marco de organizaciones que repudiarán el fallo de la Corte Suprema de Justicia de la semana pasada, que eliminó los límites para la adquisición de campos argentinos por parte de extranjeros. La jornada de lucha de los movimientos sociales busca también preparar nuevas acciones para el jueves 15 de octubre, cuando la Cámara de Diputados tiene prevista una sesión especial para tratar el DNU 70/23.


Más de 70 organizaciones sociales, territoriales y piqueteras se movilizarán este martes 6 de octubre contra las políticas de ajuste del gobierno de Javier Milei y en rechazo al fallo de la Corte Suprema que dejó vigente la derogación de la Ley N° 279 de Tierras Rurales. La jornada comenzará a las 13.30 con una conferencia de prensa frente al histórico edificio del Ministerio de Capital Humano (ex Desarrollo Social), a cargo de Sandra Pettovello, y continuará con una movilización hacia el Palacio de Justicia.


Imagen: CTA Autónoma.


“Más de 70 organizaciones territoriales, sociales y piqueteras que venimos luchando en los barrios contra la destrucción y el ataque sistemático a las condiciones de vida de la enorme mayoría de las y los trabajadores, nos convocamos este martes 6 de octubre a las 13 en el histórico edificio del Ministerio de Desarrollo Social para realizar una conferencia de prensa”, señalan en la convocatoria.


Concentración de la UTEP frente al Ministerio de Capital Humano contra el hambre.


“Esta situación se da en un cuadro de crecimiento de la desocupación y la precarización laboral, caída del consumo y cierre de empresas, mientras la mayoría de las familias se encuentra endeudada a niveles insostenibles para poder llegar a fin de mes”, sostienen las organizaciones. En ese mismo sentido, un informe del Instituto de Investigación Social Económica y Política Ciudadana (ISEPCI) calculó que la eliminación del programa Volver al Trabajo, efectiva desde abril de 2026, dejó sin ese ingreso a cerca de 950.000 trabajadores informales y afectó a más de tres millones de personas al considerar a sus grupos familiares.


Otro de los ejes está puesto en la asistencia alimentaria: «venimos, además, de sufrir el corte abrupto e injustificado de la entrega de alimentos a más de 45.000 comedores populares, situación por la cual la ministra Sandra Pettovello ha sido llevada a juicio». El reclamo contra la política social se articula además con la eliminación del programa Volver al Trabajo: “Milei eliminó el programa Volver al Trabajo, dejando a casi un millón de trabajadores sociales, cocineras, recicladores y otros trabajadores de la economía popular sin el único ingreso que percibían por trabajar”. La medida efectivamente alcanzó a cientos de miles de titulares y, según un informe del ISEPCI, implicó el retiro de unos $74.100 millones mensuales del circuito de consumo popular.


Foto: David Briasco.


Luego de la conferencia de prensa, anuncian: “marcharemos al Palacio de Justicia en repudio al infame y cipayo fallo de la Corte Suprema, que sostiene la extranjerización de la tierra mediante la ratificación del inconstitucional Decreto 70/23”.


Para las organizaciones convocantes, la cuestión territorial forma parte de una ofensiva más amplia: “este decreto no solo habilita la entrega del territorio nacional al capital extranjero, sino que agrava la situación de tenencia precaria que padecen los pueblos originarios y la población trabajadora, amenazada permanentemente por desalojos en terrenos recuperados mediante enormes luchas para defender un pedazo de tierra donde vivir y producir”. El reclamo se produce, además, después de una jornada federal el pasado 6 de agosto en la que organizaciones indígenas, campesinas, ambientales, sociales y sindicales se movilizaron contra la extranjerización de la tierra y denunciaron el proyecto de Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada.

title: Ebola Death Toll in DRC Tops 4,000; Trump USAID Cuts Fuel Outbreak
content:
We go to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the site of the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history. Health authorities believe the outbreak first began in January but was not detected until May, in part due to cuts in global health investments, like the dismantling of

USAID

. Since then, over 8,000 cases have been recorded, with more than 4,000 fatalities so far. From Bunia, Ituri province, the epicenter of the outbreak, we speak to Congolese journalist Akilimali Chomachoma. Chomachoma describes the strain on the underfunded Congolese healthcare system as the disease spreads. Many frontline workers have not been paid for months.


“We are seeing this outbreak emerge, and really unfurl, in a setting of decreased global health support,” says Craig Spencer, a doctor and public health expert based in the United States who contracted Ebola while on a medical mission to Guinea in 2014. “The U.S. has not shown up in the same way that it has in previous Ebola outbreaks.” Spencer also comments on the “unprecedented” measles outbreak in the United States, which he warns is likely to continue and lead to additional deaths.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Avex Río Cuarto: trabajadores se movilizaron por salarios, trabajo y ayuda económica
content:
Marcharon este lunes desde el Sindicato de la Carne hasta el Concejo Deliberante y la Municipalidad de Río Cuarto, en la provincia de Córdoba. Hace dos semanas la planta de Granja Tres Arroyos está paralizada.


Durante la mañana de este lunes hasta el mediodía, más de un centenar de trabajadores se movilizaron para exigir la regularización de la planta Avex SA (propiedad de Granja Tres Arroyos), el cobro de los salarios y el aguinaldo adeudado y un alivio financiero por parte del Estado.


“Hace tres meses que no cobramos y sólo hemos recibido bolsones de mercadería, nada más”, dijo Luis Fernández, delegado de la planta. “Hoy no hay nadie en la planta. No hay faena, ni guardia mínima ni nada. Está parada la planta hace dos semanas”, comentó y cuantíficó el número de los afectados: 200 empleos directo y 350, contando los indirectos (granja y planta de incubación).


Granja Tres Arroyos solicitó un Procedimiento Preventivo de Crisis en 2024 y el conflicto se trasladó a todas las plantas del país (seis, repartidas entre las provincias de Buenos Aires y Entre Ríos). Avex, por su parte, presentó su concurso preventivo de acreedores hace diez días.


“La situación es desesperante”


Cristian Francois, titular del Sindicato de la Carne, comentó respecto al petitorio presentado en el Concejo Deliberante de Río Cuarto: “estamos pidiendo que nos puedan subsidiar los impuestos, un subsidio económico como ya ocurrió en otras provincias, o también mercadería”.


Los gremialistas fueron recibidos por la presidenta del Legislativo, Ana Medina y por miembros de los bloques.


“Estamos desesperados. Tenemos mucha necesidad por el tema del colegio y el transporte”, plantearon. “Lo que queremos es que la empresa retome la actividad. Nuestros salarios se vuelcan completamente en la ciudad, así que lo que buscamos es que nos ayuden a salir de la situación financiera que tenemos”, dijeron y entregaron el petitorio, que será ingresado en la próxima sesión este jueves.


“No sabemos el rumbo que va a tomar la empresa. Días atrás se hablaba de que A.C.A. iba a retomar la actividad. Se cayó el negocio por una situación empresarial y volvimos a foja cero”, comentaron también los trabajadores.


“Lo único que queremos es trabajar”


En la Municipalidad fueron recibidos primeramente por Ariel Peralta, Subsecretario de Empleo y Formación Laboral y luego por el Secretario de Gobierno, Roberto Koch.


“Venimos a pedir que regularicen la situación de la empresa Avex del grupo GTA”, dijo el vocero del sindicato, Sergio González. “Venimos a visualizar y a ver si a través de ellos se pueden viabilizar algunas cosas. Lo único que queremos es trabajar”, insistió.

author: Corey Larocque
title: PQ’s Sonia Caron takes Ungava as her party wins minority government
content:
Nunavimmiut will be represented by Parti Québécois candidate Sonia Caron, who was elected Monday in Quebec’s geographically largest riding.


The PQ won a minority government in Monday’s provincial election, taking the largest number of seats in Quebec’s national assembly.


In Ungava, the massive riding that includes Nunavik and other parts of northern Quebec, Caron got 3,312 votes — 39.5 per cent of ballots cast, according to Élections Québec’s website.


Caron, originally from Chibougamau, is the director of professional development at the Centre de services scolaire de la Baie-James, which oversees trades programs in northern Quebec. She described herself in an

interview

 last week as a lifelong supporter of the PQ.


She had a 25-year career in education before making the jump to politics this year after she was approached by several parties to be their candidate.


Caron told Nunatsiaq News she got into politics because the lack of front-line health services and the need for clean drinking water in many remote communities need urgent attention.


“I told myself, ‘We have to do something,’ because our region is undergoing major upheavals, and public services are constantly deteriorating,” Caron said in an interview before the election.


Liberal Sandrine Rious finished second in the five-way race, taking 2,308 votes, or 27.5 per cent of ballots. Conservative Marc Damant got 1,447 votes (17.3 per cent) while the Coalition Avenir Québec’s Amélie Béchard received 863 votes (10.3 per cent) and Québec solidaire’s Antoine Côté got 452 votes (5.4 per cent).


There was no incumbent seeking re-election in Ungava. Denis Lamothe, who represented the riding since 2018, as a Coalition Avenir Québec MNA, did not run for a third term. He was elected in 2018 and re-elected in 2022.


Monday’s voter turnout in Ungava was 27.7 per cent with 8,557 of 30,849 registered voters casting ballots.


Across Quebec, voter turnout stood at a much higher 66.9 per cent, with 4.3 million of the province’s 6.5 million voters casting ballots.


Led by Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, who is poised to become premier, the PQ won 59 seats in the 127-seat assembly. To secure a majority government, a party needed to win 64 seats.


Historically, the PQ has been Quebec’s separatist party. During the campaign, Plamondon said a PQ government would hold a third sovereignty referendum during its first term — but only after U.S. President Donald Trump’s term ends in 2029. (Quebecers voted in sovereignty referendums in 1980 and 1995, choosing both times to remain in Canada.)


The provincial Liberals finished Monday in second place with 40 seats, followed by the Quebec Conservative party’s 19, and Québec solidaire’s nine.


The PQ win ended eight years of rule by the province’s Coalition Avenir Québec’s party, which did not win any seats in the assembly.


François Legault had led the Coalition party’s government from 2018 until April of this year, when he resigned as party leader and premier.


Legault’s departure made way for Christine Frechette to take over as premier earlier this year. She also lost her seat in the election.

author: Mag
title: „Refugee Law Clinics“ gegen den Mangel an unabhängiger Asylberatung
content:
Dossier


In einem

Interview von Niko Kappel vom 3. Juli 2018 bei „jetzt“


 erzählt Maximilian Oehl von

„Refugee Law Clinics“


, warum für einen Rechtsstaat unabhängige Rechtsberatung so wichtig ist: „…

Viele Menschen stellen generelle Fragen zum Asylverfahren. Wie lang es dauert. Ob man arbeiten kann. Ob man in eine eigene Wohnung ziehen darf und so weiter. Wenn ein Asylantrag abgelehnt wurde, muss man entscheiden, ob man dagegen gerichtlich vorgeht. Und genau da brauchen die Menschen unsere Unterstützung. (…)

Es gibt in letzter Zeit die Tendenz bei Behörden, Fälle immer schneller abwickeln zu wollen. Am schnellsten ginge das natürlich, wenn der oder die Betroffene nicht um seine Rechte weiß und sich deshalb nicht gerichtlich zur Wehr setzen kann. Das ist für mich aber konträr zur Idee des Rechtsstaates. (…) Es ist wichtig, dass es eine unabhängige Asylverfahrensberatung für Geflüchtete gibt. Das fordern auch die Wohlfahrtsverbände schon lange..

.“ Und mehr dazu und darüber:


Dobrindt stoppt unabhängige Asylberatung: Die Bundesregierung will ausgerechnet dort kürzen, wo Rechtsstaatlichkeit beginnt


Zur Notwendigkeit einer behördenunabhängigen Asylverfahrensberatung


„

Gem. § 12a AsylG fördert der Bund die behördenunabhängige, ergebnisoffene, unentgeltliche, individuelle und freiwillige Asylverfahrensberatung. In Sachsen erbringt unter anderem der Sächsische Flüchtlingsrat e.V. dieses Beratungsangebot. Hier erfolgen unzählige Beratungen unterstützt durch anwaltliche Supervision.


Die Finanzierung der unabhängigen Beratungsstrukturen in Asylverfahren ist über das Jahr 2026 hinaus gefährdet, da der Regierungsentwurf des Bundeshaushalts eine drastische Kürzung der Fördermittel von bis zu 80% vorsieht (

https://www.diakonie.de/informieren/infothek/2026/juli/diakonie-deutschland-unabhaengige-asylverfahrensberatung-wirkt


) Es bliebe lediglich die sogenannte unentgeltliche behördliche Rechtsauskunft durch das Bundesamt für Migration und Flüchtlinge (BAMF). Diese sieht jedoch weder eine individuelle Beratung, noch direkte Verfahrensfragen vor. Das BAMF ist zudem auch die zuständige Behörde, die inhaltlich über den Schutzstatus einer asylsuchenden Person entscheidet, sie soll also zeitgleich über Verfahrensrechte, Erfolgsaussichten und Rechtsmittel informieren und in der Sache entscheiden. (…)


Eine behördenunabhängige Asylverfahrensberatung ist ein wesentlicher Teil des ungehinderten Zugangs zum Recht.


Gerade Asylsuchende, die (noch) keine anwaltliche Vertretung haben, können wesentliche Informationen zum Verfahren erhalten und individuell vorbereitet werden. Effektiver Rechtsschutz setzt voraus, dass Betroffene ihre Rechte kennen und wahrnehmen können. Ein Asylverfahren ist komplex, an enge Fristen gebunden und in seinen materiellen wie prozessualen Anforderungen durch das GEAS kaum eigenständig zu durchdringen. Die unabhängige Beratung wirkt hier dem Machtgefälle zwischen der Behörde und der schutzsuchenden Einzelperson entgegen

.

(…)


Sollte die Bundesregierung keine ausreichenden Fördermittel zur Verfügung stellen, droht die Einschränkung der unabhängigen Asylverfahrensberatung bis hin zum kompletten Verlust. Laut Sächsischen Flüchtlingsrat e.V. existieren weder eine ausreichende Landesförderung noch kommunale Finanzierungsmodelle, die die Arbeit der unabhängigen Beratungsstellen sichern könnten (

https://www.saechsischer-fluechtlingsrat.de/2026/07/21/pressemitteilung-nein-zum-foerderaus-der-asylverfahrensberatung/


).


Eine faktische Abschaffung der unabhängigen Beratungsstrukturen durch fehlende Fördermittel läuft den rechtsstaatlichen Anforderungen an ein faires Asylverfahren zuwider

…“

Pressemitteilung der RAV-Regionalgruppe Ost vom 6.10.2026

 


„

Die unabhängige #Asylverfahrensberatung soll massiv (um 80%) gekürzt werden & nach Ansicht des BMI dann nur noch für „vulnerable“ Gruppen gelten, aber nicht mehr für alle, obwohl durch GEAS alles komplizierter gemacht hat.

Es ist kein Sparen, es ist Zerschlagen von unabhängigen Beratungsstrukturen

.“

Post von Hessischer Flüchtlingsrat vom 30.09.2026 auf bsky

 


Selbst das Bamf lobt die Asylberatung – doch Dobrindt sägt daran.


„

Eine Studie des Bundesamts für Migration bestätigt den Nutzen der unabhängigen Beratung von Schutzsuchenden

.


Das Forschungszentrum des Bundesamts für Migration und Flüchtlinge (Bamf) hat die behördenunabhängige Asylverfahrensberatung (AVB) evaluiert. Der mit einem halben Jahr Verspätung vorgelegte Bericht …
