title: Obdachlosigkeit und Profitwirtschaft (nicht nur am Beispiel Hamburg)
content:
Dossier


„…

Nur wenige hundert Meter Luftlinie von der Elbphilharmonie entfernt sind die Aussichten nicht ganz so gut. Zu Füssen der Hauptkirche St. Michaelis, allgemein nur Michel genannt, ist die Kehrseite des obszönen Luxuslebens zu besichtigen, das sich die hanseatische Upper Class gönnt. Hier machen Obdachlose „Platte“, versuchen – eingerollt in Schlafsäcke oder notdürftig in Decken eingewickelt – die kalten Winternächte zu überstehen. (…) Ende November starb der vierte Obdachlose in einer Nacht des Hamburger Winters 2018/19. Der etwa 50 Jahre alte Mann krepierte einsam in einem Fussgängertunnel unter der Lombardsbrücke zwischen Binnen- und Aussenalster. Erst zwei Wochen später wurde sein Tod überhaupt öffentlich, denn die Polizei fand den Vorfall nicht berichtenswert

…“ – aus dem

Beitrag „Hamburg: Zwischen Obdachlosigkeit und Dekadenz“ am 06. März 2019 im Untergrund-Blättle


 über (vor allem) die eine Seite der Profitjagd. Siehe dazu leider weitere, nur beispielhaft für alle Städte in Deutschland:


Protestaktion von obdachlosen und armen Menschen am 07.10.2026 am Düsseldorfer Rathaus: Gegen ein Bettelverbot – die Armut bekämpfen und nicht die Armen


„

Am Mittwoch, den 07.10.2026 wird die Verschärfung der Düsseldorfer Straßenordnung im Ordnungs- und Verkehrsausschuss behandelt. Deshalb protestieren am Mittwoch, den 07.10. um 15.30 Uhr arme und obdachlose Menschen, die in der Altstadt die fiftyfifty verkaufen oder betteln, unter dem Motto „Armut bekämpfen, aber nicht die Armen!“ vor dem Rathaus. Stilecht werden sie in einem Luxusauto und verkleidet als richtige Mafiabosse vorfahren.


Hintergrund ist, dass am Freitag letzter Woche die Düsseldorfer CDU eine Verschärfung der Düsseldorfer Straßenordnung angekündigt hat, u.a. soll im Umkreis von fünf Metern zu Gastroterrassen ein grundsätzliches Bettelverbot gelten. Das würde in bestimmten Straßen der Düsseldorfer Altstadt zu einer „No-Go-Area“ für arme und obdachlose Menschen führen. Auch der Verkauf des Straßenmagazins fiftyfifty wäre dann dort nicht mehr möglich. Als Hauptgrund für das Verbot nennen Sprecher der CDU sog. „Bettelbanden“ oder sogar eine „Bettelmafia“, die angeblich in der Düsseldorfer Altstadt tätig seien. „Ein Bettelverbot passt überhaupt nicht zum toleranten Düsseldorf. Repressive Maßnahmen sind keine Lösung für soziale Probleme. Die Düsseldorfer Straßensatzung ist schon in ihrer heutigen Fassung in Teilen rechtswidrig“, erklärt Oliver Ongaro vom Straßenmagazin fiftyfifty

…“ Aufruf von

Straßenmagazin fiftyfifty


 (per e-mail) zur Protestaktion vor dem Düsseldorfer Rathaus um 15.30 Uhr am Mittwoch, 07.10.2026


[Bettelverbote in immer mehr Städten] Armutsbekämpfung auf Deutsch: Ehrliche Deutsche wollen in Ruhe Kaffee trinken 


„

In Deutschland meint man, Armut dadurch zu bekämpfen, dass man sie unter Strafe stellt. Die neuen Bettelverbote bieten keine Lösung an, sie kriminalisieren lediglich Arme.


In Dortmund gilt seit Anfang August ein besonderes Bettelverbot. Künftig müssen bettelnde Menschen einen Abstand von fünf Metern zu Tischen der Außengastronomie halten. Diesen Beschluss fasste das Kommunalparlament in seiner letzten Sitzung vor der Sommerpause mit den Stimmen von SPD, CDU, FDP, BSW und AfD. Der Grund dafür seien Beschwerden von Gastronom:innen und Kund:innen von Cafés und Restaurants rund um den Alten Markt in Dortmund gewesen. Verstoßen Bettelnde gegen das Verbot, drohen ihnen Bußgelder, die im (wahrscheinlichen) Fall der Nichtbegleichung zu mehrwöchiger Erzwingungshaft führen können.


Kurz darauf zog eine weitere Stadt in Nordrhein-Westfalen nach: In Düren gilt von nun an ein Bettelverbot, das weiter reicht als das in Dortmund. Verboten wurde nicht nur jede Bitte nach Geld im Umkreis von fünf Meter um die Außengastronomie, sondern ebenso das Betteln in Begleitung von Kindern ­sowie das Vortäuschen von Behinderungen oder Krankheiten. Damit solle verhindert werden, dass auf diese Weise Mitleid erregt würde. (…)


Erst im Zuge der Liberalisierungsbewegung in den sechziger Jahren wurde in der BRD 1969 ein Erlass aufgehoben, der sogar die Zwangseinweisung in ein Arbeitshaus ermöglicht hatte. 1974 wurde schließlich der Bettelparagraph aus dem Strafgesetzbuch gestrichen. Seit über fünfzig Jahren ist Betteln also grundsätzlich erlaubt.


Jedoch beschließen immer mehr Kommunen Einschränkungen. In München ist es etwa verboten, in der Altstadt oder auf dem Oktoberfestgelände nach Geld zu fragen. In Bremen ist jenes Verhalten …

title: Jornada de lucha “Todxs por Virginia Aparicio”
content:
Será este martes 6 de octubre en las puertas de la Catedral de Mar del Plata. A las 13.30, habrá conferencia de prensa, y a las 14 se leerán los resultados del proyecto Sprint, que la ingeniera agrónoma del INTA-Conicet coordinó y donde se encontró presencia de plaguicidas en distintas matrices ambientales, incluidas muestras humanas. Cabe recordar que en la actualidad el Consejo Directivo del Conicet intenta exonerar a Virginia, lo que implica la inhabilitación de por vida para ejercer en un cargo público. Por eso asambleas y organizaciones se unen para decir: «¡No a la exoneración de Virginia Aparicio!, ¡Por la Ciencia Digna y la Salud!, ¡Basta de Fumigarnos!».

Por Red Eco Alternativo.


“La posibilidad de investigar con independencia, sin presiones ni amenazas, resulta fundamental para producir conocimiento sobre aquello que afecta nuestras vidas y nuestro ambiente. Defender a la Dra. Aparicio es defender la libertad de investigación y, en este caso concreto, el derecho de la población a saber qué la está envenenando, quiénes son responsables y qué medidas son necesarias para revertirlo”, afirman los convocantes.


Entre ellas se encuentran: Naranja Ciencia y Técnica, APINTA, Vecinxs por la agroecologia, Paren de Fumigar, Asamblea Luna Roja, EcoAsamblea Parque Camet, Surfrider, AVATAR, Asamblea por los Bienes Comunes Chapadmalal, Mar Libre de Petroleras, Facultad de Cs de la Salud y Trabajo Social UNMDP, Plenario de Trabajadoras, Tribuna de Salud, CEGCEN – Conducción EPI, Foro Ambiental Balcarce.

title: Marcia popolare No Tav: le voci dal corteo
content:
Sabato 3 ottobre tantissimi giovani  e meno giovani hanno preso parte alla marcia popolare da Sant’Ambrogio ad Avigliana, hanno sfilato insieme ai Sindaci dell’Unione Montana e ai comitati dell’Alta e Bassa Valle. 


In particolare a essere messa sotto l’obiettivo è la tratta alta velocità Avigliana-Orbassano, nuova meta della cantierizzazione e devastazione dei territori in bassa Valle: un’area estesa intorno alla città di Torino. Un progetto che avrebbe  impatti importanti in particolar modo sulle falde acquifere e che metterebbe in luce il paradosso della carenza di trasporto pubblico in città: la questione della linea metro 2 viene dunque portata come emblema dell’agire irrazionale di chi dovrebbe gestire le risorse. 


In questi articoli avevamo riportato il piano tecnico che coinvolge i Comuni di

Rivoli, Rivalta

 e

Avigliana

. Oggi restituiamo un pezzettino della vivacità ed eterogeneità del Movimento No Tav capace di accogliere, coinvolgere nuove e vecchie generazioni, capace di rimettere al centro del dibattito politico una questione aperta ed emblematica del nostro tempo.

author: Stelinsky
title: «Πάντα μπροστά, μέχρι την νίκη»* / Κάποιες σκέψεις για το δικαστήριό μας (τοποθέτηση από την έγκλειστη συντρόφισσα Μαριάννα Μανουρά)
content:
*Αποχαιρετισμός της Άννας Μαρίας Μαντίνι στον πεσόντα από πυρά μπάτσων αδερφό της και μέλος της NAP, Λούκα Μαντίνι.

Στις 24 Μαΐου 2026 ολοκληρώθηκε η εκδίκαση της λεγόμενης «υπόθεσης των Αμπελοκήπων», μετά από εξαντλητικές και συνεχόμενες συνεδριάσεις, και ύστερα από δώδεκα πυκνές δικασίμους, η έδρα με πρόεδρο τον Σπύρο Γεωργουλέα και εισαγγελέα την Αλεξάνδρα Πίσχοινα, αποφάσισε να αποδώσει σε εμένα την ποινή των 19 ετών για τις κατηγορίες της ένταξης και συμμετοχής σε τρομοκρατική οργάνωση, της κατασκευής εκρηκτικών μηχανισμών, της προμήθειας εκρηκτικών υλών, της έκρηξης με ενδεχόμενο δόλο και της φθοράς ξένης περιουσίας, και την ποινή των 8 ετών στη συντρόφισσα Δήμητρα Ζαραφέτα για τις τρεις πρώτες από τις παραπάνω πέντε κατηγορίες.

Η απόφαση αυτή μπορεί να μην αποτελεί εξαίρεση στον κανόνα, αλλά είναι σε θέση να αναδείξει τους συσχετισμούς οι οποίοι δημιουργούν το πεδίο της νέας κατασταλτικής πολιτικής, ειδικά απέναντι σε όποιον και όποια αντιστέκεται. Οι ποινές που αποδόθηκαν τόσο σε εμένα όσο και στη συντρόφισσα, στηρίζονταν εξολοκλήρου στις επιταγές του Υπουργείου ΠροΠο, τις υποθέσεις της αντιτρομοκρατικής και την ενεργητική ερμηνεία της έδρας, της οποίας η φαινομενική τήρηση της νομιμότητας και της αντικειμενικότητας της φάνηκε να εξαντλείται στην αποδέσμευση των τριών από τους τέσσερις μη εμπλεκόμενων με την υπόθεση συγκατηγορουμένων. Αυτό βέβαια δεν συνέβη στη συντρόφισσα Δήμητρα Ζαραφέτα, όπου η έδρα –με καλπάζουσα φαντασία– την καταδίκασε σε 8 χρόνια για πράξεις με τις οποίες δεν είχε καμία σχέση, με μοναδικό στοιχείο την αναρχική πολιτική της ταυτότητα, τις προσωπικές και συντροφικές σχέσεις με εμένα και τον σύντροφο Κυριάκο, και την ανυποχώρητη και αλληλέγγυα στάση της καθ’ όλη τη διάρκεια του εγκλεισμού μας και της ακροαματικής διαδικασίας. Με τη συγκεκριμένη απόφαση ο κατασταλτικός και δικαστικός μηχανισμός προσπάθησαν να στείλουν ανεπιτυχώς, μηνύματα εκφοβισμού και παραδειγματισμού, καθώς και να επιβάλουν συντροφική και κοινωνική απομόνωση σε όσους αγωνιστές και αγωνίστριες επιλέγουν την ένοπλη πάλη ή συνδράμουν σε αυτή.

Από την άλλη, στη δική μου περίπτωση, ο κατασταλτικός μηχανισμός ξεδίπλωσε την εκδικητικότητά του, αποδίδοντάς μου όλες τις αρχικές κατηγορίες παρά την ευνοϊκότερη πρόταση της εισαγγελέως. Παρά το αόριστο κατηγορητήριο, την αδυναμία να προσδιοριστούν η (άγνωστη) τρομοκρατική οργάνωση, πόσο δε μάλλον τα (άγνωστα) λοιπά μέλη της και οι (άγνωστες) «ενέργειές» της, μου αποδόθηκε μια δυσανάλογα υψηλή ποινή με πρώτο στοιχείο την –από δική μου επιλογή– παραδοχή της απόφασης του συντρόφου μου να επιλέξει μεταξύ άλλων την ένοπλη δράση, οραματιζόμενος τον κοινωνικό μετασχηματισμό της κοινωνίας και την κατάργηση κράτους και κεφαλαίου. Και χρησιμοποιώντας ως δεύτερο «στοιχείο» την –και πάλι με δική μου απόφαση– ανάληψη πολιτικής ευθύνης για τη συνδρομή μου σε αυτή του την απόφαση. Την επιλογή μου αυτή την υπερασπίστηκα από την πρώτη στιγμή και θα συνεχίσω να την υπερασπίζομαι μέχρι τέλους. Όχι μόνο επειδή με αυτόν τον τρόπο βρέθηκα πλάι στο σύντροφό μου μέχρι την τελευταία του στιγμή, αλλά και επειδή συνέβαλα, συνδράμοντάς τον, στο πολύπλοκο μωσαϊκό της αντίστασης.

Αυτή μου η συμβολή, όπως και η απόφαση του συντρόφου, δεν εκδηλώθηκε σε ιστορικό κενό, αλλά μέσα σε μια πολύ συγκεκριμένη συγκυρία. Σε μια από τις δυσκολότερες μάλιστα περιόδους της μεταπολιτευτικής ιστορίας, όπου ο κρατικός μηχανισμός περιορίζεται πρώτον στο να επιδεικνύει τους «κινδύνους» από τους οποίους μας προστατεύει, αποπροσανατολίζοντας με αυτόν τον τρόπο τη διάχυτη δυσαρέσκεια και δευτερευόντως στο να θωρακίζεται συνεχώς μέσω της αυστηροποίησης των υπαρχόντων νόμων και της θέσπισης νέων αντεπαναστατικών νομοθεσιών, διατηρώντας με αυτόν τον τρόπο την κυριαρχία του και προετοιμάζοντας ένα νομικό οπλοστάσιο καταστολής οποιασδήποτε κοινωνικής αντίστασης. Πέραν της στρατηγικής του κρατικού μηχανισμού, ο κατασταλτικός ταυτόχρονα ενισχύεται με ειδικές ομάδες και ολοένα πιο εξελιγμένα τεχνολογικά μέσα, προσπαθώντας να επιβάλει τον νόμο και την τάξη που ο κρατικός μηχανισμός ευαγγελίζεται. Και όλα αυτά ενώ τα ριζοσπαστικά κινήματα δείχνουν προς το παρόν να χάνουν τη βεβαιότητα της συλλογικής ικανότητας δημιουργίας ενός νέου κόσμου, εσωτερικεύοντας παράλληλα ένα αίσθημα ανισχυρότητας, βουλιάζοντας σε μια φάση οπισθοχώρησης. Αυτή η δυσμενής συγκυρία προσδίδει ιδιαίτερη βαρύτητα σε επιλογές σαν και αυτή. Συγκεκριμένα, ο σύντροφος με αισιοδοξία επέλεξε να ξεπεράσει τόσο τον ίδιο τον εαυτό του όσο και τις αντίξοες συνθήκες βαδίζοντας …

title: „Die Kürzungen sind unerträglich“: Ein breites Bündnis hat den Kampf zur Verteidigung des öffentlichen Bildungswesens in Madrid aufgenommen
content:
Dossier


„

Mehr als 20 Organisationen haben sich zusammengeschlossen, um zu versuchen, das, was sie als Plan der Regionalregierung zur Dekapitalisierung des öffentlichen Bildungswesens zugunsten des privaten Bildungswesens ansehen, rückgängig zu machen. Mit dem Ruf „Bildungsqualität oder unbefristeter Streik“ haben Tausende von Menschen heute Morgen im Zentrum der Hauptstadt mehr Mittel für die öffentliche Bildung in Madrid gefordert. An der von mehr als 20 Organisationen, darunter Gewerkschaften, Universitätsversammlungen und verschiedene soziale Gruppen, organisierten Demonstration nahmen Vertreter und konkrete Forderungen aus allen Bildungsbereichen, von den 0- bis 3-Jährigen bis zu den Studenten und der Berufsausbildung, sowie politische Parteien teil. Nach Angaben der Organisatoren nahmen etwa 120.000 Menschen an der Demonstration teil

…“ So beginnt der umfangreiche span.

Artikel von Guillermo Martínez vom 23. Februar 2025 in elDiario.es


 (maschinenübersetzt) mit schönen Fotos der Transparente – siehe mehr Infos:


„Rettet das öffentliche Bildungswesen“: Allein zur Mobilisierung für den unbefristeten Streik ab 14. Oktober marschierten 20.000 durch Madrid zur Verteidigung der Rechte auf Bildung aber auch Wohnen


Madrid setzt sich für das öffentliche Bildungswesen ein: Tausende Menschen marschieren von Atocha nach Sol als Auftakt zum unbefristeten Streik


„

Tausende Menschen sind an diesem Sonntag in Madrid auf die Straße gegangen, um bei einer Großdemonstration, die durch die Hauptverkehrsachse der Hauptstadt von der Nähe des Bahnhofs Atocha (Cuesta de Moyano) bis zur Puerta del Sol führte, für das öffentliche Bildungswesen einzutreten. Der Protest, der gemeinsam von Gewerkschaften, Studentenorganisationen und Familienverbänden organisiert wurde, ist ein klares Zeichen der Stärke im Vorfeld des unbefristeten Streiks, der für den kommenden 14. Oktober in allen Bildungsstufen mit Ausnahme der Hochschulen geplant ist. Unter dem Motto „Lehrer und Schüler gemeinsam gegen Ayuso“ skandierten die Demonstranten Parolen und trugen Transparente mit den wichtigsten Forderungen der Branche, die einen Kurswechsel in der Bildungspolitik der Autonomen Gemeinschaft Madrid fordern. Das Gemeinsame Streikkomitee für das öffentliche Bildungswesen in Madrid, das die Mobilisierung initiiert hat, hat eine Reihe von Forderungen formuliert, die sich auf die Verbesserung der Arbeitsbedingungen des Lehrpersonals und der Unterrichtsqualität konzentrieren. (…) Die Demonstration der Bildungsbewegung hat sich an der Puerta del Sol mit zwei weiteren Protestaktionen vereinigt, die am selben Ort stattfinden. Zum einen handelt es sich um das Zeltlager für das Recht auf Wohnen, das in der Nacht vom 26. September nach der Zwangsräumung von Mari Carmen begann und bei dem weiterhin mehr als 150 Zelte auf dem Platz stehen. Zum anderen die Demonstration, zu der der Verband der Nachbarschaftsvereine von Madrid (FRAVM), „Ecologistas en Acción“ und andere Plattformen gegen das LIDER-Gesetz aufgerufen haben, das von der Regierung unter Isabel Díaz Ayuso vorangetriebene regionale Bodengesetz. Die Organisatoren des Bildungsmarsches haben betont, dass dieses Zusammentreffen „die gegenseitige Unterstützung und den gemeinsamen Kampf für die Verteidigung grundlegender Rechte wie Bildung oder Wohnen“ verdeutliche. Der Tag hat eine zunehmende Koordinierung zwischen verschiedenen sozialen Bewegungen in Madrid deutlich gemacht, wobei die Forderungen nach hochwertigen öffentlichen Dienstleistungen mit dem Kampf gegen Immobilienspekulation und für das Recht auf menschenwürdigen Wohnraum verbunden wurden

…“ span.

Bericht der Redaktion von LQSomos vom 27. September 2026


 mit Fotogalerie (maschinenübersetzt), siehe zum kommenden Streik:


„

Das öffentliche nicht-universitäre Bildungswesen tritt ab dem 14. Oktober in einen unbefristeten Streik. Und an diesem Sonntag, dem 27. September, gehen sie auf die Straße, um die PP-Regierung zu warnen, was auf sie zukommt, wenn sie die Forderungen nicht akzeptiert.  Wir von den Plattformen für die öffentliche Universität solidarisieren uns mit dem übrigen öffentlichen Bildungswesen, denn dessen Kampf ist auch unser Kampf. Und wir organisieren uns bereits in den Versammlungen, um unsere Kräfte einzuschätzen und zu entscheiden, wie wir die Mobilisierung und den Streik auch auf die Universitäten ausweiten können

…“ span.

author: Simon Childs
title: Goldsmiths University Hires ‘Fake Teachers’ for Arts Psychotherapy to Break Strikes
content:
Art psychotherapy students are among the many new starters at Goldsmiths facing utter chaos at the start of the academic year, as their course appears to be virtually on the brink of collapse. For some, what should be an exciting new chapter has become a disappointing nightmare.


Goldsmiths is well known for alumni such as artist Damien Hirst, writer Mark Fisher, anthropologist David Graeber and Blur frontman Damon Albarn. But it has also become known as a particularly dismal example of the crisis facing universities. Lecturers are currently striking against the third massive round of redundancies in five years. With lecturers taking industrial action, Goldsmiths has resorted to hiring inexperienced substitutes in chaotic circumstances to break the strike.


One Art Psychotherapy student who did not give her name for fear of repercussions told Novara Media she turned up to her induction on 28 September to teachers who had been hired as recently as that very morning.


“I moved all the way to London for this, I’ve left everything behind,” she said. “I want to help people. I want to help people with eating disorders, I want to help veterans with PTSD. That’s what I want to read about, that’s what I want to learn about. I did not come to Goldsmiths to learn how to become an activist, and now my time is full of writing letters and attending protests and demonstrations.”


Des Freedman, professor of Media and Communication Studies at the university, said: “Some students are being offered modules that are not their core modules, some students are being taught by people who they weren’t expecting to teach, and in some cases, the university is hiring in replacement staff in lieu of striking staff.”


Concerns over the suitability of the temporary teachers on the Art Psychotherapy course have not been soothed by a recent job listing on the British Association of Art Therapists (BAAT) website for a temporary lecturer seen by Novara Media, which merely requires the candidates to have “an interest in teaching”. A previous job listing for a permanent role requires the candidate to have “experience of working within UK higher education and a track record of research or scholarship in art psychotherapy”.


Psychotherapy courses are intense, requiring students to be in psychotherapy themselves and be put on placements with severely mentally unwell people – making the unavailability of trusted teachers feel especially hard to deal with.


Kawther Luau, a second year Arts Psychotherapy student, said: “You kind of enter very deep, vulnerable processes with yourself and each other and with the tutors. For that safety and trust for that to be disturbed – for temporary staff to be brought in – is obscene and communicates a real lack of understanding of what our training requires.”


The first-year student who chose not to give her name said the temporary teachers had made matters worse, not better. “I completely stand with the strikes,” she said. “I feel like they [the strikes] could have been resolved, but the university is making it so much worse by getting these fake teachers. It has put our entire course in jeopardy.” 


She fears that if the course becomes so poor that it doesn’t meet the requirements of the Health and Care Professions Council (HPHC), it could be scrapped altogether.


Last week, students organised an event where first, second and third-year students could meet. Here, a second-year student shared their first-year timetable with the freshers. “They had about three times as many classes as we’re supposed to be having. Us first-years came together and realised that the university is really banking on us not having any knowledge of what our year is supposed to look like”, the first-year student said.


A Goldsmiths spokesperson told Novara Media that timetables are not directly comparable from year to year as “teaching delivery is different between cohorts”. 


Other courses at Goldsmiths have also been affected. Joe Newman, the University and College Union (UCU) branch president at Goldsmiths,

told Times Higher Education

 he found out that the optional module he runs in the music department had been dropped only when a student who attended the branch’s picket line told him.  


The chaos in south London is

part of a sector-wide crisis

, which has seen

tens of thousands of jobs

 cut across the country in recent years. Numerous branches of the UCU are taking strike action, including at the universities of …

author: Unknown
title: Two young Kurdish women athletes arrested by Iranian forces in Saqqez
content:
Iranian forces have arrested two young Kurdish women athletes, Rojan Ebrahimi and Aida Ghaderi, in Saqqez, Kurdistan Province, in recent days.


The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has reported that Ghaderi, a swimming coach, was arrested on 4 October after forces from the Ministry of Intelligence raided her family home in Saqqez without presenting a warrant.


Ebrahimi, an MMA athlete from Saqqez, was arrested a day earlier, on 3 October, after Ministry of Intelligence forces raided her family home.


Both arrests were carried out without warrants.


Any charges against the two women, as well as their current whereabouts and status, remain unknown.

title: Two Iraqi police officers killed in ISIS attack
content:
ISIS militants attacked a position belonging to the Iraqi Federal Police forces in the Hawija district of Kirkuk.


Clashes reportedly broke out between ISIS militants and Iraqi federal police officers during the attack. Two police officers were killed, and several others were wounded in the clashes.


It was also reported that thermal cameras belonging to the police were destroyed by the militants. Following the attack, the Federal Police launched an investigation to locate the ISIS militants who attacked their position.

author: Unknown
title: Protest outside Sincan Prison over delayed releases of women
content:
A statement was made outside Sincan Women’s Closed Prison under the leadership of the Federation of Legal Solidarity Associations for Prisoners’ Families (TUHAD-FED) over the blocking of women prisoners’ releases.


The protest was attended by members of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), lawyers from the Lawyers for Freedom Association (ÖHD) and many others. Participants unfurled a banner reading: “We are holding a vigil against the blocking of political prisoners’ releases.”


TUHAD-FED Ankara Representative Sihan Kaya said the releases of many women prisoners had been postponed on various grounds since the establishment of the Prison Administration and Observation Boards in 2021.


Kaya said the releases of at least eight women prisoners at Sincan Women’s Closed Prison had been blocked. She said Nedime Yaklav’s release had been postponed seven times; those of Hicran Binici, Nuriye Adet and Devrim Adet five times; Zeliha Ustabaş four times; Melike Göksü, Emine Abiş and Fatma Aslan three times; and Pınar Tikit twice.


‘A second mechanism of punishment’


Kaya said the women included prisoners who were ill and others who had been imprisoned for 30 years, and condemned the postponement of their releases on subjective grounds such as “good conduct”, “remorse” and “compliance with rules”.


Kaya said the Prison Administration and Observation Boards had effectively become “a second mechanism of punishment” that extended sentences imposed by courts, and called for an end to the repeated postponement of women prisoners’ releases.


TUHAD-FED called for the release of women who had met the conditions for release, for decisions by the boards to be made transparent and compliant with the law, and for the necessary legal proceedings to be initiated against board members.


‘Article 7 must be implemented’


DEM Party Ağrı MP Heval Bozdağ said the current practices were undermining confidence in the law and in the ongoing process.


Bozdağ said Article 7 of the Commission Report should be reviewed and implemented, adding that the article also contained provisions concerning the structure and abolition of the Prison Administration and Observation Boards.


TUHAD-FED announced that it would continue its protests until the women prisoners whose releases had been blocked were freed.

author: Peter C. Gøtzsche, MD
title: Didn’t Anyone Tell You It Is Okay to Be Different?
content:
T

he Mad in Norway film festival took place in Lillehammer, 24-26 September. It was a remarkable experience. The participants came from many parts of the world and counted psychiatrists, psychologists, other health professionals, filmmakers, musicians, other artists, and previous and current patients.


It struck me that, despite all the diversity, people agreed that mental health needs to be systematically reformed, with more emphasis on psychosocial interventions, as was

recently recommended

 by the United Nations and the World Health Organization. What I felt the strongest during the festival was how rewarding it was to interact with so many kind people who could think for themselves and look through the drug industry propaganda.


Photo of the Mad in Norway Film Festival by Kermit Cole


The stories I heard during the breaks confirmed how harmful drug focused psychiatry is. A German woman told me she lost her husband three years earlier. After they tripled the dose of his antidepressant, he developed adverse effects. In response, they also tripled his dose of olanzapine, and he died two days later.


Another German woman told me she became diagnosed with anxiety and depression after she had been prescribed a birth control pill as a teenager. Depression is a well-known harm of such pills described in the package inserts. This led to treatment with an SSRI. When she stopped the birth control pill, her anxiety vanished, but she got withdrawal symptoms every time she tried to come off the SSRI. It went on for years because the withdrawal symptoms were constantly labelled as relapse, which led to further drugging. When she finally tried to discontinue all the drugs according to psychiatric advice, she developed akathisia, and to her great surprise, her psychiatrists didn’t know what this was; they had never heard the word before. They claimed her symptoms were just psychological. But she survived a nine-month hell of akathisia and is now slowly tapering off the last drug.


Akathisia is one of the worst harms of psychiatric drugs. There is no excuse for not knowing about it because it is listed in the package inserts and is mentioned in

psychiatric textbooks

. Moreover, patients often complain about it.


Akathisia is characterised by intense restlessness, inner turmoil, agitation, and a compelling need to move frantically around. Patients may think they have gone mad and may describe it as wanting to jump out of their skin. They cannot control their agitated manner and can experience unbearable rage, delusions, and dissociation. It is a life-threatening condition because it

increases markedly

 the risk of suicide and violence. Patient reports on the Internet show that suicidal thoughts when taking psychosis pills are

strongly associated

 with akathisia; 13.8% of respondents reporting akathisia also reported suicidal thoughts, compared with only 1.5% of those who didn’t mention akathisia (P < 0.001).


The film

Diagnonsense

 was made by Norwegian filmmaker Ane-Martha Tamnes Hansgård. She felt she didn’t fit in with the other kids in school and tried to kill herself at age 14. During the following 15 years, she received 12 different diagnoses, which never addressed the deeper causes of the emotional  pain she had. An inner conflict related to her homosexuality remained unrecognised, as she was heavily medicated and lost touch with her sexuality. At one time, she was treated with three different antidepressants and two antiepileptics simultaneously.


Her many diagnoses and drugs made matters worse and she started questioning the diagnoses. She consulted two psychiatrists in the United States who said she was bipolar. She doubted this diagnosis was correct, and on her way back to Norway, she passed New Orleans and saw an ad for a shaman. He listened to her and said one simple sentence that was the defining moment for her:


“Didn’t anyone tell you it’s okay to be different?”


He also told her that it was up to her to choose if she wanted to define herself or if she preferred that others did it for her.


She decided it was okay not to be like most people. She made several courageous attempts to stop taking the drugs, but without proper support, this proved nearly impossible. The hospital offered no meaningful alternatives and left her to manage on her own because she had chosen to discontinue the treatment. Even when she had developed horrible withdrawal symptoms compatible with akathisia and desperately …

author: Fozzie
title: Chapter 18: Different Formulae for the Rate of Surplus-value
content:
Harry Cleaver's study guide to Marx's Capital volume 1, chapter 18.

In this chapter Marx, pauses a moment before the section on wages, to juxtapose his own formulations to those of classical political economy and to critique the latter in ways that foreshadow the critiques he will make in the next three chapters.

By always comparing surplus value (or product) to the total value (or product), classical political economists portrayed the relationship between workers and capitalists in ways that 1) hid the existence of exploitation and 2) created an illusion that labor was getting its fair share. The existence of exploitation was hidden by making it appear that each factor of production, i.e., labor and capital, is rewarded according to its contribution to production. So, surplus value, s, appears to equal capital’s contribution and s/(s + v), its share, while by implication, variable capital, v, appears to equal labor’s contribution and v/(v+s), its share. Within a few decades after Capital was published, neoclassical economists, having substituted utility for labor value, would use the same trick but with fancier mathematics.

Mathematical concepts such as production functions, e.g., Q = f(K, L), permitted the use of calculus to derive marginal products for K (dQ/dK) and L (dQ/dL) and with a few more assumptions, conclude that wages = market value of dQ/dL and profits = the market value of dQ/dK. In the development of this theory of production, the labor theory of value of the classical political economists was set aside, so the only “value” left was money price determined by markets. Yet the conclusion was essentially the same, both the old formulae and the new ones hid exploitation by reducing the antagonistic social relations of production to engineering-like technical relations among things.(1)

For Marx, by formulating the value of labor as one part of the working day, the classical political economic formulation understated what was for him the essential issue: how much of workers’ time toiling produced the means of consumption they needed (or their value/money equivalent) and how much of their work time produced the means of production (or their value/money equivalent) capital needed. Clearly, both formulations of the rate of surplus-value, the classical one, s/(v+s), and his own, s/v, are possible measures of capital’s share of the total new value created. He preferred s/v because it provided a more direct representation of the division of workers’ days. When he notes how s/(v+s) is a “mode of presentation which arises, by the way, out of the capitalist mode of production itself” (2) and promises to return to the point later on, odds have it that he was thinking about the parallel between s/(v+s) and s/(c+v), the rate of profit. He did return to juxtapose the rate of profit to the rate of exploitation in material included in Volume III of Capital where he presents the rate of profit as expressing capital’s preoccupation with the rate of return on its investment (c+v) and the rate of exploitation as expressing the degree to which workers are being exploited, i.e., forced to produce products and value for someone else.(3)

Commenting on the “popular expression” that juxtaposes unpaid to paid labor, instead of surplus to necessary labor, Marx affirms the reasonableness of that way of talking about exploitation in money terms. By pretending to buy labor, rather than labor-power, capitalists argue that all labor is paid for. But as workers grasp intuitively and Marx’s analysis in Chapter 6 demonstrated, although fluctuations in supply and demand can push wages above, or drive them below the value of labor-power, on the average workers are only paid wages equivalent to the amount of work that produces the value of their labor-power and capitalists arrogate to themselves the fruits of all excess labor beyond that—with no compensation to those performing it. He concludes, “Capital, therefore, is not only command over labour, as Adam Smith thought. It is essentially the command over unpaid labor. All surplus-value . . . is in substance the materialization of unpaid labor time.” (4) But what is the importance of this command over unpaid labor time? We have seen how Marx’s focus is on one, and only one, use of surplus-value, or unpaid labor time: investment, i.e., employing it to impose more work in the future!

1 It would not be until the 1960s, when economists at Cambridge University in England, building on the work …

author: Fozzie
title: Chapter 17: Changes of Magnitude in the Price of Labour-Power and in Surplus-Value
content:
Harry Cleaver's study guide to Marx's Capital volume 1 chapter 17.

The title of this chapter announces a transition from value analysis to money by making clear that the value of labor-power will be discussed in terms of its price. Price, as we saw in Chapter 1, is the money expression of the value of a commodity, in this case of the value of labor-power. In this chapter, Marx reiterates his analysis of past chapters in terms of changes in both the value and the price of labor-power and notes how changes in price may differ from changes in value. In passing from analysis in terms of value to one in terms of money, Marx must, and does, take into account changes in the real value of money wages, e.g., caused by a change in the price of consumer goods. Therefore, the price of labor-power may not equal its value.

Throughout this analysis, the price of labor-power can be assumed to be wages, in as much as money wages were predominant over other expressions of the value of labor-power in the period in which Marx was writing. (As opposed to wages in kind, salaries, commissions or government payments to the unemployed or the poor.)

While the reiteration of previously explained material has often caused this chapter to be passed over as pure pedantry, there are two reasons for its close study. First, thinking of the value of labor-power in terms of its price, its monetary equivalent, lays the groundwork for Part VI, Chapters 19-22 on wages. Second, among familiar words and phrases there are also politically important points well worth repetition.

The first of these is his highlighting of how, in the dynamic of capitalist development, despite the existence of some zero-sum relationships where one class can benefit only at the expense of the other, there are situations in which the material situation of both can be improved. The most important of these being when a rise in the productivity of labor results, to use modern terms, in an increase in the size of the pie being produced. When the pie/output grows, it is at least possible for both workers and capitalists to get more of what they want: means of consumption and life for workers, means of production to impose more work for capitalists. Marx writes that it is “possible that owing to an increase in the productivity of labor both the worker and the capitalist may simultaneously be able to appropriate a greater quantity of means of subsistence [or of means of production] without any change in the price of labor-power or in surplus-value.”(1) The same mutual benefit is possible with increases in the length and intensity of the working day; where more is produced, more could potentially be shared. In this second case, because longer and/or more intense working hours use up workers’ energy faster, any increase in real consumption requires an excess over the necessary compensation for the accelerated wearing out of workers. But it is at least possible for the increase to be large enough.

The importance of these observations is they show how his theory is perfectly compatible with historically observed increases in standards of living among some workers, even as others are thrown into poverty and pauperism. It is also compatible with, and indeed predates, the recognition by neoclassical economists (from at least Alfred and Mary Marshall on) that increases in wages can go hand in hand with increased profits.(2) This was the reality on the basis of which John Maynard Keynes built his theory of how capitalist development could be socially progressive, i.e., one in which growing profits and investment were stimulated by growing wages and benefits.(3) In the process, he overthrew the traditional business view that any increase in wages would undermine profits and therefore had to be resisted by all means possible—including violence when necessary.

Under these circumstances, Marx also points out how the degree to which the fruits of higher productivity and more work are shared depends in large part upon the balance of class forces, i.e., on the struggle between workers seeking to share in increases in the social wealth resulting from increased productivity and the efforts by capitalists to arrogate all increases to themselves. “The new value of labor-power”, Marx writes, “depends on the relative weight thrown into the scale by the pressure of capital on the one side, and the resistance of the workers on the other.”(4) In the wake of the Russian Revolution and of World War I …

author: Diba Kosi Bilinga
title: What African Elections Can Learn from the BOORANA GADAA SYSTEM
content:
A Democracy Older Than the Ballot Box


Every election season, much of East Africa braces itself. Incumbents amend constitutions to erase term limits, and citizens wait to see whether power will change hands at the ballot box or in the streets. The pattern repeats: disputed results, ethnic mobilizations, coups, or leaders who refuse to leave.


Kenya is already in a political labor pain as the 10

th

 August 2027 election is drawing nearer. Peacebuilding groups estimate the risk of pre-election violence at between 70 and 82 percent, and officials invoke the memory of the 2007–08 post-election crisis as they warn that hate speech, disinformation and organized political gangs are returning to the country’s rallies, according to

The Standard

.


Yet in the rangelands of southern Ethiopia and northern Kenya, the

Boorana Oromo

 have long practiced

rotational

,

peacefully

 transferred leadership. Known as the

Boorana Gadaa system

, it was inscribed by

UNESCO in 2016

 as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity that regulates political and social life and protects women’s rights.


This article asks what East African leaders, electoral commissions and citizens can learn from a system that has quietly rotated power every eight years for generations, without coups or third-term referenda. It is not a call to replicate Gadaa wholesale, nor a celebration of it — the system has its own limits, discussed below — but an invitation to study its design against the region’s recurring electoral crises.


Lessons to pick from the boorana Gadaa System


To start us off, Boorana leadership rotates on a fixed eight-year cycle among

five Gogeessa

:

Addii Doyyoo, Boru Galmaa, Liiban Kusee, Arero Geedoo and Bulee Dabassaa

. Each governs for one Gadaa period of eight 8 years, then hands over, returning to the first after

40 years

 — a rotation built into the structure itself.


Compare this to East Africa’s modern pattern.

Human Rights Watch

 calls it the “constitutional coup”: leaders who cannot win re-election simply rewrite the laws in their way. Uganda’s Museveni scrapped term and age limits to claim a seventh term in January 2026; Rwanda’s Kagame did the same in 2015, and Burundi’s 2015 third-term bid by Nkurunziza triggered an attempted coup.


Gadaa’s lesson is structural: when a time limit is built into the system itself, rather than a leader’s promise, departure never has to be settled by force.


The second lesson is that the Boorana Gadaa system treats leadership as something built over decades, not switched on by an election. Members pass through age-grades from childhood, absorbing law, custom and ritual responsibility long before they are eligible to lead.


Most African political systems do the opposite: candidates are selected first, and patronage, money and ethnic arithmetic often outweigh demonstrated competence, producing leaders who improvise governance while learning on the job.


The lesson for African parties and civic institutions: build structured pipelines — local councils, youth wings, civil service — that expose future leaders to responsibility long before a national mandate.


Thirdly, at the Boorana

Balli Walirafudhu

 handover ceremony, authority passes from the outgoing ruling class to the incoming one, treated by the whole community as final and binding, as described in

an account of the Gumi Gaayo

.


Kenya’s 2007–08 crisis shows what happens without that script: a disputed result triggered ethnic violence that killed roughly 1,200 people, per

HRW’s investigation

. Tanzania, long seen as the region’s stable exception, saw its own rupture in October 2025, with dozens of political-disorder incidents in three days.


In Gadaa, succession is scripted years in advance. In much of East Africa, it is resolved only after votes are contested — precisely when it is most dangerous to leave unresolved.


Another crucial lesson is that the Boorana society has two broad blocks,

Sabboo Sadeen

 and

Goonaa Bal’aa

, each with its own sub-clans — but the

five Gogeessa

 that hold political authority cut across these lines, so no single clan can capture the system.


Kenya’s 2007–08 violence was driven largely by ethnic mobilizations, with

CSIS

 noting ethnicity as the main axis political elites mobilize around, turning elections into an ethnic census. Reprisal killings in Eldoret and Naivasha targeted communities tied to rival candidates.


Where political identity is inseparable from …

title: So many things would be better if doctors could just say “yeah that is a real problem but there…
content:
vergess

:

joy-haver

:

So many things would be better if doctors could just say “yeah that is a real problem but there isn’t much we can do to treat it so our only real recommendations are other things that raise your general health level to compensate”

instead they just say “thats normal” or “oh theres nothing wrong with you”. Because in their mind “it wont kill you and i cant fix it” means its not worth mentioning.

Affirm the problem doc, it wont kill you. Knowing that something just isnt the kind of thing doctors treat will save your patients so much time, money, and stress, all of which will improve their health.

I was going to link to that essay about how med school beats this out of doctors, complete with clinically diagnosable PTSD in 20-40% of doctors depending on field.

But then I went to collect the link on duckduckgo since I don’t have my bookmarks at work, and oh god, there’s actually thousands of these essays, and even studies now.

So uh. I’ll synthesize a bit here:

Doctors need to stop doing this, yes. But for that to happen, med school has to stop punishing this with public humiliations, residency has to stop punishing this with extra shifts, and employers have to stop firing doctors who admit this for “malpractice liability.”

The individual doctors sending their patients home ignorant and afraid are the last leg in a long chain, basically.

author: Unknown
title: Эррико Малатеста - Наша внешняя политика
content:
Автор

: Эррико Малатеста

Название

: Наша внешняя политика

Подзаголовок

: Война и Мир

Дата

: 7 марта 1914

Дополнительная информация

: К сожалению, только первые три абзаца переведены с итальянского. Остальное - с английского.

Источник

: Volontà (Ancona), год 2-1, №10. "La nostra politica estera. Guerra e Pace"


 Строго говоря, у нас не может быть внешней политики, поскольку мы находимся и хотим находиться вне и против нынешнего раздела мира на соперничающие государства.


 Для нас нет чужих. Мы хотим, чтобы все люди – каково бы ни было их место рождения, каков бы ни был этнический корень, из которого они происходят, каков бы ни был язык, на котором они говорят, – считали себя братьями, свободно объединялись в группы и сотрудничали вместе ради большего благосостояния, большей свободы, большей цивилизации для всех.


 И поскольку это всеобщее братство, эта гармонизация всех интересов, всех стремлений в обширном единстве (единстве человеческого рода), которое уважало бы и благоприятствовало свободному развитию всех различий, полной автономии всех индивидов и всех групп, всё ещё остаётся идеалом, противостоящим суровой реальности сегодняшнего дня; поскольку люди всё ещё разделены на угнетённых и угнетателей, и одни живут, эксплуатируя труд других, а трудящиеся несут бремя всех общественных тягот, стеснены в своём материальном и моральном развитии и часто низведены до самой убогой и оскотинивающей нищеты, – мы стоим, какой бы ни была наша страна рождения или место жительства, на стороне угнетённых против угнетателей, трудящихся против паразитов, не считаясь ни с какими политическими группировками, на которые исторические события, интересы и амбиции хозяев – пусть даже благоприятствуемые особыми природными условиями – разделили человечество.


 Если кто-то хочет говорить об иностранцах, то для нас иностранец – не тот, кто родился по ту сторону границы и говорит на другом языке или имеет другой цвет кожи; – иностранец, враг – это угнетатель, это эксплуататор, это всякий, в любой стране, кто подчиняет другого человека своей воле.


 — «Но мы, несмотря на наш космополитизм, всё же должны жить в государстве, в котором находимся, и подчиняться его политическому режиму. Мы можем в идеале чувствовать солидарность как с рабочим из далёкой страны, так и с тем, кто работает рядом с нами, мы можем ненавидеть иностранные правительства так же, как национальное; но на практике именно с соседями солидарность или борьба живее, сердечнее, действеннее».


 Так скажите же нам те, кто, не будучи в состоянии сделать нас патриотами и националистами с помощью обычных аргументов, основанных на преступной ненависти и глупом тщеславии, полагают, что могут воззвать к нашим боевым инстинктам и заставить нас принять самые реакционные теории под личиной революционности. И мы принимаем их тезис. Мы, несмотря на наши идеи, по необходимости итальянские граждане, то есть подданные правительства Италии; и потому это правительство угнетает нас и влияет на нас больше, чем могло бы, например, правительство Японии; и мы в свою очередь можем сделать против правительства Италии то, чего у нас не было бы средств сделать против правительства далёкой страны. Итак, вывод: для анархиста главный враг – тот угнетатель, который ближе всего к нему и против которого он может бороться эффективнее. Для итальянского анархиста и вообще для всякого итальянского рабочего, стремящегося к освобождению своему и своих товарищей, прежде всего необходимо бороться с правительством Италии и с хозяевами Италии, то есть с теми, кто называет себя нашими согражданами и соотечественниками и во имя нации и отечества хотел бы, чтобы мы покорно принимали их господство. Это ли вывод, к которому они хотели прийти? Если да, мы согласны.


 ***


 Говорят, что националистическое и патриотическое чувство – это факт, и потому его надо принять.


 Религия, преступность, нищета, рабство и тысяча индивидуальных или коллективных отклонений – тоже факты. Неужели нам поэтому придётся принять всё и отказаться от всякого действия ради улучшения положения?


 Патриотическое чувство, когда оно не просто шумиха, делаемая в интересах класса, и действительно существует в народном сознании, бывает хорошим или дурным в зависимости от обстоятельств: хорошим, когда оно служит тому, чтобы воодушевить на восстание против угнетателя, который оказывается иностранцем; дурным, когда оно толкает угнетать других и лучше принимать отечественное угнетение. author: dev
title: Tout comprendre sur Parcoursup
content:
C'est l'une des revendications les plus spontanées et récurrentes du mouvement lycéen en cours : l'abolition de Parcoursup. Si personne n'est encore en mesure de savoir

comment

 ce système de sélection opaque fonctionne, lycéens, parents et professeurs ont déjà bien compris

à quoi il sert

.


Nous proposons ici une petite sélection de nos articles sur le sujet qui ne manqueront pas d'étayer les évidences et intuitions partagées par les élèves.


Tout comprendre sur Parcoursup


« Faire patienter, c'est dominer »


« Pour comprendre la nature de “Parcoursup”, il faut partir de l'expérience directe, sans tenter d'y plaquer des interprétations hatives ou idéologiques. Pour la plupart des lycéens — ceux que les communicants qui encombrent désormais l'appareil d'Etat appellent “nos jeunes” — le processus d'affectation dans l'enseignement supérieur se présente comme une boîte noire nimbée de brouillard, comme une obscure Machine.


Son opacité ne tient pas tant à l'interface numérique par laquelle se font les connexions que dans l'impression diffuse de ne pas connaître les règles d'un “jeu” qui s'apprête à déterminer la place sociale qui sera assignée à chaque “candidat” pour le reste de son existence. »


Parcoursup et la police prédictive


La vie, le destin, l'algorithme


« Quoi de commun entre la police prédictive et Parcoursup ? Les deux reposent sur des algorithmes, certes, mais ils sont surtout deux outils plus ou moins subtils du contrôle social assisté par ordinateur. À chaque fois, l'algorithme incarne une somme de décisions politiques dont l'importance n'a d'égale que l'opacité : tout repose alors sur l'efficacité opérationelle, l'interface, la baisse du taux de criminalité ou la répartition des élèves dans les filières en fonction de leurs choix. Une fois n'est pas coutume, les causes structurelles ou les déterminations collectives sont converties et neutralisées en décisions individuelles. »


Rejeter l'école


Un lycéen décrypte le quotidien de la génération Parcoursup


« un lycéen lecteur de lundimatin nous a transmis cette excellente analyse de son expérience d'élève. Depuis l'intérieur, il évoque avec précision et érudition les nouvelles modalités d'isolement, de contrôle, de punition et d'auto-discipline qui trament le quotidien de cette nouvelle génération Parcoursup. »


Parcoursup : conseils de désorientation


Entretien avec Aïda N'Diaye, Johan Faerber et Camille


« Si l'on peut reconnaître un seul mérite à l'opacité du dispositif Parcoursup, c'est d'avoir rendu transparent ce processus de sélection. Dans ce lundisoir, nous essayons de comprendre plus précisément ce qui se joue dans l'expérience de cette plateforme. Comment les logiques d'auto-management imprègnent désormais chaque lycéen, comment les professeurs deviennent petit à petit les supplétifs de la sélection algorithmique, comment l'angoisse continue de l'évaluation devient une norme à laquelle on ne peut plus échapper. »

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: Deterioration of civic space continues under Marcos Jr — global report
content:
Activists protest in front of Department of Justice to condemn the filing of twin terror laws against activists. Photo by Dominic Gutoman/Bulatlat.

MANILA — Civic space in the Philippines continues to deteriorate with the Philippine government’s failure to implement human rights obligations, global civil society alliance CIVICUS reported.

“Since coming to power, the (Ferdinand Marcos Jr.) government has sustained a systematic pattern of repression against activists, harassing those who defend human rights with the use of trumped-up charges or anti-terror laws,” said Josef Benedict, Asia researcher of CIVICUS.

The Philippines has been rated “Repressed” for five consecutive years — the second worst rating a country can receive — indicating severe restrictions to the freedoms of expression, peaceful assembly, and association.

The country was included in the Monitor Watchlist last March 2026, flagging serious concerns about its crackdown on dissent, criminalizing protesters, and targeting activists.

Read: Philippines on human rights watchlist due to crackdown on dissent

“The government must reverse course to protect the rights of activists and allow them to work without fear, interference or retaliation,” Benedict added.

Such a rating was a product of failure of the Philippine government to fulfill its human rights obligations under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR), which it ratified in 2007.

For example, the government failed to implement the recommendations on civic space during the fourth cycle of the Universal Periodic Review in November 2022 at the United Nations Human Rights Council. It includes the need for the Philippine government to ensure enabling space for civil society and human rights defenders, end red-tagging or the linking of activists and human rights defenders to armed insurgency.

The ICCPR mandates all state parties to respect and protect civic freedoms, including freedoms of association, expression and peaceful assembly: all of which are also enshrined in the 1987 Philippines Constitution.

Among the significant forms of attack against activists is the use of fabricated charges under the twin terror laws.

Karapatan reported as of September 2026 that at least 259 individuals had been charged with the Anti-Terrorism Act (ATA) and the Terrorism Financing Prevention and Suppression Act (TFPSA).

Activists are also being charged with violations of the Public Assembly Act of 1985, a relic from the Martial Law of dictator Ferdinand Marcos Sr used against protesting activists.

The Marcos Jr. administration has been warned several times this year for its low performance on human rights and civic space. In Safety from the State metric of the Human Rights Measurement Initiative, the Philippines scored a “very bad” performance for freedom from arbitrary arrest, which is the lowest score recorded among Southeast Asian countries surveyed. Its freedom of assembly and association metric also falls under “bad” score.

Read: Philippines’ human rights record worse than average in Southeast Asia

The CIVICUS report also flagged the persistence of red-tagging and killings against activists and journalists. The Philippines remains the deadliest country for environmental and land defenders in Asia since 2012, while it maintains a low rank of 114th in the World Press Freedom Index of the Reporters Without Borders due to its press freedom violations this year.

Moreover, the impunity for the killing of 19 people in Negros Occidental this April 19, 2026, is also highlighted in the report. Not one has been held accountable for the killing of nine civilians and ten revolutionaries, with the Philippine Army maintaining that all of them died in armed encounters.

“The authorities must respect the right to protest and ensure that when arbitrary arrests occur or excessive force is used, that the perpetrators are held to account,” Benedict said.

Some of CIVICUS recommendations for the government include the abolition of the National Task Force to End Local Communist Armed Conflict (NTF-ELCAC), adoption of Human Rights Defenders Protection Act, decriminalization of libel and cyber-libel, and the withdrawal of the Digital Media Anti-False Information Bill. title: Αντιπολεμικές διαδηλώσεις ενάντια στην επίσκεψη του Αμερικάνου Υπουργού εξωτερικών Μ. Ρούμπιο, την Τρίτη 6/10
content:
Την Τρίτη 6/10, σε Θεσσαλονίκη, Αθήνα και Πάτρα, σωματεία, οργανώσεις και συλλογικότητες καλούν σε αντιπολεμικές συγκεντρώσεις ενάντια στην επερχόμενη άφιξη του Μάρκο Ρούμπιο, υπουργού εξωτερικών των ΗΠΑ. Με αντιπολεμικά συνθήματα κατά του ΝΑΤΟ και των ΗΠΑ αλλά και κατά της συνεργασίας του ελληνικού κράτους με το κράτος – δολοφόνο Ισραήλ, οι διαδηλωτ(ρι)ές δηλώνουν πως ο Μάρκο Ρούμπιο όπως και κάθε γρανάζι της πολεμικής μηχανής ΕΕ – ΝΑΤΟ – ΗΠΑ είναι ανεπιθύμητοι.


Καλέσματα:


Θεσσαλονίκη, 19.00 στη Καμάρα


Αθήνα, 19.00 στα Προπύλαια


Πάτρα, 19.30 στο Εργατικό Κέντρο


Αναλυτικά τα καλέσματα:


March to Gaza Greece


ΑΝΕΠΙΘΥΜΗΤΟΣ Ο ΡΟΥΜΠΙΟ. ΕΞΩ ΟΙ ΦΟΝΙΑΔΕΣ ΤΩΝ ΛΑΩΝ.


Την Τρίτη 6 Οκτώβρη το βράδυ φτάνει στην Αθήνα ο υπουργός Εξωτερικών των ΗΠΑ Μάρκο Ρούμπιο.


Την Τετάρτη 7 Οκτώβρη, τρία χρόνια από την αρχή της γενοκτονίας στη Γάζα, ηγείται της αμερικανικής αντιπροσωπείας στον 6ο Στρατηγικό Διάλογο Ελλάδας και ΗΠΑ και συναντιέται με τον Μητσοτάκη και τον Γεραπετρίτη.


Στην ατζέντα βρίσκονται η στρατιωτική συνεργασία, η ενέργεια και η ηλεκτρική διασύνδεση Ελλάδας, Κύπρου και Ισραήλ.


Το Ισραήλ είναι το μακρύ δόρυ της εξωτερικής αποικιοκρατικής πολιτικής των ΗΠΑ στη Δυτική Ασία.Η γενοκτονία του παλαιστινιακού λαού συντελείται με αμερικανικά όπλα και με αμερικανική διπλωματική κάλυψη, και ο Ρούμπιο είναι ο υπουργός που εγγυάται αυτή τη σχέση.


Την 1η Μάρτη 2025 ανακοίνωσε ότι παρακάμπτει το Κογκρέσο με διαδικασία «έκτακτης ανάγκης», για να επιταχύνει την παράδοση όπλων αξίας περίπου 4 δισ. δολαρίων στο Ισραήλ, ανάμεσά τους 35.529 βόμβες των 2.000 λιβρών.


Στις 18 Σεπτέμβρη 2025 οι ΗΠΑ άσκησαν το έκτο τους βέτο για τη Γάζα στο Συμβούλιο Ασφαλείας του ΟΗΕ, μόνες απέναντι σε 14 ψήφους, σε ψήφισμα που ζητούσε άμεση και μόνιμη εκεχειρία και άρση των περιορισμών στη βοήθεια.


Ο ίδιος επέβαλε κυρώσεις στην ειδική εισηγήτρια του ΟΗΕ Φραντσέσκα Αλμπανέζε, σε δικαστές του Διεθνούς Ποινικού Δικαστηρίου που ασχολήθηκαν με τα εντάλματα σύλληψης του Νετανιάχου, και στις παλαιστινιακές οργανώσεις Al-Haq, Al Mezan και PCHR, που τεκμηριώνουν τα εγκλήματα του Ισραήλ.


Από τον Γενάρη του 2026 είναι ιδρυτικό μέλος της εκτελεστικής ομάδας του «Συμβουλίου Ειρήνης» του Τραμπ, μαζί με τον Κούσνερ και τον Μπλερ, του οργάνου που επιβλέπει τη διακυβέρνηση, την ανοικοδόμηση και την «προσέλκυση επενδύσεων» στη Γάζα, πάνω στα ερείπια και ερήμην του λαού της.


Η γενοκτονία στη Γάζα συνεχίζεται, με τα στοιχεία του υπουργείου Υγείας της Γάζας στις 3 Οκτώβρη 2026 να μετρούν 74.228 νεκρούς και 175.188 τραυματίες.Από την «εκεχειρία» της 10ης Οκτώβρη 2025 έχουν σκοτωθεί άλλοι 1.445 Παλαιστίνιοι.


Η κυβέρνηση υποδέχεται τον Ρούμπιο και δένει τη χώρα ακόμη πιο βαθιά στα πολεμικά σχέδια ΗΠΑ, ΝΑΤΟ και Ισραήλ.


• Ανεπιθύμητος ο Ρούμπιο. Έξω οι φονιάδες των λαών.


• Να σταματήσει τώρα η γενοκτονία. Τέλος στην κατοχή και στον αποκλεισμό της Γάζας, ελεύθερη είσοδος τροφίμων, φαρμάκων και καυσίμων.


• Καμία στρατιωτική, οικονομική, ενεργειακή και ακαδημαϊκή συνεργασία με το κράτος του Ισραήλ. Ακύρωση όλων των εξοπλιστικών συμφωνιών και της ηλεκτρικής διασύνδεσης Ελλάδας, Κύπρου και Ισραήλ.


• Να κλείσουν η Σούδα και όλες οι βάσεις των ΗΠΑ και του ΝΑΤΟ. Κανένα λιμάνι, κανένα αεροδρόμιο, ούτε ένα χιλιόμετρο εναέριου χώρου για τη μεταφορά όπλων και στρατευμάτων.


• Καμία συμμετοχή της Ελλάδας στους πολέμους και στους σχεδιασμούς ΗΠΑ, ΝΑΤΟ και ΕΕ. Κανένας Έλληνας στρατιώτης στη Γάζα.


• Εκτέλεση των ενταλμάτων του Διεθνούς Ποινικού Δικαστηρίου για τον Νετανιάχου και τον Γκάλαντ. Άρση των κυρώσεων σε όσους τεκμηριώνουν τη γενοκτονία.


• Λευτεριά στην Παλαιστίνη.


Στηρίζουμε τις κινητοποιήσεις και τα καλέσματα ενάντια στην επίσκεψη Ρούμπιο, στην Αθήνα και σε όλη τη χώρα.


Καλούμε τα μέλη και τους φίλους μας να βρεθούν στον δρόμο:


• Τρίτη 6 Οκτώβρη, 7 μ.μ., Προπύλαια στην Αθήνα και στο άγαλμα Βενιζέλου Θεσσαλονίκη.Αντιπολεμική διαδήλωση, με πορεία στη Βουλή και στις πρεσβείες των ΗΠΑ και του Ισραήλ.


Δεν θα μείνουμε αμέτοχοι! Όλοι και όλες στους δρόμους!

 Η ΕΠΙΣΚΕΨΗ ΡΟΥΜΠΙΟ ΣΤΗΝ ΑΘΗΝΑ ΚΑΙ Η ΒΑΘΥΤΕΡΗ ΠΡΟΣΔΕΣΗ ΤΗΣ ΕΛΛΑΔΑΣ ΣΤΟΥΣ ΣΧΕΔΙΑΣΜΟΥΣ ΗΠΑ–ΙΣΡΑΗΛ


 Ο Αμερικανός υπουργός Εξωτερικών Μάρκο Ρούμπιο έρχεται στην Αθήνα στις 6–7 Οκτωβρίου για τον 6ο Στρατηγικό Διάλογο Ελλάδας–ΗΠΑ. Στην ατζέντα βρίσκονται η άμυνα, η ενέργεια και η περιφερειακή ασφάλεια. Στην πράξη, πρόκειται για ακόμη έναν κρίκο σε μια μακρά διαδικασία βαθύτερης στρατιωτικής, ενεργειακής και γεωπολιτικής πρόσδεσης της Ελλάδας στις ΗΠΑ.

author: Fozzie
title: Part IV: The Production of Relative Surplus-Value
content:
Harry Cleaver's study guide to Marx's Capital volume 1, chapter 18.


    Submitted by

Fozzie

 on October 6, 2026


Outline of Marx’s Analysis


Marx’s formulae

 –

s/v

 = surplus-value/(value of

LP

) = (surplus labor)/(necessary labor)

 Classical political economy formulae

 – (surplus labor)/(working day) = surplus-value/(value of product) = (surplus product)/(total product)

 – working day, value of product, total product =

s+v

 in Marx’s terms (leaves out

MP

 or

c

)

 Political economy formulae

 – understates rate of surplus-value

 – conceals exchange of wage for

LP


 – creates the illusion of sharing according to contribution vs actual antagonism


v

 = paid labor,

s

 = unpaid labor, popular expressions for (surplus labor)/(necessary labor)

 capital = command over unpaid labor


Commentary


In this chapter Marx, pauses a moment before the section on wages, to juxtapose his own formulations to those of classical political economy and to critique the latter in ways that foreshadow the critiques he will make in the next three chapters.


By always comparing surplus value (or product) to the total value (or product), classical political economists portrayed the relationship between workers and capitalists in ways that 1) hid the existence of exploitation and 2) created an illusion that labor was getting its fair share. The existence of exploitation was hidden by making it appear that each factor of production, i.e., labor and capital, is rewarded according to its contribution to production. So, surplus value,

s

, appears to equal capital’s contribution and

s/(s + v)

, its share, while by implication, variable capital,

v

, appears to equal labor’s contribution and

v/(v+s)

, its share. Within a few decades after

Capital

 was published, neoclassical economists, having substituted utility for labor value, would use the same trick but with fancier mathematics.


Mathematical concepts such as production functions, e.g.,

Q = f(K, L)

, permitted the use of calculus to derive marginal products for

K (dQ/dK)

 and

L (dQ/dL)

 and with a few more assumptions, conclude that wages = market value of

dQ/dL

 and profits = the market value of

dQ/dK

. In the development of this theory of production, the labor theory of value of the classical political economists was set aside, so the only “value” left was money price determined by markets. Yet the conclusion was essentially the same, both the old formulae and the new ones hid exploitation by reducing the antagonistic social relations of production to engineering-like technical relations among things.

(1)


For Marx, by formulating the value of labor as one part of the working day, the classical political economic formulation understated what was for him the essential issue: how much of workers’ time toiling produced the means of consumption they needed (or their value/money equivalent) and how much of their work time produced the means of production (or their value/money equivalent) capital needed. Clearly, both formulations of the rate of surplus-value, the classical one,

s/(v+s)

, and his own,

s/v

, are possible measures of capital’s share of the total new value created. He preferred

s/v

 because it provided a more direct representation of the division of workers’ days. When he notes how

s/(v+s)

 is a “mode of presentation which arises, by the way, out of the capitalist mode of production itself”


(2)

 and promises to return to the point later on, odds have it that he was thinking about the parallel between

s/(v+s)

 and

s/(c+v)

, the rate of profit. He did return to juxtapose the rate of profit to the rate of exploitation in material included in Volume III of

Capital

 where he presents the rate of profit as expressing capital’s preoccupation with the rate of return on its investment

(c+v)

 and the rate of exploitation as expressing the degree to which workers are being exploited, i.e., forced to produce products and value for someone else.

(3)


Commenting on the “popular expression” that juxtaposes unpaid to paid labor, instead of surplus to necessary labor, Marx affirms the reasonableness of that way of talking about exploitation in money terms. By pretending to buy labor, rather than labor-power, capitalists argue that all labor is paid for. But as workers grasp intuitively and Marx’s analysis in

Chapter 6

author: Katja Diehl
title: Part 1/3: Vom „schlechten Weg" zum elektrischen Tuk Tuk: Graubünden zeigt, was geht.
content:
Es ist zwar erst ein paar Tage her, aber aus den Erlebnissen werden schon Erinnerungen.


Meine Delegationsreise in die Schweiz, genauer gesagt nach Graubünden, hat mich mit Energie „vollgepumpt”, dieses Format zu verstetigen. Dieser Wissenstransfer ist nur möglich, wenn Menschen sich begegnen. Die Gruppe lernte hautnah beim „Erfahren“ der gerechten Mobilität, wie Expert*innen vor Ort diese gestaltet hatten - aber auch die Gastgebenden konnten von der Gruppe und ihren Hinweisen profitieren.


Hier ein Rückblick auf unseren ersten Tag, den wir mit einer Führung „in die Vergangenheit“ begannen. Während Autobahnen in Deutschland eher geschichtslos sind, da sie erst mit dem Aufkommen des Automobils entstanden sind, können die Wege in Graubünden, auf denen sich heute sowohl Autos als auch Waren bewegen, auf eine Geschichte zurückblicken, die bis in die Römerzeit zurückreicht. „Viamala” (zu Deutsch: „schlechter Weg”) war ein berüchtigtes Teilstück beim Überqueren von Alpenpässen, da es sehr gefährlich war. In Thusis, unserer ersten Station, wurden die erschöpften Pferde seinerzeit gegen frische ausgetauscht.


In Deutschland undenkbar:


Ein 150-Seelen-Dorf wird mittels einer elektrischen Seilbahn an das Nahverkehrsnetz angeschlossen. Die Fahrt mit der Gondel dauert nur sieben Minuten, mit dem Bus hingegen 40 Minuten. Die Fahrgastzahlen erreichten innerhalb kurzer Zeit Rekordniveau, da dieses Angebot auch für Tourist*innen ein Ziel erschloss, das sie zuvor vielleicht nicht auf der Karte hatten. Die Bahn fährt bis tief in den Abend, danach kann das Publicar, ein Rufbus, bestellt werden. Ein Traum.


Krönender Abschluss des Sonntags war die Begrüßung durch Remi Crameri, Gemeindeammann von Thusis, mit ihm durfte ich bereits am Donnerstag einen Talkabend über Mobilität gestalten. Er berichtete uns von einer anstehenden Ratssitzung, in der das Gesamtkonzept des Verkehrs im Kanton Graubünden bis in die Dörfer hinein aufeinander abgestimmt werden soll, um weitere Verbesserungen zu erzielen. Ein besonderes Highlight für ihn ist das Projekt mit Elektro-Tuk-Tuks. Diese sollen Tourist*innen bequem vom Bahnhof Thusis in die Viamala-Schlucht bringen. Das zeigt, wie wichtig der Tourismus für eine gerechte Mobilität ist.


Die nächste Delegation ist bereits terminiert, kommentiere einfach LUXEMBURG, dann schicke ich dir den Stand der Planungen gern zu! Das besondere Highlight hier: Der ehemalige Verkehrsminister und "Vater" des kostenlosen ÖPNV in Luxemburg, François Bausch, wird unser lokaler Guide sein.


Danke an alle, die dabei waren - ich hoffe für uns alle, dass ich diese Konzept ausweiten kann. Es funktioniert umwerfend gut!

author: CNT Granollers
title: La seguridad de las personas trabajadoras debe estar por delante de los beneficios
content:
Desde la CNT del Vallès Oriental queremos denunciar la gestión del episodio de lluvias intensas y, especialmente, la carencia de medidas suficientes para garantizar la seguridad de las personas trabajadoras de la comarca.


Cuando las autoridades activan avisos y alertas por fenómenos meteorológicos adversos, no es suficiente con informar a la población. Es necesario adoptar medidas preventivas que eviten que miles de personas se vean obligadas a desplazarse por las calles y carreteras para llegar a sus puestos de trabajo en unas condiciones potencialmente peligrosas.


Las empresas y la patronal también deben asumir su responsabilidad en materia de prevención de riesgos laborales.


Consideramos especialmente grave que no se haya paralizado o restringido la actividad económica cuando las condiciones meteorológicas y avisos existentes podían comportar riesgos para los desplazamientos y para el desarrollo de determinadas actividades laborales. La protección de la vida y la integridad física de las personas trabajadoras debe estar por delante de cualquier consideración productiva o económica.


Pero la responsabilidad no recae únicamente sobre las administraciones. Las empresas y la patronal también deben asumir su responsabilidad en materia de prevención de riesgos laborales. No es aceptable que, ante un episodio meteorológico adverso, se mantenga la presión para que las plantillas acudan presencialmente a los centros de trabajo como si no estuviera ocurriendo nada. Las empresas deben evaluar los riesgos, activar medidas preventivas y, cuando las circunstancias lo requieran, detener la actividad o facilitar alternativas que eviten exponer a las personas trabajadoras a riesgos innecesarios.


La patronal no puede reclamar que la actividad económica se mantenga a cualquier precio mientras los costes y riesgos de esta decisión recaen sobre las personas trabajadoras. No puede hablarse de normalidad productiva cuando llegar al puesto de trabajo puede implicar poner en riesgo la integridad física. La prevención no puede quedar subordinada a los intereses empresariales ni a la necesidad de mantener sus ritmos de producción.


También queremos poner el foco en el momento en que se hizo llegar la alerta a la población. Una alerta que llega cuando miles de trabajadores y trabajadoras han salido ya de casa y se encuentran desplazándose hacia sus centros de trabajo pierde buena parte de su función preventiva. La información ante un episodio meteorológico adverso debe ser suficientemente anticipada para que las personas puedan tomar decisiones seguras y para que empresas y administraciones puedan activar medidas preventivas con tiempo.


Ante este tipo de episodios, es preciso recordar que las personas trabajadoras tienen derechos que las empresas deben respetar. El artículo 37.3.g del Estatuto de los Trabajadores reconoce un permiso retribuido de hasta cuatro días cuando no sea posible acceder al centro de trabajo o transitar por las vías necesarias para ello, ya sea por las recomendaciones, limitaciones o prohibiciones de las autoridades o por una situación de riesgo grave e inminente. Ningún trabajador o trabajadora debería tener que escoger entre proteger su integridad física y conservar su salario. Ante una situación de riesgo, el derecho a la seguridad debe prevalecer sobre la obligación de acudir presencialmente al puesto de trabajo. Y las empresas deben informar adecuadamente a sus plantillas sobre estos derechos, en lugar de exigir una normalidad laboral que las condiciones meteorológicas no permiten.


No podemos normalizar que, ante una situación meteorológica adversa, la responsabilidad recaiga individualmente sobre cada trabajador o trabajadora, obligándole a decidir entre exponerse a un riesgo durante el desplazamiento o arriesgarse a sufrir consecuencias laborales por no acudir a su puesto de trabajo. La prevención de riesgos no puede convertirse en responsabilidad individual de quien trabaja: es una obligación empresarial.


La seguridad no puede llegar después del horario de entrada al trabajo. Cuando existe riesgo, prevenir también significa detener.


Desde la CNT del Vallès Oriental continuaremos defendiendo que ninguna actividad económica puede justificar poner en riesgo la integridad de las personas trabajadoras. Los beneficios empresariales no pueden estar por encima de nuestras vidas.

author: Unknown
title: Çelik: Peace requires a democratic state
content:
Debate over a new period aimed at resolving the Kurdish question continues in Turkey. The process, which followed statements by Nationalist Movement Party (MHP) leader Devlet Bahçeli in October 2024 and began with the Call for Peace and Democratic Society issued by Kurdish People’s Leader Abdullah Öcalan on 27 February 2025, has remained on the public agenda for nearly two years.


Different sections of society have expressed a range of views on the process and the resolution of the Kurdish question, while expectations for peace have also continued to be debated over the past two years.


Reis Çelik, director of Let There Be Light (Işıklar Sönmesin), one of the first films to address the resolution of the Kurdish question in Turkey, spoke to ANF about the current state of cinema in Turkey and his views on the Peace and Democratic Society Process.


As a socialist, I am more inclined to tell the stories of what society experiences


Çelik said art was a field that gave voice to what remained unsaid and documented every aspect of life through different forms: “The primary function of art is to say what is left unsaid, to do what cannot otherwise be done, and to document every aspect of life through different means. Music does this, painting does this, sculpture does this, and literature does this. Cinema shows this courage more than any of them.


I am a storyteller. I do not insist on saying, ‘I am going to make political cinema’; I bear witness to my time. With so much injustice, corruption and poverty before me, what else could I think about? Of course, society also needs different things. One person makes people laugh, another makes them cry, and another tells stories about social problems. As a socialist, I suppose I am more inclined to tell the stories of what societies go through.”


Cinema was the most powerful language for saying there is a Kurdish question in this country


Reis Çelik said that when he made Let There Be Light, the state pursued an approach that denied the existence of the Kurdish question, while the arts were also under pressure. Çelik described the difficulties he faced during filming and his struggle to secure a theatrical release: “It was clear that the state’s general approach was to deny the Kurdish question. The arts had also been intimidated into silence. We were going through a period when saying, ‘There is a Kurdish question in this country,’ was considered a crime. It was a dark period in which unsolved killings had reached their peak.


I worked as a journalist for many years and spent time in conflict zones. The reports and photographs we produced as witnesses were being twisted and distorted beyond recognition. During that period, I left journalism and publishing because I wanted to tell what I had to say without allowing anyone to distort it. I decided that cinema was the most powerful language through which I could say that there was a Kurdish question in this country.


With Let There Be Light, I tried, in the simplest terms, to show ordinary people that there was a Kurdish question in this country. We wanted to shoot the film in actual conflict zones, but we were not given permission. The General Staff even sent instructions throughout the region stating that permission had not been granted for the film and that its production should be prevented. To some extent, we shot the film secretly. We tried to disguise it as though we were making a different film. We stayed in caves and did not go into the towns. We came close to freezing. Many of our colleagues needed treatment for years afterwards. Towards the end, our presence in the region was discovered and we faced serious difficulties.


A governor took the initiative and had us escorted safely out of the region. I later learned that he was the first Alevi governor to have served in Turkey. Getting the film into cinemas was also extremely difficult. Because I had worked as a journalist for many years, I was able to approach political figures I knew and eventually secure permission for the film to be shown in cinemas, albeit on a limited basis. My aim was not to become the ‘victimised, heroic director’ of a banned film. Nor was it to sell myself to the machinery of the imperialist Western world. What I wanted was to confront people with their own reality.”


Audiences were subjected to identity checks outside cinemas

author: Unknown
title: Kobanê students react to the Ministry of Higher Education’s decision
content:
Kobanê students gathered in front of Kobanê University to protest the Syrian Ministry of Higher Education’s decision to close the faculties and academies and turn them into part of Aleppo University, demanding that their right to study at Kobanê University be upheld.


The students made several demands of the Kobanê University administration and called for their demands to be taken into consideration and followed up.


The students listed their demands as follows:


1. The preservation of all existing faculties, institutes, and departments


2. Guaranteeing Kobanê students’ right to receive their education in the city where they live


3. Preserving and continuing the experience of education in Kurdish


4. Guaranteeing students’ education and preventing them from suffering academic losses


5. Ensuring the full participation of students in decisions to be made concerning the future of the university


6. Preserving the name “Kobanê University”


7. Preserving the distinct character of Kobanê University throughout the process of organization and integration.


The statement concluded with the following: “As Kobanê students, we are not asking for special privileges. We simply want our rights to receive an education at the university and to equal opportunities to be protected, as well as the city’s access to university education and professional training opportunities.”
